title: 630-646 Spadina Avenue and 67 Harbord Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, planning & development (sc);
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve an Official Plan amendment to redesignate part of the site at 630-646 Spadina Avenue and 67 Harbord Street from Neighbourhoods to Mixed Use Areas. The application proposes no new buildings or additions; the existing buildings would remain. If adopted, the amendment would go to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing for approval, since it touches a Protected Major Transit Station Area.

title: 333 College Street and 303 Augusta Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes for a 20-storey mixed-use building with 638 privately owned student residence units at 333 College Street and the rear part of 303 Augusta Avenue. The project includes at least 60 square metres of non-residential space at ground level, and staff have assessed it against the Official Plan and zoning performance standards for student residences. The front part of 303 Augusta Avenue is not part of this application and would be the subject of a future severance.

title: Dupont Street - Parking Amendments
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends a one-hour parking limit on the south side of Dupont Street near Campbell Avenue, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., in response to local businesses saying customers cannot find parking. The change would put a signed one-hour maximum in place of the current unsigned limit, plus new no-stopping rules between Campbell Avenue and Symington Avenue, to discourage long-term parking and increase turnover. City Council would authorize the changes.

title: 149 College Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve alterations to the designated heritage Stewart Building at 149 College Street, designed by E.J. Lennox in the Romanesque Revival style and designated in 1978. The plan would integrate the retained College Street north facade, east facade and partial east and south facades into a base building with a 60-storey tower above, with stepbacks and a glazed reveal between the old and new construction. Council would also authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement for the building's long-term conservation.

title: 80 Mill Street - Installation of an Accessible Loading Zone
topics: on-street parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: Councillor Chris Moise recommends replacing the 15-minute parking zone on the north side of Mill Street outside 80 Mill Street with an accessible loading zone. The change, developed with local residents and the Gooderham and Worts Neighbourhood Association, would let Wheel-Trans vehicles and people with accessibility permits be picked up and dropped off safely outside the building. Council would rescind the existing 15-minute parking rule and designate the accessible loading zone in its place.

title: King Street East - Passenger Loading Zone
topics: intersections, loading zones, public transit; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: City Council will decide whether to replace the taxi stand on the south side of King Street East, east of Ontario Street, with a passenger loading zone. The change is meant to better suit current street needs, including shuttle bus pick-up and drop-off for the Globe and Mail building at 351 King Street East, with minimal impact on traffic and parking. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on King Street East.

title: 149 College Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes for a 60-storey mixed-use building at 149 College Street, integrating the existing six-storey heritage building. The proposal includes 620 privately owned student residence units, 225 dwelling units and 4,817 square metres of institutional space, with a 235-square-metre public space at the north-east corner. A separate heritage report on the designated Stewart Building will be considered at the same time.

title: On-Street Electric Vehicle Charging Stations - Parking Amendments (Non-Delegated Locations)
topics: on-street parking, parking facilities; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: City Council will decide whether to designate two new on-street electric vehicle charging areas with four charging stations: two spaces on Lansdowne Avenue near Davenport Road and two on Pape Avenue near Strathcona Avenue, for exclusive use by electric vehicles. The report also makes technical fixes to existing EV charging parking rules on Carlton Street, Dovercourt Road and Queen Street East, which were set up in 2022. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on the affected streets.

title: Accessible Parking Space - Davenport Road (Non-Delegated)
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, parking spaces; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking spots, ttc
brief: City Council will decide whether to designate a new on-street accessible parking space for people with disabilities on the south side of Davenport Road near Dufferin Street, and rescind a nearby one whose posted signs do not match the by-law. Council approval is needed because the TTC operates transit on Davenport Road. The correction aligns the signs with the actual by-lawed regulations.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support the 505 Dundas 6-Minute Network
topics: parking regulations, public transit, transportation schedules; airline schedules; bus schedules; rail schedules, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Transportation Services, on behalf of the TTC, is asking City Council to approve parking and traffic changes to support streetcars running every six minutes on the 505 Dundas route from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily. The changes span Dundas Street West between Bloor Street West and Dovercourt Road and Dundas Street East between Yonge and Parliament streets, expanding no-stopping coverage to both morning and afternoon peaks on both sides of the street plus new and expanded left-turn bans. The six-minute service would begin in November 2025, with the priority measures implemented in January 2026, benefiting over 205,000 weekly riders.

title: 257-259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East (Quayside Blocks 1 and 2) - Zoning By-law Amendment and Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: part lot control, zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for the first two blocks of the Quayside waterfront development at Lake Shore Boulevard East and Queens Quay East. Approval would allow two towers instead of one on the north-west block, resulting in four mixed-use towers of 50, 57, 66 and 53 storeys plus two 12-storey buildings fronting Queens Quay East. The blocks would hold about 2,850 homes, including 553 affordable rental units making up 23 percent of the residential floor area, with 45,645 square metres of affordable rental housing. The staff report also references amounts of $538 and $1076.

title: Harbour Street (200 Queens Quay West) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: City Council will decide whether to close the Waterfront Trail and the eastbound curb lane on the south side of Harbour Street, between Lower Simcoe Street and a point 140 metres east, for 55 months from December 31, 2025 to July 30, 2030. The closure would make room for construction staging for a 59-storey condominium at 200 Queens Quay West, with pedestrians using the north sidewalk and cyclists detoured to nearby bike lanes. The staging would be in place during the FIFA World Cup 2026, with delivery restrictions on match days. Council approval is required because Harbour Street is a major arterial road.

title: 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West - TTC Tunnel Construction (Stage1) -Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction; building
brief: City Council will decide whether to extend the construction staging area on Bloor Street West around Dufferin Street, from February 2026 to February 2027, for the underground pedestrian tunnel connecting Dufferin TTC station to the new 33-storey building at 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West. The project has been delayed by approvals, permits, legal agreements and sign-offs, and earlier staging approvals from 2024 and 2025 have already been extended once. Council approval is required because Bloor Street West is a major arterial road.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Team Canada FanFest - February 6-8, 2026
topics: [events in culture];
brief: City Council will decide whether to let the Canadian Olympic Committee use Nathan Phillips Square for the Team Canada FanFest from February 6 to 8, 2026, including a beer and wine VQA garden and alcohol service. Permissions would also cover soliciting donations, sports demonstrations and open flame, all conditional on provincial alcohol approval, the Medical Officer of Health's approval, the city's alcohol policy and event permits. The square is booked through the city's event permitting process.

title: 1 Front Street West - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the Union Station Heritage Conservation District Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve alterations to the heritage Dominion Public Building at 1 Front Street West, a contributing building in the Union Station Heritage Conservation District. The changes would lower 14 of the 18 existing openings on the north facade to give access to new ground-floor retail units, while keeping the building's stone base, symmetrical form and some original windows. Council would also authorize amending the existing Heritage Easement Agreement, in connection with the approved mixed-use towers.

title: 1266 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve demolishing a non-contributing building at 1266 Queen Street West in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District and replacing it with a 27-storey mixed-use building. A zoning amendment for a 24-storey tower with a five-storey podium was approved in June 2024, and a revision for the 27-storey version is under review by planning staff. Heritage staff say the demolition and new building comply with the district plan.

title: Elm Street Streetscape Vision - Final Report
topics: construction, heritage properties, planning & development (sc); building, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council votes on adopting the Elm Street Streetscape Vision for Elm Street between Yonge Street and Bay Street. The vision sets pedestrian-oriented design standards, including better walking conditions, public and cafe seating, planting areas, a possible mid-block crossing and road safety upgrades, developed with community input. Staff would use it when reviewing current and future development applications on the street, with implementation happening in phases.

title: 1 Front Street West  - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve changes to the previously approved development at 1 Front Street West, allowing more residential floor area and less office space in the west tower. No changes are proposed to the approved heights, building envelopes, setbacks or overall floor area of the two towers. The proposal also modifies the north facade of the heritage Dominion Public Building, lowering fourteen windows to open up the proposed retail spaces. The staff report also references an amount of $300,000.

title: Bloor West Village Avenue Study - Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: heritage properties, planning & development (sc), urban design; civic improvements, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: City Council decides whether to adopt the Bloor West Village Avenue Study urban design guidelines, to guide how development applications along Bloor Street West between Keele Street and the Humber River are reviewed. The guidelines support gentle mid-rise intensification that keeps the area's pedestrian-oriented, retail character, and council would also endorse a biodiverse landscape manual for the High Park neighbourhood area and identify specified properties as having cultural heritage value.

title: 59-81 Lawton Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: apartment neighbourhoods, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor to oppose, at the Ontario Land Tribunal, a proposal for 38- and 43-storey residential buildings with 706 homes at 59-81 Lawton Boulevard, while talks with the applicant continue. The applicant appealed on July 14, 2025 after Council missed the Planning Act decision deadline. The proposal includes a 353-square-metre on-site parkland dedication.

title: 1-13 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse a proposed 49-storey mixed-use building with 340 homes at 1-13 St. Clair Avenue West. The 160.6-metre proposal would integrate an existing 12-storey designated heritage office building, but staff say it has not shown how a tall building fits the site, raising wind, servicing, vehicle access and loading concerns and an unresolved relationship with the heritage building. Council is also asked to have the City Solicitor defend the refusal if it is appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 38-50 Park Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: building permits, planning & development (sc), zoning; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service
brief: Staff recommend City Council refuse a proposed 31-storey mixed-use building with 289 homes at 38-50 Park Road. The 107.9-metre building, which would include 40 replacement rental units, does not fit the existing or planned low-rise context of the Rosedale Valley area, according to staff, who cite its height, massing and lack of transition to surrounding Neighbourhoods-designated properties and parkland. Council is also asked to have the City Solicitor defend the refusal if the applicant appeals to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 2451-2495 Danforth Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building permits, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes for two mixed-use buildings of 13 and 29 storeys with 620 homes at 2451-2495 Danforth Avenue. The proposal includes a 2,277-square-metre grocery store, 943 square metres of retail, 354 square metres of public open space at ground level, and 254 vehicle and 714 bicycle parking spaces. Staff say the proposal fits the area's context and conforms with the Official Plan.

title: 6 Dawes Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes to raise the east block at 6 Dawes Road from the approved 17 storeys to 39 storeys. The building would hold 452 rental homes, including three new affordable rental units, with a small ground-floor retail space, 69 vehicle and 508 bicycle parking spaces. A holding provision would keep the zoning from taking effect until Metrolinx accepts the rail safety report.

title: 354-358 Pape Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: building permits, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 10-storey mixed-use building with 41 homes at 354-358 Pape Avenue. The proposal includes one level of underground parking, ground-floor retail and second-floor office space. Staff say it fits the provincial planning statement and the city's Official Plan.

title: 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve demolishing 29 rental homes at 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue so a 12-storey building with 282 units, including 29 replacement rental homes, can be built. Approval would come with a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation. If the owner fails to finish the new building on time, a $20,000.00 charge per demolished unit would be added to the property tax bill as a lien on the land. The related zoning application is being considered at the same time.

title: 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue - Zoning By-law Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 12-storey mixed-use building with 278 homes at 1291-1311 Gerrard Street East and 243-247 Greenwood Avenue. The proposal includes ground-floor retail, 29 replacement rental units and 6 new affordable rental units, and would permit demolition of the 29 existing rental homes. Staff would also study excluding the development from on-street permit parking.

title: 1012, 1014, 1016 and 1018 Gerrard Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 14-storey mixed-use building with 112 homes at 1012 to 1018 Gerrard Street East. The proposal includes 291 square metres of commercial space and one level of underground parking, near a future transit station. The development would be excluded from on-street permit parking.

title: 138 Dowling Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 16-storey apartment building with 145 homes at 138 Dowling Avenue. Staff say the proposal is consistent with the provincial planning statement and conforms with the city's Official Plan. Staff would also study whether to exclude the development from on-street permit parking.

title: 1099 Broadview Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes for a mixed-use building at 1099 Broadview Avenue, with two towers of 14 and 16 storeys above a shared five-storey podium. The building would provide 313 homes, 633 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, an 800-square-metre rear courtyard, and 207 vehicle and 363 bicycle parking spaces. Staff say the proposal fits the area's context and conforms with the Official Plan.

title: 543 Yonge Street - Demolition of a Building within the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District and Approval of a Replacement Building
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve demolishing the four-storey commercial building at 543 Yonge Street, identified as non-contributing within the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District, and replacing it with a 68-storey mixed-use building with retail at street level and homes above. The district plan allows demolition of non-contributing buildings, and staff say the new building fits the district's objectives. A separate zoning report covers the development approval.

title: 543-555 Yonge Street -Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning, zoning designations; permitted use requests; permitted uses
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 68-storey mixed-use building with 679 homes at 543-555 Yonge Street. The 222-metre building would cantilever above the existing building at 555 Yonge Street, which would be kept, and include 402 square metres of non-residential space. Staff would also study whether to exclude the development from on-street permit parking, and a separate heritage report will be considered at the same time.

title: 530-550 Yonge Street, 6-8 Breadalbane Street and 145 St. Luke Lane - Alterations, Demolition and New Construction of Buildings on a Designated Heritage Property under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: construction, demolitions, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; building, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 530-550 Yonge Street, 6-8 Breadalbane Street and 145 St. Luke Lane, to allow the proposed 67-storey mixed-use building. The plan would keep the front facade of 538 Yonge Street and retain 544 and 546-550 Yonge Street in place within the two-storey podium, while 145 St. Luke Lane would be demolished and replaced with a public space fronting the lane. Council would also authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement, and staff say the proposal conserves the heritage properties.

title: 530-550 Yonge Street, 145 St. Luke Lane and 6-8 Breadalbane Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 67-storey mixed-use building with 822 homes at 530-550 Yonge Street. The 213.5-metre building would include 1,012 square metres of non-residential space along Yonge Street and a 168-square-metre privately owned public space facing Dr. Lillian McGregor Park. One rental unit would be demolished, with a tenant assistance plan, and a separate heritage report on the designated properties will be considered at the same time.

title: 170 Merton Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve alterations to the designated heritage property at 170 Merton Street, the former Visiting Homemakers Association headquarters built in 1969. The Late Modern building, with its octagonal towers, ribbon windows and concrete brick, would have a portion retained and its terrace used as outdoor amenity space within a proposed 45-storey mixed-use redevelopment. Council would also authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement to protect the retained heritage elements.

title: 170 and 180 Merton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, heritage designation, planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes for a 45-storey mixed-use building with 531 homes at 170 and 180 Merton Street. The 141.3-metre building would include 198.3 square metres of ground-floor retail, with non-residential uses secured instead of replacement office space, and the owner would be asked to find an off-site parkland dedication. A separate heritage report on the designated building at 170 Merton Street will be considered at the same time.

title: 1673 and 1675 Bathurst Street - Plan of Condominium Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, condominium housing, planning & development (sc); application process, condominiums; condos
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve the draft plan of condominium for 1673 and 1675 Bathurst Street, the legal step that would let the existing eight-unit apartment building become condominiums. No alterations to the building are proposed, and a separate rental conversion application is being considered alongside it. Approval would come with conditions, including agreements to secure them before final registration.

title: 1673-1675 Bathurst Street - Rental Housing Conversion Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve converting an eight-unit rental apartment building at 1673-1675 Bathurst Street to condominium. All eight units rent above the city's Official Plan mid-range rents, and the conversion would not alter the building or change tenants' security of tenure. Conditions include confirming tenants were told about their rights under the Residential Tenancies Act and a written promise not to pass conversion costs on to tenants.

title: Metrolinx’s Scarborough Subway Extension - Fourth Quarter 2025 Semi-Annual Update
topics: [activities in transportation], construction, transportation infrastructure; building, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to receive for information a semi-annual progress update on Metrolinx's Scarborough Subway Extension construction project, with the next update due by the third quarter of 2026. No policy change is proposed.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2549, 743 Warden Avenue, Zahavish Downtown Developments Ltd
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: The city would take over responsibility for the roads and underground services built for the subdivision at 743 Warden Avenue under a 2017 agreement with the developer, as amended in 2024. The city's performance guarantee would be released. Council is asked to approve.

title: 6175 to 6183 Kingston Road, 1, 2, 4, 7, 10 and 11 Franklin Avenue (Blocks 11 and 12) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report
brief: Blocks 11 and 12 at 6175-6183 Kingston Road would be exempted from part lot control rules so 32 lots can be created for 16 semi-detached and townhouse homes, with each home getting its own property title. Staff recommend approving the exemption, which council decides. No design changes are proposed.

title: Kingston Road - Pay-and-Display Parking
topics: change, parking meters, parking prohibitions; amendments; conversion; modification, no parking, on-street meters; single space meters
brief: Staff recommend adding pay-and-display on-street parking on the south side of Kingston Road between Birchmount Road and Cliffside Drive, adjusting existing parking bans to fit, with the rate set at $3.00 in the report. The Toronto Parking Authority says the added turnover would support local businesses. Because the TTC runs buses on Kingston Road, city council approval is required.

title: 6175 to 6183 Kingston Road, 1, 2, 4, 7, 10 and 11 Franklin Avenue (Lots 8 and 9) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: Two lots at 6175-6183 Kingston Road would be exempted from part lot control rules so they can be split into four separate lots for two semi-detached homes, giving each home its own property title. Staff recommend approving the exemption, which council decides. No design changes are proposed.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: council reviews the order paper listing the items to be considered at the meeting. No decision is being asked for.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: the meeting features various informational presentations, introductions and announcements from council. No decisions are being asked for at this stage.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council may file petitions during the meeting for the record. No decision is being asked for at this stage.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: councillors declare any interests they hold under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is being asked for at this stage.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: the mayor and committee chairs introduce committee reports and new business from city officials. No decision is being asked for.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its regular meeting held on November 12 and 13, 2025, as an accurate record.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the council meeting begins with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is being asked for.

title: Enabling Construction at Parkdale Hub - West Block
topics: agreements, road construction; tenancy agreements
brief: Up to $17,724,000 in capital funding to the Neighbourhood Land Trust to build the community space at Parkdale Hub's West Block — the first of three phases at Queen Street West and Cowan Avenue — would be authorized by council, with Toronto Community Housing preparing the TCH-owned property at 245 Dunn Avenue for off-site parking and a shared driveway.

title: Tenancy Update with Beech Hall Housing Co-operative and Alexandra Park Housing Co-operative
topics: co-operative housing, tenants; co-op housing; coop housing; cooperative housing, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: The lease agreements with the Beech Hall and Alexandra Park housing co-operatives would be extended by up to two years on current terms, while new lease and operating agreements are negotiated, pending a council vote. A one-year extension granted in November 2024 was not enough to finish the negotiations.

title: Housing Action Plan: Avenues Policy Review Phase Two: Initial Study of Wards 9 and 11
topics: avenue study, housing; homes; residences
brief: Official Plan amendments for lands along Avenues in Wards 9 (Davenport) and 11 (University-Rosedale), enabling mid-rise housing as part of phase two of the Avenues Policy Review, would take effect if council adopts it. This is the first implementation study under the phase two work plan adopted in June 2025, following OPA 778, which the Ontario Land Tribunal brought into effect city-wide on July 24, 2025.

title: Multi-Tenant Houses Regulatory Framework: Implementation Update
topics: affordable housing, implementation, multi-residential properties, multi-unit dwellings, policy development; affordable homes; housing projects, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, policy making
brief: The multi-tenant (rooming) house rules, updating definitions in the licensing by-law as part of rolling out the city's regulatory framework for these homes, would be amended, if council agrees. Multi-tenant houses are among the most affordable housing forms, serving students, seniors, newcomers, low-income residents and people exiting homelessness. The framework, adopted in December 2022 and in effect since March 2024, introduced city-wide zoning permission and licensing for these houses.

title: 444 Logan Avenue - Making Quality of Life and Environmental Improvements for Seniors
topics: quality of life, seniors; elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens
brief: A new social housing agreement with WoodGreen Community Housing for the 160-unit seniors building at 444 Logan Avenue (Ray McCleary Towers), with the property returning to the city after 40 years would be authorized by council. The agreement would exempt the building from property taxes for 40 years — its annual property taxes are estimated at $239,473. Approving the recommendations would let WoodGreen secure about $27 million in federal funding and low-cost financing for a deep energy retrofit and modernization of the building, improving heating, cooling, and home quality for the 160 low-income senior tenants.

title: 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Two pairs of 1886-1888 Victorian semi-detached houses at 6-8 and 10-12 Sumach Street in Corktown — remnants of the area's late-19th-century residential character beside the Don Valley Parkway ramps — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 39 Wynford Drive - Inclusion on the City of Toronto's Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The 1962 International Style office building at 39 Wynford Drive in Flemingdon Park — built for the A.C. Nielsen Company of Canada and designed by Peter Dickson Associates, completed by Webb, Zerafa, Menkes — could be added to the City of Toronto's Heritage Register. Council decides whether to list the property, a first step toward possible heritage designation that flags its heritage value while full designation is studied further. A demolition permit application for the site was filed in September 2025; staff would report back on designation after the Don Mills area study, by July 2026.

title: 262-264 St. George Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Two 1893 semi-detached Annex-style houses at 262-264 St. George Street could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 241 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The 1911 Edwardian Classicism building at 241 Yonge Street — purpose-built for the Art Metropole artist material supply company — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: Permanent Closure of a Portion of the Public Laneway at 66-66Y Third Street
topics: laneways, road closures; back alleys; mews, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: A section of public laneway running through the parking lot at 66-66Y Third Street would be permanently closed. Council decides on the closure, which is needed for the shelter development approved under the Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy — the existing laneway immediately to the north is unaffected.

title: Community Improvement Plan Amendment for the Economic Development and Growth in Employment (EDGE) Incentive Program to Increase Tax Increment Equivalent Grants and Annual Program Update Report
topics: community improvement plans, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs
brief: To support business investment and jobs amid U.S. tariffs, council is asked to temporarily boost the EDGE tax-incentive program: eligible applicants by December 31, 2027 would get development grants equal to 100 percent of the municipal tax increase over five years. The program keeps its existing annual funding cap of $20 million, and all other eligibility requirements stay the same.

title: 1 Herons Hill Way - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a 34-storey (110-metre) residential building with 343 homes on the eastern part of 1 Herons Hill Way, while keeping the existing two-storey office building on the western part. The approval would amend the ConsumersNext Secondary Plan and the zoning by-law. City Council is being asked to approve.

title: 1125 Sheppard Avenue East (Block 2) - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend refusing a mixed-use development at 1125 Sheppard Avenue East (Block 2): 52- and 48-storey residential towers on a shared six-storey podium with 1,238 homes, plus a publicly accessible open space and a landscaped mid-block link between Sheppard Avenue East and Singer Court. North York Community Council is being asked to adopt the refusal, keeping the current rules for the site.

title: 2135 Sheppard Avenue East, 325, Yorkland Boulevard, 125 Consumers Road, 15 Smooth Rose Court, and 55 Smooth Rose Court - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Staff recommend approving taller, denser buildings at 2135 Sheppard Avenue East, 325 Yorkland Boulevard, 125 Consumers Road, 15 Smooth Rose Court and 55 Smooth Rose Court: Building A would rise from the approved 35 storeys (105.5 metres) to 43 storeys (129.5 metres), with more homes overall and a new mix of unit types. City Council is being asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning amendments. In exchange for the added density, the developer would provide a $350,000 community benefit contribution toward improvements to the nearby Toronto Public Library branch.

title: 71 Talara Drive - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a 36-storey (108.1 metres plus penthouse) residential building with 385 homes at 71 Talara Drive, including 29 rental replacement units and a five-level underground garage with 197 parking spaces. The proposal amends Official Plan Amendment 614 and site-specific By-law 891-2022. City Council is being asked to approve the changes. The item's source material also references $600,000.00 and $2,850,000.00.

title: 544-552 Eglinton Avenue East  and 12-14 Bruce Park Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: Official Plans, applications, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend refusing a 25-storey (82.5 metres plus penthouse, 89.1 metres total) residential building with 256 homes and ground-floor shops facing Eglinton Avenue East at 544-552 Eglinton Avenue East and 12-14 Bruce Park Avenue; the floor space would be 11.96 times the lot area. North York Community Council is being asked to adopt the refusal, keeping the current rules for the site.

title: Metrolinx’s Ontario Line Construction within the North York District - Fourth Quarter 2025 Update
topics: construction, programs, stations; building
brief: City staff are reporting back with the fourth-quarter 2025 update on Metrolinx's Ontario Line construction and provincial Transit-Oriented Communities projects in North York, covering three Ontario Line stations and a transit-oriented communities proposal. North York Community Council is being asked to receive the update for information; no decision is required.

title: O'Connor Drive - Mid-Block Pedestrian Traffic Control Signal - at a point 145 metres North of Sunrise Avenue
topics: pedestrians, traffic, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, pedestrianization
brief: A pedestrian-activated traffic signal is proposed on O'Connor Drive, 145 metres north of Sunrise Avenue. Transportation Services says the signal is justified by its assessment and would improve safety for all road users. Because the TTC runs transit on O'Connor Drive, City Council approval is required.

title: 45 to 47 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, applications, zoning bylaws; application process, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a four-tower mixed-use development at 45-47 Sheppard Avenue East, with towers of 30, 49, 53 and 59 storeys, 2,377 homes and 1,723 square metres of ground-floor shops. The plan includes four levels of underground parking with 689 spaces and an on-site parkland dedication. City Council is being asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes.

title: 36-40 Avondale Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
topics: official plan amendments, residential properties, zoning bylaws; residential real estate, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend refusing a 49-storey (160.15 metres plus penthouse) residential building with 504 homes at 36-40 Avondale Avenue, which would sit on a five-storey podium with 61 resident and 7 visitor parking spaces. North York Community Council is being asked to adopt the refusal, keeping the current rules for the site. If appealed, city staff would defend the refusal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 5318 - 5324 Yonge Street and 11 Churchill Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, demolitions, rental housing; application process, rental properties; rental units
brief: Staff recommend approving the demolition of a three-storey apartment building with 17 rental homes at 11 Churchill Avenue, to be replaced as part of the new development on the site. The proposal includes a tenant assistance plan with a right of return at similar rents and financial compensation for hardship. City Council is being asked to approve the demolition. The item's source material also references $20,000.00.

title: 241-243 Finch Avenue East - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, exemptions, part lot control; application process, exceptions
brief: Staff recommend exempting 241-243 Finch Avenue East from the Planning Act's part-lot control rules so eight townhouse units can be created as separate freehold lots, tied to a common-elements condominium. City Council is being asked to approve the exemption.

title: 32 - 50 Forest Manor Road, North York - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2515
topics: agreements, assumption of services, subdivision (land); subdivision of land, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a technical item: whether to formally assume the municipal services in the subdivision at 32-50 Forest Manor Road (registered plan 66M-2515), built under a 2013 subdivision agreement with Emerald City Development and others is before City Council. Once assumed, the city takes over maintaining the roads and services.

title: 2925 Keele Street (Stanley Greene Block G) Subdivision - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2520
topics: agreements, assumption of services, municipal services; city services, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a technical item: formally assuming the roads and underground services in the Stanley Greene Block G subdivision (registered plan 66M-2520, at 2925 Keele Street), built under a 2018 subdivision agreement with Stafford / Goldman Downsview Ltd goes to City Council for approval. Once assumed, the city takes over maintaining them.

title: 245-251 Marlee Avenue, 1-7 Romar Crescent and 16 Stayner Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Two buildings of 37 and 35 storeys with 886 homes and ground-floor shops are proposed at 245-251 Marlee Avenue, 1-7 Romar Crescent and 16 Stayner Avenue. The applicant appealed the planning applications to the Ontario Land Tribunal after filing in February 2025, and North York Community Council is being asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the hearing.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the CreateTO Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would recommend two public members to City Council for appointment to the CreateTO Board for a term ending December 19, 2029, and to the Build Toronto and Toronto Port Lands Company boards for a term ending December 19, 2027, with the chair recommended from among the candidates — plus recommend re-appointing Marcie Zajdeman to Build Toronto and the Toronto Port Lands Company for a term ending June 16, 2027. Confidential attachments on the candidates would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would recommend two candidates to City Council for appointment to the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board, for a term ending December 19, 2028. Confidential attachments on the candidates would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Naming of the Central Pathway in Earlscourt Park to “Claude Bergeron Pathway” - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: naming, parks, recreation centres; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: The central pathway in Earlscourt Park would be named the Claude Bergeron Pathway, honouring the community advocate who helped improve the park from the early 2000s until 2023. Council would approve the naming requested by the Joseph J. Piccininni Community Recreation Centre Advisory Council — Bergeron advised City staff for 17 years on the walking path and park improvements including the southeast entrance, pool fence and St. Clair Avenue West frontage. The park is near Davenport Road and Lansdowne Avenue. Park users would see the new name.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Street Haven at the Crossroads - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: women; shelters for women
brief: Street Haven at the Crossroads, a women's shelter at 87 Pembroke Street, would get $50,000.00 for fire safety upgrades. Council would release the Section 37 funds from 319 to 323 Jarvis Street for the work bringing the second floor to the latest fire code — including audible and visual alarms meeting Toronto Shelter Standards, accessibility guidance and the Ontario Building Code — which would increase the available shelter space. Street Haven has served women seeking shelter, housing and health care since 1965. The women using the shelter would benefit from the safer building.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2024 Participatory Budgeting Projects for the Mural Project at 237 Gerrard Street East (West Face) - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: public art, urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: A mural on the west face of 237 Gerrard Street East would get $50,000.00 in resident-voted developer funds. Council would release the Section 37 money from the $750,000 Ward 13 participatory budgeting envelope for the St. James Town mural project, which needed additional review after the 2024 voting. Residents chose the projects through crowdsourced ideas vetted for cost and feasibility. The mural would add public art to the Gerrard Street East building.

title: 369 Cummer Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The City would go to the Toronto Local Appeal Body to support the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of a lot severance and variances at 369 Cummer Avenue. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to oppose the applicant's appeal of the October 23, 2025 refusal — which covered splitting the land into two lots, each with a new dwelling and garden suite (three units per lot), requiring frontage and area variances. Planning staff had recommended refusal, saying the consent failed the Planning Act tests. The motion also covers negotiating a settlement.

title: Authority to Enter into a Crossing Agreement with Sun-Canadian Pipe Line Company Limited to Facilitate the Replacement of the Playground at Clarinda Park - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: construction, playgrounds; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, building
brief: This is a procedural item: Council would let parks staff sign a crossing agreement with Sun-Canadian Pipe Line Company Limited so construction equipment can cross the pipeline right of way to replace the playground at 31A Clarinda Drive in Ward 17. The Technical Standards and Safety Act requires written permission from the pipeline operator before vehicles cross its right of way; Sun-Canadian has reviewed the City's plans and is prepared to consent. No policy change is proposed.

title: Advancing Housing Development at 838 Broadview Avenue - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: development, parking; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff would report back in March 2026 with a plan to develop the city-owned lands at 838 Broadview Avenue for mixed-income affordable housing under the Toronto Builds framework. Council would request the plan for the site — bought by the Toronto Parking Authority in 2016 for parking, with a 2019-approved affordable and market housing project alongside 840, 842 and 844 Broadview Avenue that stalled after four six-month extensions of the owner-led process. The City lands now hold a retail building and surface parking lot. The plan would aim to maximize affordable housing on the combined lands.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - 10 Rosehill Avenue - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: arts and culture, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Council would start a city-led zoning change for 10 Rosehill Avenue to allow temporary arts and culture uses supporting Toronto's creative sector while longer-term housing plans continue. The CreateTO-administered property is being explored with Economic Development and Culture and the Toronto Music Office for cultural and music-related uses — possibly including an entertainment venue or performing arts studio — not currently permitted under the zoning, while due diligence continues on the Toronto Builds housing site. The motion is urgent to get direction before a first-quarter 2026 report-back. Artists and audiences would use the temporary space.

title: Protecting the Ontario Science Centre Building and Preserving Recreation Assets for Flemingdon and Thorncliffe Park Residents - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: science & technology (sc);
brief: The province would be asked for a full update on the condition of the closed Ontario Science Centre building — what repair work has been done since June 2024 and what stabilization is planned. Council would make the request after the province closed the 770 Don Mills Road building and announced a move to a smaller Ontario Place site without consulting Flemingdon Park and Thorncliffe Park residents, who relied on the centre for jobs and education; over 96,000 letters have gone to the Premier through the Save Ontario Science Centre campaign. The motion says the province has lease obligations to maintain the building but Council has seen no verification, and the building's upkeep affects any future science programming there. The decision on the building rests with the province.

title: 2444 Eglinton Avenue East - Project Amendments - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: affordable housing, official plan amendments; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Council would amend the approved business terms for the Housing Now affordable housing project at 2444 Eglinton Avenue East, removing the market-rate lands portion of the deal. The project — three residential towers, one market ownership and two co-op buildings developed by Kennedy Green Non-Profit Homes, delivering 612 new co-op homes as one of Ontario's largest affordable housing projects in 25 years — was advanced through a 2023 competitive market call. The amendment changes the deal structure while keeping the affordable housing. Future residents of the co-op homes would be the beneficiaries.

title: Amendment to Retainer Agreement Purchase Order 6057271 with Borden Ladner Gervais LLP for Legal Services Related to Quayside Phase 1 - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: The City's legal services retainer with Borden Ladner Gervais LLP for the Quayside affordable housing development would rise from $500,000 to $750,000. Council would approve the $250,000 increase to purchase order 6057271 — entered June 16, 2025 after an invitation for legal services — to support the City's negotiations with Waterfront Toronto, the developer, the development manager, affordable housing providers and Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation on acquiring property interests and securing financing, construction, delivery and operation of the purpose-built and affordable rental buildings in Quayside Phase 1. The increase would fund the complex legal work behind the affordable housing project.

title: Authorization to Redirect Section 37 Funds to the Ralph Thornton Community Centre - by Councilor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councilor Alejandra Bravo
topics: funding; financing
brief: The Ralph Thornton Community Centre would get $80,000 in redirected developer funds for capital work, including replacing worn second-floor flooring. Council would redirect the Section 37 money — $50,000 for 3,260 square feet of second-floor flooring whose nail-heads are exposed and boards are disintegrating, and $30,000 for exterior signage and wayfinding including the blade sign; the item's figures also list $40,572.19, $13,217.68 and $26,210.13 — for the two projects at the heritage building. Heritage Planning has been consulted on the signage. Centre users would get safer floors and clearer signage.

title: Authority to Conduct a Sweepstakes and to Purchase Host City Allocated Tickets and Additional Hospitality Assets to Generate Revenue for the City of Toronto’s Hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026 - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: revenue generation, tickets; revenue tools
brief: The City's FIFA World Cup 2026 secretariat could buy the city's full ticket allotment and run a sweepstakes to generate hosting revenue. Council would authorize buying Toronto's allocation — 591 tickets per match, 3,546 across the six Toronto matches, of which 1,594 (about 45 percent) are already in the Host City Commercial Hospitality Program — with the remaining 1,952 tickets to expand commercial sales; the item's figures list $10.7 million and $380.0 million. Like Vancouver, the City could also run a promotional sweepstakes for fans, with ticket costs treated as a commercial sales expense paid from sales and donations revenue. The revenue would offset the City's World Cup hosting costs.

title: Support for Establishing a combined Federal, Provincial and Municipal Law Enforcement Task Force to Combat Antisemitic Acts of Hate and Terror - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: safety; public safety
brief: The federal and provincial governments would be asked to work with the City on a joint law enforcement task force to combat antisemitic acts of hate and violence. Council would make the request after the motion cites the December 14 terrorist attack at Bondi Beach in Sydney, Australia — where fifteen people were killed at the annual Chanukah by the Sea event — and ongoing antisemitism at Toronto's places of worship, schools and businesses. The motion notes Toronto Police's Project Resolute has cost the City more than $30 million above the approved police budget, largely to protect the Jewish community with only nominal federal or provincial support, and that the City created a $2.5 million Hostile Vehicle Mitigation Grant for vulnerable institutions. The task force would plan for, combat and prevent antisemitic hate and violence.

title: Providing Circular Materials with Access to the City’s Dual-Use Waste Collection Containers for the Collection of Blue Box Materials from Impacted Properties - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: waste collection; collection (activity); collection routes
brief: Solid waste staff could sign an agreement with Circular Materials so recyclables can be collected from the City's dual-use bins. Council would authorize the deal for the 358 properties — mostly with tight storage space — that use one green-lidded bin for garbage one week and recycling the next, a practice in place since about 2008. Circular Materials requested access to the City-owned bins for Blue Box collection. The motion is urgent because the Blue Box transition to Extended Producer Responsibility ends December 31, 2025, when producers take over. Residents with dual-use bins would see no interruption in recycling pickup.

title: Amending Item 2023.PH7.5 - Parkdale Hub - 1303, 1313, 1325, 1337 and 1345 Queen Street West and 212, 220 and 224 Cowan Avenue - Municipal Address Correction, by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: This is a technical correction: Council would remove references to 1345 Queen Street West from the Parkdale Hub development approvals, correcting the municipal addresses. The Parkdale Hub concept — improving City-owned facilities and community agency space and unlocking City-owned lands for affordable rental housing, approved in November 2023 with site-specific by-law 1145-2023 — was enacted for lands that did not include 1345 Queen Street West. Amending item 2023.PH7.5 is required. No policy change is proposed.

title: Amending 2024.NY16.1 - 6125 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would update its September 2024 approval for the 16-storey mixed-use building at 6125 Yonge Street with refined zoning wording on landscaping, accessible parking, building height, first floor height, setbacks and encroachments. The applicant worked with the City on the draft by-law revisions, including clarifying the maximum height to cover the mechanical penthouse and exempting the site from a rear landscaping setback next to the laneway. Amending item 2024.NY16.1 is required. No policy change is proposed.

title: Amending Items 2017.CC34.5 and 2025.GG24.14 respecting Non-Profit Licensed Daycare Centre at 115 and 117 to 127 Broadway Avenue - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos-Lin
topics: child care facilities; child care agencies; child care centres; day cares; day nurseries; home care agencies; home child care providers; nursery schools
brief: Council would update its earlier decisions on the non-profit licensed daycare at 115 to 127 Broadway Avenue so the lease details follow the City's Child Care Term Sheet. The daycare was secured as a Section 37 benefit through a 2017 Local Planning Appeal Tribunal settlement, with the long-term lease registered on title in 2020; the amendments to items 2017.CC34.5 and 2025.GG24.14 are technical. The change affects the lease terms for the daycare facility in the development.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.MM33.44 - Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds from the Development at 109 Vaughan Road for Streetscape Improvements in the Hillcrest Village Business Improvement Area - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: business improvement areas, sidewalks; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is a technical correction: Council would fix its earlier decision on Hillcrest Village streetscape funding, replacing the $41,340 approved in error — money that does not exist in the account — with the correct $10,052.86. Reopening item 2025.MM33.44 is required; the item's figures break the corrected amount into $1,966 and $8,086.86, funded by Committee of Adjustment decisions for 109 Vaughan Road and 834 to 840 St. Clair Avenue West. The accessible ramp, stairs, planters and seating project in front of 803 to 815 St. Clair Avenue West is already underway. No new policy is proposed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds to the Toronto Transit Commission for the Installation of Public Art at Yorkdale Subway Station - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: arts and culture, subway stations;
brief: The TTC would get $727,528.00 to restore the Arc-en-Ciel public art installation at Yorkdale subway station. Council would add $727,528.00 gross ($0 debt) to the TTC's 2025-2034 capital budget, fully funded by Section 45 developer funds, so artist Michael Hayden's 1987 installation — 79 chromatic arches of 158 hand-painted neon glass tube pairs forming a rainbow in the station's transparent ceiling, removed in the mid-1990s over maintenance issues — can be rebuilt with updated LED lighting. The artist and the TTC have agreed in principle. Riders at Yorkdale would see the restored artwork.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.NY25.9 - 133 and 141 Erskine Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would fix a clerical error in its earlier approval for demolishing 26 rental units at 133 Erskine Avenue, correcting the rents and rent classifications for two of the replacement rental units. Reopening item 2025.NY25.9 is required. The motion is urgent to correct the approved recommendations.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.PH18.1 - 267-275 Merton Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: pedestrian crossovers, zoning bylaws; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would remove the parts of its earlier approval for 267 to 275 Merton Street that required the developer to design, construct and deliver a public park connecting Merton Street to the Kay Gardner Beltline Trail. The affordable housing project by Collecdev-Markee on City-owned land already carries the mid-block connection obligation — design, construction, maintenance and operation for 99 years — in its ground lease negotiated by CreateTO, making the zoning approval wording redundant. Reopening item 2025.PH18.1 is required. No new policy is proposed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Design and Construction of an Outdoor Learning and Community Seating Area at Cliffside Public School - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Cliffside Public School in Scarborough would get a $100,000.00 outdoor learning and community seating area. Council would release $100,000.00 in Section 37 Ward 20 funds to the Toronto District School Board for benches, shade features and accessible pathways supporting structured outdoor learning, small group instruction and environmental education. The space would serve students during the school day and be open to the public after hours, adding gathering space the area lacks. Cliffside families and students would use it.

title: Advancing the West Scarborough Rail Trail - Connecting Scarborough, Enhancing Mobility Options - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: improvement, public transit; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: Transportation staff would start a study to advance the proposed West Scarborough Rail Trail between the Warden and Kennedy subway stations. Council would direct the work — including early design and options for a continuous trail along the former GN-GECO rail spur — building on the Warden Woods Community Secondary Plan direction from 2022 and recommendations Council considered in June 2024, with a feasibility study due in the third quarter of 2026. The corridor would eventually connect north to the Meadoway toward Rouge Park and south to the Taylor Massey Creek Trail. Scarborough cyclists and pedestrians would use the trail.

title: Community Services Partnership Funding Increase Request for Cecil Community Centre - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: community centres, funding; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, financing
brief: The Mayor would be asked to consider adding $135,000 to the 2026 budget for the Cecil Community Centre. Council would make the request for the downtown centre — which serves a high-needs, low-income population with childcare, housing and employment support, English language resources and warming centre surge service — after it lost paid bookings and fundraising capacity while operating as a warming centre. The centre currently receives only $6,567 a year from the Community Services Partnership grant program, far less than the eight other Association of Community Centres members, with no meaningful increase in over a decade. The request aims to bring its funding into equitable alignment.

title: 17 St. Andrew Street - Technical Amendment to By-law 447-2023 - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: by-laws, zoning; bylaws
brief: This is a technical correction: Council would fix minor errors in the site-specific zoning by-law for 17 St. Andrew Street so construction of the approved 5-storey mixed-use building can continue. The corrections to By-law 447-2023 cover Type G loading space access, unit locations on the same storey, angular plane projection along the rear yard setback, landscaping next to a residential zone and lane access — reflecting the development concept Council already approved. No policy change is proposed.

title: Union Station Enhancement Project, Package 1 - Amendment to Funding Agreement for Real Estate Services and Agreements - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: real estate transactions, stations;
brief: The City could accept $830,000.00 in additional Metrolinx funding for a temporary real estate staff position on the Union Station Enhancement Project. Council would amend the funding agreement so the City can take the Metrolinx money to fund one more temporary full-time staffer — bringing the Metrolinx-funded City staff on the project to three — plus increase the retainer for external legal advice on property agreements and add other incremental resources for real estate services on USEP-1, the enabling works for a south concourse connecting into Union Station. The resources are conditional on full Metrolinx funding. The motion is urgent to keep the GO Expansion package moving.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2024.PH17.3 - 50 Wilson Heights Boulevard (Block 1) - City Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
topics: zoning;
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would update its December 2024 approval for Block 1 at 50 Wilson Heights Boulevard with revised building height, stepbacks, amenity rates and parking requirements. The applicant proposed a slight height increase, a modified stepback, removal of the ground-floor dwelling unit requirement, reduced amenity rates and removal of the parking rate requirement; staff support the changes through a supplementary report. Reopening item 2024.PH17.3 is required. No policy change is proposed.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.IE19.7 - Wastewater Energy Program Implementation - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: environmental programs, wastewater; environmental initiatives; green living, sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would clarify when the term of wastewater energy agreements begins, tying the start date to delivery of a commissioning notice rather than agreement execution. The March 2025 authorization lets Toronto Water and Environment, Climate and Forestry sign Wastewater Thermal Energy Agreements of up to 30 years — the first project serves Toronto Western Hospital, and a second at Exhibition Place would serve 2.5 million square feet and cut greenhouse gas emissions by about 90,000 tonnes over 30 years. Reopening item 2025.IE19.7 is required. The change affects when the 30-year clock starts for the low-carbon heating and cooling projects.

title: Prioritizing Ward 20 Listed Heritage Properties and Conserving the former General Engineering Company (Canada) Limited Lands - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Planning staff would review ten listed heritage properties in Ward 20 for formal designation before a provincial deadline removes them from the heritage register on January 1, 2027. Council would direct the review under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act — with consultation of property owners and the local councillor — after Bill 23 set the deemed expiry for properties listed before January 1, 2023. The motion also covers conserving the former General Engineering Company (Canada) Ltd. lands, the Second World War munitions plant site. Designation would protect the sites' heritage features.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 30 Tippett Road for Streetscape Improvements in the Wilson Village Business Improvement Area - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Streetscape improvements in the Wilson Village business improvement area in North York would get $60,000.00 this year. Council would add $60,000.00 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Non-Program operating budget, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from the development at 30 Tippett Road (south lands), and forward the money to the Wilson Village BIA. The BIA developed the streetscape project with the City's BIA office. Shoppers and businesses in the area would see the upgrades.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Buddies in Bad Times - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: improvement, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: Buddies in Bad Times theatre would get $524,447.73 in building upgrades, including accessibility, safety and energy efficiency work. Council would release $524,447.73 in Section 37 developer community benefits from 89 to 99 Church Street for the capital improvements at 12 Alexander Street — a City-owned building the company has used for over two decades. The theatre, described as the world's longest-running and largest queer theatre, would proceed with the work in 2026. Audiences, artists and staff using the space would benefit.

title: Ontario Big Mayors Meeting Hosted at the City of Toronto - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: mayors;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council would receive, for information, a report on the December 5, 2025 Ontario Big City Mayors meeting hosted at Toronto City Hall. The report, presented by Councillor Paul Ainslie on behalf of Mayor Olivia Chow, covers the meeting's agenda of mental health and homelessness, infrastructure, and updates from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities and the Association of Municipalities of Ontario, including the new PULSE panel. No policy change is proposed.

title: Showing Respect for Transit Customers: Implementing a Toronto Transit Commission Money-Back Guarantee - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, transit fares; ttc
brief: The TTC board would be asked to create a money-back guarantee giving riders refunds when a trip is delayed by 15 minutes or more from expected on-time performance. Council would make the request, citing the motion's argument that riders budget extra time for regular disruptions and should not bear the cost of arriving late — and pointing to refund models used in London, Singapore, Washington D.C. and by GO Transit in Ontario, plus slow service on the new Line 6 Finch West LRT. The refund system would be designed to push the TTC to improve performance. Transit riders across Toronto would be the ones getting the refunds.

title: Public Education on Provincial Legislative Impacts on Municipal Planning - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: public education;
brief: Planning staff would create plain-language, multilingual materials explaining how recent provincial laws affect the city's ability to plan for growth and investment in neighbourhoods. Council would request the printed resource — covering Bill 23, Bill 109, Bill 17 and Bill 60 and their regulations, reviewed annually — in addition to Planning's updated community consultation presentation template on Major Transit Station Areas and Inclusionary Zoning. The motion says the City can help residents understand how provincial decisions impact local planning. Community members attending consultations would use the materials.

title: Speeding Up Light Rail Transit and Streetcars - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: light rail transit, public transit, transportation (sc); local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, lrt
brief: The City Manager would work with Metrolinx and the TTC to push ahead with transit signal priority at intersections along the surface sections of the Eglinton and Finch West light rail lines, with a progress update in early 2026. Council would direct the work after the Finch West LRT — Line 6, launched December 7 with a projected 51,000 daily riders and 230,000 people within walking distance — opened without full green-light priority, which riders and experts say it needs to be fast and convenient. Now that the TTC has full operational control, the City can help speed the line up. Riders in the northwest would get faster trips.

title: Amending Item 2024.CC20.24 - 200 University Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment and Site Plan Control Applications - Appeal Report - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
