topics: affordable housing, rental housing, zoning bylaws; affordable homes; housing projects, rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Council would update its earlier approval for 200 University Avenue to reflect an increase from 20 to 24 affordable rental units, making those units eligible for planning and development fee waivers. The applicant's detailed design added the four units within the affordable floor area required by the June 2024 settlement — a minimum of 15 percent of converted office floor space, at least 2,020 square metres, with a 40-year affordability period — on levels 2 and 3 of the existing building. The item's figures list $162,223.00 and $1,213,036.00. The change would add four more affordable homes to the development.

title: Raising of the Kurdish Flag in Remembrance of the Victims on the 38th Anniversary of the Halabja Chemical Attack and Anfal Campaign - by Councillor Nick Mantas, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: flag raising;
brief: The Kurdish flag would be raised each March at a city flagpole, near the anniversary of the 1988 Halabja chemical attack, to remember the victims of the attack and the Anfal campaign. Council would allow the annual raising marking March 16, 1988, when a chemical attack on Halabja killed more than 5,000 people and injured more than 7,000 — defined in 2010 by the Supreme Iraqi Criminal Tribunal as a genocidal massacre — and the wider Anfal campaign in which an estimated 182,000 Kurdish people were killed. Toronto's growing Kurdish community would have the annual commemoration.

title: 199 College Street Community Benefits Charge, College Streetscape - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: community benefits, planning & development (sc);
brief: The community benefits charge from the 191-199 College Street redevelopment would be directed toward streetscape improvements on College Street, in line with the Little Italy business group's master plan. Council would ask the Mayor to direct the charge — from the 2024-approved redevelopment of 191-199 College Street and 74-76 Henry Street, now in demolition — to the BIA's vision for improved lighting, trees, benches and pedestrian facilities, which has strong local support but has been largely unfunded. Pedestrians and businesses on College Street would see the upgrades.

title: Securing More Good Jobs in Toronto: Support for Hosting the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank Headquarters - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: economy, employment opportunities; careers; employment; job applications; job boards; job openings; job opportunities; job postings; job vacancies; jobs; vacancies (jobs)
brief: Council would express support for Toronto as the headquarters of the new Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, a multilateral institution. The motion says the bank — being set up by Canada and partner nations to finance critical infrastructure, secure supply chains and strengthen cyber resilience — is choosing a headquarters that could bring more than 3,500 jobs, and that Toronto faces close to 9 percent unemployment with more than 70,000 residents leaving in the last year; Ottawa has also declared interest. The support would position Toronto in the competition for the institution. The headquarters decision rests with the bank's founders.

title: Moving Forward with Transform Yonge: Visionary Public Realm and Cycling Gains, Without Losing a Lane - We Want it All! - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: Staff would study whether the Transform Yonge redesign of Yonge Street between Sheppard and Finch can keep its safety and cycling improvements without removing a vehicle lane, and whether the plan can extend north to Steeles Avenue. Council would request the study of the 2020 REimagining Yonge plan — road-safety improvements, cycle tracks and public realm upgrades on North York's downtown backbone — amid provincial policies that could stall protected bike lanes. The motion says delaying the project would jeopardize community health and safety. Drivers, pedestrians, transit riders, businesses and cyclists on the corridor would be affected by the outcome.

title: Safety on all City Sidewalks; E-bikes Enforcement - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: enforcement, sidewalks, transportation; transportation services
brief: Transportation staff would report on legal options to let police seize e-bikes and e-scooters being ridden on city sidewalks. Council would ask the General Manager of Transportation Services, with the City Solicitor and the Toronto Police Service Board, to report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the first quarter of 2026 — after Council directed a public education campaign and enforcement blitzes in October 2025, with the motion saying injuries are increasing and stronger enforcement is needed. Riding e-bikes and e-scooters on sidewalks is already illegal and dangerous to pedestrians, especially those with disabilities. Pedestrians would be the ones protected by the enforcement.

title: Update on the Working Group to Advance the Widening of Steeles Avenue East Between Ninth Line and Beare Road to Support Regional Growth
topics: advisory committees, road reconstruction, road transportation; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is receiving an update for information on the working group advancing the widening of Steeles Avenue East between Ninth Line and Beare Road to support regional growth. No policy change is proposed.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2025 Cycling Infrastructure Fourth Quarter Update
topics: bike lanes, bike paths, bikeway networks, cycling; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, bicycle paths; bicycle trails; bike trails; cycling paths; cycling trails; off-road paths (cycling), bicycling
brief: Approval of new bike lanes and trails at several locations — including Ingleton Boulevard, Keele Street, Kingston Road, Kipling Avenue, and Albion Road — totalling 20.5 centreline kilometres of new bikeways, is before City Council. No motor vehicle travel lanes would be removed. The projects are part of the 2025–2027 near-term implementation of the Cycling Network Plan.

title: City of Toronto / Ministry of Transportation of Ontario Agreement for the Maintenance and Operation of Ministry Owned Traffic Control Devices
topics: maintenance, traffic control systems, transportation; traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment, transportation services
brief: Letting staff negotiate a renewed agreement with Ontario's Ministry of Transportation spelling out each side's responsibilities for operating and maintaining ministry-owned traffic signals, signs, and road markings at on-off ramps where they meet city arterial roads goes to City Council for approval. The previous ten-year agreement expired June 30, 2024; the renewed one would run one year with automatic yearly renewals.

title: Proposed Parking Signage Pilot
topics: parking, pilot projects, road safety;
brief: City Council faces a decision on approving an up to 18-month pilot testing four new parking sign designs with larger fonts and simpler language — plus calendar-style signs, illuminated snow-route signs, and fine/tow-away tabs — aimed at reducing confusion and parking violations. In 2024, over 1.8 million parking violation notices were issued for curbside infractions. The pilot would launch in spring 2026 with findings informing future citywide rollout.

title: TransformTO Net Zero Strategy: Action Plan (2026-2030)
topics: climate, climate change, environmental impacts; climate protection, environmental effects; environmental footprint; environmental impact
brief: The TransformTO Net Zero Strategy Action Plan for 2026 to 2030 — which maps out the City's next steps toward net zero emissions by 2040 — goes to City Council for information, along with having staff report back in 2028 with a financial analysis. The plan was co-developed with City divisions and agencies, including Finance and Treasury Services. The City has allocated $1.95 billion in its 2025 capital budget for climate action, plus $13.87 billion in the 10-year capital plan and $78.47 million in the 2025 operating budget.

title: Formal Approval of Gerrard-Carlaw Dogs Off Leash Area
topics: dog off-leash areas, parks, parks and open space areas; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks, green spaces; open spaces
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff work with the local councillor to ensure proper public consultation, design, and budget for rebuilding the Gerrard-Carlaw dog off-leash area after Metrolinx construction ends in 2031, with final approval before construction. The off-leash area closed for the Gerrard Station build; Metrolinx will build a plaza and reinstall the off-leash area when it opens.

title: Opposition to the Amalgamation of Conservation Authorities
topics: conservation authorities, provincial governments, provincial legislation;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to tell the Ontario government it opposes the proposed forced amalgamation of conservation authorities, and to urge the province to pause the plan, keep watershed-based governance, and consult municipalities. The motion says Schedule 3 of Bill 68 would merge Ontario's 36 conservation authorities into seven, weakening municipal control over development on hazard lands.

title: Weston Loop Master Plan
topics: Master Plans, community outreach, parks; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This member motion asks City Council to implement the Weston Loop Master Plan, a community-led vision for 74 acres of connected parkland across five parks along the Humber River in Weston, over the next 25 years. The plan was developed through focus groups, consultations, pop-up engagements, and a local stakeholder advisory group; Parks and Recreation staff participated throughout.

title: Accepting a Donation and Entering into Agreements with the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto for an Asian Garden Project at Cynthia Lai Park
topics: donation, garden parks, horticulture; bequest; toy drive, gardeners; gardening; horticulturalists
brief: Accepting an in-kind donation of up to $15.0 million goes to City Council for approval from the Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Toronto to build an Asian Garden at Cynthia Lai Park (1051 Progress Avenue), and to authorize the related agreements. Council endorsed the project in principle in 2022, provided it is fully funded by the Centre at no cost to the City; the Centre is a non-profit promoting Chinese culture and intercultural understanding.

title: Seeking Clarity on the City of Toronto’s Application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund
topics: funding, housing, sports; financing, homes; residences
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor James Pasternak (Ward 6, York Centre) is asking City staff about the status of the City's application to the province's Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund. The Fund is a $200 million provincial capital program for sport and recreation infrastructure, with a maximum grant of $10 million; there are conflicting accounts of whether the City received any funding.

title: Rallies and Protests Policy
topics: protests; demonstrations; protest marches
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor James Pasternak (Ward 6, York Centre) is asking City staff for information on when Council will receive an updated staff-recommended rallies and protests policy for debate. The inquiry states that managing the more than 3,500 rallies and protests since October 2023 has cost the City over $30 million in police time, and describes disruptions to transit, roadways, and businesses.

title: FIFA Traffic Management
topics: road closures, traffic management; street closures; temporary highway closings, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Josh Matlow (Ward 12, St. Paul's) is asking City staff about the expected impact of the June–July 2026 FIFA World Cup on traffic management — including effects on drivers, pedestrians, and transit riders, road closures around fan zones and the stadium security perimeter, and when the FIFA-mandated transport mobility plan will come to Council.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Axon Enterprise Inc., for Axon Justice Premier Licences
topics: contracts, digital libraries, information & communication (sc), legal matters, licences; legal issues, licenses; licensing, online libraries
brief: Entering a non-competitive contract with Axon Enterprise worth $511,020 ($520,014 net of HST recoveries) for Axon Justice Premier licences to manage Legal Services' digital evidence needs goes to City Council for approval. Axon is the sole provider of the proprietary cloud platform, already used by Toronto Police Services, which receives, redacts, stores and discloses digital evidence from police and fire services for prosecution disclosure in Provincial Offences courts. The deal covers 85 licences over three years at $170,340 ($173,338 net of HST recoveries) per year. The source documents also list $500,000, $511,020, as a figure with a trailing comma, and $511,020. City Council decides.

title: Community Groups Animation of City Hall Podium Rooftop Floral Gardens
topics: community gardens, green roofs, natural gardens, natural lawn and garden care; environmentally friendly lawn care; natural garden care; natural lawn care; organic gardening; organic horticulture; pesticide free lawn care, rooftop gardens
brief: The item asks City Council to have parks and real estate staff set up a process letting community groups and non-profits plant, maintain and animate the floral gardens on the City Hall podium rooftop starting with the spring 2026 season, under city guidelines. Staff would report back to the General Government Committee in the second quarter of 2026 on how it went. City Council decides.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Report: End of Year 2024
topics: health (sc), injuries, insurance, safety, workplaces; bonding; health coverage, job sites; telework; work from home; worksites, public safety
brief: City Council is getting the 2024 occupational health and safety report: lost-time injuries fell 3.2 percent from 2023, recurrences fell 11.8 percent and medical-aid injuries fell 9.4 percent, but invoiced WSIB costs rose from $57.3 million in 2023 to $65.9 million in 2024, driven mainly by claims for mental and emotional illnesses, firefighter cancers and musculoskeletal disorders. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Licence Extension and Amending Agreement for Air Quality Monitoring Station at Metro Hall, 55 John Street
topics: air quality, city-owned properties, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, licences; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems, city owned properties; city properties, licenses; licensing
brief: Up for approval at City Council: a five-year licence extension and amending agreement, at nominal cost, letting Ontario keep operating its air quality monitoring station at Metro Hall, 55 John Street. The station would move from the John and Wellington corner to the King Street West frontage to make room for Fire Station 332's relocation from 260 Adelaide Street West, and it remains the city's only street-level fixed monitoring station for traffic-related air pollution. City Council decides.

title: George Weston Recital Hall Renovations at the Meridian Arts Centre
topics: agreements, construction, projects, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities, building, tenancy agreements
brief: Whether to authorize negotiating and executing agreements, including non-competitive ones above $500,000, for the George Weston Recital Hall renovations at the Meridian Arts Centre, which are solely and fully funded by private donations held by the Toronto Live Foundation is before City Council. The planning and scope phase wraps in January 2026 with construction to begin in July 2026; the project transferred to Corporate Real Estate Management for delivery. The source documents list $500,000, plus $500,000, as a figure with a trailing comma. City Council decides.

title: George Street Revitalization Project - Progress Update and Project Delivery Model
topics: community & life (sc), construction, housing services, projects; building
brief: City Council is being asked to grant delegated authority for the George Street Revitalization Project — the downtown east site combining shelter services, a long-term care home, supportive housing and a community hub, where Council approved a City-delivered two-phase approach in April 2025 — to use a Construction Manager at Risk delivery model and to retain external legal counsel non-competitively to support the construction agreements. The source documents list $500,000, $480,000 and $488,448. City Council decides.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests near Summerhill Station for the Secondary Exit Project - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, properties (real estate), subway stations; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, property; real estate, ttc
brief: Whether to approve the second stage of expropriating permanent and temporary easements at 10 and 20 Scrivener Square near Summerhill Station for the TTC's second exit and fire ventilation upgrade project is before City Council. Council authorized the first stage in 2021 and added easements in July 2025; no one requested an inquiry within the 30-day window, so the expropriation can now proceed to registering the plan. City Council decides.

title: Councillors' Constituency Offices - Designation of Portions of Properties used as Municipal Capital Facilities
topics: councillors, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), taxes; aldermen; alderwomen; city councellors; city councillors; council members; councilors; members of council, city facilities; municipal buildings, levies, property; real estate
brief: City Council faces a decision on designating two leased constituency offices — 582 square feet at 622 College Street (Ward 11) and 1,314 square feet at 215 Morrish Road (Ward 25), about 1,896 square feet combined — as municipal capital facilities exempt from municipal and education taxes. City Council decides.

title: 550 Broadview Avenue - Designation of a Portion of the Property Used by East End Arts Toronto as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: [locations in community and life], arts and culture, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), taxes; city facilities; municipal buildings, levies, property; real estate
brief: Up for approval at City Council: designating about 1,700 square feet plus ancillary parking at 550 Broadview Avenue, leased to East End Arts Toronto, as a municipal capital facility exempt from municipal and education taxes, since it serves as a city community centre. City Council decides.

title: 160 Eglinton Avenue East - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by Central Eglinton Community Centre as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: community centres, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), taxes; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, city facilities; municipal buildings, levies, property; real estate
brief: On the agenda at City Council: designating suite 203, about 2,105 square feet at 160 Eglinton Avenue East, as a municipal capital facility exempt from municipal and education taxes, since it serves as the Central Eglinton Community Centre. The agreement would be with the landlord, 1594342 Ontario Limited. City Council decides.

title: Request for Approval to Apply Proposal Fees and Break Fees on Gardiner Expressway Rehabilitation Section 4, Grand Magazine Street to York Street
topics: construction, highways, projects, transportation infrastructure; building, freeways; motorways; parkways, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: Approval of proposal fees and break fees for the Gardiner Expressway Rehabilitation Section 4 procurement (Grand Magazine Street to York Street), which Stantec is designing in two parts, Grand Magazine to Spadina and Spadina to York is before City Council. Proposal fees partially offset unsuccessful bidders' costs for compliant proposals, while break fees offset costs if the procurement is cancelled; Council previously used the same mechanisms for Section 2. The procurement is expected to begin with a request for qualifications in early 2026. City Council decides.

title: Suspension of Capital Sewer Services Inc., and Affiliated Persons
topics: agreements, contracts, suspension; tenancy agreements
brief: Whether to suspend Capital Sewer Services Inc is before City Council. and its affiliated persons — its parent Capital Infrastructure Group plus five other subsidiaries (Utility Force Construction, Capital Utility Services, CEC Mechanical, MarkerVac and Clean Water Works) — from bidding on or being awarded any city contracts for five years. The city's investigation, prompted by internal controls and Auditor General fraud hotline complaints in March 2024, found irregularities in change order documentation and contraventions of the supplier code of conduct against over-billing and false claims. The source documents list $1.1 million. City Council decides.

title: Revised and Restated Non-Competitive Master Services Agreement with SmartSimple Software Inc., for Toronto Grants, Rebates, and Incentives Portal
topics: agreements, contracts, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council faces a decision on approving a revised three-year master services agreement with SmartSimple Software worth $1,173,706 ($1,194,363 net of HST recoveries), with two optional one-year renewals, for the Toronto Grants, Rebates, and Incentives Portal. The portal is the central online hub where non-profits and resident groups apply for city grants across several divisions. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement of Heritage-Compliant Marble from Tennessee Marble Company for Union Station Great Hall Flooring Restoration
topics: agreements, contracts, purchasing, restoration; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, rehabilitation (property), tenancy agreements
brief: City Council faces a decision on entering a non-competitive contract with Tennessee Marble Company to buy the marble needed to finish the Union Station Great Hall flooring restoration. Only two-thirds of the floor was restored during the revitalization because the rest was cut for budget reasons; the remaining third now poses tripping hazards, and federal heritage rules require marble matching the original quarry, ahead of the station's 100th anniversary in 2027. The source documents list $500,000, $3,100,415 and $3,154,982. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement with Symphony Talent, LLC, for Skills Assessment Services
topics: agreements, contracts, government services, service delivery, services; tenancy agreements
brief: Up for approval at City Council: entering a non-competitive agreement with Symphony Talent for skills assessment software used in city recruitment, supporting about 10,000 candidate assessments a year. The existing contract expires December 31, 2025, and a new recruitment system is still being procured, so this deal maintains operational continuity and avoids hiring delays. The source documents list $500,000, $190,045 and $193,390. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Various Suppliers for the Purchase of Proprietary Parts and Services for Maintenance of Specialized Laboratory Instruments for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, maintenance, purchasing, water, water laboratories; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, private laboratories; water labs; water quality laboratories
brief: On the agenda at City Council: entering two non-competitive contracts with Thermo Fisher Scientific (Mississauga) and Waters Limited for proprietary parts and services for Toronto Water laboratory instruments, totalling $236,650 ($240,815 net of HST recoveries) over three years. The instruments analyze drinking water and wastewater, and only each manufacturer can supply its proprietary parts and service, so competitive bidding is not possible. The source documents also list $500,000, $81,853 ($83,294) and $154,797 ($157,521). City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with IBM Canada Limited for IBM Maximo Application Suite Software as a Service
topics: agreements, contracts, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, tenancy agreements
brief: Whether to enter a non-competitive contract with IBM Canada worth $34,300,219 ($34,903,904 net of HST recoveries) for IBM Maximo Application Suite software-as-a-service subscriptions and support, for two years from January 1, 2026 with an optional one-year extension is before City Council. The deal moves over 1,500 staff across six divisions from the end-of-life on-premises Maximo system to the cloud platform and adds Toronto Water as a new user; a 2025 competitive solicitation failed, so the city is going direct to IBM. brief: Whether to extend the non-competitive catering contract with 2790584 Ontario Inc is before City Council. at two temporary shelter hotel sites and winter respite sites from December 31, 2025 to August 31, 2026, since it exceeds the five-year cumulative threshold. Council can adjust the rates when the budget is adopted, expected in February 2026. The interim rebate for eligible low-income seniors and disabled persons would be $1.4589 per cubic metre, 30 percent below the Block 1 rate.

The item responds to a December 2024 council direction on opportunities for joint projects that could benefit from senior government funding. The report cites a $5 million figure.

The item responds to council's December 2024 endorsement of the 26-degree standard, after staff engagement in 2025, and matters to tenants without air conditioning or heat pumps, since extreme heat is described as Toronto's most urgent climate threat.

title: 2026 Interim Solid Waste Management Services Rates and Fees

brief: Luxury home buyers could pay more land transfer tax. Council is asked to raise land transfer tax rates on luxury homes, starting at 4.4 percent for homes over $3,000,000 and rising to 8.6 percent for homes over $20,000,000, effective April 1, 2026, so higher-priced buyers contribute more to city services. The item cites thresholds of $3,000,000, $4,000,000, $5,000,000, $10,000,000 and $20,000,000, notes the 2024 luxury rate change affected only 2 percent of home buyers and brought in $138 million, and cites a $1,200 figure in connection with family savings from other city measures.

City Council is asked to approve a new Access to Shelter Framework — a structured process for reviewing and assessing proposed changes to shelter eligibility — and to authorize staff to keep running the Emergency Family Shelter Support program while funding is available in the operating budget. With Toronto running the largest municipal shelter system in Canada under unprecedented demand, driven by the housing affordability crisis and the arrival of refugee claimants, the framework affects people seeking emergency shelter access.

title: Reducing Barriers to Youth Employment

brief: This is an information item: staff give an overview of the city's youth employment programs, noting Toronto's 19.7 percent youth unemployment rate, one of the highest in Ontario, with Indigenous, Black, newcomer, and 2SLGBTQ+ youth facing the greatest barriers to stable work. The report notes the city employs more youth aged 15 to 29 per capita than any other Canadian municipality, with over 16,000 youth employed across the city system each year. The committee is asked to receive the report for information.

The Community Partnership Investment Program's 2025 operating budget is $32.197 million gross ($31.314 million net). The report also cites $1.95 million in funding figures, and notes $2.125 million went to 49 organizations serving Toronto's diverse Black communities in 2024-2025. It matters to the community-led, culturally grounded organizations that rely on these grants to deliver programs and services.

The original plan, adopted in April 2022, contains 28 actions and 141 sub-actions guided by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Calls to Action. The funding and engagement affect Indigenous communities and organizations across Toronto.

title: Mount Dennis Community For All Action Plan

brief: A ten-year plan for the Mount Dennis neighbourhood is up for adoption. City Council is asked to adopt the Mount Dennis Community for All Action Plan, responding to new development and transit investment making the area one of the city's most transit-accessible locations, and to establish an interdivisional working group to implement it. The report includes a $50,000 figure tied to the plan. It matters to Mount Dennis residents, including its many new immigrants, Black residents, low-income households, vulnerable seniors, and youth, as growth pressures could displace people from one of the few remaining affordable neighbourhoods.

title: Establishing a Toronto Community Crisis Service Training Centre to Strengthen Toronto’s Fourth Emergency Service

brief: Whether to approve a lease for a Toronto Community Crisis Service (TCCS) training centre goes to council. The centre would train TCCS, the city's non-police mental health crisis team, as part of the SafeTO ten-year community safety plan. It affects how people in mental health crisis in Toronto are served.

brief: Making festivals and events work for people with disabilities is the aim of this item. City Council is asked to direct staff to develop an Accessibility Handbook for Event Organizers, a plain-language guide with standards and checklists so events at city facilities are welcoming and accessible. The staff report notes that barriers in physical spaces, communication and program design can limit participation by people with disabilities.

brief: This is a procedural item: following council's October 2025 direction, the Property Standards Committee is being asked to appoint the Executive Director of Court Services as its Secretary effective January 1, 2026, with authority to delegate the role to each panel.

title: Rules of Procedure for the Property Standards Committee and Electronic Hearings
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee administrator will present on the Property Standards Committee's consolidated rules of procedure and its electronic hearing guide. No decision is being asked for.

title: Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 629, Property Standards, and the Building Code Act, 1992
brief: This is a procedural item: city staff will present on Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 629 (Property Standards) and the Building Code Act, 1992. No decision is being asked for.

title: Governance of the Property Standards Committee Member Training
brief: This is a procedural item: city solicitors will train Property Standards Committee members on the legislation governing the committee and its hearings, in a closed session permitted under the City of Toronto Act for member education. No decision is being asked for.

title: Terms of Board Appointment for the Property Standards Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: city staff will present to the Property Standards Committee on the terms and conditions of board appointment. No decision is being asked for.

title: Code of Conduct and Municipal Conflict of Interest Act for the Property Standards Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: the Integrity Commissioner will present to the Property Standards Committee on the Code of Conduct for adjudicative boards and the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is being asked for.

title: Election of City-Wide Chair
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee is electing its city-wide Chair for the appointed term of office, to serve until a successor is chosen. No policy decision is involved.

title: Introduction of By-laws
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will introduce bills, meaning proposed new by-laws, at this meeting. Introducing bills is a standard step in the by-law process; no policy change is proposed in this item itself.

title: A New Vision for the Washroom/Fieldhouse at Trinity Bellwoods Park
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: community councils, parks and open space areas, washrooms; bathrooms, green spaces; open spaces
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik recommends asking the parks department to consult the public on the future of the washroom and fieldhouse site at Trinity Bellwoods Park. The building was badly damaged in an October 25 fire and city staff say it needs to be demolished, after sitting out of service for some time. The consultation plan would involve the ward councillor, community groups like the Friends of Trinity Bellwoods Park, and city staff.

title: Water Shuttle Pilot - Bathurst Quay Traffic Impact Review
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: vessels; boats
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking the Toronto and East York Community Council to have transportation and waterfront staff report back in May 2026 on traffic impacts and management in Bathurst Quay. The review is tied to Waterfront Toronto's planned east-west water shuttle pilot, expected to start in June 2026, with a stop at Portland Slip in the busy Bathurst Quay residential area. Staff would work with Waterfront Toronto and Toronto Police Service on the review.

title: Improving Traffic Calming Measures on Salem Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends adding one speed hump on Salem Avenue between Bloor Street West and Dupont Street to close a 90-metre gap between existing humps near Dupont Street, where residents report near misses and accidents. The new hump would reduce the spacing to 44 metres, in line with the city's updated traffic calming policy. The motion would also set a 30 km/h speed limit on Salem Avenue between Bloor Street West and Southview Avenue, and between Fernbank Avenue and Dupont Street.

title: Improving Traffic Calming Measures on Gladstone Avenue, between Bloor Street West and Hallam Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends adding three speed humps on Gladstone Avenue between Bloor Street West and Hallam Street to fill gaps between the existing speed humps. The existing humps date to 2000 and leave gaps of over 90 metres, which residents say drivers speed through on their way to the next hump. The new humps would match current city spacing standards and work with humps recently installed on Gladstone Avenue north of Hallam Street.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Sellers Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing nine speed humps on Sellers Avenue between Bloem Avenue and Goodwood Avenue. Residents report persistent speeding at all hours and drivers bypassing arterial roads, with serious incidents including accidents that injured pets and near misses involving children. A survey by the councillor's office found residents voted in strong support, and the motion would also rescind existing permit parking rules on parts of the street.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Hatherley Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing six speed humps on Hatherley Road between Eversfield Road and Harvie Avenue. Drivers often use the local street to avoid nearby major intersections, and residents report speeding through stop signs and aggressive driving, with many young children living on and walking along the road. A neighbourhood survey found residents voted in strong support, and the motion would also rescind parking prohibitions on parts of the street.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Eversfield Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing five speed humps on Eversfield Road between Earlscourt Avenue and Dufferin Street. Residents report near misses with speeding vehicles coming off Dufferin Street to avoid traffic, and a survey by the councillor's office found a strong majority in favour. The motion would also rescind parking prohibitions and permit parking rules on parts of the street to align with the changes.

title: Speed Bumps in Public Lane south of Gerrard Street East, west of Boulton Avenue and Public Lane east of Broadview Avenue, south of Gerrard Street East
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher recommends installing speed bumps in two public lanes near Gerrard Street East and Broadview Avenue: the lane south of Gerrard Street East west of Boulton Avenue, and the lane east of Broadview Avenue south of Gerrard Street East. Residents report persistent speeding, and vehicles have repeatedly damaged the home at 244 Boulton Avenue despite existing bollards. The Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Queen Street East Construction - Parking Replacement near Queen Street East and Broadview Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher recommends temporary parking changes on Carroll Street to replace 25 parking spots on Queen Street East lost to TTC and Toronto Water construction between Broadview Avenue and Davies Avenue. The changes would allow one-hour parking from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on the east side of Carroll Street between Queen Street East and Thompson Street for the duration of the construction, which was delayed and is now rescheduled for January 2026. Staff would also work with the local councillor and the Riverside BIA on further replacement parking nearby.

title: Power Street - Heavy Truck Prohibition
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: heavy truck prohibitions;
brief: Councillor Chris Moise recommends banning heavy vehicles at all times on Power Street between Queen Street East and King Street East. Residents have raised safety concerns for years about truck traffic on the small local road, which is home to several residential buildings and a dog off-leash area and sits near the Don Valley Parkway off-ramp onto Richmond Street East. The ban was proposed by residents and is supported by staff, alongside new traffic signals being installed at Power Street and Richmond Street East and at Power Street and Adelaide Street East.

title: Rosemary Lane Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking;
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow recommends removing the parking ban on the north and east side of Rosemary Lane between Dewbourne Avenue and Bathurst Street. Residents said they struggle to find parking on their street, and the motion would shift the existing weekday morning prohibition to cover the north and east side between Dewbourne Avenue and Bathurst Street. The Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: All-way Stop Control- Soudan Avenue and Lillian Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: signalized intersections; controlled intersections; pedestrian crossings; signalised intersections
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow recommends an all-way stop at the intersection of Soudan Avenue and Lillian Street. Residents have raised sustained concerns about speeding on Soudan Avenue and drivers not obeying the one-way rule on Lillian Street, creating unsafe conditions at the intersection. The Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: John Street Project Communication, Engagement and Construction Management Update
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction; building
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik is asking the Toronto and East York Community Council to have transportation staff report back in January 2026 on the John Street cultural corridor project. The update would cover communication with stakeholders, commitments to community engagement, construction phasing and construction management for the corridor between Stephanie Street and south of Front Street West. The request follows calls from the Toronto Downtown West BIA for reliable, proactive communication about the project, which serves major institutions including the Art Gallery of Ontario, the CBC Broadcast Centre and the TIFF Bell Lightbox.

title: Frederick Street Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik recommends installing three speed humps on Frederick Street between The Esplanade and Henry Lane Terrace. Her office heard from residents seeking traffic calming over safety concerns and received a petition in support. The Toronto and East York Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Via Italia
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing six speed humps on Via Italia between St. Clair Avenue West and Nunes Lane. Residents report speeding vehicles routinely ignoring stop signs, with parents describing near misses involving young children, and a survey by the councillor's office found residents overwhelmingly in support. The motion would also adjust parking prohibitions on the street.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Peterborough Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing seven speed humps on Peterborough Avenue between Greenlaw Avenue and Dufferin Street. Residents report speeding vehicles cutting through off Dufferin Street to avoid nearby intersections, and a survey by the councillor's office found a strong majority in favour. The motion would also adjust permit parking rules on the street.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Morrison Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing six speed humps on Morrison Avenue between Dufferin Street and Harvie Avenue. Residents and the North Corso Residents' Association report drivers speeding excessively down the street, which connects hundreds of residents to shops, schools, parks and transit, and a survey by the councillor's office found residents overwhelmingly in support. The humps would add to existing traffic calming on neighbouring streets.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures on Bloem Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing three speed humps on Bloem Avenue between Dufferin Street and the public laneway east of Boon Avenue. Residents report speeding and drivers using Bloem as a cut-through off Dufferin Street, near the New Hope Community Church, and a survey by the councillor's office found strong support. The humps would work alongside a recently approved turn ban on Dufferin Street to reduce cut-through traffic.

title: Installation of Traffic Calming Measures and Parking Amendments on Boon Avenue, between Morrison Avenue and Eversfield Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming;
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo recommends installing three speed humps on Boon Avenue between Morrison Avenue and Eversfield Road, where residents report speeding vehicles causing accidents and near misses. A survey by the councillor's office found strong support, and the humps would fill a gap left when the section north of Rogers Road was missed in an earlier round of traffic calming. The motion would also remove an existing traffic calming measure that is no longer needed and correct mismatches between parking by-laws and posted signs.

title: Barton Avenue Traffic Calming
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming measures, traffic direction; one way operations; one way streets; one way traffic; two way operations; two way streets; two way traffic, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to make Barton Avenue one-way westbound between Clinton Street and Christie Street. The narrow residential street has drawn cut-through traffic funnelled by navigation apps like Waze, after a previous councillor's maze of one-ways on other Seaton Village streets shifted traffic onto Barton. Local consultation by the Seaton Village Residents' Association and the councillor found residents prefer discouraging eastbound cut-through traffic, and action is more pressing with the coming RapidTO Bathurst streetcar lane.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item TE24.61, Brock Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking;
brief: The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to re-open item TE24.61 on Brock Avenue parking and fix a bylaw issue identified between Bloor Street West and Wallace Avenue. The fix would rescind the daytime stopping prohibition on the east side of Brock Avenue between Wallace Avenue and 160 metres south, ban parking at all times from there to Bloor Street West, and ban stopping at all times between Wallace Avenue and 160 metres south. The re-open follows council's July 2025 motion removing switchover parking days on Brock Avenue.

title: Re-opening Item TE25.15 - 236-254 Old Weston Road - Residential Demolition Applications
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, street occupation permits; curblane permits; road use permits; street closure permits; streets and sidewalks
brief: The item asks the Toronto and East York Community Council to re-open item TE25.15 on the residential demolitions at 236-254 Old Weston Road and drop the condition requiring sod to be laid. Staff support the change because the site will soon be used as a fenced construction access point for the Davenport Road Extension project, with excavation, utility work and roadworks, so laying sod would be a temporary and unnecessary public expense. The site would still have to be kept free of garbage and weeds.

title: Cadorna Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install speed humps on Cadorna Avenue between Davies Crescent and O'Connor Drive. Staff reviewed the request and found the street does not meet the warrant criteria in the Traffic Calming Policy, so they recommend against the humps. Community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Billings Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install speed humps on Billings Avenue between Athletic Avenue and Dundas Street East. Staff reviewed the request and found the street does not meet the warrant criteria in the Traffic Calming Policy, so they recommend against the humps. Community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) - Various Streets in Ward 4
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, transportation; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, transportation services
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install speed humps on seven streets in Ward 4: Alhambra Avenue, Glendonwynne Road, Gwynne Avenue, Humberside Avenue, Indian Road Crescent, Montye Avenue and Vernon Street. Staff assessed each street and found all meet the city's traffic calming criteria. The report would also fix a mismatch between posted signs and by-lawed stop controls on Alhambra Avenue.

title: Compulsory Stop Control - May Street and South Drive
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: intersections, signs, stop signs, traffic; all-way stop controls; technical warrants, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, signage
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install a compulsory stop for southbound traffic at the uncontrolled T-intersection of May Street and South Drive. Staff recommend the stop to clearly define the right-of-way and improve safety for all road users. Community council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Elm Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to extend the afternoon no-standing rule on the south side of Elm Avenue, between Mount Pleasant Road and Sherbourne Street North, to also cover 7 to 9 a.m. weekdays. The morning extension would keep traffic moving during Branksome Hall's school drop-off times, while a parking prohibition would be extended eastward near the Clifton Manor Apartments driveway to protect sightlines for residents. Community council has delegated authority to decide.

title: On-Street Electric Vehicle Charging Stations - Parking Amendments (Delegated Locations)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: on-street parking, stations; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to designate three on-street electric vehicle charging areas with six charging stations: two spaces each on Browning Avenue near Carlaw Avenue, Hallam Street near Concord Avenue, and Humberside Avenue near Mavety Street, for exclusive use by electric vehicles. The locations have been reviewed and supported by the local councillors, and community council has delegated authority to make the final decision. The parking by-law would be amended accordingly.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - November 2025 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, accessible permit parking, parking spaces; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking spots
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install or remove on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities at the locations listed in the November 2025 staff report. The item also adjusts stop controls on Regal Road at Westmount Avenue, replacing the eastbound-only stop with stops for both directions. Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision.

title: Vehicle Width Restriction - Public Lane south of Gerrard Street East, west of Boulton Avenue and Public Lane east of Broadview Avenue, south of Gerrard Street East
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: [land vehicles by function], road restrictions, transportation (sc); lane restrictions; road information; traffic restrictions; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to ban vehicles over two metres wide from two public lanes near Gerrard Street East and Broadview Avenue: the lane south of Gerrard Street East west of Boulton Avenue, and the lane east of Broadview Avenue south of Gerrard Street East. Staff say the ban would reduce damage to surrounding private properties from oversized vehicles using the narrow lanes.

title: Traffic Management in Ward 14 related to the King Street East and Church Street Intersection Project
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, intersections; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council votes on receiving, for information, a report on how TTC tracks and a watermain at King Street East and Church Street deteriorated to the point of needing repair, plus ongoing traffic management in the surrounding area. The report covers the area between the Don River, Eastern Avenue, Broadview Avenue and Gerrard Street East, including recommendations at Broadview and Dundas. No policy change is proposed.

title: Sidewalk Network in Liberty Village - Missing Links
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: sidewalk repairs, sidewalks; roadside repair; sidewalk brick installation; sidewalk brick maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalk ramping; sidewalk replacement; sidewalks maintenance; walkway maintenance; walkway repair
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council decides whether to receive, for information, a report on filling gaps in the Liberty Village sidewalk network ahead of FIFA 2026. Staff found it is not feasible to design and build permanent sidewalks before the tournament, but a quick-build sidewalk on the west side of Mowat Avenue between King Street West and Liberty Street is being discussed with the local councillor. No decision is proposed.

title: Pedestrian and Cycling Safety, Congestion Management, and Traffic Safety Improvements related to the proposed Ontario Place (955 Lakeshore Boulevard West) Redevelopment
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: cycling, road safety; bicycling
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council has transportation and waterfront staff report back in early 2027 on pedestrian and cycling safety, congestion management and traffic safety around the Ontario Place redevelopment at 955 Lake Shore Boulevard West. The report would update work coordinated with the province's redevelopment, including intersection improvements on Lake Shore Boulevard West and better north-south pedestrian access to Exhibition Place and transit stops. No decision on construction is proposed now.

title: 1 Roxborough Street West (Phase 2) - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), construction waste; broken concrete, curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to close the south sidewalk and part of the eastbound curb lane on Roxborough Street West, between Yonge Street and a point 35 metres west, for 25 months from December 1, 2025 to December 2027. The closures would support phase 2 construction of a 12-storey condominium at 1 Roxborough Street West, with pedestrians using the north sidewalk, and the full closure of Paul Hahn Lane would continue. The staff report also references a $4.25 rate.

title: 316-336 Campbell Avenue - Construction Staging Area (Phase 2)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction; building
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to close the west sidewalk on Campbell Avenue and parts of the public laneways for 25 months, from December 1, 2025 to December 31, 2027, for phase 2 of a 26-storey residential building going up at 316-336 Campbell Avenue. Pedestrians would be directed to the east sidewalk. Phase 1 excavation and shoring work was authorized in January 2025.

title: 1320 Queen Street East - Encroachment Appeal - Basement Entrance
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide an appeal from the owner of 1320 Queen Street East over a proposed basement entrance that would extend 2.27 metres below grade within the public right-of-way, with a 0.10-metre setback from the sidewalk. Staff recommend an encroachment agreement permitting the entrance, with conditions including that the owner indemnify the city and maintain it at their own expense.

title: 140 Cumberland Street - Encroachment Appeal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide an appeal from the owner of 140 Cumberland Street over an existing enclosed all-season patio that sits on the Cumberland Street boulevard and sidewalk. Staff recommend an encroachment agreement letting the patio stay, with conditions including that the owner indemnify the city and maintain the structure at their own expense. The staff report also references an amount of $6,955.00.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint and remove directors on ten Business Improvement Area boards, including Bloor-Yorkville, Broadview Danforth, CityPlace and Fort York, College West, Danforth Village, Greektown, Oakwood Village, Rosedale Main Street, The Beach and the Financial District. New appointees include Kimberly Bernard, Kathryn Brownlie, Kerry Chan and Sarah Watson for Bloor-Yorkville, Tracy O'Hara for Broadview Danforth, Nickolaos Papalambropoulos for Greektown, Mikael Walter-Campbell for Oakwood Village, and Jonathan Collins, Melissa Macchione, Karen MacIntosh Ritchie and Owen Stokes for The Beach, along with removing outgoing directors. BIAs are local business groups that manage main-street promotion and improvements.

title: Application for a Sidewalk Cafe Permit Located at 561 Danforth Avenue, Carlaw Avenue flankage
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boulevard cafes, permits, sidewalks; boulevard patios (restaurants); sidewalk cafes; sidewalk patios (restaurants), permit renewal
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to grant a sidewalk cafe permit for 561 Danforth Avenue, at the Carlaw Avenue side. Staff present two options: deny the application or approve it. The decision determines whether the business can place tables and chairs on the public sidewalk.

title: 47 Lewis Street - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: fences; division fences; line fences
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to exempt 47 Lewis Street from the fence height by-law. The existing wooden lattice fence measures 2.48 metres around the rear deck, 2.26 metres through the rear yard and 2.8 metres in the side yard, where the limit is 2 metres. Staff recommend refusing the exemption after a violation notice was issued.

title: 289 Barton Avenue - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: fences; division fences; line fences
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to exempt 289 Barton Avenue from the fence height by-law. The existing wooden fence with an artificial boxwood privacy screen stands 2.75 to 3 metres tall, where the limit is 2 metres. Staff recommend refusing the exemption after a violation notice was issued.

title: 33 Morse Street - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, exemptions, fences; application process, division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to let the owner of 33 Morse Street raise an existing fence from 2 metres to 2.8 metres. The applicant says the taller fence is for privacy amid an escalating dispute with a neighbour; staff recommend refusing the exemption after a violation notice was issued.

title: 34 Tubman Avenue - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, exemptions, fences; application process, division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to exempt 34 Tubman Avenue from the fence height by-law. The existing fence and gates enclosing three ground-floor condo units stand 2.1 metres tall, where the limit is 1.2 metres. Staff recommend refusing the exemption.

title: 93 Silver Birch Avenue - Application to Remove a Private Tree
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: privately-owned trees; private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide an appeal of the city's refusal to permit removal of a privately owned white oak on the boundary between 93 and 95 Silver Birch Avenue. The applicant worries the 74-centimetre tree, which leans strongly over the house, could fail; the tree is healthy and maintainable, so staff recommend denying the permit. Community Council has delegated authority to make the final call on tree-permit appeals.

title: 103 Hogarth Avenue - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, demolitions, residential properties; application process, residential real estate
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to allow demolition of a detached house at 103 Hogarth Avenue, after Toronto Building received an objection letter. Staff offer two options: approve the demolition outright, or approve it with conditions such as construction fencing, debris removal and site maintenance.

title: 5 Robinson Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether the detached house at 5 Robinson Street can be demolished before any permit for a replacement building is issued. Staff present three options: refuse the demolition, approve it outright, or approve it with conditions. The decision determines whether the lot can sit empty with no approved rebuild.

title: 835 Queen Street West - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: building permits, demolitions; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether the mixed-use building at 835 Queen Street West, with ground-floor commercial and second-floor residential space, can be demolished before a permit for a replacement building is issued. The applicant asked to tear it down early; staff present options to refuse the demolition or approve it, with or without conditions. The decision determines whether the site can sit empty with no approved rebuild.

title: 9 Dora Avenue - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: building permits, demolitions; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether the detached house at 9 Dora Avenue can be demolished before a permit for a replacement building is issued. The owner asked to tear it down early since no replacement permit has been applied for; staff present options to refuse the demolition or approve it, with or without conditions. The decision determines whether the lot can sit empty with no approved rebuild.

title: 509 Parliament Street (Carlton Theatre) - Alterations and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve altering and partly demolishing the designated heritage Carlton Theatre at 509 Parliament Street, a one-storey brick movie theatre built in 1929, to allow a new 10-storey mixed-use building. The plan would keep the theatre's west elevation along Parliament Street in place, and council would authorize a Heritage Easement Agreement. The designation by-law itself is currently under appeal at the Ontario Land Tribunal and is not yet in force.

title: Zoning By-law Amendment for Garden Suites on Parkmount Road Facing Craven Road - Final Report
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council will decide on a zoning amendment settling what garden suites are allowed on Parkmount Road properties facing Craven Road, between Danforth Avenue and Hanson Street. Council directed the review in October 2024 to consider provincial planning changes, past consultation, and better setbacks from Craven Road. Garden suites have been allowed city-wide since 2022, with over 900 building permit applications received so far.

title: Naming of a Public Lane Located West of Claremont Street, extending between Mansfield Avenue and Treford Place
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: naming;
brief: A public lane west of Claremont Street, between Mansfield Avenue and Treford Place, would be named 'Love You More Lane' under a decision before the Toronto and East York Community Council. The naming complies with the city's street naming policy.

title: Joy Drive - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing two speed humps on Joy Drive between Elinor Avenue and Tower Drive to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Community council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Guild Hall Drive - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing six speed humps on Guild Hall Drive between Warden Avenue and Ellington Drive to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Community council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Broadbent Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Staff reviewed Broadbent Avenue for speed humps and found it did not meet the city's traffic calming criteria, so they do not recommend installing them. Community council is asked to accept the staff recommendation.

title: Appointments to the Cedarbrae Markham Lawrence Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: appointments, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
