brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving a presentation from Housing Secretariat staff on the centralized access system for rent-geared-to-income homes, which will also include affordable rental homes in 2026. The presentation covers the differences between RGI and affordable rental homes, how human rights principles are informing the system's design, and answers to questions the committee previously raised. No policy change is proposed.

title: Advancing the Right to Adequate Housing in the 2026 City of Toronto Budget
topics: budgets, housing; budgets and accounts, homes; residences
brief: A recommendation that the Executive Committee request Council to ask the Mayor to consider, in the 2026 budget, ways to maximize available resources for people in greatest housing need — including those who are unhoused or facing complex health challenges — plus tenants needing eviction support, and more transparent reporting of housing and homelessness investments goes to the Housing Rights Advisory Committee.

title: Assessing Changes to the Interdivisional Protocol on Encampments (IDP) for Alignment with the Toronto Housing Charter
topics: homeless encampments, housing, supportive housing; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, homes; residences, tent cities
brief: Whether to recommend that City Council have the General Manager, Shelter and Support Services ensure that any changes to the Interdivisional Protocol on Encampments are assessed for compliance with the City's obligations under the Toronto Housing Charter, and that this be done in consultation with the committee is before the Housing Rights Advisory Committee. The recommendation follows Council's November 14, 2025 changes to the protocol; the committee's supporting text describes those changes as a concern for the rights of encampment residents.

title: Potential Impacts of Bill 60 on Vulnerable Tenants
topics: housing services, rental housing, tenants; rental properties; rental units, renters; tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving a presentation from Housing Secretariat staff on the potential impacts of provincial Bill 60 on renters and City services. No policy change is proposed.

title: Chair Update
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving an update from Housing Rights Advisory Committee Chair Elizabeth McIsaac. No policy change is proposed.

title: Committee’s Planning Process and the Presentation of an Annual Progress Report
topics: legislative process (municipal), planning; bylaw passing; bylaw procedures
brief: A motion asks the Francophone Affairs Advisory Committee to examine how it plans its work, identifying, prioritizing and aligning items with its mandate, and to request an annual progress report on achievements, challenges and areas needing attention. The committee decides whether to take this on.

title: Small Business Supports Available (Workplan Item Number 14)
topics: business improvement areas, business incentives; bia; business improvement associations, commercial facade improvement program; commercial festivals and special events program; commercial research program; community grant allocations; employment area revitalization; employment revitalization areas; facade improvement; financial incentives; mural program; streetscape improvement program
brief: Managers from Economic Development and Culture will give presentations on small business supports available, listed as workplan item 14. This is an information item; no decision is being made.

title: Collective Bargaining and Labour Update
body: Toronto Transit Commission - People, Culture and Governance Committee
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, labour relations, unions; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, labour unions; trade unions, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the People, Culture and Governance Committee is asked to adopt recommendations on collective bargaining and labour matters from a confidential attachment and keep the details private, since they concern labour relations and negotiations. No policy change is proposed.

title: Anti-Racism Policy
body: Toronto Transit Commission - People, Culture and Governance Committee
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, policies and procedures, policy development, racial discrimination; anti-racism; racism, guidelines; policies, policy making, ttc
brief: Approving the TTC's Anti-Racism Policy and forward it to the TTC Board for information, goes to the People, Culture and Governance Committee for approval. The policy follows the Board-approved 2024 Anti-Racism Strategy, developed after the TTC acknowledged public concerns about racial profiling and anti-Black racism in transit enforcement, and aims to address systemic racism in TTC workplaces and service delivery.

title: Bloor-Kipling Block 5 (970 Kipling Avenue) - Selection of Proponent
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Publicly naming the chosen developer for the affordable and rental housing project at 970 Kipling Avenue (Bloor-Kipling Block 5), while keeping the rest of the bid details confidential, would be authorized by the CreateTO board. The market offering launched June 4, 2025, closed September 16, 2025, and was overseen by an external fairness monitor, with the highest-ranked proponent selected after evaluation and interviews.

title: Housing Progress Update
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: This is a procedural item: the CreateTO board is asked to receive for information the 2025 housing progress update on priority work items — 7 sites under construction or targeted to start in 2025, 2 with secured proponents, 4 in or tracking to a market offering, 1 under the public developer model, and 5 each with and undergoing initial planning approvals. No policy change is proposed.

title: Third Quarter Financial Results
topics: financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: Approval of switching its financial reporting to the board from quarterly to semi-annual, alongside receiving the third-quarter 2025 results is before the CreateTO board. Spending for the nine months ending September 30, 2025 was $0.88 million below budget, with annual spending expected in line with the approved $15.39 million gross budget.

title: 1266 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: construction, demolitions, heritage designation; building
brief: The Preservation Board decides whether to recommend that City Council approve demolishing the existing building at 1266 Queen Street West, a non-contributing property in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District, and approve a replacement building: a 27-storey mixed-use tower on a four-storey podium.

title: 543 Yonge Street - Demolition of a Building within the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District and Approval of a Replacement Building
topics: demolitions, heritage conservation districts, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas
brief: The question before the Preservation Board: whether to recommend that City Council approve demolishing the four-storey commercial building at 543 Yonge Street (543, 545 and 549 Yonge Street), which is not considered a contributing heritage building in the Historic Yonge Street Heritage Conservation District, and approve its replacement with a 68-storey mixed-use building with a two-storey podium, shops at street level and homes above.

title: 530-550 Yonge Street, 6-8 Breadalbane Street and 145 St. Luke Lane - Alterations, Demolition and New Construction of Buildings on a Designated Heritage Property under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The question before the Preservation Board: whether to recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 530-550 Yonge Street, 6-8 Breadalbane Street and 145 St. Luke Lane, in connection with a zoning application for a 67-storey mixed-use tower, with older street-facing buildings kept in the new podium, and authorize a heritage easement agreement.
address: 530 - 550 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 145 St Luke Toronto Ontario

title: 509 Parliament Street (Carlton Theatre) - Alterations and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, easements, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board recommends that City Council approve altering and partially demolishing the heritage attributes of the 1929 Carlton Theatre at 509 Parliament Street, in connection with a zoning application for the site, and authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: 170 Merton Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board votes on recommending that City Council approve alterations to the former Visiting Homemakers Association headquarters at 170 Merton Street, built in 1969, in connection with redeveloping the site, and authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: 1 Front Street West - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property in the Union Station Heritage Conservation District Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: easements, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The Preservation Board decides whether to recommend that City Council approve alterations to the Dominion Public Building at 1 Front Street West, including altering 14 openings on its north side, in connection with redeveloping the site, and amend the existing heritage easement agreement.

title: 39 Wynford Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: demolitions, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The question before the Preservation Board: whether to recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the office building at 39 Wynford Drive, on the southeast corner of Wynford Drive and Gervais Drive near Eglinton Avenue, under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Starting the designation process would limit future demolition and alterations to the property.

title: 241 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The question before the Preservation Board: whether to recommend that City Council state its intention to designate 241 Yonge Street, on the east side of Yonge Street mid-block, under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Starting the designation process would limit future demolition and alterations to the property.

title: 262-264 St. George Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board recommends that City Council state its intention to designate 262-264 St. George Street, on the west side of St. George Street, under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Starting the designation process would limit future demolition and alterations to the property.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the CreateTO Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would select six candidates to interview for appointment to the CreateTO Board, with interviews and a recommendation of two candidates — including a chair — at its next meeting. The candidate details in the confidential attachments would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would select six candidates to interview for appointment to the Metro Toronto Convention Centre Board, with interviews and a recommendation of two candidates at its next meeting. The candidate details in the confidential attachments would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Summary of Legal Disputes Update
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: A request to direct that its latest legal disputes update stay fully confidential, since it contains litigation advice covered by solicitor-client privilege goes to the Toronto Parking Authority board. This update follows the one last given to the board in October 2025, and updates arrive twice a year as the disputes change.

title: Delegation of Authority Update: September 1 - October 31, 2025
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to receive for information the update on decisions the President made under delegated authority from September 1 to October 31, 2025. The President can make commitments up to $500,000 (raised from $250,000) and award non-competitive contracts up to $250,000. No policy change is proposed.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2026 Operating Budget and 2026-2028 Capital Budget
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: Approval of the recommended 2026 operating budget and 2026-2028 capital budget, with the 2026 annual operating plan presented at the same December 5, 2025 meeting is before the Toronto Parking Authority board. Management forecasts full-year 2025 net income of $45.5 million (+$3.6 million versus plan), EBITDA of $57.9 million (-$2.9 million versus plan), record revenue of $177.3 million (-$5.4 million versus plan, hurt by February's snow event), and operating expenses of $119.4 million ($2.4 million below plan). Bike Share contributed $1.6 million in favourable revenue. The report also references $49.9 million.

title: Audit and Risk Management Committee - Auditor's 2025 Work Plan
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to receive for information the auditor's 2025 work plan for auditing the authority's financial statements. A KPMG audit partner will review the plan with the Audit and Risk Management Committee on November 14, 2025. No policy change is proposed.

title: James Bartlett - Appeal DDRT2025-08
topics: animal bites, by-laws, dogs, municipal codes; bylaws, dog bites
brief: This is a tribunal appeal item: James Bartlett is appealing a dangerous dog order issued May 15, 2025, appeal number DDRT2025-08. The tribunal will review the order and decide whether to confirm, cancel or change it.

title: 36 Prince Arthur Avenue - Alterations to Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: heritage conservation districts, heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage districts; historic areas, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve alterations to the heritage property at 36 Prince Arthur Avenue, a two-and-a-half-storey brick building from about 1891 in the East Annex Heritage Conservation District. The plan would keep the main body of the building, remove its non-original rear addition, and build a new five-storey rear addition for office space. Staff support the change, finding the setback addition would not overpower the heritage building or be highly visible from the street.

title: 189 and 195 Old Weston Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor to oppose, at the Ontario Land Tribunal, a development proposal for 189 and 195 Old Weston Road, while talks with the applicant continue. The proposal includes an 8-storey non-residential building, residential buildings of 11 and 27 storeys, and a 3-storey above-grade parking structure, with 296 homes and 4,410 square metres of office space. The applicant appealed on June 11, 2025 after Council missed the Planning Act decision deadline; the province has since approved the Keele St. Clair Secondary Plan (OPA 537), which now governs the area.

title: Palmerston Area Character Study and Heritage Evaluation
topics: heritage conservation districts, land use designations; heritage districts; historic areas
brief: City Council has planning staff start a community character study of Palmerston Avenue and surrounding streets in 2026 and evaluate whether the area should become a Heritage Conservation District. The distinctive residential area has long been a candidate for heritage district status, and new housing policies are speeding up development there. Staff would consult the community on design aspirations and report back in the first quarter of 2027.

title: St. Clair Avenue West - Parking Amendments
topics: loading zones, parking prohibitions; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking
brief: City Council will decide whether to remove an unused commercial loading zone on the south side of St. Clair Avenue West near Via Italia. The business that requested the zone has moved away, and the local BIA confirmed none of its members need it. Removing it would restore on-street parking and help welcome visitors to the Corso Italia area.

title: Improving Traffic Flow on College Street, between Dufferin Street and Gladstone Avenue
topics: traffic calming;
brief: City Council will decide whether to ban stopping on the north side of College Street between Dufferin Street and Gladstone Avenue. Parked vehicles near transit stops interfere with the 506 streetcar, which stops traffic during pick-up and drop-off just east of Dufferin, backing up westbound drivers to Havelock Street and Rusholme Road. Nearby on-street and off-street parking would remain available.

title: Expanding the Community Safety Zone on Dufferin Street
topics: school zone review;
brief: City Council will decide whether to replace two existing community safety zones on Dufferin Street with one larger zone between Queen Street West and Bloor Street West. The expanded zone would fill the gap between the existing zones, creating a continuous corridor of higher traffic fines near schools, churches and the Roseneath Theatre. Residents have raised concerns about speeding and dangerous driving, and the designation could support future automated speed enforcement.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Ted Reeve Community Arena Board
topics: arenas, public appointments; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint four public members to the Ted Reeve Community Arena Board, for terms ending October 23, 2029. The appointees are Syeda Jaana Ali, Jay McDonald, Iain McLeod and Eric Shuell. Candidate details in confidential attachments would stay private.

title: 861 Avenue Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for two four-storey residential buildings with nine townhouse units at 861 Avenue Road, accessed from a central driveway. The owner would convey a 0.4-metre widening along Avenue Road and a 6-metre corner rounding at Avenue Road and Chaplin Crescent to the city. A landscaping plan for the public boulevard would also be required.

title: Dedication of Lands as Public Highway and Traffic Amendments - Lake Shore Boulevard East
topics: highways; freeways; motorways; parkways
brief: City Council will decide whether to officially designate rebuilt sections of Lake Shore Boulevard East as public highway, as the Port Lands flood protection and waterfront projects near completion. The work includes removing the Gardiner East access ramps at Logan Avenue, rebuilding the Lower Don River bridge, and reconfiguring Lake Shore Boulevard East between Don Roadway and Carlaw Avenue. Related traffic and parking by-law changes would also be adopted.

title: 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West (Bloor Street West at Dovercourt Road, and Bloor Street West at Lansdowne Avenue) - Temporary Traffic and Parking Amendments
topics: parking, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: City Council will decide on temporary traffic and parking amendments on Bloor Street West for construction of an underground pedestrian tunnel connecting Dufferin TTC station to a new 33-storey building at 980 Dufferin Street and 1141 Bloor Street West. The tunnel would run north to south just west of the Bloor and Dufferin intersection; an earlier staging area approval from February 2025 has not yet started work because legal agreements are still being finalized. The staff report also references a $3.00 rate.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2025 Distillery Winter Village (Non-delegated)
topics: parking, traffic calming measures; traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: City Council will decide on temporary traffic and parking changes for the 2025 Distillery Winter Village on streets with TTC service, including Parliament Street, Mill Street and Front Street East. The changes would run November 13, 2025 to January 4, 2026 to manage congestion and pedestrian safety during the event. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on these streets; a companion report covers the neighbourhood streets.

title: 55 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a taller 55-storey mixed-use building at 55 Eglinton Avenue East, replacing the previously approved 50-storey design. The 183-metre building would have 43,853 square metres of floor area, 5.3 metres taller and 2,553 square metres larger than the earlier approval. The Official Plan amendment would require 1,165 square metres of non-residential space and affordable housing instead of replacement office space, including ground-floor retail and 360 square metres of affordable housing.

title: Parking Amendments - 900 Bay Street (Macdonald Block Reconstruction Project) - (Non-Delegated)
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: City Council will decide on stopping changes on the west side of Bay Street near Wellesley Street West, tied to the Macdonald Block reconstruction project at 900 Bay Street. The changes would create a round-the-clock accessible loading zone in the lay-by south of Wellesley Street, replacing existing stopping bans and the $5.50 parking machine regulation. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on Bay Street; a companion report covers the related changes on Grosvenor Street.

title: 260-270 and 274-322 King Street West  - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve changes to the previously approved Gehry Forma development at 260-270 and 274-322 King Street West. The amendment would allow more residential floor area and less non-residential floor area in the base of the West Block building, with no changes to the approved heights, building envelopes or setbacks. The East Block is already under construction. The staff report also lists $250,000, among its figures.

title: 2760 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction; building
brief: City Council will decide whether to close the north sidewalk and two westbound traffic lanes on Dundas Street West, between Indian Grove and a point 40 metres east of Watkinson Avenue, for 17 months from November 30, 2025 to April 30, 2027. The closure would make room for construction staging for a six-storey residential building at 2760 Dundas Street West, with pedestrians using a covered walkway in the closed lane and one lane kept open each way. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit on Dundas Street West.

title: Response to City Council Direction on EX.25.4 RapidTO: Transit Priority on Dufferin Street and Bathurst Street
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This report follows up on City Council's July 2025 approval of RapidTO transit priority lanes on Dufferin Street, from King Street West to Bloor Street West, and on Bathurst Street, from Bathurst Station to Lake Shore Boulevard West. It identifies ways to handle the knock-on effects on nearby streets, including traffic spilling onto local roads, permit-parking pressure around Dufferin, and off-street parking near Bathurst around St. Moses and St. Katherine Coptic Orthodox Church. Staff are collecting data and would bring traffic-calming recommendations for affected local streets in early 2026.

title: Council Member Appointments to Fill Vacancies on Committees, Boards and External Bodies
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to recommend council members to fill vacancies on several committees and boards, including the Executive Committee, Budget Committee and Board of Health. Appointments would run until November 2026. Council makes the final appointments.

title: 402, 404, 406 and 408 Livingston Road North - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend that council refuse zoning and Official Plan changes for a proposed 35-storey residential building with 442 homes at 402-408 Livingston Road North. Staff also recommend the city lawyer oppose any appeal at the Ontario Land Tribunal. Council is asked to approve the refusal.

title: Birchmount Road and Rolark Drive/Private Access - Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations
topics: traffic control systems, traffic regulations, traffic signs; traffic regulatory signs, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Staff recommend installing traffic control signals at Birchmount Road and Rolark Drive, banning right turns on red lights there in both directions, and adjusting a nearby turn restriction. Because the TTC runs buses on Birchmount Road, city council approval is required. The signals and related work are estimated to cost $330,000, with $100,000 secured and partial funding from the proponent of the adjacent development.

title: Clonmore Drive and Queensbury Avenue/Private Access - Traffic Control Signals
topics: [rules in transportation], assessment, traffic regulations;
brief: Staff reviewed Clonmore Drive at Queensbury Avenue and do not recommend traffic signals, saying the criteria were not met, and advise keeping the existing pedestrian crossover. Because the TTC runs buses there, city council approval of the staff position is required.

title: 5705 and 5789 Steeles Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: construction, industrial properties, rezoning; building, industrial real estate, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving zoning changes to allow two single-storey warehouse buildings with offices on vacant land at 5705 and 5789 Steeles Avenue East. The project would add jobs on an underused employment site. Council would amend the zoning by-law to permit it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the order paper listing the items to be considered at the meeting. No decision is being asked for.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements are made during the City Council meeting. No decisions are being asked for at this stage.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council may file petitions during the meeting for the record. No decision is being asked for at this stage.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is being asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: the mayor and committee chairs introduce committee reports and new business from city officials. No decision is being asked for.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council confirms the minutes from its regular meeting held on October 8 and 9, 2025, as an accurate record.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the council meeting begins with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is being asked for.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Chair's 2024 Annual Report
topics: municipal codes, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to receive for information the 2024 annual report from the Chair of the Toronto Local Appeal Body, the independent tribunal that hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions on minor variances and consents. No policy change is proposed.

title: Property Standards By-law: Phase II Review and Other Property Items
topics: by-laws, evaluation, property standards; bylaws, review; reviewing
brief: Toronto's property standards by-law — the minimum maintenance rules covering everything from apartment handrails to restaurant waste bins — could be rewritten, along with a brand-new pest-management by-law. Council decides on the Phase II review recommendations, with both changes taking effect May 1, 2027. The report references figures of $50,000 and $250,000.

title: Infrastructure Cost Sharing - Regent Park Phase 4
topics: funding, infrastructure, redevelopment; financing, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Regent Park's Phase 4 revitalization needs its infrastructure costs — roads, servicing and public realm work — added to the 2026-2035 capital budget. Council is asked to authorize the budget addition and an agreement to reimburse Toronto Community Housing for eligible infrastructure costs. Phase 4 and 5 zoning, approved in 2023, allows five new TCHC buildings with 633 rent-geared-to-income units and up to 637 affordable rental units, plus six market condo buildings.

title: 2024-2025 Annual Progress Report - HousingTO 2020-2030 Action Plan and Housing Action Plan (2022-2026)
topics: [activities in community and life], housing; homes; residences
brief: The 2024-2025 progress report on the HousingTO 2020-2030 and Housing Action Plan strategies is before council for information, along with a request for $163 million and $2.6 billion from Ottawa and CMHC to build supportive homes and mixed-income communities. The report also cites figures of $13 million, $150 million, $48 million, $16 million, $23 million and $50,000. The context: the housing market downturn has persisted into 2025, and the report says the market on its own will not produce the affordable and rent-geared-to-income homes residents need.

title: Community Within Reach: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods (EHON) Neighbourhood Retail and Services Study - Phase Three Final Report
topics: commercial areas, zoning bylaws; commercial districts; retail areas, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: More corner shops and services could be allowed in residential neighbourhoods and on major streets. Council is asked to change zoning rules so growing neighbourhoods have daily needs within walking distance. City research projects about 163,785 new homes in neighbourhoods by 2051, and notes many mid-20th-century rules that pushed small local businesses out are still on the books.

title: Provincial Planning Statement 2024 Consistency Exercise Phase 1 - Recommendation Report
topics: planning, provincial legislation;
brief: Official Plan Amendment 846, the first phase of updates to bring the city's Official Plan in line with the province's 2024 Provincial Planning Statement, which took effect October 20, 2024, would take effect if council adopts it. Phase one resolves policy conflicts in six areas, including growth forecasting, transit hubs and urban growth centres. A second phase will cover Indigenous engagement, employment uses in mixed-use areas and Section 37 community benefits policies.

title: 164 and 166 Isabella Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: A pair of 1887 semi-detached red-brick houses at 164 and 166 Isabella Street in North St. James Town could begin heritage designation. The properties were listed on the Heritage Register in 1991 and a redevelopment application was received in August 2025. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act; if no objections come in, the formal by-law can follow.

title: 54, 66 and 68 Fraser Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Former early-1900s factories at 54, 66 and 68 Fraser Avenue in Liberty Village — including the 1905 Arlington Company of Canada factory and the circa 1906-09 S.F. Bowser Company factory — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 150 College Street (Medical Sciences Building - 1 King's College Circle) - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: buildings, heritage designation;
brief: The University of Toronto's Medical Sciences Building at 150 College Street (1 King's College Circle) — a 1966-1970 sculptural concrete complex with precast panels by Canadian artists Robert Downing and Ted Bieler — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 81 Isabella Street - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: change, heritage designation, heritage properties; amendments; conversion; modification, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Merlan Apartments at 81 Isabella Street — a 1927 two-storey apartment building by Norman Alexander Armstrong — were flagged for heritage designation in July 2025, and the owner objected. Council is asked to pass the designation by-law using a revised statement of significance that responds to the objection. The decision must come by November 25, 2025, or the notice of intention is deemed withdrawn under the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 4350 Steeles Avenue East - City of Markham - Development Submission - Update Report
topics: development, municipalities; boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: A development proposal just across the border in Markham — the Milliken Transit-Oriented Community on the north side of Steeles Avenue East, with 8 residential buildings, 12 towers of 25 to 50 storeys, about 5,500 homes, 10,100 square metres of non-residential space and a 1.97-hectare park — is before Markham's planners. Because the site sits near Toronto's boundary, council is asked to send Toronto's comments to the City of Markham for its consideration.

title: Technical Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 and By-law 335-2024
topics: change, zoning bylaws; amendments; conversion; modification, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a technical item: council is asked to correct typos, clarify wording and adjust map boundaries in the city-wide zoning by-law 569-2013 and By-law 335-2024. The changes do not alter what is actually permitted — they keep the by-laws in line with what council originally intended.

title: Lawrence Avenue East and Underhill Drive / Railside Road - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrians, transportation (sc); cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrianization
brief: Transportation Services recommends installing a pedestrian crossover at the southbound right-turn channel where Lawrence Avenue East meets Underhill Drive / Railside Road, based on its assessment. Because the TTC runs transit on Lawrence Avenue East, City Council approval is required.

title: 41, 43, 45, and 47 Hendon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a revised 34-storey mixed-use building at 41-47 Hendon Avenue, scaled down from the applicant's original 38 storeys, with a holding provision on the zoning. City Council is being asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes that would allow it.

title: 850 and 858 York Mills Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, applications, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving an eight-storey (35-metre) mixed-use building at 850 and 858 York Mills Road, with shops on the ground floor and self-storage and office space above, plus three marquees on the facade. City Council is being asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 2425 - 2427 Bayview Avenue and 1 The Bridle Path - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend approving a six-storey (22.5 metres plus penthouse) residential building with 56 homes and 122 parking spaces at 2425-2427 Bayview Avenue and 1 The Bridle Path. City Council is being asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes that would allow it.

title: 340 - 472 Lawrence Heights Way and 2 - 66 Green Gardens Boulevard - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control, site plan control; exceptions, site plan approvals
brief: Staff recommend exempting 340-472 Lawrence Heights Way and 2-66 Green Gardens Boulevard from the Planning Act's part-lot control rules, so individual lots can be sold or developed separately. The lands are Phase 1Fb of the Lawrence Heights Revitalization project, and the exemption would allow 101 separate parts to be created. City Council is being asked to approve the exemption.

title: Rehabilitating Amsterdam Bridge at Harbourfront Centre - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: bridge rehabilitation; bridge reconstruction; bridge repair
brief: The Amsterdam Bridge footbridge at Harbourfront Centre — closed since early 2021 — would be rehabilitated under a $640,000.00 capital project so it can reopen for the 2026 FIFA Men's World Cup waterfront celebrations. Council would create the project with $350,000.00 in Section 37 funding to Economic Development and Culture. The total project cost is $790,000.00: $350,000.00 in Section 37 funds, $150,000.00 from Harbourfront Centre, and $290,000.00 from the approved capital budgets of Economic Development and Culture and the Waterfront Revitalization Initiative. The steel cable footbridge was gifted by the Mayor of Amsterdam marking the 1974 twinning of the two cities, and a condition assessment and work plan are complete through a City-Harbourfront Centre-CreateTO partnership. Residents and visitors heading to the waterfront's restaurants and open spaces would use the reopened bridge.

title: Advancing Affordable and Supportive Housing for Veterans - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: homelessness;
brief: Staff would report by fall 2026 on opportunities to address veterans' housing needs through developments on city-owned land under the Toronto Builds framework. Council would direct the Deputy City Manager for Development and Growth Services to study the options, citing that 4.4 percent of people experiencing homelessness in Canadian cities are veterans and veterans are more than twice as likely to experience homelessness. The motion frames the report around Veterans' Week, Indigenous Veterans Day and Remembrance Day. Veterans experiencing homelessness would be the intended beneficiaries.

title: Expanding the Listening to Toronto Survey to Support Ward-Level Insights - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: research, service delivery; studies; surveys (research)
brief: The City Manager would explore expanding the Listening to Toronto resident survey so its results are statistically meaningful at the ward level, and report back with options in spring 2026. Council would request the study because the survey currently represents Toronto as a whole but cannot show ward-level differences in satisfaction, service access and investment gaps. The motion frames the expansion as supporting equity and data-informed governance. Councillors and residents would get localized data for their wards.

title: Adding Swim to Survive to the Ontario Curriculum to Improve Water Safety and Save Lives - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: swim policy, swimming pools; aquatic centres; bathing pavilions; pools; public pools, swim ratio policy
brief: Ontario's Ministry of Education would be urged to make water safety and Swim to Survive training part of the elementary school curriculum for all students. Council would make the request, citing Lifesaving Society of Ontario research that drowning is a leading cause of preventable child deaths and most children who drown never intended to be in the water — and that many children lack access to swimming lessons outside school for financial, cultural or geographic reasons. Dryden, St. Catharines and Niagara Region have adopted similar calls. The decision rests with the province; the change would affect elementary students across Ontario.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Fabrication and Installation of a Commemorative Plaque at Halbert Pool in Honour of Dave Harper - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: outdoor pools, plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques, outdoor swimming pools
brief: A commemorative plaque at Halbert Pool would honour Dave Harper, a longtime Scarborough community member and pool regular of 59 years. Council would release $2,882.00 in Section 37 developer community benefits for the plaque at Halbert Park in Cliffcrest, marking Harper — known as the Rain Man for recalling the day of the week anyone was born — who recently turned 75 and helps neighbours with garbage, recycling and compost every Thursday. The pool marks its 60th anniversary next year. The plaque would give the community a permanent tribute.

title: Protecting Playgrounds and Parks: Ensuring Safety for Children and Families - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: homeless encampments, playgrounds, safety; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, public safety, tent cities
brief: The city's encampment protocol would change so encampments within 200 metres of a school, daycare or playground are prioritized for removal within 48 hours of being reported. Council would make the change after the motion describes impacts at Stanley G. Grizzle Park in Ward 19 — adjacent to a daycare — where residents reported drug use, needles, garbage, noise, human waste, drug sales to minors, package theft and assaults, saying repeated escalation to City officials did not resolve it. The motion frames parks near schools and daycares as needing safe access for families. People living in the encampments and nearby residents would both be affected by the enforcement change.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 871 to 899 College Street for Lakeview Avenue Parkette Improvements - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: development, funding; developing land; development (land); land development, financing
brief: The Lakeview Avenue Parkette on Dundas Street West would get an extra $131,014 after design work showed the earlier budget was not enough. Council would add $131,014 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Non-Program operating budget, fully funded by Section 37 funds from the 871 to 899 College Street development, forwarding the money to the Little Portugal BIA — on top of the $200,000 Council approved in 2024 — to realize the full design vision for the parkette as a destination in the Little Portugal BIA. Locals and tourists using the parkette would see the completed space.

title: Expressing Gratitude to the Weston Lions Club - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: community & life (sc), volunteering; volunteer groups; volunteers
brief: This is a recognition item: Council would thank the Weston Lions Club for more than 80 years of volunteer service to the Weston neighbourhood. The volunteer-run club's projects include the Weston Lions Arena — home to the Weston Dukes, Weston Dodgers, Weston Minor Hockey League, Weston Figure Skating Club and other groups — and its long-time chair Sandy Ross. No policy change is proposed.

title: Reimbursing Certain Reasonable Legal Expenses of Shelter Operators and Consultants - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: homelessness, persons who are homeless; homeless; homeless individuals
brief: The City Solicitor would continue opposing lawsuits aimed at stopping new housing and shelter projects, and consultants named in those suits could be reimbursed up to $50,000 for their legal costs. Council would authorize the reimbursement for shelter operators and community engagement consultants named as defendants in cases targeting projects on Cummer Avenue, Adelaide Street West, Wardlaw Crescent, Sheppard Avenue East and Third Street. The motion says the City's shelter system is at capacity, with people turned away nightly and hundreds in encampments, and frames the litigation as delaying needed housing. The decision would affect the consultants' legal bills and the pace of the housing projects.

title: Supporting the Delivery of Affordable and Rent-Controlled Homes at 1117 Danforth Avenue Through a Property Tax Exemption - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: affordable housing, property taxes; affordable homes; housing projects, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: The affordable and rent-controlled homes at 1117 Danforth Avenue would be exempt from municipal and school property taxes through construction and a 99-year affordability period. Council would approve the exemption for the development — 67 affordable units (including 11 rent supplement units) and 41 rent-controlled units, approved for incentives and capital funding through the Rental Housing Supply Program, with a municipal housing facility agreement signed February 7, 2025; the item's figures list $48,370.01. Construction is underway. The exemption would support the project's affordable rents.

title: Following Up on Plans to Advance the Extension of the Finch West Light Rail Transit  - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: The province and Metrolinx would be asked for a status update by early 2026 on planning for a Finch West light rail extension to Woodbine and onward to Pearson Airport. Council would request the update — plus a Metrolinx work plan for an emergency access lane across the LRT guideway for Division 23 Station along Finch Avenue west of Kipling — citing a Toronto Region Board of Trade survey that commuting is the top challenge for workers in the Pearson Economic Zone, which employs 400,000 people and contributes $53 billion to Ontario's economy. The motion frames the extension as bringing higher-order transit to Etobicoke. Riders in the northwest would be the beneficiaries.

title: Municipal Capital Facility - 877 Yonge Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: by-laws, religious diversity; bylaws, multi faith; spirituality
brief: Part of the city-owned property at 877 Yonge Street, leased to St. Clare's MultiFaith Housing for supportive housing, would be designated a municipal capital facility with an exemption from municipal and education property taxes. Council would pass the by-law for the property the City bought for supportive housing, operated by St. Clare's since 2021 under a long-term lease; part of the non-housing space has become the Nancy and Ed Jackman Performance Centre with a 2,600-square-foot performance hall and 775-square-foot rehearsal and recording space. The designation would reduce the property's tax costs. The housing operator and theatre partners use the site.

title: Relief from Environmental Peer Review Requirements for Affordable Housing and Long-Term Care Development at 640 Lansdowne Avenue - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: The planned 256-bed long-term care home and 57 affordable rental units at 640 Lansdowne Avenue would be exempt from the city policy requiring environmental peer review of lands being conveyed to the city. Council would grant the relief for the seven-storey mixed-use development on TTC-owned land leased to Magellan Community Charities — which has provincial and city funding and is moving toward permit issuance — because CreateTO initiated the environmental assessment under the lease structure and construction timing is tight. The project would house seniors, including those with mental and physical disabilities. The exemption would let the project proceed without the extra review step.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE22.3 - 72 Perth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: planning & development (sc), zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would change the required unit mix for the 13 affordable rental units at 72 Perth Avenue from three studios, five one-bedrooms, four two-bedrooms and one three-bedroom to eight one-bedrooms, four two-bedrooms and one three-bedroom. The applicant requested the revision to provide more accessible, spacious units; City Planning and Housing Secretariat staff support it. Reopening item 2025.TE22.3 is required. The change affects the affordable homes delivered as the development's in-kind contribution.

title: Accelerating Rehabilitation of the Cross Harbour Tunnel - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: water supply; water delivery; water distribution; water hook-up; water installation; water service; water shut off; water shut-off; water turn off; water turn on
brief: Toronto Water could negotiate an agreement with PortsToronto to speed up repairs to the Cross Harbour Tunnel. Council would authorize the General Manager to enter the agreement to accelerate rehabilitation of 600 metres of the 1.4-kilometre tunnel — built in 1908, connecting the Toronto Island Water Treatment Plant to the John Street Pumping Station and carrying 20 percent of the city's drinking water plus the source for Enwave's Deep Lake Water Cooling. An 800-metre section was rehabilitated in 2020-2021; the rest can proceed earlier in coordination with PortsToronto, including the winter shutdown period. The motion is urgent to order materials in time. The repairs protect a critical piece of water infrastructure.

title: Joint Appointment of Waterfront Toronto Chair - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: Kevin Sullivan would be appointed director and chair of Waterfront Toronto for three years, jointly with the provincial and federal governments. Council would make the appointment — Sullivan has been on the board since 2019 as a provincial appointee and currently chairs it — with federal and provincial partners moving in parallel, under the Toronto Waterfront Revitalization Corporation Act. The three governments are advancing the $975 million Next Phase of Waterfront Revitalization approved by Council in 2024. The appointment would fill the board's leadership for the next phase.

title: Driving Efficiencies at Toronto Parking Authority to Reduce 2026 Budget Pressures - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: budgets, parking; budgets and accounts
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority board would be changed to include five city officials serving without extra pay, as part of efforts to streamline the agency and reduce 2026 budget pressures. Council would make the governance change while the 2026 budget process addresses an opening operating pressure of $1.072 billion — building on $680 million and $620 million in reductions and offsets identified in the 2025 and 2024 budgets. The parking authority has over $144 million in 2025 operating expenses and a 10-year capital plan of just under $400 million, with management, technology and external costs that duplicate City resources. The change would affect how the agency is run.

title: Allowing Staff to Tow Unlicensed Vehicles on City Streets - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: parking, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation staff would report on what by-law changes would allow unlicensed or abandoned vehicles on city streets to be towed without warning. Council would have staff, with police and the Parking Authority, investigate the amendments after complaints about vehicles occupying limited parking spaces, blocking sightlines and impeding pedestrians, cyclists and emergency services — with urgent high-risk locations in wards six and seven. The change would let parking enforcement and right-of-way officers tow immediately. Drivers of unlicensed vehicles and residents competing for parking would be affected.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Surface Impression LTD for the Provision and Completion of a Digital Learning Resource Where the Water Met the Land for Economic Development and Culture - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Alejandra Bravo
topics: economic development; business development; business opportunities; business retention; investment attraction; investment marketing
brief: Council would approve a non-competitive contract of up to about $31,000 with Surface Impression Ltd. to finish the Where the Water Met the Land digital learning resource for middle school students. The contract — $31,225.25 net ($31,774.81 net of HST recoveries), funded by the federal government through Digital Museums of Canada — would complete the immersive online experience about how land and water lines around Fort York National Historic Site and Spadina Museum have evolved; the previous purchase order expired in June 2024 (the $500,000.00 figure is the staff spending-authority threshold this vendor's cumulative commitments exceed, which is why Council approval is needed). Indigenous community engagement informed the resource, which aligns with the City's reconciliation priorities. Educators and middle school students would use the finished resource.

title: Respecting Local Authority Over Road Design - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Dianne Saxe
topics: road safety, transportation (sc);
brief: Council would oppose proposed provincial changes affecting municipal authority over road design and ask the province to confirm cities can decide their own road designs under the City of Toronto Act. The motion builds on Council's November 2024 opposition to Bill 212's Highway Traffic Act amendments, expressing concern about provincial intervention in decisions affecting the safety of all road users, and cites the urgency of Bill 60, Fighting Delays, Building Faster Act. The decision on the legislation rests with the province.

title: 712 Eglinton Avenue East - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councilor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City would appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a garden suite at 712 Eglinton Avenue East. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the North York District panel's October 23, 2025 approval of the rear-yard ancillary building — even though the applicant made all seven modifications planning staff requested — and to oppose the development at the Toronto Local Appeal Body. The motion also covers hiring outside consultants and negotiating a resolution.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE21.7 - 315-325 Front Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would update its April 2025 approval for 315 to 325 Front Street West with refined wording on parkland cash contributions, public art indexing, the child care centre obligations and easements around the transmission watermain, plus minor fixes aligning the draft by-law with architectural drawings. The August 2025 provincial approval of Protected Major Transit Station Area boundaries also requires changes to the parking provisions. Reopening item 2025.TE21.7 is required. The motion is framed as urgent to advance housing and community infrastructure.

title: Comments on the Request for a Minister’s Zoning Order to Restrict Building Heights - 1875 Steeles Avenue West to Protect Operational Viability of the Sanofi Pasteur Limited Manufacturing Facilities and Headquarters - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: zoning;
brief: Council would support a provincial zoning order limiting building heights at 1875 Steeles Avenue West to 33 metres, to protect the Sanofi Pasteur vaccine manufacturing campus next door. The Ministry of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade has asked the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing for the order, capping all buildings on the site at 33 metres to safeguard the biomanufacturing campus at 1755 Steeles Avenue West. The site currently has a 4-storey, 120-unit rental building; Council refused a 39- and 33-storey tower proposal in 2024 and the owner appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The final decision on the order rests with the province.

title: Waiving Permit Fee Charges for the Annual Heroes of Suicide March - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: The $151.58 permit fee for the annual Heroes of Suicide Memorial March would be waived for 2025 and future years. Council would approve the waiver for the march hosted by the Royal Canadian Legion Todmorden Branch 10, honouring veterans and first responders lost to PTSD, operational stress injuries and other mental health struggles — the tenth annual march and candlelight vigil was held September 28, 2025 in East York. Members of the Toronto Police, Fire, Paramedic Services and TTC take part alongside families. The waiver removes the fee for the memorial event.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Hillcrest Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Cresthaven Park - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: donation, sports clubs, tennis; badminton clubs; baseball associations; baseball leagues; bowling clubs; cross-country ski clubs; curling clubs; gymnastic clubs; hockey associations; hockey leagues; karate clubs; lacrosse clubs; lawn bowling clubs; ride clubs; rifle clubs; slo-pitch leagues; soccer clubs; soccer leagues; softball associations; softball leagues; swim clubs; tennis clubs; volleyball clubs, bequest; toy drive
brief: The four tennis courts at Cresthaven Park would be refurbished with up to $150,000.00 in donated work from the Hillcrest Tennis Club. Council would accept the in-kind donation — funded from the club's capital reserve and delivered through a construction and donation agreement with Parks and Recreation — under the 2004 Policy for Community Tennis Club Operations, with work planned for spring 2026. The club operates the four hard courts at 37 Cresthaven Drive in Ward 17, Don Valley North. Players using the public courts would get the upgraded surfaces.

title: Automated Speed Enforcement Program Update
topics: enforcement, speed limits, traffic cameras, traffic speed; compass cameras; rescu cameras; rescu equipment
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is receiving an update for information on the Automated Speed Enforcement camera program, which grew from 50 cameras at launch in 2020 to 75 in 2023 and 150 by early 2025 under the Vision Zero road safety plan. The update covers changes Council has requested, including operating hours, ticket limits, and signage. Council also asked the Province of Ontario to reimburse the full operating cost of the 911 crossing guard program ($31.2 million) and 18 traffic safety police officers ($3.9 million), and to reimburse $210 million in accelerated road safety capital spending — $95.8 million for local safety improvements, $13.92 million for traffic calming, and $40.60 million for traffic lights and other safety measures. Limiting the number of tickets a vehicle owner can get from one camera before the first mailed notice would need a $36,000 system update.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown LRT - At-grade Segment - Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments
topics: by-laws, regional transportation agencies, transportation; bylaws, commuter rail systems; go transit; intercity transportation; interregional public transit systems; interregional transit systems; interurban transit organizations; metrolinx; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; regional transit authorities; regional transportation authorities; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, transportation services
brief: On the agenda at City Council: approving traffic and parking by-law changes for Eglinton Avenue East between Kennedy Road and Brentcliffe Road to match the final road layout of the Eglinton Crosstown LRT at-grade segment, ahead of its opening. Train testing and revenue service demonstration are underway to verify the system's readiness.

title: Redesign Study of the Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Road Expressway - Update
topics: expressways, research, transportation; municipal highways, studies; surveys (research), transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is receiving a status update for information on the study of redesign options for the Eglinton Avenue West and Allen Road expressway intersection. The report covers background on the intersection's redesign during Eglinton Crosstown construction, mitigation measures evaluated and implemented, and ongoing work on neighbourhood traffic infiltration. No policy change is proposed.

title: Next Generation Water Metering, Advanced Metering Infrastructure - Procurement Strategy
topics: sewer and water infrastructure, water billing, water meters; remote water meters, sewer and water services; water and sewer infrastructure; water management systems, water accounts; water bills; water charges
brief: Up for approval at City Council: starting procurement planning for a next-generation water metering system — Advanced Metering Infrastructure — to replace the 2015 automated meter reading system, including hiring an industry expert to develop requirements and assist with vendor selection. Toronto Water's 2024 assessment found the current system no longer meets customer and operational needs.

title: Enhancing the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program to Reduce Basement Flooding Risks
topics: basement flooding, city initiatives, stormwater management; basement flood cleanup; basement flooding response, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, storm water management; swm; wet weather flow management
brief: Whether to strengthen the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program from May 2026, raising subsidies for flood protection measures such as backwater valves and sump pumps, and adding a new subsidy of up to $500 for a professional plumbing assessment is before City Council. The program helps eligible homeowners isolate their homes from the City's sewer system; more than a thousand properties flooded in the July and August 2024 storms. The listed subsidies are: up to $300 per household for a battery backup for sump pumps, a raised maximum of $6,650 per property across the program, and an overall $12,000 per-property cap the General Manager must work within.

title: Transition of the Blue Box Program to Extended Producer Responsibility: Post-Transition Plan
topics: blue bin materials, blue bins, recyclables, recycling, solid waste, solid waste management, waste diversion; 3 rs; reduce reuse recycle, blue boxes; recycling boxes, commercial waste; municipal solid waste; refuse, single stream recyclable materials, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: This item updates Council on the Blue Box program's shift to producer responsibility from January 1, 2026, and asks for authority to negotiate service agreements with producer organizations for non-Blue Box materials like batteries, tires, and electronics through June 30, 2031. It also seeks authority to re-negotiate and extend existing agreements for the supply and maintenance of recycling bins, garbage bins, and green bins.

title: High Pollution Days and Two Stroke Engines
topics: air pollution, air quality, air quality health index, air quality indicators, diesel fuel, fuels, leaf blowers; air pollution index; air quality index; aqhi; aqi
brief: This member motion asks City Council to request that City operations, businesses, and residents avoid using highly polluting engines — such as gas-powered leaf blowers and pre-2008 diesel engines — on days when the Air Quality Health Index reaches high to very high risk levels (7–10). The motion cites wildfire smoke that pushed Toronto's air quality to the worst in the world this summer.

title: 10-Year Circular Economy Road Map
topics: city initiatives, environmental impacts, landfills; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, dumps; garbage dumps; landfill areas; landfill facilities; landfill sites, environmental effects; environmental footprint; environmental impact
brief: Implementing a 10-year Circular Economy Road Map to reduce landfill waste by reusing and recovering materials — and letting staff sign non-procurement agreements through 2036 to support the plan — goes to City Council for approval. The road map sets out five strategic directions and 15 actions, building on Council's 2016 aspirational zero-waste goal. Implementing the road map in 2026 would need $2.4 million — $1.2 million in capital and about $1.2 million in operating funding — including four temporary positions.

title: Understanding the Impacts of Bill 60 on Health and Well-Being in Toronto
brief: Whether to have the Medical Officer of Health review Bill 60, the Fighting Delays, Building Faster Act, along with provincial proposals on security of tenure and rent control, and assess their potential health and well-being impacts in Toronto is before the Board of Health. Toronto Public Health identifies housing as a key determinant of health, and the proposed provincial changes could mean more evictions and housing instability for renters. The analysis would be done with Toronto Shelter and Support Services and the Housing Secretariat to inform City Council debate.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47025543 with OpenText Corporation for Enterprise Document and Records Management Products and Professional Services Leveraging the Provincial Volume Licensing Agreement
topics: contracts, databases, projects, purchasing, records; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: The General Government Committee is being asked to authorize adding $8,970,589 ($9,128,471.00 net of HST recoveries) to the OpenText blanket contract for enterprise document and records management products and services, raising it from $1,440,328 ($1,465,678 net of HST recoveries) to $10,410,917 ($10,594,149 net of HST recoveries), and to extend the contract three years from 2028 to 2030. Buying through the province's volume licensing agreement keeps the city's purchasing power behind the deal. The General Government Committee decides.

title: 2024 Annual Human Rights Office Report
topics: complaints, human rights, policy development, workplaces; job sites; telework; work from home; worksites, policy making
brief: City Council is being asked to adopt the amended Human Rights and Anti-Harassment / Discrimination Policy. The item comes with the city's Human Rights Office 2024 activity report: it received 1,574 inquiries, up 32 percent in a single year and up 89 percent since 2019, reflecting sharply rising demand from city employees and the public. The office ran with eight staff doing case management work and resumed conducting its own investigations. City Council decides.

title: Designation of the Properties Used by Toronto Shelter and Support Services as Municipal Capital Facilities
topics: housing, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), supportive housing, taxes; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, city facilities; municipal buildings, homes; residences, levies, property; real estate
brief: Whether to designate eight leased properties used as shelters as municipal capital facilities, exempting them from municipal and education taxes for the life of each lease or licence is before City Council. The properties span Wards 1, 7, 10, 17, 21 and 24, including hotel shelters at 2180 Islington Avenue, 185 Yorkland Boulevard, 1677 Wilson Avenue, 50 Estate Drive, 55 Hallcrown Place, 77 Ryerson Road, 445 Rexdale Boulevard and 22 Metropolitan Road. The designation produces net city savings from reduced shelter costs. City Council decides.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate a Portion of 20 Humberview Crescent and 50 St. Phillips Road - Stage 1
topics: easements, expropriations, property (sc), trail systems; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, footpaths; multi-pupose trails; multi-purpose paths; multi-use pathways; multi-use trails; pedestrian trails; recreational trails; trail networks; trails; walking paths; waterfront trail
brief: Up for approval at City Council: starting the first stage of expropriating parts of 20 Humberview Crescent and 50 St. Phillips Road for the council-approved Mid Humber Gap trail project, which has completed its environmental assessment. Owners get 30 days to request a hearing on whether the taking is fair, sound and reasonably necessary, and staff would return with a stage-two report on values and costs. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Zoll Medical Canada Inc., for the Provision of Cardiac Monitors / Defibrillators with all Accessories, Proprietary Consumables and Extended Maintenance Agreements
topics: contracts, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ems
brief: On the agenda at City Council: approving a non-competitive contract with Zoll Medical Canada at $24,758,371 ($25,194,118 net of HST recoveries) for cardiac monitors and defibrillators with accessories, proprietary consumables and extended maintenance for paramedics, fire services and public health. Sticking with the Zoll X Series avoids the cost of replacing the whole system, and the deal supports paramedic service growth under the multi-year staffing plan Council adopted in June 2025. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

The city owns three snowmelters that are key to winter operations, melting snow in place instead of hauling it away. The source documents list $2,869,780, $2,852,013, $2,820,145, $3,940,350, $4,452,595, $3,872,199 and $500,000. City Council decides.

Horgan Water Treatment Plant, raising it from $1,067,017 ($1,085,796 net of HST recoveries) to $1,242,017 ($1,263,876 net of HST recoveries). The extra engineering covered accelerated work so critical tasks finished by June 2024 without delaying the Scarborough pump station rehabilitation. City Council decides.

Councillor Frances Nunziata recommends City Council make the change to improve peak-period traffic flow and safety.

brief: The northwest baseball diamond at Martingrove Gardens Park, 31 Lavington Road, would be named the Jim Horton Baseball Diamond in honour of the late coach, who died February 6, 2025 at age 76. Horton coached from 1987, was known as Mr. Everything for Martingrove Baseball, served on its executive for more than 35 years, and helped secure the city's commitment and the Optimist Club's funding for the Centennial Park diamond at a cost of $100,000. City Council decides on the naming.

The arena has been city-owned and managed by the Weston Lions Club under a nominal lease since 1970. The report cites a $25 million figure in connection with the revitalization.

The item follows the February 2025 storms and the interim reviews by Municipal VU Consulting and the Internal Audit Division. title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
brief: An updated buying plan for goods and services needed to host the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Toronto goes to Council for approval, along with authorization for staff to negotiate and award contracts with vendors that meet the plan's cost targets. The update includes contracts awarded to date and items captured in a confidential attachment.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Legacy Update
brief: World Cup legacy money is being directed to community programs. Council is asked to move World Cup 2026 legacy funding, $37,500 to Parks and Recreation and $120,000 to Social Development, at no extra cost to taxpayers, so community programs can benefit from Toronto's hosting of the tournament. The report also cites a $5 million figure in connection with the legacy funding.

title: Impacts of Provincial Legislation that Weakens Rental Protections
brief: Council could push back on provincial rental law changes. Council is asked to tell Ontario it opposes Bill 60 changes to renter protections, including weaker rent control and security of tenure, and to renew its request for rent control on rentals first occupied after 2018, with a legal review of options. The motion notes fifty percent of Torontonians rent their homes; supporters of Bill 60 have claimed the changes would encourage developers to build, while the motion's supporters argue easing evictions is not what builds homes. Council adopted the item with added directions: a legal review of options including potential Charter protections, a first-quarter 2026 report on what proportion of homelessness in Toronto is due to federal versus provincial decisions, submission of the report to Ontario's Regulatory Registry, and a renewed request for a Build More Homes Rebate of at least $596 million — equivalent to the development charges payable — for 15,830 purpose-built rental homes.

title: Toronto Sports and Culture Should Be For Everyone
topics: professional sports, sports;
brief: Ticket resale prices for the Blue Jays' World Series run and the six upcoming FIFA World Cup matches are the focus of this item. The Economic and Community Development Committee is asked to direct staff to explore consumer protection enforcement for major sporting events and to call on the Ontario government to legislate against reselling event tickets above face value. The motion cites a 1993 World Series ticket costing less than $32 versus resale tickets now going for up to $10,000, and notes that Quebec already bans above-face-value resale while Ontario scrapped similar planned legislation in 2019. It affects fans buying tickets, parking, and vending at major Toronto events.
