The Economic and Community Development Committee is asked to direct staff to work with community partners on developing specialized care for Black seniors and those of Caribbean or African diasporas, and to apply the city's Community Benefits Framework, which sets hard targets for social and economic benefits on large civic projects. It matters to future residents of the home and to the surrounding Scarborough community, since the facility is part of a plan to redevelop five city long-term care homes totalling 1,232 beds.

The item links community facilities to mental health, social ties and belonging.

brief: The General Government Committee faces a decision on adding $652,875 ($664,366.00 net of HST recoveries) to the ePlanSoft blanket contract for the e-PlanREVIEW tool Toronto Building uses to review and mark up building plan drawings, raising it from $2,532,550.00 ($2,577,122.00 net of HST recoveries) to $3,185,425.00 ($3,241,488.00 net of HST recoveries) Expanding the tool's use for Toronto Building supports housing delivery city-wide after the old markup tool was retired. The committee decides.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract 47024408 with Computacenter TeraMach Inc., for Veritas Software Licences and Maintenance to Support City Data Centre Backup and Recovery
topics: contracts, databases, information and communication technology, software licences; ict; information and communication systems; information and technology; information technology; it, software licenses
brief: Up for approval at the General Government Committee: adding $3,500,000 ($3,561,600 net of HST recoveries) to the Computacenter TeraMach blanket contract for Veritas NetBackup software that runs the city data centre's automated backup and disaster recovery, raising it from $4,072,592 ($4,144,270 net of HST recoveries) to $7,572,592 ($7,705,870 net of HST recoveries). The extension keeps critical backup infrastructure supported through July 2027, with a new competitive process planned for early 2027. The committee decides.

title: Amendment to Agreement with Motorola Solutions Canada Inc., for Two-Way Radio Products and Services for Radio Replacement Lifecycle Project for the Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: agreements, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing, telecommunications; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ems, phone services; telephone services; voice communication; voice mail, tenancy agreements
brief: On the agenda at the General Government Committee: amending the Motorola Solutions two-way radio agreement for Toronto Paramedic Services' radio replacement project, adding $1,500,000 ($1,526,400 net of HST recoveries) to raise the value from $5,168,000.00 to $6,668,000 ($6,785,357 net of HST recoveries). The money replaces obsolete and unsupported equipment and buys more gear for growing operational demands. The committee decides.

title: Amendment to Agreement with Crestline Coach Ltd., for the Non-exclusive Supply and Delivery of New Ambulances for the Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: ambulances, contracts, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, ems
brief: Whether to amend the Crestline Coach ambulance agreement, adding $29,020,000 ($29,530,752 net of HST recoveries) to raise the target value from $27,242,618 to $56,262,618 ($57,252,840 net of HST recoveries) is before the General Government Committee. Procurement delays and COVID-era supply chain disruption meant paramedics got no new ambulances from 2022 to 2025 while costs rose, and old ambulances stayed in service longer to keep daily operations covered. The committee decides.

title: Introduction of By-law
topics: by-laws, draft by-laws; bylaws, draft bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the General Government Committee will introduce a confirming bill. It carries no policy decision of its own.

title: Summary of the Bid Award Panel's Use of Extended Authority During City Council's 2025 Summer Recess
topics: awards, committees of council, contracts, delegation of authority; council committees, signing authorities
brief: Before its dissolution on October 1, 2025, the Bid Award Panel is reporting the contracts it awarded during Council's 2025 summer recess under its extended authority, which let it award open competitive solicitations above its usual $20 million limit. The Chief Procurement Officer recommends the General Government Committee receive the summary for information.

title: Cancellation, Reduction or Refund of Property of Taxes or Payment in Lieu of Taxes - October 23, 2025
topics: business associations, property (sc), property taxes, taxes; industry associations; marketing alliances; trade associations, levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: This is a procedural tax item: the General Government Committee is asked to decide on property tax appeal applications for cancellation, reduction or refund of taxes or payments in lieu of taxes, covering the October 23, 2025 batch. The law allows relief when a property is destroyed or demolished, becomes tax-exempt, changes use, or was overcharged through an assessment error, and the committee must hold a public meeting before deciding. The General Government Committee decides.

title: Non-Union Separation Costs for 2024
topics: employees, employment termination, labour relations, workplaces; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, employee exit; layoff; termination of employment, job sites; telework; work from home; worksites, staff
brief: Staff are reporting 2024 non-union employee separation costs to the General Government Committee: payments above legislative minimums when the employer unilaterally exits employees, set using factors courts consider such as length of service, age and job prospects. A 2014 Auditor General review found these costs were awarded in line with city policy, legislation and jurisprudence. The committee receives the report for information.

title: Litigation Arising from the Rehabilitation of Section 1 of the F.G. Gardiner Expressway (Jarvis Street to Cherry Street) - Supplier Suspension Status Update
topics: construction, contract termination, contracts, engineering, legal matters; building, legal issues
brief: The General Government Committee is getting a status update on whether WSP Canada should be suspended from city contracts over the Gardiner Expressway Section 1 rehabilitation dispute: suspension was not recommended in April 2025, but Council then told the Chief Procurement Officer to notify WSP of a proposed suspension under the supplier suspension procedure and report back. The committee receives the update.
address: Toronto Ontario Gardiner Cherry; Toronto Ontario Gardiner Jarvis

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6055480 with Rossclair Contractors Inc., for General Contracting Services at 2299 Dundas Street West
topics: city-owned properties, contracts, housing, projects, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city owned properties; city properties, homes; residences
brief: Whether to add $2,500,000 ($2,544,000 net of HST recoveries) to the Rossclair Contractors purchase order for general contracting at the city-owned building at 2299 Dundas Street West, raising it from $15,356,111 ($15,626,379 net of HST recoveries) to $17,856,111 ($18,170,379 net of HST recoveries) is before the General Government Committee. The building was bought in 2018 as a transition site for the George Street Revitalization project and is being converted for clients relocating from the Seaton House Annex program. The committee decides.

title: Apportionment of Property Taxes - October 23, 2025, Hearing
topics: land severance, properties (real estate), property taxes, tax apportionment; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, property; real estate, severance (land)
brief: This is a procedural tax item: the General Government Committee will hold its October 23, 2025 hearing on 11 property tax apportionment applications, which divide unpaid taxes from severed land onto the newly created parcels. The law requires a public meeting where affected owners can appear before the committee decides. The committee has delegated authority to make the final decisions.

title: 5 Robinson Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether the detached house at 5 Robinson Street can be demolished before any permit for a replacement building is issued. Staff present three options: refuse the demolition, approve it outright, or approve it with conditions. The decision determines whether the lot can sit empty with no approved rebuild.

title: Introduction of By-laws
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will introduce the bills needed to give legal effect to the decisions made at this meeting. No policy change is proposed.

title: Denvale Road Traffic Calming - Speed Hump Relocation
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to relocate an already-approved speed hump on Denvale Road between Eden Park Road and Ashall Boulevard. Residents raised concerns about the hump's original location after it was approved, and staff re-evaluated and recommended alternative spots. The change follows the earlier Denvale Road traffic calming decision.
address: Toronto Ontario Denvale Ashail; Toronto Ontario Denvale Eden Park

title: Zoning By-law Amendment for Garden Suites on Parkmount Road Facing Craven Road - Final Report
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: zoning;
brief: City Council will decide on a zoning amendment settling what garden suites are allowed on Parkmount Road properties facing Craven Road, between Danforth Avenue and Hanson Street. Council directed the review in October 2024 to consider provincial planning changes, past consultation, and better setbacks from Craven Road. Garden suites have been allowed city-wide since 2022, with over 900 building permit applications received so far.

title: Parking Amendments - Dentonia Park Avenue (Northside between Avonlea Boulevard and Sibley Avenue)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to limit parking to one hour on the north side of Dentonia Park Avenue between Avonlea Boulevard and Sibley Avenue, from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday to Friday. Residents petitioned for the change over limited parking availability; on-street permit holders would stay exempt from the limit.

title: Kensington Orphan Lanes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: lanes; traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: The question before the Toronto and East York Community Council: whether to have staff investigate how to provide street lighting and garbage pickup to privately owned 'orphan lanes' in Kensington Market, and report back in spring 2026. The lanes, registered to people who died in the 19th century, provide essential access to homes and businesses, including Cyril Lane, the fire exit for Kensington Community School, and Ellen Lane, the only vehicle access to a seniors housing building. The lanes are broken, unlit and filled with trash, and the city cannot enforce standards without a current owner.

title: Implementation of Permit Parking on Clifton Road between Glenrose Avenue and the south end of Clifton Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to introduce permit-only parking on Clifton Road from Glenrose Avenue to the street's south end, from 12:01 a.m. to 10 a.m. daily. Residents south of Glenrose, some with no off-street parking, requested the change after receiving many tickets. Existing parking and stopping bans on parts of the street would be removed to make room for the permit zone.

title: Naming a Parkette at 55B Brock Avenue in Honour of Pat Capponi
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parkettes, street names; renaming; road names; street naming
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to name a new parkette at 55B Brock Avenue the 'Pat Capponi Parkette.' The proposal, submitted by the Ward 4 councillor, drew support from long-time Parkdale residents who worked with Pat Capponi or recognize her impact on the community. Staff reviewed it against the city's property naming policy and commemorative principles and found it meets the criteria.

title: Roxborough Street West Parking
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to create a paid parking zone on Roxborough Street West between Yonge Street and Avenue Road, at $6.75 per hour for up to two hours. The Green P mobile-only zone would run 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Monday to Saturday and 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday. Residents with parking permits struggle to find spots because of non-resident pressure near Ramsden Park, and a similar Green P zone on nearby Berryman Street has improved turnover.

title: Pedestrian Safety at University of Toronto
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians; pedestrianization
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to ban northbound left turns and southbound right turns at St. George Street and Ursula Franklin Street on weekdays from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., with bicycles excepted. The University of Toronto requested the restrictions urgently, saying turning drivers encounter heavy pedestrian flows when classes change and some push through the crowds. The university would then work with a traffic consultant on longer-term fixes.
address: Toronto Ontario St. George Ursula Franklin

title: Children’s Safety in Jean Sibelius Square
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety; public safety
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will direct staff to install signs prohibiting bicycles on the paved paths in Jean Sibelius Square, keeping them for pedestrians only. The path crosses between two play areas in the small, heavily used park, and a four-year-old child was recently knocked down and seriously injured by a cyclist there. Earlier signs asking cyclists to slow down did not change behaviour.

title: Barton Avenue Traffic Calming
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic calming measures, traffic direction; one way operations; one way streets; one way traffic; two way operations; two way streets; two way traffic, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will direct staff to make Barton Avenue one-way westbound between Clinton Street and Christie Street. The narrow Seaton Village street now carries cut-through traffic funnelled by navigation apps, and residents and the Seaton Village Residents' Association have preferred the one-way option since consultations began in 2018. The change comes ahead of the RapidTO Bathurst streetcar lane.

title: 1099 Broadview Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: official plan amendments, zoning;
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes for a mixed-use building at 1099 Broadview Avenue, with two towers of 14 and 16 storeys above a shared five-storey podium. The building would provide 313 homes, 633 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, an 800-square-metre rear courtyard, and 207 vehicle and 363 bicycle parking spaces. Staff say the proposal fits the area's context and conforms with the Official Plan.

title: Appointments to The 519 Church Street Community Centre Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management, community centres, public appointments; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint Mohamed Omar to The 519 Church Street Community Centre Board of Management, for a term ending September 27, 2029. He replaces Aaron Hewitt, who resigned effective July 31, 2025.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the William H. (Bill) Bolton Arena Board
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: arenas, public appointments; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint five public members to the William H. (Bill) Bolton Arena Board, for terms ending October 23, 2029. The appointees are Michael Kane, Alina Ma, Connor Mellegers, Lisa Bernstein and Stephen Adler. Candidate details in confidential attachments would stay private.

title: Appointment to the Community Centre 55 Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, boards of management, community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will re-appoint Laura Beaune to the Community Centre 55 Board of Management, for a term ending June 30, 2029. The board confirms she is qualified to continue serving under the city's public appointments policy.

title: Rescinding appointments made in error to the Community Centre 55 Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will rescind the July 2025 appointments of Natalie Johnson and Pauline Grant to the Community Centre 55 Board of Management. The board's request letter was submitted in error because the board already had its full complement of members. No new appointments are proposed in this item.

title: Benlamond Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install four speed humps on Benlamond Avenue between Main Street and Norwood Road. Staff assessed the street against the city's traffic calming policy and found the criteria were met. A by-law to alter the roadway would follow approval.

title: Streetscape Improvements and Parking Amendments - Colborne Street between Church Street and Leader Lane
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: improvement, parking regulations; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on traffic and parking changes on Colborne Street between Church Street and Leader Lane to support streetscape work planned for spring 2026. The project would widen sidewalks, add curb extensions at Leader Lane, and create seasonal patio space for nearby businesses in the Old Town Toronto BIA, while removing on-street paid parking on the south side. A companion report would make Leader Lane pedestrian-only.

title: Pedestrian Way Designation and Streetscape Improvements - Leader Lane between Wellington Street East and Colborne Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: improvement, pedestrian walkways; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to designate Leader Lane, between Wellington Street East and Colborne Street, as a pedestrian way and permanently close it to vehicles. The laneway is set for reconstruction and streetscape improvements in spring 2026, and the pedestrian-only designation would improve the walking connection to Berczy Park in the St. Lawrence Market neighbourhood. A companion report covers related parking changes on Colborne Street.

title: Traffic Management in Ward 14 related to the King Street East and Church Street Intersection Project
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, intersections; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council votes on receiving, for information, a report on how TTC tracks and a watermain at King Street East and Church Street deteriorated to the point of needing repair, plus ongoing traffic management in the surrounding area. The report covers the area between the Don River, Eastern Avenue, Broadview Avenue and Gerrard Street East, including recommendations at Broadview and Dundas. No policy change is proposed.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic By-Law Regulations on Westmount Avenue, between Amherst Avenue and Rogers Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic regulations, transportation; transportation services
brief: To make room for Fairbank Silverthorn flood protection sewer construction, the Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on temporary traffic changes on Westmount Avenue between Amherst Avenue and Rogers Road. The one-way southbound street would become two-way while Westmount Avenue is closed between Martin Street and Genesee Avenue, with new stop controls at Amherst and Genesee avenues. The changes would run from November 2025 to about April 2026, with restoration by June 2026.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations and the Extension of Permit Parking Hours - 2025 Distillery Winter Village (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on temporary traffic and parking changes on neighbourhood streets near the Distillery District for the 2025 Winter Village, running November 13, 2025 to January 4, 2026. The changes, based on the organizers' operational plans and lessons from past years, aim to manage congestion and keep pedestrians safe during the event. A companion report covers the changes on streets with TTC service, which need City Council approval.

title: Adelaide Street West and Portugal Square - All-Way Stop Control
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: stopping prohibitions, traffic control systems; no stopping, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install all-way stop signs at the intersection of Adelaide Street West and Portugal Square. Staff assessed the intersection and found the stop controls would improve safety for all road users.

title: Adelaide Street East, Lombard Street and Church Street - On-Street Parking Review
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: on-street parking, parking prohibitions; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, no parking
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council changed paid-parking hours on Adelaide Street East, Lombard Street and Church Street near Masjid Toronto Mosque. Parking machines on these streets will stop charging from noon to 3 p.m. on Fridays, while keeping the $6.75-per-hour, three-hour limit at other times. The change follows a request for free Friday-afternoon parking near the mosque; staff had recommended against such exemptions, saying city-wide parking policies for religious institutions were still being developed.

title: St. Helen's Avenue - Commercial Loading Zone
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: loading zones, parking regulations; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to create a commercial loading zone on the west side of St. Helen's Avenue between Dublin Street and Whytock Avenue, operating 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on weekdays. The zone would help local businesses with loading and unloading. Staff also found mismatches between the parking by-law and posted signs on the street and recommend fixing them.

title: Breadalbane Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on parking changes on the south side of Breadalbane Street between Bay Street and Yonge Street. The existing $5.50 per hour parking machine regulation would be shortened, and three short-term parking spaces would be added for weekday morning and afternoon pick-up and drop-off. The changes would help families using the Toronto YMCA Family Development Child Care Centre at 15 Breadalbane Street, though the spaces would be open to anyone needing short-term parking.

title: Parking Amendments - 900 Bay Street (Macdonald Block Reconstruction Project) - (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on parking changes on Grosvenor Street near 900 Bay Street, tied to the Macdonald Block reconstruction project. The existing $5.50 per hour, three-hour-maximum parking machine regulation on the north side of Grosvenor Street would be rescinded to create a round-the-clock accessible loading zone in the lay-by east of Surrey Place. A companion report covers the related changes on Bay Street, which need City Council approval because the TTC runs there.

title: Jenet Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to replace the one-hour parking limit with a no-stopping rule on parts of the north side of Jenet Avenue near Lansdowne Avenue. The change would keep the entrance of 20 Janet Avenue clear for pedestrians with accessibility needs, emergency vehicles and deliveries, matching stopping bans already in front of other building entrances on the street. Staff also found mismatches between the parking by-law and posted signs on Jenet Avenue and recommend fixing them.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - October 2025 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, parking spaces; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking spots
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install or remove on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities at the locations listed in the October 2025 staff report. Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision on these spaces, along with related technical parking regulation amendments.

title: Advancing Local Infrastructure Improvements in Liberty Village in Advance of the FIFA World Cup 2026
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: infrastructure;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council receives, for information, a report on planned sidewalk and safety improvements in Liberty Village ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The report covers sidewalk installations on the west side of the neighbourhood, intersection safety upgrades, boulevard work at 65-85 East Liberty Street, and lighting and maintenance for the King/Liberty pedestrian bridge. No decision is proposed.

title: 55 Belmont Street - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: fire routes, prevention; fire access routes
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to designate parts of the private roads at 55 Belmont Street as fire routes under the city's fire route by-law. Designation lets the city enforce no-parking and emergency-access rules on those roads. Fire Services uses designated fire routes to regulate fire prevention and keep access clear for fire protection.

title: 370 Queens Quay West - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: fire routes, prevention; fire access routes
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to designate parts of the private roads at 370 Queens Quay West as fire routes under the city's fire route by-law. Designation lets the city enforce no-parking and emergency-access rules on those roads. Fire Services uses designated fire routes to regulate fire prevention and keep access clear for fire protection.

title: 610 Bloor Street West - Encroachment Appeal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide an appeal from the owner of 610 Bloor Street West over an existing enclosed marketing structure that sits on the public right-of-way. Staff recommend an encroachment agreement letting the structure stay, with conditions including that the owner indemnify the city and maintain the structure at their own expense. The staff report also references an amount of $5,350.00.

title: 629 Adelaide Street West - Encroachment Appeal - Privacy Fence
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide an appeal from the owner of 629 Adelaide Street West over a 1.8-metre wooden privacy fence that extends onto city property. Staff recommend ratifying an encroachment agreement letting the fence stay, retroactive to May 13, 2025, saying it does not harm pedestrian or traffic use of the right-of-way. The owner would pay the required appeal fee.

title: 70 Caledonia Park Road - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction permits (right-of-way); curb cut permits; driveway paving permits; driveway resurfacing permits; driveway widening permits; landscaping permits (right-if way)
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to close the west sidewalk and part of the southbound curb lane on Caledonia Park Road, between St. Clair Avenue West and Davenport Road, for 8 months from October 31, 2025 to July 1, 2026. The closure would make room for construction staging for a six-storey self-storage facility at 70 Caledonia Park Road, with a protected walkway for pedestrians and two-way traffic maintained. The closure would temporarily remove 14 parking machine spaces, with the applicant paying for the lost revenue. The staff report also references a $3.00 rate.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint and remove directors on five Business Improvement Area boards. Karen Lee would join Roncesvalles Village, Joel Sartorelli would join The Junction, and Peter Topos and Niki Kanavas would join Greektown on the Danforth; Natalee Jannetta would leave Danforth Mosaic, Eddie Gabel and Charalambe Sotiriopoulos would leave Greektown, and James Aldridge would leave Toronto Downtown West. BIAs are local business groups that manage main-street promotion and improvements.

title: 86 Kilbarry Road - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to exempt 86 Kilbarry Road from the fence height by-law. The owner wants to build a 1.83-metre black aluminum picket fence, but an existing hedge acting as a fence blocks the sightline near the driveway, raising visibility concerns. Staff recommend refusing the exemption.

title: 34 Tubman Avenue - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, exemptions, fences; application process, division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to exempt 34 Tubman Avenue from the fence height by-law. The existing fence and gates enclosing three ground-floor condo units stand 2.1 metres tall, where the limit is 1.2 metres. Staff recommend refusing the exemption.

title: 171 Neville Park Boulevard - Application to Remove a Private Tree
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: tree removal, trees; ash trees
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide an appeal of the city's refusal to permit removal of a privately owned, ravine-protected red oak at 171 Neville Park Boulevard. The applicant wants the 93-centimetre tree removed as a precaution against failure that could cause injury; the tree is healthy and maintainable, so staff recommend denying the permit. Community Council has delegated authority to make the final call on tree-permit appeals.

title: 1913-1915, 1919-1923 Yonge Street and 17 and 21 Millwood Road - Residential Demolition Applications
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions;
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether two-storey mixed-use buildings at 1913 to 1923 Yonge Street and detached houses at 17 and 21 Millwood Road can be demolished before replacement building permits are issued. The owner asked to tear them down early; staff present options to refuse the demolitions or approve them, with or without conditions. The decision determines whether the sites can sit empty with no approved rebuild.
address: 17 Millwood Toronto Ontario; 21 Millwood Toronto Ontario; 1919 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 1923 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 1913 Yonge Toronto Ontario; 1915 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: 554 and 556 Dupont Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: building permits; building records; commercial xpress service; residential fastrack service
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether two townhouses at 554 and 556 Dupont Street can be demolished before a permit for a replacement building is issued. The owner asked to tear them down early since no replacement permit has been applied for; staff present options to refuse the demolition or approve it, with or without conditions. The decision determines whether the lots can sit empty with no approved rebuild.
address: 554 Dupont Toronto Ontario; 556 Dupont Toronto Ontario

title: 501 Palmerston Boulevard - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, demolitions, residential properties; application process, residential real estate
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to allow demolition of a two-and-a-half-storey detached house at 501 Palmerston Boulevard. The community sent objection letters raising concerns about the building design and proposed construction. Staff offer two options: approve the demolition outright, or approve it with conditions such as construction fencing, debris removal and site maintenance.

title: 155 Strachan Avenue - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, demolitions, residential properties; application process, residential real estate
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to allow demolition of a one-storey semi-detached house at 155 Strachan Avenue. Toronto Building received an objection letter from neighbours raising concerns about the structural stability of the walls and foundation. Staff offer two options: approve the demolition outright, or approve it with conditions such as construction fencing, debris removal and site maintenance.

title: Naming of an existing Public Lane North of King Street East, extending Westerly from Bright Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: street names; renaming; road names; street naming
brief: An existing public lane north of King Street East, running west from Bright Street, would be named 'Joyce Wieland Lane' under a decision before the Toronto and East York Community Council. The naming complies with the city's street naming policy and its principles for commemoration in the public realm.

The deal would run up to 20 years with revenue sharing, subject to City licences or leases for the infrastructure. Negotiation details stay confidential.

brief: Approving creating a Campus Plan Steering Committee and appoint three board members to it, goes to the Zoo board for approval. The committee would guide development of a new 2027 Toronto Zoo Campus Plan, which will shape the Zoo's future growth, with the planning process launching in 2026.

It includes raising the Community Conservation Centre construction commitment with PCL from $75.0 million to $77.0 million, with related contract amendments.

title: 2026 Operating Plan and Budget
topics: operating budgets, zoos;
brief: Approving the Toronto Zoo's 2026 Operating Plan and Budget, goes to the Zoo board for approval. The Policy and Finance Committee reviewed it on September 23, 2025 and recommended approval.

brief: This is a procedural item: the CreateTO board is noting council's July 2025 direction to work with city and development partners on the detailed design of the housing development at 3725 Bloor Street West — the 43-storey project with about 698 homes including 230 affordable units — and to secure the development requirements in a lease agreement.

brief: This is a procedural item: city staff from the Housing Secretariat and Housing Development Office will present to the CreateTO board on the Toronto Builds policy framework and its implementation, adopted by council in May and July 2025 to activate city land for more affordable homes. No decision is being asked for.

brief: This is a procedural item: the CreateTO board is asked to approve its 2026 meeting schedule — January 26, March 6, April 27, June 12, July 27 and November 10, 2026 — set to avoid conflicts with the City Council calendar.

The supporting letter says grassroots founders often face food, financial and housing insecurity and that high-capacity organizations win most grant funding.

brief: This is a procedural item: staff will present the proposed directions for the new Parkland Strategy and Parks and Recreation Facilities Plan, sharing community engagement results, followed by a question-and-answer period. No decision is being asked for.

brief: This is a procedural item: the 2SLGBTQ+ Advisory Committee will elect a member of the public as Vice-Chair, in accordance with its terms of reference. No other decision is being asked for.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Legacy Update
topics: soccer;
brief: Staff are updating the FIFA World Cup 2026 Subcommittee on tournament legacy initiatives and seeking Council approval for in-year budget adjustments to advance 2025 work. The infrastructure projects at Toronto Stadium and Centennial Park are described as the largest legacy investments that will serve Torontonians after the tournament. The source documents list $37,500, $120,000 and $5 million. The subcommittee considers the update before it goes to Council.

topics: international events, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, international event bids; olympic bids
brief: City Council is being asked to direct the Executive Director, FIFA World Cup 2026, Toronto Secretariat, and the Chief Procurement Officer to proceed under the updated procurement plan: contracts awarded to date, requests to negotiate and award items in a confidential attachment, and updated procurement award authority thresholds. The recommendations cover capital and operational services previously approved by Council. The item is before the FIFA World Cup 2026 Subcommittee on its way to Council.

topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: a property owner at 2372 Midland Avenue is appealing a city property standards order. The Property Standards Committee will hear the appeal and decide whether the order stands. No policy change is proposed.

topics: by-laws, municipal codes, property standards; bylaws

brief: This is a procedural item: a property owner at 10 Macey Avenue, 206 is appealing a city property standards order. The Property Standards Committee will hear the appeal and decide whether the order stands. No policy change is proposed.

title: 26 Laing Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 14-storey mixed-use building plus a separate four-storey townhouse block at 26 Laing Street. The proposal has 170 homes, 111.6 square metres of ground-floor commercial space, 13 vehicle and 197 bicycle parking spaces. Staff would also report on converting Laing Street to two-way traffic from the proposed driveway to Eastern Avenue.

title: 15 Toronto Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve Official Plan and zoning changes, with a holding provision, for a 56-storey mixed-use building with 394 homes at 15 Toronto Street. The proposal includes about 13 social housing units and 175 square metres of retail, with the social housing provided in place of replacement office space. A separate heritage report on demolishing the existing 11-storey building in the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood Heritage Conservation District will be considered alongside it.

title: Wellington Street Loading Zone
brief: City Council will decide whether to revert parking by-laws to restore a 15-minute loading zone on Wellington Street West at its original location near Bathurst Street, used mainly by 1Hotel. The zone had been moved to Bathurst Street during the Wellington Street bikeway project, but the new spot caused snow-clearing and peak-hour traffic problems, and the hotel paid to rebuild the sidewalk at the original spot. The change would return the loading zone to where it was.

title: 2323-2329 and 2345 Yonge Street - Official Plan Amendment Application and 2323-2329 Yonge Street Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a 65-storey mixed-use building with about 784 homes at 2323-2329 Yonge Street. The Official Plan amendment would cover both that site and 2345 Yonge Street, under the same ownership, letting the sites provide affordable housing and non-residential space instead of the full replacement office space normally required. A separate zoning application for 2345 Yonge Street is still under review and would come back in a future report.

title: Establishing a Community Safety Zone on Dovercourt Road, between College Street and Dundas Street West
topics: safety, traffic regulations; public safety
brief: City Council will decide whether to designate a Community Safety Zone, in effect at all times on both sides of Dovercourt Road, between College Street and Dundas Street West. The stretch links families to several schools, the West End Parents Daycare, a local YMCA and neighbourhood parks, and residents have reported speeding, crosswalk violations and near misses with pedestrians and cyclists. The designation would increase traffic fines and could support future automated speed enforcement.

title: Bloem Avenue - Turn Prohibition
topics: transportation, turn prohibitions (traffic); transportation services
brief: City Council will decide whether to ban southbound right turns from Dufferin Street onto Bloem Avenue on weekday afternoons, from 3:30 p.m. to 6:30 p.m., with bicycles excepted. Residents of the small residential street say cut-through drivers avoiding Dufferin Street cause speeding, backups and near accidents, and a neighbourhood survey supported the ban. The restriction would pair with planned traffic calming measures.

title: 135 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 49-storey mixed-use building with 576 homes at 135 St. Clair Avenue West. The 164.3-metre building would include 948 square metres of non-residential space and a mid-block pedestrian connection between Foxbar Road and Avenue Road. Before the by-law is enacted, the owner must show the area's sewers and watermain can handle the development.

title: Temporary Amendments to Traffic and Parking Regulations and Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions during the Queen Street East Closures
topics: parking regulations, traffic, traffic regulations, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, transportation services
brief: City Council will decide on temporary traffic and parking changes around Queen Street East between Davies Avenue and Broadview Avenue, from October 2025 to May 2026, during watermain and streetcar track replacement. The work would cut Queen Street East to one lane each way, then a single eastbound lane during track work, with stopping banned on both sides and Hamilton Street temporarily made two-way. Transit priority measures would also be added on Dundas Street East between Parliament and River Streets while the 501 Queen, 503 Kingston Road and 504 King routes are diverted. The staff report also references a $3.00 rate.

title: 425 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: approval, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes for a 30-storey mixed-use building with 472 homes at 425 Bloor Street West. The proposal includes 798 square metres of non-residential space, and the owner would be asked to find a suitable off-site parkland dedication in the area instead of providing parkland on the site. The building would add hundreds of homes near Bloor Street West.

title: Improving the Speed and Reliability of the 7 Bathurst
topics: parking regulations, public transit, traffic regulations, transportation; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, transportation services
brief: City Council will decide on measures to speed up the 7 Bathurst bus between Eglinton Avenue West and Bathurst Station. Staff recommend extending afternoon and weekend no-stopping hours on the east side of Bathurst Street and changing some turn bans at Davenport Road and Dupont Street, to keep parked and turning vehicles from blocking buses in congestion. The TTC is also studying bunching and gapping on the route to even out bus spacing. The changes are expected to cost about $30,000, funded from the TTC's capital budget.

title: 1648-1664 Dupont Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: permits, zoning bylaws; permit renewal, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve zoning changes, with a holding provision, for an 11-storey mixed-use building with 163 homes and ground-floor retail at 1648 to 1664 Dupont Street. The application extends a 2024 approval for 1650, 1660 and 1664 Dupont Street onto the additional property at 1648 Dupont Street, plus a small city-owned strip. The holding provision stays until engineering, servicing, noise and vibration matters are finalized. The building would include 26 vehicle and 103 bicycle parking spaces.

title: 307 Sherbourne Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: City Council will decide whether to close the east sidewalk and the northbound bike lane on Sherbourne Street, between Gerrard Street East and a point 35 metres south, for eight months from October 15, 2025 to May 31, 2026. The closure would make room for construction of an 18-storey student residence at 307 Sherbourne Street, with a covered walkway for pedestrians and a temporary bike lane for cyclists. Council approval is required because the TTC runs transit service on Sherbourne Street.

title: 1304-1318 King Street West and 143, 143a and 145 Cowan Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve demolishing 8 rental homes at 1304-1318 King Street West and 143 Cowan Avenue, with the owner required to provide 8 replacement rental units and a tenant assistance plan. The Ontario Land Tribunal has already approved, on an interim basis, an 18-storey mixed-use building with 230 homes for the site, and is withholding its final order until Council decides on the demolition. If the owner fails to finish the new building on time, a $20,000.00 charge per demolished unit would be added to the property tax bill as a lien on the land. Existing tenants would have the right to return at similar rents with financial compensation for hardship.

title: 27 Grosvenor Street and 26 Grenville Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Amendment to Section 37 Agreement
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City Council will decide whether to update the development deal for the approved two-tower project (32 and 46 storeys) at 27 Grosvenor Street and 26 Grenville Street. The changes would reduce required one-bedroom affordable rental units from 92 to 63, add 31 affordable studio units, convert one two-bedroom unit to a three-bedroom, extend the affordability period from 40 years to 99 years, and move the non-profit child care centre from the north tower to the south tower. The amendment would reshape the 231 affordable rental units secured under the Section 37 agreement.

title: 2, 4 and 80 Union Street - Official Plan and Zoning  By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Staff recommend City Council direct the City Solicitor to oppose, at the Ontario Land Tribunal, a proposal for three mixed-use towers of 39 to 49 storeys at 2, 4 and 80 Union Street, while discussions with the applicant continue. The application would redesignate the lands from Core Employment Areas to Mixed Use Areas, and the applicant appealed on April 23, 2025 after Council missed the Planning Act decision deadline. Since then, the province has approved the Keele St. Clair Secondary Plan (OPA 537), which now governs the area.

title: 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend City Council send the City Solicitor to the Ontario Land Tribunal to oppose a 27-storey, 367-unit mixed-use building proposed at 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West, while talks with the applicant continue. The developer appealed on April 7, 2025 after Council failed to decide within the 90-day Planning Act deadline. The proposal includes ground-floor retail and would replace existing buildings containing 10 rental units; staff say it does not conform with the Official Plan, including Site and Area Specific Policy 566.

topics: pedestrian crossovers, road safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: Staff reviewed Milner Avenue at Executive Court for pedestrian crossing protection and do not recommend it, also advising against banning pedestrian crossings there. Because the TTC runs buses on Milner Avenue, city council approval of the staff position is required.

title: Washburn Way - Traffic Safety Improvement
topics: road safety, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Staff recommend safety changes on Washburn Way, including lowering the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h and installing speed cushions. The measures come from a neighbourhood streets plan for Malvern West. Because the TTC runs buses there, city council approval is required.

topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: The city would take over responsibility for the roads and underground services in the Malvern (McLevin) subdivision, also known as Pinery Trail, built under a 2001 agreement with Canada Lands Company. The city's performance guarantee would be released. Council is asked to approve.

title: Kingston Road - Community Safety Zone
topics: safety, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, public safety
brief: A councillor recommends creating a Community Safety Zone on both sides of Kingston Road between Valhalla Boulevard and Birchmount Road, where community groups have raised traffic safety concerns. The designation would enable automated speed enforcement in the corridor. Council is asked to approve.

title: City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Re-allocating Section 37 Funds within Ward 23 - Decision Report - Approval

brief: Staff recommend a city-initiated zoning change to re-allocate $674,905.89 in unspent Section 37 community benefit funds, secured from development approvals near McCowan Road and Finch Avenue East, Midland Avenue and McNicoll Avenue, 5789 Steeles Avenue East, and 1088 Progress Avenue. The funds would go to other capital facility improvements in Ward 23 near those sites, with no new development proposed. City council decides whether to approve the re-allocation.

title: 126 Bellamy Road North -  Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [buildings by function], [buildings by height], development, residential properties, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Staff recommend approving zoning changes to allow a new eight-storey building with 184 homes at 126 Bellamy Road North, keeping the existing 16-storey apartment tower and adding a new public park. Council would amend the zoning by-law to permit the project.

brief: Staff recommend replacing the pedestrian refuge island on Sheppard Avenue East, 130 metres east of Allanford Road, with full traffic control signals for safer crossings. Because the TTC runs buses there, city council approval is required.

brief: Staff recommend approving zoning changes to allow a 12-storey mixed-use building at 2950 Birchmount Road and 3600 Finch Avenue East, with 356 homes and ground-floor shops and offices. Council would amend the zoning by-law to permit the project.

Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.
