brief: The Mount Dennis Bank of Nova Scotia at 1151 Weston Road — a 1949 limestone bank building designed by Gordon S. Adamson at Weston Road and Eglinton Avenue West — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. A development application for the site was submitted in July 2025 and is under review, and the formal by-law follows if no objections come in.

title: 496 Evans Avenue - Area-Specific Amendment to the Sign By-law
topics: by-laws, signs; bylaws, signage
brief: An application to allow a large third-party electronic ground sign at 496 Evans Avenue could be refused. Council is asked to turn down the amendment sought by the Bader Group for owner Mersen Canada DN Ltd. The site has an area restriction prohibiting third-party signs, and the proposed sign would be three times larger and more than 50% taller than the rules allow.

title: 3 Bestobell Road - Area-Specific Amendment to the Sign By-law
topics: by-laws, change, signs; amendments; conversion; modification, bylaws, signage
brief: An application to allow a large third-party electronic ground sign at 3 Bestobell Road could be refused. Council is asked to turn down the amendment sought by the Bader Group for owner Fisnik Pristine. The site is covered by two area restrictions that prohibit third-party signs, and the proposed sign would be three times larger and more than 50% taller than the rules allow.

title: 2 College Street - Area-Specific Amendment to the Sign By-law
topics: signs; signage
brief: An application to allow a large third-party electronic roof sign at 2 College Street could be refused. Council is asked to turn down the sign by-law amendment sought by the Bader Group for owner Gemstone Property Ltd. The sign type is expressly prohibited outside the Dundas Square special district, would be 18 times larger and nearly 10 times taller than current rules allow, and would sit less than 100 metres from another third-party sign.

title: 21-31 Windsor Street, 18 Buckingham Street, 60 Newcastle Street and 95 Portland Street - Designation of a Municipal Shelter as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: development, women; developing land; development (land); land development, shelters for women
brief: A seven-storey building at 21-31 Windsor Street, with 18 Buckingham Street, 60 Newcastle Street and 95 Portland Street, will replace the Elisa House women's shelter with 36 supportive homes, 32 emergency beds and 72 shelter beds. Council is asked to pass a by-law designating it a municipal capital facility and exempting about 36,000 square feet of social and health services space from development charges. Council is also asked to waive an estimated $88,000 in building permit fees for the affordable co-operative and supportive units. The current shelter is owned and operated by the Society of Saint Vincent de Paul.

title: Amendments to Zoning By-law 569-2013 relating to Accessible and Bicycle Parking Requirements for New Development
topics: accessible permit parking, bicycle parking, change, zoning bylaws; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), amendments; conversion; modification, bike parking, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a technical item: council is asked to make minor corrections and clarifications to the city-wide zoning rules on accessible parking and bicycle parking for new developments, such as rates for accessible spaces and counting rules for bike parking. The changes do not alter what By-law 223-2025 intended, and separate reviews of bike parking for mid-rise buildings and visitor parking continue.

title: Open and Accessible In-Person Public Transit Oriented Community Open Houses
topics: public consultation, public transit; community consultation; consultation; public hearing, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: A request that Infrastructure Ontario hold all Transit Oriented Community meetings in person, after residents asked for face-to-face answers about the Ontario Line projects goes to council. Residents have cited confusion from ongoing changes and provincially imposed zoning orders.

title: Property Included on the City's Heritage Register - Consideration of Objection for 1771 Bayview Avenue and 36 Green Valley Road
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Two property owners have objected to their properties being listed on the city's Heritage Register: 1771 Bayview Avenue in Leaside-Bennington, a mid-1930s apartment building, and 36 Green Valley Road in Bridle Path-Sunnybrook-York Mills, a Mid-Century Modern house. Council decides whether to keep both properties on the register despite the objections.

title: 506, 510, and 512 Jarvis Street - Notice of Intention to Designate Properties under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Three house-form buildings at 506, 510 and 512 Jarvis Street in Church-Wellesley — including an 1889 Annex-style house by Langley and Burke once used as a home for retired United Church missionaries — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 336, 340, and 342-344 Jarvis Street - Notice of Intention to Designate Properties under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Three Victorian-era properties at 336, 340 and 342-344 Jarvis Street in the Church-Wellesley neighbourhood could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act — 336 Jarvis, built in 1863, was home to artist Frederic Bell-Smith. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 207, 209, 211, 213, 215, 217 and 219 Jarvis Street - Notice of Intention to Designate Properties under   Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Seven 19th-century properties at 207 through 219 Jarvis Street in Moss Park — including an 1863 Italianate terrace and an 1879 Second Empire block — could begin heritage designation. Council decides whether to state its intention to designate under the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 85 Hanna Avenue and 109 Atlantic Avenue - Official Plan Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, planning;
brief: The employment lands at 85 Hanna Avenue and 109 Atlantic Avenue, on the southeast corner of King Street West and Atlantic Avenue, could be redesignated to mixed-use. Council decides on an Official Plan amendment that would require any future redevelopment to include non-residential space and affordable rental homes — though no redevelopment is proposed now. The provincial Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing makes the final approval decision.

title: 3138 Bayview Avenue - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, zoning, zoning bylaws; developing land; development (land); land development, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving five three-storey townhouses at 3138 Bayview Avenue, fronting onto Bayview with a total of 976.25 square metres of floor area. Each home would get one parking space via a private rear driveway. City Council is being asked to amend the city-wide zoning by-law to allow the project.

title: 40, 42, 44, 46 and 48 Hendon Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, official plan amendments, zoning; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Staff recommend approving an 11-storey (41-metre) residential building with 148 homes at 40, 42, 44, 46 and 48 Hendon Avenue, with a holding provision on the zoning. The project would have about 10,144 square metres of floor area. City Council is being asked to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes that would allow it.

title: 4949 Bathurst Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, by-laws, zoning; bylaws
brief: Staff recommend approving a revised 26-storey mixed-use building at 4949 Bathurst Street, 92.45 metres tall, scaled down from the originally proposed 39 storeys. The six-storey podium would hold shops, offices and a private daycare, with homes in the podium and tower above. City Council is being asked to approve the zoning change.

title: 6 Foxdale Court - Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, by-laws, zoning; application process, bylaws
brief: Staff recommend approving zoning for six two-storey detached houses at 6 Foxdale Court, with a total of 2,192 square metres of floor area, fronting a new private street to be created through a future condominium application. Twelve parking spaces would be provided, and a holding provision would apply. City Council is being asked to approve the zoning change.

title: Maniza Road - Parking Restrictions - Referral of item NY23.28 from Toronto City Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council sent proposed parking restrictions for Maniza Road back to North York Community Council, at its June 25-26, 2025 meeting, for another look. The community council is being asked to reconsider item NY23.28.

title: York Mills Road and Ness Drive - All-Way Stop Control
topics: pedestrian crossovers, roads, stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants, circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: The pedestrian crossover on York Mills Road just east of Ness Drive would be removed and replaced with all-way stop signs at the York Mills Road and Ness Drive intersection. Transportation Services says the change is justified by its assessment. Because the TTC runs transit on York Mills Road, City Council approval is required.

title: York Mills Road and Upjohn Road - Traffic Control Signals
topics: roads, traffic signals, transportation; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, transportation services
brief: Traffic signals are proposed for York Mills Road and Upjohn Road. Transportation Services says the signals are justified by its assessment and would improve safety for all road users. Because the TTC runs transit on York Mills Road, City Council approval is required.

title: 824 Sheppard Avenue West and 181 Cocksfield Avenue - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, development, residential properties; building, developing land; development (land); land development, residential real estate
brief: ACLP - Sheppard Avenue Group is building a 12-storey residential building at 824 Sheppard Avenue West and 181 Cocksfield Avenue, in two phases with varying road closures. Because the TTC runs transit on Sheppard Avenue West, City Council approval is required for the temporary use of the road for construction. Transportation Services is recommending the staging area be authorized.

title: Appointment of Public Members and Tenant Directors to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board of Directors
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would recommend five public members and two tenant directors to City Council for appointment to the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Board of Directors — with one recommended as chair — for terms ending October 10, 2027. The council meeting considering the item would be treated as a special shareholder meeting. Confidential attachments would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Replacing a Missing Plaque at Tommy Thompson Park Honouring Renowned Marathon Swimmer Vicki Keith - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: athletes, plaques, swimming; aquafit; aquatics; drop-in swimming; leisure swim; leisure swimming; recreational swimming; swimming lessons; swimming programs, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: The missing plaque honouring marathon swimmer Vicki Keith at Tommy Thompson Park would be replaced by June 2026, with a ceremony. Council would direct parks and conservation staff to reinstall the plaque — first erected in 1998 for the 10th anniversary of her swims across all five Great Lakes, naming the spot Vicki Keith Point, where she launched her first Lake Ontario swim in 1986 and later became the first swimmer to complete a two-way Lake Ontario crossing. Keith, a coach of disabled athletes and recipient of 41 awards, also crossed the English Channel and other waters by butterfly stroke. Park visitors would see the restored tribute.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority for Improvements to the Gatineau Hydro Corridor - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: capital budgets;
brief: The Toronto and Region Conservation Authority would get $769,170.59 in developer community benefits for meadow habitat restoration and public realm work in the Gatineau Hydro Corridor near Markham Road and Brimorton Drive. Council would add $769,170.59 to the TRCA's 2025-2034 capital budget, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from 1 and 2 Meadowglen Place — $225,780.17 to be spent in 2028 and $543,390.42 in 2026 — for The Meadoway's native meadow restoration, rest areas and benches. The work supports pollinators, birds and wildlife and makes the corridor more accessible. Residents along the corridor would use the improved space.

title: Authority to Waive Permit Fees for Winchester Junior and Senior Public School for Use of Winchester Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: parks permits, public schools;
brief: Winchester Junior and Senior Public School would get $1,017.75 in park permit fees waived to use Winchester Park while its schoolyard is under construction. Council would direct Parks and Recreation to waive the fees (excluding HST) on a one-time basis for Toronto District School Board permits through the end of 2025, since no shared-use agreement covers the park. Students would get the extra outdoor space during construction.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.NY25.31 - Renaming of Balmoral Park to Michael Mostyn Park - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: naming, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Balmoral Park would become Michael Mostyn Balmoral Park, keeping the original name at the homeowners' association's request. Council would amend its July 2025 renaming decision (item 2025.NY25.31) by inserting Balmoral after Michael Mostyn, still honouring Mostyn while retaining the park's historic name. Reopening the item is required. The change affects the park's official name and signage.

title: Protecting Public Investment and Advancing Interim Solutions Along Sheppard Avenue East - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: bike lanes, traffic management; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: Tendering and construction of the Sheppard Avenue East road-safety and bike-lane project would be paused until the province approves it under new rules, with interim safety measures explored meanwhile. Council would direct staff to hold off on the project — approved in June 2023 with road safety improvements, cycle tracks and public realm upgrades between Bayview Avenue and Leslie Street — because Bill 212 now requires Toronto to get the Minister of Transportation's approval before installing bike lanes that remove vehicle lanes, and the approval process has not been released. The motion warns proceeding could risk the project being halted or the infrastructure removed. Drivers, cyclists and pedestrians on Sheppard East would be affected by the delay.

title: Municipal Resolution of Support for Rooftop Solar Photovoltaic Projects - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: renewable energy; green energy; green power
brief: Council would express general support for rooftop solar panel projects in Toronto that advance the city's net-zero goals, through a blanket municipal support resolution. The Independent Electricity System Operator requires such resolutions for energy projects in its Long Term 2 procurement; staff received a request for a rooftop solar project in Etobicoke and recommend the blanket form. The City Manager could file any needed forms with other governments. The October 8-10 council meeting is the proponent's last chance before the October 16 proposal window closes.

title: Implementation of Permit Parking on Clifton Road Between Glenrose Avenue and the South End of Clifton Road - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Permit parking on Clifton Road between Glenrose Avenue and the street's south end would be fast-tracked, skipping the usual polling step. Council would exempt the implementation from the polling requirement in Municipal Code Chapter 925 after almost all residents on the street petitioned for it, citing increased parking pressure, frequent tickets, no off-street parking and no alternative parking locations. The request would go to the October Toronto and East York Community Council meeting. Residents of Clifton Road would get the permit system sooner.

title: Exploring a New Community Garden in the Hydro Corridor at the Rear of 2 Fieldway Road - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: gardens, parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces
brief: Land behind 2 Fieldway Road in the hydro corridor could become a community garden. Council would direct parks staff, with Hydro One and the local councillor, to study the feasibility of the site — bounded by the Islington TTC station Fieldway lot, 2 and 8 Fieldway Road, and the rail corridor and Bloor Street West — and identify funding, after a resident's proposal gathered over 60 signatures of support. Community garden space is in high demand with long wait lists. The motion is urgent because of 2026 parks capital budget timing.

title: Traffic Amendments to The Esplanade to Create a Motorcoach Loading Zone - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: A bus loading zone on The Esplanade would move closer to the Novotel hotel's front door at 45 The Esplanade. Council would approve the parking and traffic changes — placing the Bus Loading Zone on the north side of The Esplanade nearer the hotel entrance and adding a No Standing zone just east of it for passenger pick-up and drop-off — as part of the Esplanade and Mill Street Connection Project, which is under construction with by-law amendments needed by October. The hotel requested the change and Transportation Services supports the revised design. Hotel guests and transit riders on The Esplanade would be affected.

title: Community Mailboxes: Protecting our Public Space - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: mail services; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms
brief: The City Manager would get details from Canada Post about plans to replace door-to-door delivery with community mailboxes in Toronto and report back on the impacts. Council would request the information after the federal government announced the shift — the Toronto Star reported 2,500 to 11,000 boxes would be needed — and given the challenges of placing concrete-slab boxes at least 9 metres from intersections in dense older neighbourhoods. A similar plan was cancelled in 2018 after public pushback. Residents receiving home delivery would be the ones affected.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds from the Development at 109 Vaughan Road for Streetscape Improvements in the Hillcrest Village Business Improvement Area - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations
brief: Accessible sidewalk improvements in the Hillcrest Village business area would get $41,340 in developer funds. Council would release $41,340 in Section 45 funds from the development at 109 Vaughan Road to the Economic Development and Culture capital budget for the ramp, stairs, planters and integrated seating in front of 803 to 815 St. Clair Avenue West (the item's figures also list $10,000). The BIA designed the accessible sidewalk with the City's BIA office, and the project is already underway. Shoppers and pedestrians on the block would use the improved sidewalk.

title: 289 to 299 Balliol Street and 305 Balliol Street - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: parkland dedication;
brief: The developer of 289 to 299 Balliol Street would get two years after the first above-grade building permit to arrange its off-site parkland dedication. Council would grant the extension — instead of requiring the dedication before the permit — after the owner reached a tentative, staff-approved agreement to buy a property for the dedication, while the property's current occupant seeks a one-year lease-back to find alternate housing. Council authorized the off-site dedication approach in July 2025 (item 2025.MM32.33). The timing change would let the 31-storey project proceed while the parkland purchase is finalized.

title: Re-opening of Item 2025.EX23.3 - Metrolinx Ontario Line - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: road closures, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would extend the approved road-closure window for Ontario Line work on the Don Valley Parkway and Gardiner Expressway to November 29, 2025. Reopening item 2025.EX23.3 is required because supply chain and fabrication delays pushed the earliest achievable fabrication date to October 20, 2025, leaving too little time within the original September 22 to October 24 window to install the trestle structure across the Don Valley Parkway. The revised closure would be coordinated with Remembrance Day and the Santa Claus Parade. Drivers on the two expressways would face the extended lane closures.

title: Representation at an Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing with Respect to 145 Saint George Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: committees of adjustment, minor variances; committee of adjustment, variance
brief: The City would go to the Ontario Land Tribunal to defend the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of variances for a tall residential building at 145 Saint George Street. Council would authorize the City Solicitor, staff and outside consultants to oppose the applicant's appeal of the September 3, 2025 refusal, which covered maximum building height, gross floor area, unit count and setbacks from the site-specific by-law's permitted 96.0-metre height. The motion also lets the Solicitor negotiate a settlement. The Tribunal outcome would decide the building's final size.

title: Amending Item 2022.TE34.12 - 91-101 Raglan Avenue - Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Applications - Final Report - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos-Lin
topics: rental housing, zoning; rental properties; rental units
brief: The developer of 91 to 101 Raglan Avenue could demolish three vacant rental units before excavation and shoring permits are issued. Council would amend its 2022 approval (2022.TE34.12) by removing the precondition tying demolition permits to those permits, so construction can be expedited — the applicant has another project under construction nearby and says it will proceed immediately once the demolition permit, otherwise ready, is issued. All three units are vacant. The change mirrors similar demolition-timing motions Council has approved for other sites.

title: Taking Back Control of Our City Services to Deliver Higher Standards, Lower Costs and Greater Accountability - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: City divisions could be told to favour in-house staff over outside consultants, under a motion citing a sharp rise in consulting spending. Council would direct divisions to prioritize using City employees and review the City's policy on hiring consultants. The motion says City and agency spending on outside consultants rose from $11.2 million in 2014 to $57.7 million in 2023, not counting consultants on capital projects, and argues core work like playground design, planning studies and crosswalks should be done in-house. The change would affect how the City sources professional services.

title: Appointment of Members of Council to the Economic and Community Development Committee and the Toronto Zoo Board of Management - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: appointments, zoos;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council would appoint newly elected Ward 25 Councillor Neethan Shan — elected September 29, 2025 in the Scarborough—Rouge Park by-election — to the Economic and Community Development Committee until November 2026 and to the Toronto Zoo Board of Management. The motion also appoints Deputy Mayor Paul Ainslie as Chair of the Zoo board, filling vacancies left when the former ward councillor was elected to the House of Commons. The appointments let the new councillor assume duties and keep the board's leadership filled.

title: Mascot Brewery By-the-Glass Permit Application to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: applications; application process
brief: City Council would tell Ontario's alcohol regulator it supports Mascot Brewery's Etobicoke location getting a manufacturer's licence to sell its beer by the glass. Council would advise the AGCO in favour of the application for Mascot Brewery and Restaurant at 37 Advance Road — whose licence has expired, leaving the business unable to serve its beer — with the motion describing the brewery as a community hub hosting markets, events and Daily Bread Food Bank collections. The decision on the licence rests with the AGCO.

title: Amending Item 2017.TE27.10 - 263 to 267 Adelaide Street West - Rental Housing Demolition Application- Final Report - by  Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: The developer of 263 to 267 Adelaide Street West could demolish 12 vacant rental units earlier, without waiting for excavation and shoring permits. Council would amend its 2017 approval (item 2017.TE27.10) by removing the precondition tying demolition to those permits, so demolition can follow the project's construction phasing — which includes heritage conservation and rental housing replacement requirements that have been fulfilled. The tenants have moved out with assistance and compensation. The change would let the project proceed on its timeline.

title: Ensuring Residents Continue to Receive Important Notices During Mail Disruptions - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: mail services; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms
brief: Communications and clerk staff would consider alternative ways to notify residents about city work and meetings during the postal disruption. Council would have them look at options like digital ads, social media and flyers — after residents missed community consultation meetings or learned about construction only after it started during the Canada Post labour disruption — and review the notice processes. Mailings are often the first and only direct notice residents get, and newspaper notices do not always reach the target audience. Residents relying on city notices would be the ones affected.

title: Re-opening and Rescinding Item 2025.SC22.3 - 1555 Midland Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Michael Thompson, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: This is a technical correction: Council would cancel its earlier part-lot control exemption for 1555 Midland Avenue and repeal the related by-law, because a section 118 land-title restriction was accidentally left out. The exemption from May 2025 (By-law 487-2025) was meant to allow orderly land division; without the restriction there is a risk of problematic division, and the applicant says the exemption is no longer needed anyway. Reopening item 2025.SC22.3 is required. No policy change is involved.

title: Honouring Dr. Jane Goodall and Dr. Anne Innis Dagg: Getting More Kids to the Toronto Zoo - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Neethan Shan
brief: Staff would report, through the 2026 budget process, on a program offering free weekday Toronto Zoo field trips for schoolchildren, honouring conservationists Jane Goodall and Anne Innis Dagg. Council would request the report on the program celebrating Goodall's chimpanzee research and youth empowerment work and Innis Dagg's pioneering giraffe field research and advocacy for women in science. The motion says zoo visits give students experiential learning they cannot get in the classroom. Schoolchildren across Toronto would be the ones going on the trips.

title: Facilitating Intersectoral Supports in Social and Supportive Housing for Housing Stability - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: housing, supportive housing; alternative housing; special needs housing; supported housing, homes; residences
brief: Shelter services staff could sign data-sharing agreements with health and support partners to connect consenting clients with the right services. Council would authorize the agreements so basic information for clients who agree can be matched with city lists — including the By-Name List used by the Coordinated Access to Housing and Supports system to prioritize housing for people experiencing homelessness — with partners like nurse practitioners, personal support workers and mental health supports. The motion frames the move as strengthening intersectoral supports for housing stability. People moving from homelessness into City-funded housing would be the ones affected.

title: Ensuring Business Improvement Area Notices During Postal Strike - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: labour disruptions, mail services; courier services; mail rooms; mailrooms, labor disruptions; lockouts; strikes
brief: This is a procedural item: Council would let business improvement area boards notify members of annual general meetings by email or other alternatives instead of mail during the Canada Post labour disruption. The motion responds to an Economic Development and Culture request, since Municipal Code Chapter 19 requires mailed notice at least 15 business days before the meeting and the City cannot mail the notices. The temporary measure would let BIA boards use their own resources to reach members. No permanent policy change is involved.

title: 226 Olive Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: appeals, hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: The City would appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a three-storey fourplex with a garden suite at 226 Olive Avenue. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the North York District panel's September 11, 2025 approval — which came after planning staff requested six modifications and the applicant deferred the June hearing to make them — and to oppose the development at the Toronto Local Appeal Body. The motion also covers hiring outside consultants and negotiating a resolution.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Gardiner Public Realm Plan Strachan Gate Connection Design - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: funding, public realm; financing, public spaces
brief: The design of the Strachan Gate connection — a key junction under the Gardiner Expressway between the future Ontario Line Exhibition Place Station and destinations like Fort York, The Bentway and Exhibition Place — would get $273,000 in developer community benefits. Council would release $273,000 for the design work under the Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan, approved in April 2024 for the 7-kilometre corridor from Dufferin Street to the Don Valley Parkway; the item's figures break the total into $140,000 and $133,000. Pedestrians and cyclists moving through the Exhibition area would use the connection.

title: Mitigating Fire Risks with Strong Lithium-Ion Battery Regulation - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: fire hazards;
brief: The federal transport and health ministers would be asked to introduce stronger rules for uncertified lithium-ion batteries. Council would make the request after Toronto Fire Services reported a 591 percent increase in battery fire incidents from 2020 to 2024, with several failures linked to products lacking certification from bodies like the Canadian Standards Association or Underwriters Laboratories. Toronto Fire has launched a multilingual safety campaign; the motion says gaps remain in regulating battery sales and enforcing safety standards for products entering Canada. Anyone using e-bikes, scooters and other battery-powered devices would be affected by the rules.

title: Right-sizing Regent Park: Providing Adequate Affordable Housing to Over-housed Families - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Toronto Community Housing would study the needs of over-housed households in Regent Park and bring back recommendations so families can move to right-sized units without leaving the community. Council would request the study from the TCHC board as Phases 4 and 5 of the Regent Park revitalization approach — household sizes have shifted since 2007, with some families told to move to smaller units but no options available in the neighbourhood. The aim is to keep long-time residents rooted while making better use of the housing stock. Regent Park families in mismatched units would be the ones affected.

title: Shining a Light on Intimate Partner Violence: Empowering Survivors Through Awareness, Support and Prevention - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: abuse; assault; domestic violence; violence
brief: Social development staff would deliver a citywide public education campaign on intimate partner violence, with health, police and frontline groups. Council would direct the campaign covering awareness, available supports and prevention — after Council declared intimate partner and gender-based violence an epidemic in July 2023, and with services like the Barbra Schlifer Clinic reporting 18,000 survivors served from April 2023 to March 2024. The motion notes many people do not know services exist or feel afraid to reach out. Survivors and people at risk across Toronto are the intended audience.

title: Advancing Indigenous Affordable Housing - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: First Nations, affordable housing; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, affordable homes; housing projects
brief: Real estate staff could negotiate transferring 1 to 3 Strathmore Boulevard to the Indigenous housing provider Wigwamen, replacing the 429 Pape Avenue property Metrolinx expropriated for the Ontario Line. Council would authorize the negotiations for the site — declared surplus to the TTC in September 2025 after the Donlands Station Second Exit project, most recently used as a construction office — continuing the City's work with Wigwamen since the August 1, 2025 expropriation of the home it had operated since 2010. The property was originally residential and can be converted to housing. The move would restore a housing site for vulnerable residents.

title: An Updated Pickleball Play Assessment - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: noise complaints, noise control, recreation & tourism (sc); noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Parks staff would build noise mitigation into planning for temporary and seasonal pickleball courts. Council would ask the General Manager of Parks and Recreation to study other cities' approaches — including Ottawa's and the BC Recreation and Parks Association's strategies — and include options like setbacks, barriers and court surfaces in the Parks and Recreation Facilities Plan's pickleball recommendations. Councillors' offices are getting more noise complaints as the sport grows, with the loud crack of the hard plastic ball on the paddle. Players and neighbours near the courts would both be affected by the standards.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The City would go to the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose an appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of a lot severance and variances for a fourplex at 180 Queens Drive. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to oppose the applicant's appeal of the August 14, 2025 refusal — which covered front yard setback, building length and platform variances for the severance and new fourplex — after Urban Forestry recommended denial over impacts to by-law-protected trees. The motion also covers hiring outside consultants and negotiating a settlement.

title: Supporting the Elect Respect Campaign and Pledge - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: city initiatives; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives
brief: City Council would endorse the Elect Respect pledge promoting civility and opposing harassment of candidates and elected officials. Council would sign on to the pledge — started by Halton elected representatives and covering respect in public, private and online spaces, rejecting personal attacks, and calling on authorities to protect officials facing abuse — and share its support with municipal associations and provincial and federal leaders. The motion cites the Association of Municipalities of Ontario's finding that fewer people are voting and running for municipal office. Anyone participating in local democracy would be covered by the pledge's aims.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Guild Park and Gardens Improvements - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
topics: gardens, operating budgets;
brief: Guild Park and Gardens in Scarborough would get $6,035 in improvements. Council would release $6,035 — budgeted as $6,035.00 — in Section 37 community benefits from the development at 65 and 67 Livingston Road to the Parks and Recreation 2025 operating budget for capital improvements at the park. The local councillor requested the release. Park visitors in Scarborough would see the upgrades.

title: Promoting and Delivering School Based Vision Testing in Selected Toronto High Needs Schools - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: optometry services, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, contact lenses; eye care; eye glasses; eyeglasses; eyewear; optometrists; optomology services
brief: The Board of Health would be asked to develop a plan for a pilot mobile eye-testing program in selected high-needs Toronto schools. Council would request the plan for the opt-in, school-based vision testing program — modelled on the dental program — citing studies showing visual impairments limit children's learning, with visual processing involved in 75 percent of school learning. Toronto Public Health currently promotes eye exams but does not offer school-based testing. Students with undiagnosed vision problems would be the ones helped.

title: Aligning Cultural Use Tenancy Agreement for Ward 9 - Davenport - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: arts and culture, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities
brief: Two Ward 9 arts groups would get five-year nominal leases to keep running cultural programming in City-owned buildings. Council would approve the leases with Clay and Paper Theatre, operating out of the Dufferin Grove Fieldhouse at 875 Dufferin Street, and Sick Muse Art Projects, operating out of the Earlscourt Park Community Concession Building at 1595 St. Clair Avenue West — aligning the terms with the City's Community Space Tenancy policy, as done for two Ward 14 groups in March 2025. Both organizations have run programming from the spaces for five years. Davenport residents using the cultural programs would be affected.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.MM32.16 - Addressing Unlicensed Jet Ski Rentals and Safety on Toronto’s Waterfront - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: boat rentals, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: The City would expand its earlier jet ski decision with a review of who enforces the rules against unlicensed rental operators on the waterfront. Council would reopen item 2025.MM32.16 and ask the City Manager to review roles and responsibilities for motorized watercraft and jet skis, set up a working group and recommend stronger enforcement before the 2026 summer season. The motion says illicit, unlicensed operators endanger customers and everyone enjoying the waterfront. Swimmers, kayakers and boaters on Lake Ontario and the city's rivers are the ones affected.

title: Making our Communities Safe by Supporting a Common Sense Approach to Speed Cameras - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: traffic speed;
brief: Transportation staff would report on the impact of speed cameras on road safety — including pedestrian deaths, serious injuries and collisions — and on how camera tickets are issued, and would set and publish a reasonable enforcement threshold so drivers who only slightly exceed the speed limit are not fined. Council would request the report and the threshold under a motion titled Making our Communities Safe by Supporting a Common Sense Approach to Speed Cameras. The motion's background cites a SickKids and Toronto Metropolitan University study finding speed cameras reduced speeding by 45 percent in Toronto, and says enforcement has not happened transparently, undermining public confidence; it also criticizes the provincial government's handling of the cameras. The report would inform how the City runs its automated speed enforcement program.

title: Protecting the Cottonwood Flats and the Lower Don Lands - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: nature trails, parks and open space areas; green spaces; open spaces, interpretive trails; urban wilderness trails
brief: City staff, police and conservation groups would develop a plan to stop unpermitted events that have damaged the Cottonwood Flats and Lower Don natural areas. Council would have them create the action plan after illegal raves this summer and last summer left tire marks, destroyed plants, damaged sensitive soil, noise complaints and waste, undermining years of restoration by groups like Don't Mess with the Don, Toronto Field Naturalists and Nature Stewards. The plan would cover deterring unpermitted events and restoring and protecting the lands. Hikers and wildlife in the Don Valley would benefit from the protections.

title: Making Sports More Accessible and Free in City of Toronto Parks - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: accessibility, parks, sports; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Sports equipment stations would be installed in City parks under a three-year sponsorship valued at $500,000.00, giving residents free access to balls, paddles and other gear. Council would approve the sponsorship arrangement — the item's figures list $500,000.00 — through which Canadian Tire Jumpstart funds Equip to install, operate and maintain the open-access equipment lockers at no cost to the City or users, under the City's Sponsorship Policy. The motion says the partnership reduces barriers to physical activity and promotes equity in recreation. Park users across Toronto would get the free equipment.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Future Saint Lawrence Toronto Public Library Branch - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: library boards; public library boards
brief: The future relocated Saint Lawrence branch of the Toronto Public Library would get $3 million in enhancements. Council would release $3 million — budgeted as $3,000,000.00 — in Section 37 developer community benefits for the new 30,000-square-foot district library, replacing the undersized 4,833-square-foot branch at 171 Front Street East. The branch was originally to move to the First Parliament site at 271 Front Street East before the province expropriated those lands for the Ontario Line; an existing site in the Saint Lawrence neighbourhood was then found for a faster, lower-cost build. Library users in the neighbourhood would get the larger branch.

title: Authorizing the Release of Section 37 Funds for Central Eglinton Community Centre for Facility Renovations - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: community centres, facilities; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: The Central Eglinton Community Centre would get $94,096.25 for kitchen renovations and new equipment. Council would add $94,096.25 gross ($0 net) to the Association of Community Centres' 2025 operating budget for the centre, fully funded by Section 37 community benefits, to renovate the kitchen and buy equipment for cooking workshops. The Yonge/Eglinton centre serves a wide range of users, from childcare to income tax preparation seminars. Program participants would use the upgraded kitchen.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.TE24.16 - 2720, 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a technical amendment: Council would update its July 2025 approval for 2720, 2726 and 2734 Danforth Avenue, removing the holding provision now that updated Functional Servicing and Stormwater Management Reports have been reviewed and accepted. Reopening item 2025.TE24.16 is required to swap the attachment reference to the October 1, 2025 Information Report. Staff support the change. No policy change is involved.

title: Exploring a New Dog Off-Leash Area Along Aukland Road - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: dog off-leash areas; dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks
brief: Parks staff would study whether greenspace in the Hydro One corridor along Aukland Road could become a dog off-leash area. Council would direct the General Manager of Parks and Recreation, with the local councillor, to explore the feasibility of the site between Bloor Street West and Dundas Street West in Ward 3 and identify potential funding sources, through the Secondary Land Use agreement process. Residents have long wanted the facility, the growing area around Kipling Station would use it, and Hydro One has indicated willingness to evaluate the site. Dog owners in the area would be the main beneficiaries.

title: Authority to Enter Into a Maintenance and Rehabilitation Agreement on the Etobicoke Creek Trail - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: construction, park maintenance; building, parks maintenance
brief: Parks staff would get authority to sign a maintenance and rehabilitation agreement with Ontario's Ministry of Transportation for the Etobicoke Creek Trail section on provincial land. Council would grant the authority so the City can finish the trail construction begun in 2018 — delayed when the ministry did its own Queen Elizabeth Way overpass work — and do regular maintenance and future rehabilitation; the ministry requires the agreement to issue construction permits. Council already authorized a construction agreement in 2012 items. Trail users in Etobicoke would get the completed connection.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.EY22.22 - Dundas Street West at Dundas Street West - Traffic Regulation Amendments - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: intersections, traffic regulations;
brief: This is a technical correction: Council would fix its earlier decision on Dundas Street West so the reserved transit lane runs eastbound, not westbound as first written. The amendment to item 2025.EY22.22 changes Part 5 to designate the southerly eastbound lane on Dundas Street West, between Dundas Street West and a point 40 metres east, as a reserved public transit lane at all times. The wrong direction was approved in May 2025. Transit riders on Dundas Street West are the ones affected.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Heritage Toronto for Production and Installation of a Heritage Plaque Recognizing the Bomb Girls - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: A heritage plaque would honour the women who worked at Scarborough's Second World War munitions plant, at Civic Road and Warden Avenue. Council would release $10,000.00 in Section 37 developer community benefits to Heritage Toronto for the plaque marking the General Engineering Company (Canada) Ltd. plant — 346 acres, 172 buildings and over four kilometres of tunnels, where 21,000 workers, predominantly women, filled over 256 million fuses for the Allies. Scarborough's Sc/C emblem was etched onto every fuse. The plaque would commemorate the Bomb Girls' wartime contribution.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Parks and Recreation for Installation of Planters at Joseph Tough Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: park maintenance, planter boxes, tree planting; parks maintenance, reforestation; tree advocacy
brief: Planters would be installed at Joseph Tough Park for $2,500.00 so vines can grow on a Toronto Community Housing fence to screen a garbage area. Council would add $2,500.00 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Parks and Recreation operating budget, funded by Section 37 benefits from 124 and 128 Pears Avenue earmarked for 250 Davenport Road. The planters at the park abutting 250 Davenport Road would support vine planting on the existing fence frame. Tenants at 250 Davenport Road would see the screened view.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Heritage Toronto for Production and Installation of a Heritage Plaque Recognizing the Village Corner Music Venue - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: heritage properties, music, plaques; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: A heritage plaque at 174 Avenue Road would mark the Village Corner club, described as a birthplace of Canadian folk music. Council would release $5,300 in Section 37 developer community benefits to Heritage Toronto for the plaque at the Ward 11 site, where the club operated from 1960 to 1967, charged 50-cent memberships and helped launch Ian and Sylvia, David Wiffen and Gordon Lightfoot — whose Two Tones recorded his first album there. The club focused on Canadian folk musicians and also hosted blues artists like Sonny Terry and Brownie McGhie. The plaque would preserve the site's musical history for passersby.

title: Green Lane Landfill Renewable Natural Gas Project Update
topics: natural gas, projects, waste diversion; 3 rs; reduce reuse recycle
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving an update for information on the project to turn Green Lane Landfill gas into renewable natural gas with Enbridge Gas Ontario. Enbridge completed a feasibility study and, on July 3, 2025, told the City it no longer wishes to proceed and is terminating the agreement; staff intend to explore alternative ways to use the landfill gas. The update also covers the planned investment opportunity for three nearby First Nations.

title: Review of Automated Speed Enforcement (ASE) Ticket Appeals Process
topics: appeals, enforcement, road safety;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have Court Services review the process for disputing automated speed camera tickets and report back with improvement recommendations by October 2025. Residents report problems including ticket numbers not recognized online, outdated email addresses, dropped phone calls after long waits, and no updates after submitting appeal forms.

title: Revised Free-Floating Car-Share Program
topics: car sharing, carpooling, parking; car pooling; car pools; car-pooling; carpools
brief: On the agenda at the committee: considering a revised free-floating car-share program, including its impact on winter maintenance and parking enforcement, and options for car-share vehicles to use off-street parking for drop-off and pick-up. Council referred the item to the committee in June 2024 for consideration with the Parking Strategy in the first quarter of 2025.

title: Optimizing the Automated Speed Enforcement Program to Stop Speeding
topics: enforcement, red light cameras, speed limits, traffic, traffic cameras; compass cameras; rescu cameras; rescu equipment, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, red light monitoring
brief: This motion from the Mayor asks Council to adjust the automated speed enforcement camera program, including a seven-day grace period before a second ticket from the same camera, and to install additional and larger warning signs near cameras by October 31, 2025. The motion cites a study by SickKids and Toronto Metropolitan University researchers finding that speed cameras reduced speeding by 45 per cent in Toronto, and the July 2025 death of 15-year-old Christina Huang near Finch Avenue East and McCowan Road.

title: Proposed Incentive Pilot Programs to Collect and Manage Stormwater on Private Property in Support of Climate Resilience
topics: climate change, pilot projects, stormwater management; climate protection, storm water management; swm; wet weather flow management
brief: Whether to approve two pilot programs to help residents manage stormwater on private property: subsidized rain barrels and downspout diverters for one year, and incentives for green infrastructure such as rain gardens for three years is before City Council. The programs respond to more frequent intense storms — Toronto has seen at least four storms exceeding the 100-year level in 20 years — and aim to reduce localized flooding.

title: Tree Maintenance Review Update 2025
topics: city-owned trees, privately-owned trees, tree maintenance; city owned trees; public owned trees; publicly owned trees; trees on public property, private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: Up for direction at City Council: having staff begin shifting tree maintenance work from contractors to City crews, aiming for an equal balance between City staff and contracted services, following the Auditor General's tree maintenance audit and a 2024 quality service pilot. Progress to date includes improved contract language and management practices.

title: Micromobility Update
topics: city initiatives, personal mobility devices, public education; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, electric wheelchairs; medical scooters; motorized scooters; scooters
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is receiving an update for information on electric micromobility, such as e-scooters, covering its benefits, safety risks for pedestrians, and the need for coordinated policy. The report covers progress since the 2024 Micromobility Strategy, including a public education campaign and a dedicated working group. No policy change is proposed.

title: Automated Speed Enforcement Program
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Stephen Holyday (Ward 2, Etobicoke Centre) is asking City staff for details on the Automated Speed Enforcement program from January 20, 2025 to present — including the number and cost of screening services and hearing reviews for speed-camera penalty disputes, and the breakdown of dispute outcomes.

title: 502 to 508 Parliament Street Construction Delays
topics: construction; building
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Chris Moise (Ward 13, Toronto Centre) is asking City staff for an update on delays and cost escalation for the affordable rental units under construction at 502 to 508 Parliament Street. Council approved $6,000,000 in Section 37 funding for Dixon Hall toward the project in June 2020; staff say estimated renovation costs rose from $6.44 million to $13.96 million by December 2024, and the opening moved from the third quarter of 2025 to the first quarter of 2026. The project would add over 40 units with wraparound services under the HousingTO 2020–2030 Action Plan.

title: Harbord/Hoskin Reconstruction
topics: road reconstruction; road alterations; road narrowing; road widening
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Dianne Saxe (Ward 11, University–Rosedale) is asking City staff for information about road construction delays on Harbord and Hoskin Streets, where watermain replacement finished in 2024 but the same road was dug up again for reconstruction through most of 2025. The inquiry raises resident concerns about prolonged closures, dust, noise, parking restrictions, and gaps in contractor presence.

title: Review and Renewal of Technology Maintenance Contracts for Sustainment of City Services from 2026 - 2030
topics: contracts, infrastructure, maintenance, purchasing, science & technology (sc); acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: On the agenda at City Council: renegotiating and renewing 219 technology maintenance contracts non-competitively for 2026 to 2030, since the exclusive-rights suppliers are the only ones who can maintain the city's existing systems. The contracts cover updates, backups, support and cybersecurity and privacy compliance for city technology infrastructure. The source documents list $14.56 million, $500,000, $226,894,541, $230,887,885, $16,750,326 and $17,045,132. City Council decides.

title: Administrative Penalty Tribunal Chair's 2024 Annual Report
topics: administration, hearings, parking, penalties;
brief: The Chair of the Administrative Penalty Tribunal is presenting the tribunal's 2024 annual report to City Council. The tribunal's 25 hearing officers give parking violation disputes a second, independent review after screening, with final decisions that cannot be further appealed. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Status of Outstanding Payments in Lieu of Tax Amounts for Federal, Provincial and Municipal Properties
topics: finance (sc), municipal services, payment, property (sc), taxes; city services, levies, paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments
brief: Staff are reporting to City Council on outstanding payments in lieu of taxes owed by federal, provincial and municipal properties: $1,188,452 remained outstanding as at July 31, 2025 for the 2024 tax year. These are voluntary payments governments make to compensate the city for services to their properties, and most agencies pay in full. Council receives the annual status update for information.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - State of Good Repair Program
topics: carparks, parking, parking facilities; car parks; car-parks; city parking lots; municipal parking lots; parking lots; public parking
brief: The Toronto Parking Authority's board is recommending that City Council receive its state-of-good-repair strategy and capital plan overview, covering 2024 performance and the forward plan for 2025 and beyond. The authority describes a long-term approach integrating asset management, state-of-good-repair and risk management for its parking infrastructure. The source documents list $280 million, $20.17 million, $15.38 million, $12.6 million, $128 million and $152 million. City Council decides.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests near St. Clair West Station for the Fire Ventilation Upgrade Project - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, land acquisition, properties (real estate), subway stations; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions, property; real estate, ttc
brief: Whether to approve the second stage of expropriating permanent and temporary easements at 396 St. Clair Avenue West to build a permanent fire ventilation storage room at St. Clair West Station, part of the TTC's fire ventilation upgrade project is before City Council. City Council decides.

title: 4913 Bathurst Street - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by the Toronto Public Library as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: libraries, library branches, municipal facilities, property (sc), taxes; branches, city facilities; municipal buildings, levies
brief: Designating about 1,622 square feet at 4913 Bathurst Street as a municipal capital facility, giving it exemptions from municipal and education taxes goes to City Council for approval. The space will temporarily house the Toronto Public Library's Centennial Branch while its home at 578 Finch Avenue West undergoes construction. City Council decides.

title: 115 Broadway Avenue - Below Market Sublease Agreement with Macaulay Centres for Children For Child Care Services
topics: child care, child care facilities, community & life (sc), leasing, properties (real estate); child care agencies; child care centres; day cares; day nurseries; home care agencies; home child care providers; nursery schools, childcare, leases, property; real estate
brief: Approval of a ten-year nominal sublease with Macaulay Centres for Children for a new child care centre on the ground floor at 115 Broadway Avenue, with occupancy expected in the first quarter of 2026 is before City Council. The city itself will hold a 99-year head lease with the developer for the space, and the operator was chosen through a Children's Services expression-of-interest process. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Vermeer Canada Incorporated for the Provision of Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Service for Parks and Recreation
topics: agreements, contracts, parks, repairs; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, tenancy agreements
brief: On the agenda at City Council: approving a non-competitive contract with Vermeer Canada, the only authorized Ontario dealer for proprietary Vermeer chipper, stumper and skid steer parts and service, at $30,009 ($30,528 net of HST recoveries) for one year from October 23, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with four optional one-year extensions. If all extensions are used, the potential total is $194,408 ($197,830 net of HST recoveries). The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Ontario Medical Supply Inc., for the Supply and Delivery of Pharmaceuticals for Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: contracts, emergency medical services, paramedics, suppliers; ems
brief: Up for approval at City Council: a non-competitive one-year contract with Ontario Medical Supply Inc. at $1,500,000 ($1,526,400 net of HST recoveries) from November 1, 2025 to October 31, 2026 for pharmaceuticals for Toronto Paramedic Services, with no optional extensions. The existing blanket contract's final option period expires October 31, 2025 and paramedics still need the supply. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6053584 to Crestline Coach Ltd., for the Provision of a Ministry of Health Certified Multi-Patient Ambulance for Toronto Paramedic Services
topics: ambulances, city vehicles, emergency medical services, paramedics, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet, ems
brief: Up for approval at City Council: amending and extending the non-competitive Crestline Coach purchase order for Ministry of Health certified multi-patient ambulances, adding $2,406,813 ($2,449,173 net of HST recoveries) to raise it from $685,105 ($697,163 net of HST recoveries) to $3,091,918 ($3,146,336 net of HST recoveries) The expiry would move from March 31, 2026 to December 31, 2027, covering higher unit prices from changed chassis requirements, project delays and inflation. City Council decides.

title: 2024 Write-off of Uncollectible Property Taxes and Accounts Receivable
topics: assessment, finance (sc), financial write-offs, property taxes, taxes; financial write offs, levies, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: Writing off uncollectible property taxes and receivables from 2024: 13 property tax accounts with 118 receivable amounts totalling $824,656, covering tax years 1989 to 2024, recommended because the amounts are off the assessment roll or further collection is extremely unlikely goes to City Council for approval. The source documents also list $1,893,544 and $3,492,998.47. City Council decides.

title: 875 The Queensway - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300)
topics: [attributes in environment], noise; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise
brief: The lands at 875 The Queensway would be designated a Class 4 Noise Area under the province's NPC-300 noise guidelines, addressing noise impacts on the site from surrounding commercial and industrial uses. City Council decides on the classification. The designation matters for what gets built there and what noise protections future residents can expect.

title: 564-580 Evans Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Adding a Holding Provision
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a procedural item: for the approved development at 564-580 Evans Avenue, a 9-storey seniors' residence, two blocks of 3-storey townhouses and four towers of 21 to 38 storeys, staff recommend moving an outstanding pre-enactment condition into a holding provision on the zoning by-law. The applicant has consented. City Council decides.

title: 2335 St. Clair Avenue West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision - Approval
topics: [buildings by function], [buildings by height], residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: An 11-storey residential building with 72 homes and 16 parking spaces is proposed for 2335 St. Clair Avenue West, with a six-storey streetwall and stepbacks at the upper levels. City Council decides on the zoning amendment.

title: 87 Ethel Avenue and 2595 St. Clair Avenue West - Fee Removal for Lifting of Hold Applications
topics: applications, fees; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, application process
brief: The item asks that application fees be waived for lifting holding provisions at 87 Ethel Avenue and 2595 St. Clair Avenue West, two Ward 5 sites approved for nearly 2,000 new homes including 141 affordable units. Holding provisions had been used to bring the zoning by-laws to Council quickly, and staff have been working to speed up approvals for more housing. City Council decides on the fee waiver request.

title: Lane Designation - Kipling Avenue at Steeles Avenue West
topics: lanes; traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: The easterly northbound curb lane on Kipling Avenue, from Steeles Avenue West to a point 30.5 metres south, would be designated for northbound right turns only, buses excepted, to define lane use clearly and reduce vehicle conflicts. City Council decides, since the TTC operates transit service on Kipling Avenue.

title: 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The 39-storey, 490-home proposal for 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West is back as an appeal report: City Council is being asked to set its position on the Official Plan and zoning amendments for the mixed-use tower with 14 rental replacement units and ground-floor commercial space. The appeal itself will be decided by the provincial tribunal.

title: Transferring Secretary Role for Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal and Property Standards Committee to Court Services
topics: appointments, courts, special purpose bodies; abccs; abcds; agencies; boards; commissions; committees of management; local boards
brief: Two city tribunals are changing administrators. Council is asked to move the secretary role for the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal and the Property Standards Committee from the City Clerk to Court Services starting January 1, 2026, along with two staff positions and $0.209 million gross ($0.169 million net) in budget funding, consolidating responsibility for most city tribunals within Court Services.

title: Western Beaches Breakwaters Action Plan Progress Update
topics: beaches, structures, water;
brief: Repairs to the western beaches breakwaters are being planned. Council is asked to have staff work with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority on repair recommendations and funding needs for high-risk breakwaters along the western beaches, from the Humber River to Ontario Place, with a report back in spring 2026. Staff will bring a separate 2026 report on the broader dock walls work across the waterfront.

title: Toronto Water 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: capital budgets, projects, water;
brief: Toronto Water's capital budget and 10-year plan would shift money between projects: $38.7 million in project timing shifts and $7.9 million from under-budget or finished projects to ones needing more, with no change to the overall budget. Council is asked to approve.

title: Deferred Revenue (Obligatory Reserve Funds), Reserves and Discretionary Reserve Funds as at June 30, 2025
topics: financial reports, reserve funds, revenue generation; annual financial reports; financial statements, reserves and reserve funds, revenue tools
brief: Reserve fund balances get their mid-year review. Council is asked to move $8 million from the waste management reserve to the Green Lane landfill reserve for its capital and operating needs, and about $80.1 million into a reserve that steadies land transfer tax revenue in slow real estate markets.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Six Months Ended June 30, 2025
topics: annual reports, financial reports, operating budgets; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards, annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to approve amendments to the 2025 operating budget that do not change the net budget, and to amend employee and elected-official benefit plans for those retiring on or after November 1, 2025. The variance report covers the six months ended June 30, 2025, with year-end projections, citing figures of $31.7 million, $105.4 million, $19.0 million and $44.4 million.
