title: 134 Carlton Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board recommends that City Council state its intention to designate 134 Carlton Street, between Homewood Avenue and Jarvis Street in the Cabbagetown-South St. Jamestown neighbourhood, under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Starting the designation process would limit future demolition and alterations to the property.

title: Proposed 2026 Meeting Schedule for Toronto Preservation Board
topics: meetings, schedules; project schedules; scheduling; timing
brief: This is a procedural item: adopting its 2026 meeting schedule, developed with Heritage Planning and the board secretariat, starting Monday, January 19, 2026 at 9:30 a.m., is up for a decision by the Preservation Board.

title: 1151 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board votes on recommending that City Council state its intention to designate 1151 Weston Road, on the northeast corner of Weston Road and Eglinton Avenue West, under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Starting the designation process would limit future demolition and alterations to the property.

title: Selection of Candidates for Interview for the CreateTO Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would select six candidates to interview for appointment to the CreateTO Board, with interviews and a recommendation of two candidates including a chair at its next meeting. Confidential attachments would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Soft Drink Sponsorship Agreement - Coca-Cola Canada
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, sponsorship; corporate sponsorship; sponsorship opportunities, tenancy agreements
brief: Coke could become the exclusive soft drink provider. The Exhibition Place board is asked to request city council approval of a five-year agreement with Coca-Cola Canada Bottling Ltd. as the official and exclusive soft drink provider to the Enercare Centre and Automotive Building, following a public proposal call that closed August 18, 2025.

title: Exhibition Place Management Report - Second Quarter June 30, 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, annual reports; annual financial reports; annual report cards; report cards
brief: This is a procedural item: the Chief Executive Officer's second quarter 2025 management report, with graphs and tables on key information, is provided to the board. The board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Multi-year Agreement with a Consumer Show Client 1
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements; tenancy agreements
brief: A first consumer show client deal is also on the agenda. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve multi-year licence agreements with a first consumer show client for the Enercare Centre, for a three-year term from 2026 to 2028, with the financial details kept confidential.

title: Multi-year Agreement with Consumer Show Client 2
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements; tenancy agreements
brief: Another multi-year show deal is before the board. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve multi-year licence agreements with a second consumer show client for the Enercare Centre, for a three-year term from 2026 to 2028, with the financial details kept confidential.

title: Response to Demonstrations Policy
topics: Exhibition Place, policies and procedures, protests; demonstrations; protest marches, guidelines; policies
brief: Exhibition Place is writing its own demonstrations policy. The board is asked to approve its Response to Demonstrations Policy, developed to align with city council's Policy Framework for City Response to Demonstrations adopted in December 2024, which directed all city agencies to develop their own aligned policies and procedures.

title: Business Travel GSX - Global Security Exchange Conference
topics: Exhibition Place, business travel (municipal), expenses, travel; conference travel; seminar travel, corporate travel
brief: A security manager could head to a security conference. The Exhibition Place board is asked to authorize travel expenses of up to $5,100 plus HST for Vasilis Androutsos, Security Manager, to attend the Global Security Exchange conference hosted by ASIS International in New Orleans from September 26 to October 1, 2025, covering flights, accommodation, and incidentals.

title: Lighting Upgrade at the Princes' Gates and Automotive Building
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, maintenance;
brief: New lighting is going up at the Princes' Gates and Automotive Building. The Exhibition Place board is asked to concur with the earlier approval of a $341,419.00 contract to Rogul Electric Company Limited for the lighting upgrade, awarded to the lowest compliant bidder. The project is time-sensitive because the existing lighting equipment is becoming obsolete with extensive lead times for replacements. The report also cites a $30,000.00 figure.

title: Agreement with the Festival Management Corporation for the Toronto Caribbean Carnival 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, tenancy agreements
brief: The Caribbean Carnival Grand Parade is locked in. The Exhibition Place board is asked to concur with the earlier approval of a one-year agreement with the Festival Management Corporation for the Toronto Caribbean Carnival Grand Parade on August 2, 2025, on the same terms and conditions as 2024.

title: 2026 Schedule of Meetings
topics: committee meetings, schedules; project schedules; scheduling; timing
brief: This is a procedural item: the Exhibition Place board sets its 2026 schedule of regular meetings, developed to avoid conflicts with the city council schedule and days of cultural or religious significance. No policy change is proposed.

title: Community Liaison Meeting - June 17, 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, community outreach, meetings, public meetings; awareness programs; community engagement; outreach; promotion (communication); public outreach
brief: This is a procedural item: staff summarize the Community Liaison Consultation meeting held June 17, 2025, attended by 28 community members in person and virtually, co-hosted by board members Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik and Malcolm Bromley. The board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Billboard Sign New Licence Agreement with Astral Media Outdoor L.P. at Exhibition Place
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, billboards; tenancy agreements
brief: A digital billboard at 2 Strachan Avenue is staying. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve a new agreement with Astral Media Outdoor L.P., a division of Bell Media, to continue operating the existing outdoor digital billboard just south of the Gardiner Expressway for a term of four years, two months and fifteen days. The previous agreement expired June 30, 2025.

title: Exhibition Place Financial Report - Second Quarter June 30, 2025
topics: Exhibition Place, financial reports; annual financial reports; financial statements
brief: This is a procedural item: staff report a full financial summary of all Exhibition Place program areas for the second quarter ending June 30, 2025. The board is asked to receive the report for information and to keep Confidential Attachment 1 confidential, since it contains financial information belonging to the board with monetary value.

title: Agreement for the Provision of Electrical and Mechanical Show Services for Events and Exhibitor Administrative Services at Exhibition Place
topics: Exhibition Place, agreements, festivals and special events, services; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, tenancy agreements
brief: ShowTech Power and Lighting could become the exclusive electrical and mechanical show services provider. The Exhibition Place board is asked to request city council approval of a five-year agreement starting September 15, 2025, with a possible two-year extension, after ShowTech was recommended following a Request for Proposal that drew three proponents.

title: Coliseum Complex Walkways, Driveways, and Masonry Rehabilitation
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, maintenance, restoration; rehabilitation (property)
brief: Walkways and masonry at the Coliseum Complex need repair. The Exhibition Place board is asked to concur with the earlier approval of an $883,000.00 contract to Clifford Restoration Limited for walkway, driveway, and masonry rehabilitation, awarded to the lowest compliant bidder. The project is time-sensitive because exterior site works must be completed in the summer and fall. The report also cites a $65,000.00 figure.

title: Introduction of By-laws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Debenture Committee is asked to introduce a general bill and a confirming bill, the formal step that turns its approved decisions into official bylaws. No new policy is proposed.

title: Authority to Issue a Debenture
topics: bonds, finance (sc); debentures; notes
brief: The city is borrowing $200 million through a green bond whose proceeds fund environmentally beneficial projects. The Debenture Committee is asked to approve issuing a 10-year sinking fund green debenture for $200 million and enact the borrowing bylaw to give it effect. The debenture was arranged on September 9, 2025 and delivered to investors on September 25, 2025.

title: Award of Request for Tender Doc5122222325 to Black & McDonald Limited for the Installation of a Standby Generator for Critical Loads at the R.C. Harris Water Treatment Plant, and POA to 6055119 with Arcadis Professional Service (Canada) Inc. for Contract Administration and Post-Construction Services
topics: construction, contracts, purchasing, water treatment plants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, building, filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities
brief: The General Government Committee faces a decision on awarding Black & McDonald a $5,364,167 contract ($5,458,576 net of HST recoveries) to install a standby generator for critical loads at the R.C. Harris Water Treatment Plant, and to add $669,076 ($680,852 net of HST recoveries) to the Arcadis contract administration purchase order, raising it from $365,751 ($372,188 net of HST recoveries) to $1,034,827 ($1,053,040 net of HST recoveries) with delivery extended to December 31, 2029. The committee decides.

title: Award of Doc5092797820 to 671860 Ontario Inc., Operating as Somerville Construction for David Crombie Park Improvements and The Esplanade - Mill Street Connection Project for Parks and Recreation and Transportation Services
topics: community & life (sc), contracts, parks, parks and open space areas, projects, transportation projects; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, green spaces; open spaces
brief: Up for approval at the General Government Committee: awarding a $26,604,666 contract ($27,072,908 net of HST recoveries) to Somerville Construction for the David Crombie Park improvements and the Esplanade-Mill Street cycling connection, running to October 31, 2028. The project covers the multi-block park plus streetscape, road safety and cycling upgrades along The Esplanade. The committee decides on the award.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order Number 6053569 with Xylem Canada LP for Equipment and Services for the Integrated Pumping Station at Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant
topics: contracts, infrastructure, municipal facilities, purchasing, water treatment plants; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city facilities; municipal buildings, filtration plants; water filtration plants; water treatment and supply plants; water treatment facilities
brief: Adding $25,536,656 ($25,986,102 net of HST recoveries) to the Xylem Canada purchase order for equipment and services for the integrated pumping station at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant, raising it from $71,178,263 ($72,431,000 net of HST recoveries) to $96,714,919 ($98,417,102 net of HST recoveries) goes to the General Government Committee for approval. The increase reflects higher equipment costs from inflation since the 2021 proposal, as allowed under the contract's price escalation clause. The committee decides.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract Number 47025181 with Zamboni Company Ltd., for an Additional Fifty-Three Electric Ice Rink Resurfacers
topics: arenas, city vehicles, contracts, ice rinks; airs (rinks); civic centre ice rinks; hockey rinks; ice pads; ice surfaces; natural ice rinks; nirs; rinks; skating rinks, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet, indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: The General Government Committee faces a decision on amending the Zamboni blanket contract so Fleet Services can buy 53 more electric ice rink resurfacers, adding $9,444,987 ($9,611,219 net of HST recoveries) to raise the contract from $6,252,004 ($6,362,039 net of HST recoveries) to $15,696,991 ($15,973,258 net of HST recoveries). The purchase replaces aging machines, cuts the state-of-good-repair backlog and advances the city's zero-emission fleet targets; Zamboni builds the machines in Brantford, Ontario. The committee decides.

title: Amendment to Blanket Contract Number 47023252 with Toronto Star for the Placement of Legal and Statutory Notices for Strategic Public and Employee Communications
topics: advertising, contracts, external services, information & communication (sc); consultants; consulting services; professional services
brief: The General Government Committee faces a decision on adding $190,000 ($193,344 net of HST recoveries) to the Toronto Star blanket contract for publishing the city's statutory legal notices, raising it from $2,254,247 ($2,293,922 net of HST recoveries) to $2,444,247 ($2,487,266 net of HST recoveries). Provincial law requires these notices to run in daily English-language newspapers with home delivery, and no other publication bid for the work. The committee decides.

title: Expanding Health Benefits for Toronto City Staff
topics: benefits, employees, employment & labour (sc), health, unions; health coverage, labour unions; trade unions, staff
brief: Staff are updating the General Government Committee on adding gender-affirming care to the city's employee health benefits, following Council's March 2024 direction to review options for covering care not covered by OHIP and report back by the third quarter of 2025. The report goes to both this committee and the 2SLGBTQ+ advisory committee. The committee receives it for information.

title: Environmentally Responsible Procurement Update
topics: city initiatives, environmental policies, environmental projects, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, environmental policy; environmental standards; sewer use bylaws
brief: Purchasing staff are updating the General Government Committee on work to align city procurement with the TransformTO Net Zero Strategy, covering climate-friendly and resource-efficient purchasing projects and next steps. The update was postponed from the first to the third quarter of 2025 to advance key projects. The committee receives it for information.

title: Nominal Sublicence Agreement with Foodshare Toronto for Use of a Portion of the East Flemingdon Park Hydro Corridor as a Community Garden
topics: agreements, city-owned properties, community & life (sc), community gardens, gardens; city owned properties; city properties, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council faces a decision on approving a nominal five-year sublicense, with an option for five more years, letting FoodShare Toronto keep operating and potentially expand its urban farm on up to 0.874 acres of the East Flemingdon Park Hydro Corridor at 150 Grenoble Drive. FoodShare has farmed the land since 2021 under the city's community gardens program, serving the Flemingdon Park neighbourhood. City Council decides.

title: Introduction of By-laws
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will introduce the bills needed to give legal effect to the decisions made at this meeting. No policy change is proposed.

title: Ontario Place Event Traffic Management Strategy
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: arts and culture, concerts, transportation; transportation services
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council requests a traffic management strategy for event pick-up and drop-off around Ontario Place and the Budweiser Stage. Concert crowds, with over 70 events scheduled in 2025, cause congestion and unsafe conditions on Lake Shore Boulevard West as rideshares stop in curb lanes. Staff would work with Live Nation, Ontario Place, Exhibition Place, licensing staff and police, test measures through the rest of the 2025 season, and report back before the 2026 season.

title: Speed Humps and Safety Improvements - Benlamond Avenue (Between Main Street and Norwood Road)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Ordering staff to prepare drawings and recommendations for speed humps on Benlamond Avenue between Main Street and Norwood Road, for the October 22, 2025 meeting would get the Toronto and East York Community Council's approval. Residents petitioned for the humps in January 2025 over pedestrian safety, after an earlier direction to staff was not completed. Staff would also study interim safety improvements at the Benlamond Avenue and Norwood Road/Glen Oak Drive intersection for 2026.

title: 61-75 Brownlow Avenue - Residential Demolition Applications
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council has the final say on whether eight townhouses at 61-75 Brownlow Avenue can be demolished before permits for replacement buildings are issued. The owner asked to tear them down early; staff present three options: refuse the demolition, approve it outright, or approve it with conditions. The decision determines whether the lots can sit empty with no approved rebuild.

title: Speed Humps on Pape Avenue between Gerrard Street East and Austin Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: security, speed humps, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install three speed humps on Pape Avenue between Gerrard Street East and Austin Avenue. Residents raised speeding concerns in the Metrolinx Ontario Line work zone, where construction has pushed up traffic volumes, and a community ballot showed strong support for the humps. The humps aim to slow traffic while the transit construction continues.

title: Electric Vehicle Charging Stations in East York
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: energy efficiency, energy infrastructure, transit vehicles; alternative energy; electricity usage; energy use; sustainable energy, hydro property
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will ask city staff to work with the Toronto Parking Authority and report back with recommended locations for electric vehicle chargers in East York. Residents say many East York homes lack accessible charging, and the focus would be the high-traffic area near Coxwell Avenue and Mortimer Avenue, close to schools, a community centre and a hospital.

title: Lennox Street Two - Way
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic regulations, transportation; transportation services
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will direct staff to evaluate reopening the one-way eastbound block of Lennox Street, between Markham Street and Palmerston Boulevard, to two-way traffic, and to report back in the first quarter of 2026. Area residents requested the change to ease congestion at Lennox and Markham and to avoid funnelling traffic through the pedestrian-priority Mirvish Village retail area on Markham Street.

title: Exclusion of Mirvish Village Development from On-street Residential Permit Parking
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: on-street parking, permit parking, residential properties; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits, residential real estate
brief: Ordering a staff study on excluding the Mirvish Village development at Bathurst and Bloor from the on-street residential permit parking program is up for a decision by the Toronto and East York Community Council. The development holds about 890 homes plus shops, and the original zoning deal expected tenants to use its underground parking; with no exclusion in place, tenants have begun applying for on-street permits even though underground space sits empty. The study would cover 569 and 571 Bloor Street West, 625 and 601 Markham Street, and 762, 760 and 748 Bathurst Street.

title: Elm Avenue Traffic Calming
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install three speed humps on Elm Avenue between Mount Pleasant Road and Sherbourne Street North, and to study expanded no-stopping and no-parking hours near Branksome Hall school. The school's traffic consultant recommended calming measures and a traffic light at Elm and Sherbourne, but most neighbours opposed the light and asked for speed humps and expanded stopping bans instead. The humps aim to ease heavy drop-off and pick-up traffic that has grown with nearby construction and cut-through driving.

title: Improving Parking Availability on Concord Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on parking changes for Concord Avenue between Dupont Street and Hallam Street. Residents petitioned to cut the maximum parking time from 3 hours to 1 hour during non-permit hours, saying visitors to nearby businesses park for many hours and leave no spaces for residents coming home. The change would turn over visitor spaces while keeping parking available for residents.

title: Extending Traffic Calming Measures on Public Laneways near Bloor Street West and Gladstone Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming, traffic calming measures; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to add speed humps to public laneways near Bloor Street West and Gladstone Avenue. After a neighbourhood walk with residents, the local councillor found large sections of the laneways lacked enough traffic calming, with speeding and cut-through driving behind homes and along routes used by families and cyclists heading to Dufferin station. The humps would go in the lane north of Bloor Street West east of Dufferin, and in the lane north of Bloor Street West west of Bartlett Avenue.

title: Charles Street West Two-Way
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic direction, transportation; one way operations; one way streets; one way traffic; two way operations; two way streets; two way traffic, transportation services
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will direct staff to evaluate reopening the one-way westbound block of Charles Street West, between Yonge and Balmuto streets, to two-way traffic, and to report back in late 2025 for possible implementation in early 2026. The Bloor Yorkville BIA and the Greater Yorkville Residents' Association have requested the change for over four years to ease congestion at Bloor and Yonge, worsened by long-term construction. A similar 2021 direction to study the change was never acted on.

title: Castle Frank and South Drive Pedestrian Safety
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians, safety, sidewalks; pedestrianization, public safety
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will direct staff to report back in the first quarter of 2026 with recommendations for safe pedestrian access around Castle Frank Road and South Drive. The curving residential streets now carry high-speed cut-through traffic, and there are no traffic lights or marked crosswalks at heavily used spots, including the Craigleigh Gardens entrance, the Milkman's Lane access point, the Elm Avenue intersection, and the building at 36 Castle Frank Road. Speed humps have not slowed the speeding, according to the local councillor.

title: Installation of Speed Bumps in the Public Laneway East of Gladstone Avenue and South of Collahie Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: laneways, speed humps; back alleys; mews, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install speed humps in the public laneway east of Gladstone Avenue, south of Collahie Street, between Cross Street and Collahie Street. The laneway serves Fairview Nursing Home, which houses over 100 long-term care residents, and staff say speeding vehicles have made residents feel unsafe walking there. The humps would slow traffic for residents, families and staff.

title: Installation of Speed Bumps in the Public Laneway South of Corby Avenue and West of Caledonia Road
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: laneways, speed humps; back alleys; mews, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install speed bumps in the public laneway south of Corby Avenue, west of Caledonia Road, between Gilbert Avenue and Caledonia Road. The laneway is heavily used by parents and children at F.H. Miller Junior Public School, whose exit and playground open onto it. Residents and school staff raised concerns about speeding cut-through traffic, including near misses with students.

title: Cross Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, transportation; no parking, transportation services
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on parking changes for Cross Street, a small residential street near Dundas Street West and Gladstone Avenue. The changes would remove the Thursday side-switching rule, fix parking on the north side where there are more spaces, and expand permit parking hours. Residents surveyed supported the changes, which aim to end conflicts over the few available visitor spaces.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item TE24.61, Brock Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, transportation; transportation services
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will reopen its July 2025 decision on Brock Avenue parking amendments to fix a technical wording error. The corrected wording would keep overnight permit parking on the west side of Brock Avenue between Bloor Street West and Wallace Avenue, from 12:01 a.m. to 7 a.m. daily. The substance of the original decision, which removed switchover parking days, does not change.

title: Appointment of New Board Members of the Ralph Thornton Community Centre
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management, public appointments; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint three new members to the Ralph Thornton Community Centre Board of Management, for terms ending June 30, 2028. The appointees are Allison Macdonald-Buchanan, Amanda Munday and Brittany Rodrigues, replacing Maggi Redmonds and Hongmei Cai, who did not stand for re-election.

title: Appointment of Community Members to the Eastview Neighbourhood Community Centre Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, boards of management, community centres; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint and reappoint six community members to the Eastview Neighbourhood Community Centre Board of Management, for terms ending June 30, 2027. Gillian Grant would be newly appointed, while Rebecca Heersink, Abas Barra, Rob MacKinnon, Andrea Nameth and Courtney Fitton would be reappointed.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the McCormick Playground Arena Board
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: board members, members, playgrounds; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, memberships
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint Philip Roe as a public member of the McCormick Playground Arena Board, for a term ending July 10, 2029. Candidate details in a confidential attachment would stay private.

title: Cedarcrest Boulevard - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install seven speed humps on Cedarcrest Boulevard between Glencrest Boulevard and Glen Albert Drive. Staff assessed the street against the city's traffic calming policy and found the criteria were met. A by-law to alter the roadway would follow approval.

title: Leroy Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install four speed humps on Leroy Avenue between Sammon Avenue and Mortimer Avenue. Staff assessed the street against the city's traffic calming policy and found the criteria were met. A by-law to alter the roadway would follow approval.

title: Turner Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install four speed humps on Turner Road between Davenport Road and Tyrrel Avenue. Staff assessed the street against the city's traffic calming policy and found the criteria were met. A by-law to alter the roadway would follow approval.

title: Traffic Management in Ward 14 related to the King Street East and Church Street intersection project
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, intersections; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council votes on receiving, for information, a report on traffic management in Ward 14 around the King Street East and Church Street intersection project. The report explains why the TTC track and watermain work was scheduled for 2025 and summarizes ongoing traffic measures for the area between the Don River, Eastern Avenue, Broadview Avenue and Gerrard Street East, including recommendations at Broadview and Dundas. No policy change is proposed.

title: Sherbourne Street North and Elm Avenue/Maple Avenue - Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, ttc
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic signals at Sherbourne Street North and Elm Avenue/Maple Avenue, replacing the existing all-way stop. To make the signals work safely at the complex intersection, northbound right turns on red from Sherbourne Street North to Elm Avenue would be banned at all times, and Maple Avenue would become one-way eastbound between Sherbourne Street North and Glen Road. Council approval is required because the TTC operates transit on these streets.

title: Compulsory Stop Controls - Various Intersections in Ward 4
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: intersections, safety; public safety
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install stop signs at five currently uncontrolled T-intersections in Ward 4, on Beresford, Lincoln, Mapleview and Herman avenues. The locations are southbound Beresford at MacGregor, westbound Lincoln at Beresford, northbound Mapleview at Lincoln, southbound Mapleview at MacGregor, and eastbound Herman at Ritchie. Staff say the signs would clarify right-of-way and improve safety for all road users.

title: Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking - Permit Area 9A Thyra Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking regulations, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to introduce overnight permit parking on the west side of Thyra Avenue, between Danforth Avenue and Dentonia Park Avenue, from 12:01 a.m. to 7 a.m. daily within Permit Parking Area 9A. The change would replace the current alternating monthly no-parking rules that force residents to switch sides of the street. Residents requested the change to meet their long-term parking needs.

title: Melinda Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: local roads, parking prohibitions; no parking
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to upgrade the existing no-parking rule to a stricter no-standing ban on the north side of Melinda Street, between Yonge Street and a point 35 metres west. The change would keep the roadway clear in front of the One King West Hotel and Residence entrance. Standing bans prohibit even brief stops, unlike parking bans.

title: Howard Street and Redrocket Lane - Traffic and Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide on traffic and parking amendments on Howard Street and Redrocket Lane required by the site plan agreement for a new development at 603-611 Sherbourne Street and 4-6 Howard Street. The changes include new all-times stopping bans and peak-hour parking bans on the south side of Howard Street. The staff report lists parking rates of $3.00 and $2.00 in the affected regulations.

title: Earlscourt Avenue - Accessible Loading Zone
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessible permit parking, parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled)
brief: The Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to create an accessible loading zone on the east side of Earlscourt Avenue between Hope Street and Ascot Avenue, operating 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. The zone would give TTC Wheel-Trans users unimpeded curbside access. Staff also found mismatches between the parking by-law and the posted signs on the street, and recommend fixing them.

title: Pay-and-Display and On-Street Residential Permit Parking - Dovercourt Road - September 2025 (Delegated)

topics: Toronto Transit Commission; ttc
brief: Chair Jamaal Myers is asking the TTC Board to let TTC staff work with Municipal Licensing and Standards on whether a centralized on-demand accessible taxi dispatch service could run through the existing Wheel-Trans service. Six bids were received: $1,514,000.00 from Midome Construction Services Ltd., $1,656,325.00 from Gio Contracting Inc., $1,798,000.00 from 2489960 Ontario Inc., $1,816,325.00 from Sanscon Construction Limited, $2,184,819.00 from Gio-Crete Construction Ltd., and $2,548,060.00 from CRCE Construction Ltd. (found non-compliant). The contract runs from the award date through October 31, 2025.

title: City Manager’s Office Staff Update on Action Items and Agenda Planning
topics: planning;
brief: This is a procedural item: staff will update the committee on action items in progress, and members will discuss topics for upcoming meetings. No policy decision is involved.

title: Changes Impacting Access to Social Infrastructure
topics: planning;
brief: A staff presentation will cover changes affecting how people access social infrastructure — community supports and services — including the city's plan for communicating those changes to the public. No decision is proposed.

title: East Bayfront Community Recreation Centre Indigenous Naming
topics: recreation centres; rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: Staff will present a status update on the process to give the East Bayfront Community Recreation Centre an Indigenous name, including the engagement plan, project timelines and background. No decision is requested at this meeting.

title: Update Downsview Project: Overview and Urban Indigenous Engagement
topics: planning;
brief: Staff will give an overview of the Downsview redevelopment project and share the urban Indigenous engagement plan, which includes setting up a Downsview Indigenous Community Resource Group and hosting Indigenous Sharing Meetings. This is an information item; no decision is requested.

title: 1675 and 1685 Eglinton Avenue West - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve demolishing 75 rental homes at 1675 and 1685 Eglinton Avenue West so a 37-storey building with 424 units, including 75 replacement rental homes, can be built on the site. Approval would come with conditions, including a tenant assistance plan giving existing tenants the right to return at similar rents plus financial compensation. If the owner fails to finish the new building on time, a $20,000.00 charge per demolished unit would be added to the property tax bill as a lien on the land. The related zoning application for the new building is being considered at the same time.

title: Parking Amendments - Carlaw Avenue at Badgerow Avenue (Pape Avenue Junior Public School and Pape Children’s House)
topics: parking, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: City Council will decide whether to create a temporary school bus loading zone on the east side of Carlaw Avenue at Badgerow Avenue, in effect 7:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. on weekdays from September 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027. The zone would serve three buses for Pape Avenue Junior Public School and Pape Children's House, which the school board temporarily relocated to 540 Jones Avenue because of Ontario Line construction at Pape and Langley. Council would also rescind the existing $3.00 per hour, three-hour-maximum parking machine regulation on that stretch for the same period.

title: Designating a Portion of Fort York Boulevard as a Community Safety Zone
topics: community safety, pedestrians; pedestrianization
brief: Drivers speeding on Fort York Boulevard between Spadina Avenue and Dan Leckie Way could face higher fines if City Council designates the stretch a Community Safety Zone, in effect at all times on both sides of the road. The corridor sees heavy foot traffic, including school-age children travelling to Jean Lumb Public School, Bishop Macdonnell Catholic School and a child care centre, and vehicles often exceed the posted 30 km/h limit. The designation would raise speeding fines as part of the city's Vision Zero road safety plan.

title: 1675 and 1685 Eglinton Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 37-storey mixed-use building with 424 homes, including 75 replacement rental units, is proposed for 1675 and 1685 Eglinton Avenue West, and City Council will decide whether to approve the Official Plan and zoning changes. The 123.5-metre building would hold 26,600 square metres of space with ground-floor shops, 482 bicycle and 91 vehicle parking spaces, and a land dedication for a future public laneway. A separate rental demolition application covers the 75 existing rental homes, with a tenant assistance plan for current residents. The staff report also references amounts of $538 and $1,076.

title: Assumption of Services from Toronto Community Housing Corporation, 66M-2491, Regent Park Phase 2
topics: by-laws, roads; bylaws, circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads)
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council formally takes over the roads and municipal services built in Regent Park Phase 2 (registered plan 66M-2491) from Toronto Community Housing Corporation. The move would release the performance guarantee held under the 2011 subdivision agreement, authorize an assumption by-law for the public highway, and transfer the street lighting system to Toronto Hydro. It shifts long-term maintenance of the new neighbourhood's streets from the housing corporation to the city.

title: 931 Kingston Road - Accessible Loading Zone
topics: accessibility, loading zones; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: An accessible loading zone is proposed on the south side of Kingston Road near Silver Birch Avenue, operating 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. on weekdays, for staff with accessibility needs at a local business. Full council approval is requested.

title: Traffic and Parking Non-Delegated By-Law Changes for the 2025 Canadian National Exhibition  (Non-Delegated)
topics: pedestrians, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, pedestrianization
brief: Temporary traffic and parking changes are proposed on TTC-served streets near Exhibition Place for the 2025 Canadian National Exhibition, from August 15 to September 1, to improve traffic operations and pedestrian safety. Because the TTC runs transit on the streets, full council approval is required.

title: 2161 Yonge Street - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: The lands at 2161 Yonge Street would be exempted from Part Lot Control for two years, to allow minor property boundary adjustments within the proposed 38-storey mixed-use development. The owner would also register a restriction ensuring no part of the land can be sold or mortgaged without City approval. Approval would enact the exemption by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 126, 128 and 130 Avenue Road - Demolition and New Construction on Designated Heritage Properties Under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: construction, demolitions, heritage properties; building, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Demolishing three 'category X' buildings at 126-130 Avenue Road in the East Annex Heritage Conservation District and approving the design of an 11-storey replacement building go to Council for approval. The district plan allows demolition of 'category X' buildings when the replacement follows its guidelines, and staff say the design wouldn't detract from rated heritage buildings nearby.

title: Temporary Traffic Amendments, Bathurst Street at Lennox Street
topics: parking regulations, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Temporary turn bans are proposed at Bathurst Street and Lennox Street — banning northbound left turns and southbound right turns — to stop illegal traffic entering the one-way section of Markham Street until it reopens. Markham Street has been closed for five years, and drivers turning from Bathurst onto Lennox illegally drive south on the one-way-northbound street. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Ontario Line - Construction Update - Second Quarter 2025
topics: construction, public transit; building, local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to consider the second-quarter 2025 Ontario Line construction update, which was referred from City Council to this meeting. The report covers station work, the four main construction packages, Metrolinx's responses to council's recommendations, building surveys, truck safety and community engagement. No policy change is proposed.

title: Davenport Village Traffic Safety Plan - Left Turns on Foundry Avenue
topics: safety, turn prohibitions (traffic); public safety
brief: Northbound left turns from Foundry Avenue onto Davenport Road would be banned during weekday rush hours — 7-9 a.m. and 3:30-6:30 p.m. — to reduce backups, noise and dangerous intersection movements. Because the TTC runs transit on Davenport, full council approval is required.

title: 126, 128 and 130 Avenue Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: The owner of 126, 128 and 130 Avenue Road wants to demolish 11 rental homes, on the condition the owner provides 11 replacement rental units kept as rentals for at least 20 years, with a tenant assistance plan letting tenants return at similar rents. A related 11-storey, 60-home development is being considered at the same time. If the owner doesn't finish the replacement building on time, the City can charge $20,000.00 per demolished unit, added to the property tax bill as a lien on the land. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Jones Avenue - Temporary Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, ttc
brief: A temporary school bus loading zone is proposed on the west side of Jones Avenue near 540 Jones Avenue, from September 2025 to June 2027, to support the temporary relocation of Pape Avenue Junior Public School and Pape Children's House childcare centre during Ontario Line construction. Because the TTC runs transit on Jones Avenue, full council approval is required.

title: Danforth Avenue - Removal of Taxicab Stand
topics: taxicab stands, taxicabs; cabs; taxi fares; taxis, taxi stands
brief: The taxi stand on the north side of Danforth Avenue west of Woodbine Avenue would be removed so the space can be folded into the existing paid parking area. Because the TTC runs transit on the street, full council approval is required.

title: King Street East - Commercial Loading Zone
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, loading zones; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, ttc
brief: A commercial loading zone is proposed on the south side of King Street East between Trinity Street and Gilead Place, operating at all times except 4-6 p.m. weekday afternoons, to help businesses with loading and unloading. Because the TTC runs transit on King Street East, full council approval is required. The item lists a $3.00 fee.

title: 126 - 130 Avenue Road -  Zoning By-law Amendment, Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: An 11-storey mixed-use building with 60 homes, including 11 rental replacement units, is proposed at 126-130 Avenue Road, with ground-floor retail, an 18-car underground garage and 66 bike spaces. The three existing buildings would be demolished; a related rental demolition application covers the 11 rental homes. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions During King Street West and Dufferin Street Intersection Closure
topics: traffic, transportation; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, transportation services
brief: Temporary transit-priority measures are proposed while the King Street West and Dufferin Street intersection closes for track renewal from September to late 2025, with the 504 King, 508 Lake Shore, 29 Dufferin and 929 Dufferin Express diverted. The measures include new and longer no-stopping zones and new turn restrictions, meant to limit impacts on about 91,000 streetcar and 42,000 bus customers daily. Full council approval is requested.

title: 1134 Queen Street East - Construction Staging Area
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, pedestrian walkways; building, footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways, ttc
brief: A 3-storey condo with ground-floor retail is being built at 1134 Queen Street East, and the developer wants the north sidewalk and part of the westbound curb lane closed for 15 months, from July 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026, as a construction staging area. Pedestrians would use a temporary walkway, with traffic control people directing them during construction hours. Because the TTC runs transit on Queen Street East, full council approval is required. The item lists a $3.00 fee.

title: 53-55 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, road closures, transportation; building, street closures; temporary highway closings, transportation services
brief: Parts of the sidewalk and curb lanes on Yonge Street and Colborne Street would be temporarily closed for 10 months, from July 28, 2025 to May 1, 2026, for demolition of 53-55 Yonge Street ahead of a future development. Pedestrians would be redirected to the opposite sides. Because Yonge Street is a major arterial, full council approval is required.

title: 20-22 Front Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, transportation; building, transportation services
brief: A 51-storey rental building is being built at 20-22 Front Street West, between Bay and Yonge streets, and the developer wants the north sidewalk and part of the westbound curb lane closed for 65 months, from August 1, 2025 to December 31, 2030, as a construction staging area. Pedestrians would use a covered walkway in the closed lane. Because the TTC runs transit on Front Street West, full council approval is required. The item lists a $5.00 fee.

title: 1 Bloor Street West (Yonge Street at Bloor Street West) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction, pedestrians; building, pedestrianization
brief: The developer of the 85-storey residential tower at 1 Bloor Street West wants to temporarily close part of the southbound curb lane on Yonge Street near Bloor from August 2025 to June 2028 as a construction staging area, with a construction hotline and hoarding art requirements. Past approvals ran through March 2023, with extensions since. Because the TTC runs transit on Yonge Street, full council approval is required.

title: 2025 Road Openings and Closures in the Port Lands: Don Roadway and Villiers Street
topics: road closures, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Several road openings and closures are proposed in the Port Lands as flood-protection work continues in 2025: extending the Don Roadway closure to December 31, 2025; opening the rebuilt Don Roadway between Lake Shore Boulevard East and Commissioners Street on the new flood protection landform; permanently closing part of Villiers Street for new parkland; and creating an interim cul-de-sac on Villiers Street. Full council approval is required.

title: 101-105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 50-storey mixed-use building with 452 homes and 127 square metres of retail is proposed at 101-105 Spadina Avenue and 363 Adelaide Street West; the site was previously approved in 2023 for 39 storeys. A 1,000-square-metre city park on the north side of the site and a Toronto Parking Authority facility in the underground garage would stay as planned. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Permanent Closure and Dedication of a portion of the public laneway abutting 1747 and 1753 St. Clair Avenue West
brief: Part of the public laneway behind 1747 and 1753 St. Clair Avenue West would be permanently closed and sold for incorporation into the adjacent development, while another part would be dedicated as public laneway to form a north-south laneway serving the new development. Full council approval is required.

title: 358-360 Dufferin Street (including structure address at 350 Dufferin Street) - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of Designated Heritage Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Alterations and partial demolition of the designated heritage properties at 358-360 Dufferin Street -- part of the Late-Victorian Dominion Radiator industrial complex with buildings adapted by architect E.J. Lennox -- go to Council for approval. The work would allow three mixed-use buildings of 29, 26 and 9 storeys, with a heritage easement agreement for long-term protection.

title: 2 Old George Place - Alterations to a Designated Property in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District - Refusal
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Staff want council to refuse alterations to the designated property at 2 Old George Place in the North Rosedale Heritage Conservation District. The applicant wants to demolish the existing second storey and build a new two-storey addition, but staff say the addition's height, form and materials don't fit the district's plan or heritage-rated buildings. Refusal would be under the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 445, 447, 449 and 451 Adelaide Street West - Demolition and New Construction on Designated Heritage Properties Under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Refusal
topics: construction, demolitions; building
brief: Staff want council to refuse a heritage permit to demolish four designated heritage properties at 445-451 Adelaide Street West — contributing homes in the King-Spadina Heritage Conservation District — to build a new 17-storey hotel and restaurant building. Staff recommend refusal under the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 340-376R Dufferin Street and 2 Melbourne Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Three mixed-use buildings of 29, 26 and 9 storeys with 768 homes are proposed at 340-376R Dufferin Street and 2 Melbourne Avenue, conserving the designated heritage properties at 358-360 Dufferin Street. The 49,173-square-metre project includes shops, a greenhouse and community garden, and a new mid-block courtyard open to the public from Dufferin Street, Melbourne Avenue and Milky Way Lane. Approval would amend the Official Plan and zoning. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 699-707 Yonge Street, 1-17 Hayden Street, and 8 Charles Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Refusal
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Planning staff want council to refuse a zoning change for a 64-storey, 514-home mixed-use tower proposed at 699-707 Yonge Street, 1-17 Hayden Street and 8 Charles Street East. Staff say the tower's massing and setbacks are not acceptable and the project doesn't conserve the cultural heritage value of on-site and adjacent heritage properties. Council would also authorize city lawyers to defend the refusal at the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 462 Wellington Street West - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300)
topics: noise, noise control; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: The lands at 462 Wellington Street West would be classified as a Class 4 noise area under provincial guidelines, which allows higher daytime and night-time sound limits for the residential development there. The higher levels would be offset by noise control measures built into the project. Council would forward the decision to the Ministry of the Environment.

title: 276-294 Main Street - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: exemptions, part lot control; exceptions
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to extend the Part Lot Control exemption at 276-294 Main Street by three more years. The exemption lets the site be divided into four lots and transferred as stratified parcels; the extension allows the remaining transfers to be completed.

topics: rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: An eight- and four-storey modular mass-timber residential building with 64 rental homes, including six affordable units funded through Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, is proposed at 2720-2734 Danforth Avenue, around a central courtyard with a rebuilt two-storey heritage building. No car parking and 50 bike spaces are proposed. Approval would amend the zoning by-law with a holding provision for servicing matters. City Council makes the final decision.

topics: Official Plans, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 63-storey residential building with 590 homes is proposed at 2-12 Cawthra Square, including 14 rental replacement units and 475 square metres of community space intended as a satellite for an existing community centre. The Official Plan change would redesignate the site from Neighbourhoods to Apartment Neighbourhoods to allow the tower. A related rental demolition report is being considered at the same time. City Council makes the final decision.

brief: A 19-storey, 63.4-metre mixed-use building with 228 homes and ground-floor retail is proposed at 21-25 Imperial Street, with two ground-level live-work units. brief: Zoning and plan changes would allow a 39-storey, 129.5-metre mixed-use building with 427 homes at 1711-1741 Eglinton Avenue West, east of Northcliffe Boulevard, including 8 rental replacement units, 116 square metres of shops, 486 bike spaces and 87 vehicle spaces.
