topics: advisory committees, committees of adjustment, public appointments; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, committee of adjustment
brief: This is a procedural item: the Nominating Panel - Committee of Adjustment would recommend one interviewed candidate to City Council for appointment to the Toronto and East York panel of the Committee of Adjustment, replacing a candidate who withdrew on June 23, 2025. The term ends November 14, 2026. Confidential attachments on the candidates would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Establishing a Chief Congestion Officer for the City of Toronto
topics: city initiatives, congestion, transportation infrastructure; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, gridlock, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving a report for information outlining the responsibilities of the new Chief Congestion Officer, a role created in April 2025 to coordinate cross-division work on traffic congestion. The position oversees the Strategic Capital Coordination Office and reports to the Deputy City Manager, Infrastructure Services. No policy change is proposed.

title: Collection Options for District 2 and District Comparative Analysis
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is receiving a report for information noting that staff will report on waste collection options for District 2 at the committee's July 2025 meeting. No policy change is proposed.

title: Coxwell and Danforth Green Space
topics: facility naming, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, park naming
brief: This member motion asks City Council to formally make the green space on the south side of Danforth Avenue between Coxwell and Rhodes avenues a public park with regular upkeep, and to name it Coxwell Commons. The space has been treated and maintained like a park since a 1998 redevelopment but was never formally turned over to the parks department.

title: Highlights of the 2024 Street Needs Assessment and Advancing the City's Shelter Infrastructure
topics: emergency housing, homelessness, infrastructure, services; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)
brief: This is a procedural item: staff report highlights of the 2024 Street Needs Assessment and the city's shelter infrastructure plan, including shelter development projects, and the committee is asked to receive the report for information. The report is part of the council-approved Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy.

title: Yonge Street Tragedy Memorial Park Project Plan in Olive Square Park
topics: memorials, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This is a procedural item: staff report a plan to redesign Olive Square Park as a permanent memorial to the victims of the April 23, 2018 Yonge Street tragedy, through a design competition launching in April 2026. The plan follows council direction to develop the memorial with Parks and Recreation and Economic Development and Culture.

title: Developing Partnerships for Social Medicine / Medically-Supervised Shelter
topics: emergency housing, homelessness; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless)
brief: Whether to explore shelter spaces with medical support is before the committee. The item asks the committee to request that shelter staff, with Humber River Hospital, report back in the fourth quarter of 2025 on options for partnerships with hospitals to create shelter spaces for people leaving health facilities who need health and housing supports. The 2024 Street Needs Assessment found 26 percent of respondents reported an illness or medical condition.

title: Bloor Street Viaduct Bridge Rehabilitation Work - Safety Measures Needed
topics: bridge rehabilitation, safety barriers; bridge reconstruction; bridge repair, suicide barriers
brief: The Bloor Viaduct's suicide prevention barrier is getting attention ahead of rehabilitation work. The item asks that staff include in the September 16 report on the Luminous Veil whether there are any known issues with its functioning as a suicide prevention barrier on the Bloor Viaduct, given planned bridge rehabilitation work.

title: Advancing Action on the Impact to Action: Final Report on Anti-Black Racism in Toronto Police Services - Presentation Requests
topics: police services, racial discrimination, social problems; anti-racism; racism, police; policing
brief: Getting a policing update for the anti-Black racism advisory committee goes to the committee for approval. Following a recommendation from the Confronting Anti-Black Racism Advisory Committee, the item asks the committee to request that Toronto Police Service present to that committee on the status of implementing the Ontario Human Rights Commission recommendations, including completed and pending actions and accountability measures.

title: Award of Doc5177952812 to Vaughan Paving Ltd. for the Construction of Asphalt Speed Humps for Transportation Services
topics: construction, municipal awards, road transportation, speed humps; book awards; civic awards; civilian citations; community service volunteers awards; human rights awards; urban design awards, building, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Asphalt speed humps across Toronto, meant to slow traffic on residential streets, would be built by Vaughan Paving Ltd. under a contract valued at $2,120,800 net ($2,396,504 including HST; $2,158,126 net of HST recoveries) running through December 31, 2025, with one optional renewal year. Four bids were received: $2,050,800.00 from Vaughan Paving Ltd., $2,253,997.80 from PTR Paving Inc., $2,490,040.00 from 7850891 Canada Inc. o/a Egnatia Paving, and $3,395,172.00 from Aqua Tech Solutions Inc. The option year (2026) is valued at $2,181,724 / $2,465,348 / $2,220,122, for a two-year total of $4,302,524 / $4,861,852 / $4,378,248.

title: Award of Doc5163872820 to Aqua Tech Solutions Inc. for Roadway and Roadside General Maintenance for Transportation Services
topics: municipal awards, road transportation; book awards; civic awards; civilian citations; community service volunteers awards; human rights awards; urban design awards
brief: Road and roadside maintenance — roads, sidewalks, curbs, wheelchair ramps — in Wards 20 to 25 would go to Aqua Tech Solutions Inc. under a $776,023 contract ($876,906 including HST; $789,681 net of HST recoveries). Six bids were received: $746,022.90 from Aqua Tech Solutions Inc., $759,795.75 from Maple-Crete Inc., $878,699.28 from 1707219 Ontario Limited o/a Pave Krete Construction, $892,220.50 from PTR Paving Inc., $910,546.39 from RA Crete-Scape Ltd., and $946,130.00 from 7850891 Canada Inc. o/a Egnatia Paving. The contract runs from the award date through December 31, 2025.

title: Award of Doc5110394311 to Mianco Infrastructure Inc. for Excess Soil Removal and Construction of Haulage Road at Highland Creek Treatment Plant for Engineering and Construction Services
topics: construction, municipal awards, removal, soil; book awards; civic awards; civilian citations; community service volunteers awards; human rights awards; urban design awards, building, earth
brief: Excess soil removal and construction of a haulage road at the Highland Creek Treatment Plant would go to Mianco Infrastructure Inc. under a $4,136,050 contract ($4,673,737 including HST; $4,208,844 net of HST recoveries). Seven bids were received: $3,698,000.00 from Mianco Infrastructure Inc., $3,834,000.00 from Rafat General Contractor Inc., $4,730,188.15 from Greenspace Construction Inc., $5,203,440.18 from Tri-Phase Group Inc., $5,835,160.00 from Green Infrastructure Partners Inc., $6,255,354.00 from 614128 Ontario Ltd. o/a Trisan Construction, and $8,111,000.00 from Midome Construction Services Ltd. The contract runs from the award date through December 31, 2026.

title: Introduction of By-laws
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will introduce the bills needed to give legal effect to the decisions made at this meeting. No policy change is proposed.

title: Parking Amendments - Boulton Avenue (Dundas Junior Public School)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Parking rules on Boulton Avenue near Dundas Junior Public School would change under a decision before the Toronto and East York Community Council. Staff recommend shifting the school bus loading zone on the west side of Boulton Avenue, south of Dundas Street East, to run 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. instead of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on school days, plus adjusting short-term parking. The changes respond to safety concerns raised since June 2020 by school staff, the trustee and parents about pick-up and drop-off signage.

title: Elm Street Traffic Safety
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, traffic regulations; public safety
brief: After a year of talks between Branksome Hall school, parents and nearby residents about pick-up and drop-off safety, the Toronto and East York Community Council is being asked to order staff to draw up traffic-calming measures, including speed humps, for Elm Avenue between Mount Pleasant Road and Sherbourne Street North. The recommendations and drawings would come back to the September 18, 2025 meeting. The school and community have already agreed to interim changes, including speed humps, while discussions continue.

title: Exclusion of Galleria Mall from On-Street Residential Permit Parking
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: The question before the Toronto and East York Community Council: whether to order a staff study on whether the Galleria Mall redevelopment site should be excluded from the on-street residential permit parking program. The properties are 1245 Dupont Street, 1260 Dufferin Street, 213 Emerson Avenue and 10 Graphophone Grove. The stated rationale is that excluding new developments from permit parking manages the parking supply and encourages walking, cycling and transit; if adopted, future residents of the site could not buy on-street parking permits.

title: All-Way Compulsory Stop Controls - Leuty Avenue and Alfresco Lawn
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: stop signs; all-way stop controls; technical warrants
brief: Residents near Leuty Avenue and Alfresco Lawn petitioned for four-way stop signs over pedestrian safety concerns, and the Toronto and East York Community Council will decide whether to install them. The local councillor brought the request forward after hearing from residents worried about safety on their street. If approved, all-way compulsory stop controls would be added at the intersection.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Parking Regulations for 2025 Canadian National Exhibition (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Temporary parking changes are proposed on streets near Exhibition Place for the 2025 Canadian National Exhibition, from August 15 to September 1, to improve traffic operations and pedestrian safety. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision on streets without TTC service; a companion item covers TTC-served streets.

title: Appointments to the Community Centre 55 Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management, community centres, public appointments; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint two new members — Natalie Johnson and Pauline Gran — to the Community Centre 55 board for terms ending June 30, 2029. No policy change is proposed.

title: Logan Avenue and Carlaw Avenue Safety Improvements
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, traffic regulations; public safety
brief: Interim safety measures are proposed on Logan and Carlaw avenues after consultation on cycling connections: a four-way stop at Logan and Floyd avenues, a flexible speed sign on Mortimer Avenue, and zebra crosswalk markings at Logan and Floyd. Residents raised concerns about accessibility impacts of proposed contraflow bike lanes, so these measures improve safety while longer-term options are studied. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Re-opening and Amending Tarlton Parking Changes
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: loading zones, parking; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to reopen its June 2025 decision on Tarlton Road parking and add a daily accessible loading zone on the west side of Tarlton Road south of Eglinton Avenue West, so all staff recommendations are carried out.

title: Re-Installing a Traffic Control Personnel at Yonge and Heath Street West
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: pedestrians, traffic, traffic control systems; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, pedestrianization, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: A traffic control officer would be re-installed at Yonge Street and Heath Street West on weekday mornings (7-10 a.m.) and afternoons (3-6 p.m.), to help pedestrians cross safely until the intersection is realigned. The Deer Park community says past installations made crossings feel safer. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: St. George Street - No Standing within the On-Street Logistics Mini-hub Zone
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, tickets; no parking
brief: Standing would be banned at all times on the west side of St. George Street at the on-street logistics mini-hub, so delivery trucks can load and unload without illegally parked vehicles blocking the area. The mini-hub, run by Purolator in a parking lay-by, has had frequent illegal parking. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Advancing Speed Humps on Foxley Street
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Six speed humps are proposed for Foxley Street between Ossington Avenue and Dovercourt Road, after residents raised safety concerns about speeding and traffic near Ossington. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Stonehouse Crescent - Heavy Truck Prohibition
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: traffic, trucks; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: Heavy trucks would be banned on Stonehouse Crescent between Dufferin Street and Gladstone Avenue, except trucks delivering to properties there, after residents reported cut-through trucks blocking the narrow street. Transportation Services confirmed alternative routes exist and traffic flow wouldn't be affected. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Installation of Speed Bumps on Public Laneway West of Perth Avenue and North of Ernest Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: laneways, safety; back alleys; mews, public safety
brief: Speed bumps are proposed for the public laneway west of Perth Avenue north of Ernest Avenue, after a resident-led petition showed strong support for slowing speeding vehicles. The laneway serves a growing neighbourhood near the West Toronto Railpath. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Davenport Village Traffic Safety Plan
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: safety, traffic, traffic calming measures; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, public safety, traffic calming devices; traffic calming methods
brief: A Davenport Village traffic safety plan is proposed, installing speed humps on Powerhouse Street, Foundry Avenue and Brandon Avenue, after residents raised concerns about speeding, near misses and cut-through traffic avoiding Davenport Road. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Brock Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Thursday side-switching rule for permit parking on Brock Avenue between Bloor Street West and Wallace Avenue would be removed, keeping overnight permit parking on one side only. Residents petitioned for the change after frequent tickets and confusion on switchover days. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Biggar Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking bans on Biggar Avenue near Oakwood Avenue and St. Clair Avenue West would be eased, adding on-street parking spaces without affecting traffic flow. Residents say parking on the street is difficult, and Transportation Services found a parking ban could be reduced. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Appointment of Community Members to the Applegrove Community Complex Board of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, board members;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint five community members to the Applegrove Community Complex board — Brian Buchan, David Hoang, Juanita Morris and others — for terms ending June 30, 2027. No policy change is proposed.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the McCormick Playground Arena Board
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: arenas, members; indoor hockey rinks; rinks, memberships
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint four public members to the McCormick Playground Arena board — Christina Lee-Rotstein, Inna Rumiantseva, Monica Reddon and Nicholas Filion — for terms ending July 10, 2029. A confidential attachment with candidate details would stay private. No policy change is proposed.

title: Naming a Path in Honour of Evelyn Green
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parks, street names; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, renaming; road names; street naming
brief: A path in Cedarvale Park would be named 'Evelyn Green Way', honouring a local resident whose family was consulted on the naming. Residents on Arlington applied for the commemorative naming under the City's framework. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Virginia Avenue - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Four speed humps are proposed for Virginia Avenue between Fairside Avenue and Binswood Avenue. Staff say the street meets the City's traffic-calming criteria. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Strathcona Avenue - Temporary Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: permit parking, safety; on-street permit parking; parking permits, public safety
brief: Temporary parking and pick-up/drop-off zones are proposed on Strathcona Avenue between Jones Avenue and Blake Street, from September 2025 to June 2027, to support the temporary relocation of Pape Avenue Junior Public School during Ontario Line construction. The changes include a short-term pick-up and drop-off zone, overnight permit parking adjustments and no-stopping rules. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Sherbourne Street North and Elm Avenue/Maple Avenue - Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, ttc
brief: Traffic signals are proposed at Sherbourne Street North and Elm Avenue/Maple Avenue to improve safety, replacing the existing four-way stop, along with banning northbound right turns on red and making part of Maple Avenue one-way eastbound. Staff say the signals are justified by their assessment. Because the TTC runs transit on the streets, full council approval is required.

title: Somerset Avenue - Accessible Loading Zone Removal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, loading zones, parking prohibitions; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking
brief: The accessible loading zone on the east side of Somerset Avenue north of Geary Avenue would be removed, creating one more on-street parking space, and mismatches between the by-lawed parking rules and posted signs would be fixed. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Shirley Street - Accessible Loading Zone
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, loading zones, parking prohibitions; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking
brief: A new accessible loading zone is proposed on the south side of Shirley Street between St. Clarens and Brock avenues, operating 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, for Wheel-Trans users. Staff also found a mismatch between the by-lawed parking rules and posted signs nearby that would be fixed. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Nairn Avenue - Accessible Loading Zone
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: loading zones, parking prohibitions; drop off areas; drop off zones; loading spaces; pick up areas; pick up zones, no parking
brief: A new accessible loading zone is proposed on the west side of Nairn Avenue between Morrison Avenue and Rogers Road, operating 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekends, for Wheel-Trans users and accessible permit holders visiting The Planting Community Church at 236 Nairn Avenue. Staff also found wording errors in the by-lawed parking rules that would be fixed. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - July 2025 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, parking spaces; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking spots
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will approve the routine monthly list of on-street accessible parking spaces to be added or removed for people with disabilities, as set out in the July 2025 report. No wider policy change is proposed.

title: Traffic Management in Ward 14 related to the King Street East and Church Street intersection project
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, intersections; ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive a report on traffic management in Ward 14 related to the King Street East and Church Street intersection project — explaining why the track and watermain work was scheduled for 2025 and summarizing ongoing and planned traffic measures. No policy change is proposed.

title: Geary Avenue Mobility and Public Realm Strategy Update
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: improvement, parking, traffic; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive a status update on the Geary Avenue Mobility and Public Realm Strategy, outlining how its ten directions for the street's right-of-way and streetscape will be put in place. No policy change is proposed.

title: 113 Yonge Street (6 Adelaide Street East) - Encroachment Appeal - Permission to Repair, Restore and Maintain Existing Underground Areaways
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments, repairs;
brief: An encroachment agreement is proposed with the owner of 113 Yonge Street to let them repair, restore and maintain existing underground areaways connected to the building, beneath the Adelaide Street East sidewalk and Ching Lane. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.
address: 6 Adelaide Toronto Ontario; 113 Yonge Toronto Ontario

title: 137 Bond Street - Encroachment Appeal
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction, encroachments; building
brief: An encroachment agreement is proposed with Toronto Metropolitan University, the owner of 137 Bond Street, to let a tower crane base with concrete foundation piers, grade beams and helical piles sit within the Gould Street public right-of-way during construction. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: 86 Kilbarry Road - Encroachment Appeal - Fence and Bollards
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appeals, bollards, encroachments, fences; division fences; line fences
brief: The owner of 86 Kilbarry Road is appealing for permission to keep an aluminum fence with three stone pillars, an automated driveway gate, a pedestrian gate and four retractable steel bollards on the public right-of-way, which violates the streets and sidewalks by-law. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council not authorize the encroachment agreement.

title: Encroachment Appeal - 495-517 Wellington Street West - Proposed Ground Sign
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments, signs; signage
brief: The owner of the commercial building at 495-517 Wellington Street West is appealing for permission to install an illuminated multi-tenant ground sign on public land, which staff say conflicts with the streets and sidewalks by-law. The proposed sign would stand 4.05 metres high within the public right-of-way. Staff recommend refusing it; the Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.
address: 495 Wellington Toronto Ontario; 517 Wellington Toronto Ontario

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, board members;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint and remove business representatives on the boards of three Business Improvement Areas — Cabbagetown, Old Town Toronto and Yonge and St. Clair. The boards manage local business-area programs. No policy change is proposed.

title: Application for a Sidewalk Cafe Permit Located at 1980 Queen Street East, Waverley Street flankage
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: permits, sidewalks; permit renewal
brief: A sidewalk café was proposed at 1980 Queen Street East, at Waverley Street, and city licensing staff present the community council with options to either deny or approve the permit. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Application for a Sidewalk Cafe Permit Located at 1161 Queen Street East, Berkshire Avenue flankage
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: permits, sidewalks; permit renewal
brief: A sidewalk café was proposed at 1161 Queen Street East, at Berkshire Avenue, and city licensing staff present the community council with options to either deny or approve the permit. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: 35 Curzon Street - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The owner of 35 Curzon Street wants an exemption for existing and proposed rear-yard wooden fences taller than the by-law allows — about 3.15 metres high with an artificial boxwood privacy screen on top, where the maximum is 2.0 metres. Municipal Licensing and Standards inspected the property. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 756 Windermere Avenue - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The owner of 756 Windermere Avenue wants an exemption for a proposed rear-yard wooden fence taller than the by-law allows — one section 3.04 metres high and another 2.44 metres, where the maximum is 2.0 metres. The taller section would include an opening for fire escape through a window of the laneway suite at 754 Windermere Avenue. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 127 Kilbarry Road - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, fences, pool enclosures; application process, division fences; line fences
brief: The owner of 127 Kilbarry Road wants an exemption for a swimming pool enclosure that doesn't meet the by-law's access-protection requirements, including rules about building entrances, access through walls and self-closing gates. Municipal Licensing and Standards inspected the property. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 90 Spruce Street - Application to Remove a Private Tree
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: tree removal, trees; ash trees
brief: The owner of 90 Spruce Street is appealing the City's refusal to let them remove a healthy 41.2-centimetre ginkgo tree, citing the foul smell of its fruit and weakly attached branches in the upper canopy. Staff say the tree is healthy and maintainable, and the by-law does not allow its removal. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: 218 and 226 Soudan Avenue - Residential Demolition Applications
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The owner of detached houses at 218 and 226 Soudan Avenue wants to demolish them before replacement building permits are issued. Staff ask the Toronto and East York Community Council to consider options to refuse or approve the demolitions, with or without conditions. The community council makes the final decision.
address: 218 Soudan Toronto Ontario; 226 Soudan Toronto Ontario

title: 267 Merton Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The owner of a two-and-a-half-storey house at 267 Merton Street wants to demolish it even though no replacement building permit has been issued. Staff ask the Toronto and East York Community Council to consider options to refuse or approve the demolition, with or without conditions. The community council makes the final decision.

title: 1648 Dupont Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: buildings, demolitions;
brief: The owner of a two-storey mixed-use building at 1648 Dupont Street — with ground-floor shops and a second-floor home — wants to demolish it before a replacement building permit is issued. Staff ask the Toronto and East York Community Council to consider options to refuse or approve the demolition, with or without conditions. The community council makes the final decision.

title: 5 Robinson Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The owner of a single detached house at 5 Robinson Street wants to demolish it even though no replacement building permit has been applied for. Staff ask the Toronto and East York Community Council to consider options to refuse or approve the demolition, with or without conditions. The community council makes the final decision.

title: 149 College Street - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Alterations to the heritage-designated Stewart Building at 149 College Street -- a 6-storey E.J. Lennox building in the Romanesque Revival style, designated in 1978 -- to allow a 60-storey mixed-use building that integrates the heritage property go to Council for approval. A heritage easement agreement would ensure long-term conservation of the building.

title: Palacky Street - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Staff reviewed Palacky Street for speed humps and found it did not meet the city's traffic calming criteria, so they do not recommend installing them. Community council is asked to accept the staff recommendation.

title: Renaming Rosebank Park in Memory of Councillor Cynthia Lai
topics: parkland dedication, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: A plan to rename Rosebank Park at 1051 Progress Avenue to Cynthia Lai Park — honouring the late Ward 23 councillor under the city's commemorative naming policy — goes to community council for a decision. The renaming was first requested in December 2024.

title: Introduction of By-laws
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: Scarborough Community Council is asked to formally introduce the by-laws arising from decisions made at this meeting. Introducing by-laws makes council decisions legally take effect. No new policy is proposed.

title: Brimwood Boulevard - Parking Amendments
topics: parking regulations, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Staff recommend removing the school bus loading zone for Our Lady of Grace Catholic School on Brimwood Boulevard at the school's request, and adjusting no-stopping hours to match. Community council is asked to approve the changes.

title: Sancrest Drive - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic; motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing six speed humps on Sancrest Drive between Neapolitan Drive and Brimorton Drive to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Community council is asked to approve the installation.
