topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Two speed humps are proposed for Lippincott Street between Lennox Street and Bloor Street West, after community members asked for measures to slow cut-through speeding drivers. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Appointments to the Board of Management of the Swansea Town Hall Community Centre
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: appointments, boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to appoint seven board members to the Swansea Town Hall Community Centre board — three re-appointments (Rob Hamilton, Andrea Hazard, Michael Peddle) and four new members — for terms ending in 2026 and 2027. No policy change is proposed.

title: Traffic Circulation Changes, Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) and Parking Amendments - West Parkdale Neighbourhood
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Several traffic changes are proposed for the West Parkdale neighbourhood: Macdonell Avenue between Rideau and Fern avenues would flip from one-way southbound to one-way northbound (cyclists keep two-way), with on-street parking moved to the east side, and speed humps would be added on Wabash Avenue between Sorauren Avenue and Macdonell Avenue. The changes address neighbourhood traffic infiltration as part of the West Parkdale Cycling Connections project. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Rathnelly Avenue, between Macpherson Avenue and Poplar Plains Crescent - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Speed humps on Rathnelly Avenue between Macpherson Avenue and Poplar Plains Crescent would not be installed; staff assessed the street and found the traffic-calming criteria were not met, so they don't recommend them. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Montrose Avenue, between Bloor Street West and Harbord Street - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Seven speed humps are proposed for Montrose Avenue between Bloor Street West and Harbord Street. Staff say the street meets the City's traffic-calming criteria. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Lippincott Street, between Harbord Street and Ulster Street - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Speed humps on Lippincott Street between Harbord Street and Ulster Street would not be installed; staff assessed the street and found the traffic-calming criteria were not met, so they don't recommend them. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Elgin Avenue, between Bedford Road and Avenue Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) and Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Three speed humps are proposed for Elgin Avenue between Bedford Road and Avenue Road, and the parking ban on the south side would become a stricter no-standing ban at all times to keep two-way traffic moving. Staff say the street meets the City's traffic-calming criteria. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Charles Street West, between Queen's Park and Bay Street - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Speed humps on Charles Street West between Queen's Park and Bay Street would not be installed; staff assessed the street and found the traffic-calming criteria were not met, so they don't recommend them. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Conger Coal Lane, between Church Street and Market Street - Speed Bumps
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Speed bumps are proposed for Conger Coal Lane between Church Street and Market Street, as recommended by Transportation Services staff. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Vehicle Width Restriction - Lane south of Bloor Street West, Shaw Street to Ossington Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: lanes, width; traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: Vehicles wider than two metres would be banned from the lane south of Bloor Street West between Shaw Street and Ossington Avenue. Staff say the ban would reduce damage to surrounding private property. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations - Sherbourne Street North and Elm Avenue/Maple Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, ttc
brief: Traffic signals are proposed at Sherbourne Street North and Elm Avenue/Maple Avenue to improve safety, along with banning northbound right turns on red and making part of Maple Avenue one-way eastbound. Staff say the signals are justified by their assessment and the intersection's complex shape needs the extra rules to work safely. Because the TTC runs transit on the streets, full council approval is required.

title: Springhurst Avenue and Close Avenue - All-Way Stop Control
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: stopping prohibitions, traffic regulations; no stopping
brief: Four-way stop signs are proposed at the intersection of Springhurst Avenue and Close Avenue, following a staff traffic assessment. Staff say the all-way stop would improve safety for all road users. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Ladysmith Avenue - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, accessible permit parking, parking regulations; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The school bus loading zone on the east side of Ladysmith Avenue would shift 5.5 metres south to support safe student pick-up, after an accessible parking space was removed. The change would gain one on-street parking space. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Front Street East and Jarvis Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking and loading changes are proposed on Front Street East near Jarvis Street to support events at St. Lawrence Market North, including a commercial loading zone operating at all times. Stopping would also be banned at all times on the east side of Jarvis Street between Front and King to reduce congestion near the underground parking entrance. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Lippincott Street - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking rules on Lippincott Street between Bloor Street West and Lennox Street would be tightened after complaints about long-term parking — particularly tour buses — hurting sightlines, traffic flow and pedestrian safety. A commercial loading zone would be added near Bloor for local businesses. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Front Street West - Parking Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking machines, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws, pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Paid parking would be added in new lay-bys on the north side of Front Street West between Spadina Avenue and Draper Street, formalizing the parking rules after The Well development, with no-stopping rules outside the lay-bys. The change reinstates short-term parking in the area. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Draper Street - Streetscape Improvements and Parking By-law Amendments
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: by-laws, on-street parking; bylaws, curb parking; curbside parking; street parking
brief: Parking by-law changes are proposed for Draper Street between Front Street West and Wellington Street West, shifting on-street parking from the east side to the west side to make room for watermain replacement, road reconstruction and streetscape improvements in 2025. Staff say no parking spaces would be lost. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Pay-and-Display Parking - Various Streets - June 2025 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: New on-street paid parking locations are proposed in Wards 9 and 14, replacing existing restrictions, to encourage turnover of parking spaces near local businesses. The Toronto Parking Authority and Transportation Services identified the locations together. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - June 2025 (Delegated)
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: accessibility, accessible permit parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will approve the routine monthly list of on-street accessible parking spaces to be added or removed for people with disabilities, as set out in the June 2025 report. No wider policy change is proposed.

title: Geary Avenue Mobility and Public Realm Strategy Update
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: improvement, parking, traffic; enhancement; rehabilitation (property), motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive a status update on the Geary Avenue Mobility and Public Realm Strategy, outlining how its ten directions for the street will be put in place. The strategy came from the Geary Works Planning Study, concluded in 2021. No policy change is proposed.

title: 1134 Queen Street East - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, pedestrian walkways; building, footpaths; pedestrian ways; walking paths; walkways, ttc
brief: A 3-storey condo with ground-floor retail is being built at 1134 Queen Street East, and the developer wants the north sidewalk and part of the westbound curb lane closed for 15 months, from July 1, 2025 to September 30, 2026, as a construction staging area. Pedestrians would use a temporary walkway, with traffic control people directing them during construction hours. Because the TTC runs transit on Queen Street East, full council approval is required. The item lists a $3.00 fee.

title: 30 Merton Street - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction, parking regulations, sidewalks, traffic regulations; building, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: A 37-storey rental building is being built at 30 Merton Street, at Al Green Lane, and the developer wants the north sidewalk and part of the westbound curb lane closed for 25 months, from June 6, 2025 to June 30, 2027, as a construction staging area. Pedestrians would use a covered walkway in the closed lane. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision. The item lists a $4.25 fee.

title: 1 Bloor Street West (Yonge Street at Bloor Street West) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction, pedestrians; building, pedestrianization
brief: The developer of the 85-storey residential tower at 1 Bloor Street West (with an 86-storey tower and 8-storey retail podium planned) wants to extend the construction staging closure of the west sidewalk and part of the southbound lane on Yonge Street near Bloor to June 2028, with a temporary walkway. Past approvals ran through March 2023; the developer has said it needs the staging areas until 2028. Because the TTC runs transit on Yonge Street, full council approval is required.

title: 11 Brock Avenue - Construction Staging Area
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: construction, sidewalks; building
brief: A 4-storey residential building is being built for the City of Toronto at 11 Brock Avenue, at Noble Street, and the developer wants road and sidewalk closures around Noble Street and a public laneway for 15 months, from June 9, 2025 to August 31, 2026. The work includes closing a laneway, part of Noble Street — with a stretch becoming one-way westbound — and adding stop controls. The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.

title: Encroachment Appeal - 495-517 Wellington Street West - Proposed Ground Sign
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: encroachments, signs; signage
brief: The owner of the commercial building at 495-517 Wellington Street West is appealing for permission to install an illuminated multi-tenant ground sign on public land, which staff say breaches the streets and sidewalks by-law. The proposed sign would stand 4.05 metres high within the public right-of-way. Staff recommend refusing it; the Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.
address: 495 Wellington Toronto Ontario; 517 Wellington Toronto Ontario

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Boards of Management
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: boards of management, business improvement areas; bia; business improvement associations, boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council will appoint and remove business representatives on the boards of five Business Improvement Areas — Bloorcourt Village, Dupont by the Castle, Liberty Village, Oakwood Village and Roncesvalles Village. The boards manage local business-area programs. No policy change is proposed.

title: 12 Cluny Drive - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, houses;
brief: The owner of a three-storey detached house at 12 Cluny Drive wants to demolish it even though no replacement building permit has been applied for. Staff ask the Toronto and East York Community Council to consider options to refuse or approve the demolition, with or without conditions. The community council makes the final decision.

title: 5 Robinson Street - Residential Demolition Application
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: demolitions, residential properties; residential real estate
brief: The owner of a single detached house at 5 Robinson Street wants to demolish it even though no replacement building permit has been applied for. Staff ask the Toronto and East York Community Council to consider options to refuse or approve the demolition, with or without conditions. The community council makes the final decision.

title: 257 Seaton Street - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The owner of 257 Seaton Street wants an exemption for an existing rear-yard aluminum fence about 2.77 metres high, where the maximum allowed is 2.5 metres. City inspectors issued a violation notice for the fence. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 255 Seaton Street - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The owner of 255 Seaton Street wants an exemption for an existing rear-yard aluminum fence about 2.74 metres high, where the maximum allowed is 2.5 metres. City inspectors issued a violation notice for the fence. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 127 Kilbarry Road - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: applications, fences, pool enclosures; application process, division fences; line fences
brief: The owner of 127 Kilbarry Road wants an exemption for a swimming pool enclosure that doesn't meet the access-protection rules — including requirements about building entrances, access through walls, and self-closing gates. Municipal Licensing and Standards inspected the property. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: 365 Spadina Avenue - Application for Fence Exemption
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: exemptions, fences; division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The owner of 365 Spadina Avenue wants an exemption for rooftop deck fencing taller than the by-law allows — up to 3.66 metres on the south side and 2.6 metres on the north, where the maximum is 2.0 metres. City inspectors found the fencing violates the fence by-law. Staff recommend the Toronto and East York Community Council refuse the exemption.

title: St. Clair Avenue West and Bathurst Street Planning Framework and Forest Hill Village Urban Design Guidelines Review - Information Report
body: Toronto and East York Community Council
topics: planning, report requests;
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to receive for information a planning report reviewing the St. Clair Avenue West and Bathurst Street area and the Forest Hill Village urban design guidelines. The report covers the area's mix of housing, shops and parks, and Forest Hill Village's main-street character along Spadina Road. No policy change is proposed.

title: Naming of an existing Public Lane West of Symington Avenue, extending Northerly from Kingsley Avenue
body: Toronto and East York Community Council

brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to approve the name 'Chic and Min Johnston Lane' for an existing public laneway west of Symington Avenue, north of Kingsley Avenue. The name meets the City's street-naming policy and commemoration guidelines. No policy change is proposed.

title: Beechgrove Drive - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing 14 speed humps on Beechgrove Drive between Lawrence Avenue East and Megan Avenue to slow traffic, and lowering the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h along the same stretch. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the changes.

title: Amberjack Boulevard - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing eight speed humps on Amberjack Boulevard between Bellamy Road North (south intersection) and Brimorton Drive to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the installation. The work is estimated to cost $32,000, with funding from Transportation Services' 2025 capital budget.

title: Kingston Road and Raspberry Road/Private Access - Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Amendments
topics: change, traffic, traffic control systems, traffic signals; amendments; conversion; modification, fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo, traffic signal control systems; traffic signal equipment
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing traffic control signals at Kingston Road and Raspberry Road, as a condition of approval for two new 11-storey residential buildings at 7437-7441 Kingston Road. Related northbound and southbound through-movement restrictions would also be added. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve.

title: 49 Bellamy Road South - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: applications, tree removal; application process
brief: A property owner at 49 Bellamy Road South has asked for a permit to remove a private black walnut tree over concerns that large falling branches could damage property. City staff say the 78.5-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable and recommend refusing the permit. Scarborough Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision on the appeal.

title: 27 Lyncroft Drive - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: applications, tree removal; application process
brief: A property owner at 27 Lyncroft Drive has asked for a permit to remove a private Scots pine tree they say is declining and could become a hazard. City staff say the 33-centimetre tree is healthy and maintainable and recommend refusing the permit. Scarborough Community Council has delegated authority to make the final decision on the appeal.

title: Introduction of By-laws
topics: by-laws; bylaws
brief: This is a procedural item: Scarborough Community Council is asked to formally introduce the by-laws arising from decisions made at this meeting. Introducing by-laws makes council decisions legally take effect. No new policy is proposed.

title: Raleigh Avenue and Moira Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: change, parking regulations; amendments; conversion; modification, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Councillor Parthi Kandavel recommends parking changes on Raleigh Avenue and Moira Avenue, after residents, businesses and parking enforcement reported ongoing congestion and safety problems, worsened by redevelopment changing driveway access on the south side of Raleigh Avenue. Transportation Services supports the proposed amendments to existing parking regulations. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve.

title: Huntsmill Boulevard - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps) Re-opening Item SC22.10
topics: intersections, speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas asks Scarborough Community Council to re-open its earlier decision approving 14 speed humps on Huntsmill Boulevard, to correct a wording error. Because there are two Huntsmill Boulevard intersections with Bamburgh Circle, the decision should specify the south intersection. No new policy change is proposed.

title: 303 Nantucket Boulevard - Designation of Fire Routes and amendment to Chapter 880 - Fire Routes
topics: change, fire routes; amendments; conversion; modification, fire access routes
brief: The Fire Chief asks that private roads at 303 Nantucket Boulevard be officially designated as fire routes under Municipal Code Chapter 880. Designated fire routes keep access clear for fire vehicles and allow parking enforcement. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the designation.

title: Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking - Northview Avenue
topics: [activities in transportation], on-street parking, permit parking; curb parking; curbside parking; street parking, on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Transportation staff recommend introducing overnight permit parking from 12:01 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. daily on the south side of Northview Avenue between Victoria Park Avenue and Blantyre Avenue, after residents requested it. Parking would be banned at all times on the north side. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve.

title: Sedgemount Drive - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, school buses;
brief: Transportation staff recommend parking changes on Sedgemount Drive in front of Tredway Woodsworth Public School, to stop motorists from blocking the school bus loading zone and the school driveway. The changes adjust short-term parking and bus zone hours, and also correct a by-law inconsistency around the U-turn prohibition signage. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve.

title: Ionview Road - U-Turn Prohibition
topics: road safety, turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Transportation staff recommend banning U-turns in both directions on Ionview Road between Yorkshire Road and Bertrand Avenue, to make the street safer near Ionview Public School. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the ban.

brief: Transportation staff recommend installing 20 speed humps on Poplar Road between Cumber Avenue/Dearham Wood and Kingston Road to slow traffic, and lowering the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h along the same stretch. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the changes.

brief: Transportation staff recommend installing 11 speed humps on Marcella Street between Scarborough Golf Club Road and Samson Crescent to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

brief: Transportation staff recommend installing 18 speed humps on Lynnbrook Drive between Brimorton Drive and Bellamy Road North to slow traffic, and lowering the speed limit from 40 km/h to 30 km/h along the same stretch. title: Harfleur Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)

brief: Transportation staff recommend installing five speed humps on Harfleur Road between Glendower Circuit and Huntingwood Drive to slow traffic, and lowering the speed limit from 50 km/h to 30 km/h along the same stretch. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the changes.

brief: Transportation staff recommend installing seven speed humps on Dolly Varden Boulevard between Daventry Road and Brimorton Drive to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

title: Courcelette Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Humps)
topics: speed humps, traffic calming; sleeping policeman; sleeping policemen; speed bumps
brief: Transportation staff recommend installing three speed humps on Courcelette Road between Queen Street East and Windsor Avenue to slow traffic. The report says the street met the city's traffic calming criteria. Scarborough Community Council is asked to approve the installation.

topics: applications, exemptions, fences; application process, division fences; line fences, exceptions
brief: The applicant at 369 Soudan Avenue wants an exemption from the city's fence-height rules in Chapter 447 of the municipal code. North York Community Council, which has final authority on fence exemptions, is being asked to decide whether to grant it.

topics: fences, property lines, property owners; building owners; land owners; property ownership, division fences; line fences, property boundaries
brief: The owner at 78 Burncrest Drive wants permission to build a fence that does not meet the city's fence rules. Staff recommend North York Community Council, which has final authority, refuse the exemption under Chapter 447 of the municipal code.

brief: Whether to remove a director from the Wilson Village Business Improvement Area's board of management is before North York Community Council. title: 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, mixed use areas, redevelopment; rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: Before the Lake Shore Boulevard West tower can proceed, City Council must vote on demolishing 14 rental dwelling units and two dwelling rooms at 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West. A Tenant Assistance Plan would give existing tenants the right to return to replacement rental units at similar rents, plus financial compensation, with $20,000.00 attached to the plan in the source documents. The 14 rental homes would be rebuilt as part of the new 39-storey development on the site.
address: 3807-3815 Lake Shore Toronto Ontario; 3819-3829 Lake Shore Toronto Ontario

title: 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 39-storey mixed-use tower of 124 metres with 490 homes is proposed for 3807-3815 and 3819-3829 Lake Shore Boulevard West, including 14 rental replacement units on site. topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: A rare pre-Confederation property at 450 Rustic Road, on the north side of Rustic Road south of Highway 401 and west of Keele Street, is proposed for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate it under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 3100 Weston Road - Proposed Designation By-Law under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Council decides whether to stand by its February 5, 2025 decision to designate 3100 Weston Road as a heritage property, rejecting an objection from the owner. The Ontario Heritage Act gives Council until June 8, 2025 to decide the objection, so the formal designation by-law must pass before the deadline. The vote settles whether the Weston Road at Sheppard Avenue West property gets protected heritage status.

title: Toronto Builds - A Policy Framework to Build More Affordable Rental Homes on Public Land
topics: land, rental housing; property, rental properties; rental units
brief: Toronto Builds would become the single set of rules for developing affordable rental and mixed-income housing on city-owned land. Council is being asked to approve the policy framework, applied to all current and future sites in the portfolio, aimed at low-income and vulnerable residents, key workers and middle-income earners hit by the housing crisis. Council has previously approved about $32.2 million in financial incentives — development charge exemptions, parkland dedication exemptions, waived planning and building permit fees, and property tax exemptions — for 193 affordable rental homes at 970 Kipling Avenue and 229 at 158 Borough Drive, and this report brings those incentives under the Toronto Builds framework. The item's source material also references $150 million, $5 billion, $4.75 billion, $7.3 billion and $5 million.

title: Development Application Fee Review
topics: development review process, planning approvals; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, development control; development reviews
brief: Developers would pay more for the city to review their projects under an updated fee schedule. Council is being asked to adopt the revised development application fees, effective July 1, 2025, covering the services that shape growth, from housing supply to transit and health-care facilities. The development review service costs about $80.1 million a year to run, while current fees bring in about $62.8 million — covering roughly 78 percent of costs and leaving an estimated $17.3 million annual gap the new schedule is designed to close.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Member Complement
topics: appeals, members; memberships
brief: The Toronto Local Appeal Body, the tribunal that hears minor variance and consent appeals, would shrink from fourteen members to ten. Council is being asked to reduce the complement by not replacing members as their terms end, except for the Chair. Fewer panel members could affect how quickly planning appeals are heard.

title: Official Plan Amendments to Align with Provincial Legislative and Policy Changes Related to Employment Areas - Decision Report
topics: employment areas, official plan amendments; employment districts; employment zones
brief: Toronto's planning rules would be brought in line with new provincial definitions of employment areas under Official Plan Amendment 804. Council is being asked to adopt the amendment, aligning the Official Plan with the Planning Act's new definition of "area of employment" and the 2024 Provincial Planning Statement, along with redesignating 255 hectares across four Employment Areas largely planned as office business parks. The change sets which lands stay protected for jobs.

title: 895 Lawrence Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Planning staff recommend refusing a proposal for three residential towers, 26, 32 and 34 storeys with shops on one tower's ground floor, at 895 Lawrence Avenue East. North York Community Council is being asked to adopt the refusal, which would leave the site's current land-use rules in place. The applicant could still take the refusal to the Ontario Land Tribunal.

title: 586 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal
topics: applications, official plan amendments, redevelopment; application process, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The applicant behind a revised 35-storey building at 586 Eglinton Avenue East wants an exemption from the Yonge-Eglinton rule requiring replacement of demolished office floor area. The Official Plan amendment application was appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is being asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the hearing.

title: Growing Glencairn Phase 1 Report: Emerging Vision and Guiding Principles
topics: buildings, development, multi-unit dwellings; developing land; development (land); land development, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings
brief: City Planning has published an emerging vision and guiding principles for the Growing Glencairn study, which looks at future growth around Glencairn Subway Station, an area the province says sits below its minimum density target of 200 people and jobs per hectare. North York Community Council is being asked to endorse the vision and principles so they can guide the study's next phase. The outcome will shape what gets built near the station in the coming years.

title: 253, 255, 259, 263 Viewmount Avenue and 12, 14, 16, 18 Romar Crescent - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal
topics: buildings, residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: Two residential towers, 35 and 39 storeys, with 1,055 homes on a six-storey base are proposed at 253, 255, 259 and 263 Viewmount Avenue and 12, 14, 16 and 18 Romar Crescent, including an on-site parkland dedication. The applicant appealed the planning applications to the Ontario Land Tribunal, and North York Community Council is being asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal.

title: 250, 252, 254, 258 Viewmount Avenue - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 40-storey residential building with 477 homes is proposed at 250, 252, 254 and 258 Viewmount Avenue. The applicant appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council did not decide the application within the Planning Act time limit, and North York Community Council is being asked to direct the City Solicitor to oppose the appeal at the hearing.

title: Turn Prohibitions onto Eglinton Avenue East from Brentcliffe Road and Don Avon Drive
topics: road construction, roads, traffic signals; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: Turns onto Eglinton Avenue East from Brentcliffe Road and Don Avon Drive would be restricted to ease congestion from Crosstown LRT construction. The councillor notes road redesign and lane realignment have sharply cut capacity on Eglinton Avenue East in Ward 15, and traffic apps send trucks and cars down local roads like Donlea Drive — blocking driveways, impeding emergency vehicles and creating unsafe driving. North York Community Council is asked to approve turn prohibitions as congestion mitigation, a move residents support. Drivers on the affected roads would be affected.

title: Waiver of the Public Appointments Policy and Appointment of a Public Member to the Larry Grossman Forest Hill Memorial Arena Board
topics: appointments, arenas, management (sc), public appointments; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: City Council would waive the Public Appointments Policy's two-term limit to re-appoint Melissa Grossman to the Larry Grossman Forest Hill Memorial Arena Board, at pleasure of Council, for a term ending April 30, 2029. The confidential candidate details would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: 243-255 Consumers Road, North York - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2545
topics: highways, services, subdivision (wards); freeways; motorways; parkways, voting subdivisions
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council would formally assume the municipal services and roads in the 243-255 Consumers Road subdivision (Registered Plan 66M-2545, subdivision agreement dated September 20, 2016, between Parkway Place Holdings Ltd., 2200191 Ontario Limited, 2200195 Ontario Limited, 165 Yorkland GP Inc. and the City) by passing an assumption by-law. The acting director would release the performance guarantee held under the agreement and the City Solicitor would register the by-law. Residents of the subdivision would see the City take over the roads and services.

title: 3386-3398 Bayview Avenue and 32 Brenham Crescent - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Appeal
topics: applications, driveways, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A proposal for fifty four-storey townhomes at 3386-3398 Bayview Avenue and 32 Brenham Crescent would be refused. Staff recommend City Council reject the zoning amendment for the 12.5-metre-high townhomes — 25 fronting Bayview Avenue and 25 fronting a new private driveway to Brenham Crescent, with an outdoor amenity space in the northwest — because it does not conform to the Official Plan on site organization, tree preservation and access. A related rental housing demolition application is still under review. The decision affects what gets built on the site.

title: 23-29 Greenbriar Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, rental housing; developing land; development (land); land development, rental properties; rental units
brief: Twenty-two rental homes at 23-29 Greenbriar Road would be demolished and replaced in the new development. North York Community Council is asked to approve the Rental Housing Demolition application and the residential demolition permit, with a Tenant Relocation and Assistance Plan securing tenants' right to return to a replacement unit of the same type at similar rent; the item's figures list $20,000.00. The 22 replacement units would be part of the proposed 25-storey, 325-unit building on the site.

title: 23-29 Greenbriar Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 25-storey residential building with 325 homes, including 22 rental replacement units, would be approved at 23-29 Greenbriar Road. City Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law for the 79.6-metre building (plus mechanical penthouse), which staff say fits the Apartment Neighbourhood criteria and the Renew Sheppard East Secondary Plan. Future residents would be affected.

title: 123 and 123A Parkway Forest Drive - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, planning approvals, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; development applications; development approval applications; development approvals; planning applications; planning development approvals, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 33-storey apartment building with 384 rental homes, including six affordable rentals, would be approved at 123 and 123A Parkway Forest Drive. City Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law for the 107.2-metre tower; the existing 19-storey building with 188 rental units would be retained, five of ten rental townhouses would be demolished and five kept, and all 193 retained rental units would be secured as rental housing for 20 years. A related rental housing demolition application for the five townhouses would go to the Chief Planner if the zoning is approved. Future renters of the new homes would be affected.

title: Appointment of Public Member to the Toronto Hydro Board
topics: public appointments;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel would select six candidates to interview for appointment to the Toronto Hydro Board, with interviews and a recommendation of two candidates at its next meeting. The candidate details in the confidential attachments would stay confidential. No policy change is proposed.

title: Requesting Funding Support from Federal and Provincial Governments for Enhanced Festival Safety and Security - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: federal governments, festivals and special events, funding, provincial governments, safety; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals, financing, public safety
brief: Toronto would press the federal and provincial governments to create new funding programs for festival safety and security. Council would make the request after the City allocated $3.85 million in 2025 for festival safety — including the renewed Special Events Stabilization Initiative, which supported 81 festivals in 2024, and a new Cultural Festivals Funding Program — plus a Festival Safety Summit with Toronto Police on May 26, 2025. The motion cites the April 26, 2025 attack at Vancouver's Lapu-Lapu Day Block Party, where eleven people were killed. Festival organizers, crews, volunteers and attendees are the ones facing the rising security costs.

title: Accepting a Donation from Tennis Canada to Enhance the Tennis Courts at Malvern Park - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: donation, tennis courts; bequest; toy drive, tennis centers; tennis centres; tennis complexes; tennis facilities
brief: The tennis courts at Malvern Park would get a boost of up to $100,000.00 from Tennis Canada's Play Your Court program, funded in part by National Bank Financial. Council would authorize Parks and Recreation to accept the cash donation and increase the 2025 capital budget for Malvern Park accordingly, on top of the City's own Back on Track court improvements to lighting, fencing and surfaces. The program aims to revitalize over 100 community courts nationally by 2030. Malvern residents would get colour-coated, higher-quality public courts with no net cost to the City.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 30 Tippett Road (South Lands), in Order to Fabricate and Install Branded Street Name Signs for the Downsview Neighbourhood - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Anthony Perruzza
topics: signs; signage
brief: About 375 decorative street name signs marking the Downsview neighbourhood would be made and installed for $63,488.25. Council would add $63,488.25 to the Transportation Services capital budget, funded by Section 37 benefits from the development at 30 Tippett Road (South Lands), with the signs designed with the Downsview Lands Community Voice Association to honour the area's aviation heritage as the former Canadian Forces Base Downsview Airport. The signs would mark the boundaries of one of Toronto's prominent neighbourhoods. Local residents and drivers would see the new branded signage across the area.

title: Commencing Public Consultations for Communities Impacted by New Shelter Locations - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Parthi Kandavel
topics: homelessness;
brief: Each of the six planned new shelter locations announced in December 2024 would get its own public consultation under this motion. Council would direct the General Manager of Toronto Shelter and Support Services to arrange individual consultations per site — instead of the current generalized, collective approach — and work with each local councillor on dates and format (in-person or virtual). The motion responds to concerns that the collective process does not reflect neighbourhood-specific needs. Residents near each proposed site would get a dedicated forum on the shelter planned for their area.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 43, 49, and 51 Gerrard Street West and 695 Bay Street for Public Wi-Fi in Five Toronto Community Housing Buildings - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: Hundreds of Toronto Community Housing residents in Ward 11 would get free public Wi-Fi in their buildings' common areas under this $243,335.49 release of developer funds. Council would add $243,335.49 to the Technology Services capital budget, funded by Section 37 benefits from the development at 43, 49 and 51 Gerrard Street West and 695 Bay Street that have sat dormant since 2014. Toronto Community Housing and ConnectTO would install the Wi-Fi in five buildings, following a 2023 pilot at 250 Davenport Road. The project targets the digital divide for residents who need internet access for work, school and daily life.

title: Requesting Permission for Rugby in the Square for Nathan Phillips Square By-Law Exemption - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: by-laws, sports; bylaws
brief: Rugby Ontario's co-ed flag rugby tournament would get a noise and by-law exemption to use Nathan Phillips Square on May 30, 2025. Council would exempt Rugby in the Square from the public squares by-law so amplified sound can run past usual hours, with load-in on May 29 from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. and the event running 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; the permit stays conditional on a Noise Exemption Permit and compliance with other City policies. Teams of up to 10 players are guaranteed at least three games, with activations around the square. The exemption would let the annual citywide event proceed as planned.

title: 11 Oswald Crescent - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The City would defend the Committee of Adjustment's refusal to split the lot at 11 Oswald Crescent into two at the Toronto Local Appeal Body. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to uphold the refusal of the severance and minor variances — covering lot area, frontage, wall height and driveway width — sought for two new detached homes. The applicant appealed the April 15, 2025 refusal. The motion also lets the Solicitor hire consultants and negotiate a settlement.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Heliconian Club - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: arts and culture organizations, heritage properties; art councils; art organizations; arts councils; arts groups; cultural organizations, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Heliconian Club, a women's arts organization founded in 1909, would get $20,000 toward accessible washrooms at its historic Heliconian Hall at 35 Hazelton Avenue in Yorkville. Council would add $20,000 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Non-Program operating budget, funded by Section 37 developer community benefits, combining with contributions from neighbours' associations for the renovation. The 1876 Carpenter's Gothic building is a Toronto and National Historic Site and one of the city's small concert venues. The money would help a 150-year-old building stay usable for artists and audiences.

title: 114 Restever Gate - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: appeals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City would appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of a fourplex at 114 Restever Gate to the Toronto Local Appeal Body. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to oppose the development, hire outside consultants and negotiate a resolution. The approved application sought a 10.33-metre-tall detached fourplex with a front-yard parking space and a platform encroaching 3.22 metres into the rear yard setback; city forestry staff had recommended refusal, warning the variances could force the removal of healthy protected trees. The appeal will decide the building's final form and the fate of the trees.

title: Protecting Toronto’s Film Industry From Impacts of Uncertainty Caused by Tariff Threat - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: film and television industry; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry
brief: Toronto's film industry — 40,000 jobs and as much as $2.6 billion in direct spending in 2022 — faces uncertainty from threatened tariffs on films made outside the United States, and this motion asks other governments to step in. Council would advocate to Ontario and Ottawa for stronger Ontario film tax credits with faster payment, more direct investment in domestic production, and access to tariff-relief funds for the production and post-production industry. The motion, endorsed by the Toronto Film, Television and Digital Media Board in May 2025, is framed as urgent because summer is the industry's busiest season. Local film workers and businesses are the ones whose work is at stake.

title: 80 Lamb Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The City would go to the Toronto Local Appeal Body to fight a Committee of Adjustment decision that approved a laneway suite project at 80 Lamb Avenue. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to appeal the approval, oppose the development at the TLAB, hire outside consultants and negotiate a settlement. The approved variances covered the height and separation distance of a two-storey laneway suite behind an altered two-storey semi-detached home; planning staff had recommended refusal, saying the 6.3-metre height and 5-metre separation did not fit laneway suite policies or the neighbourhood's character. The case will decide what gets built behind the property.

title: Speeding Up Streetcars: Getting People Moving Faster During King and Church Construction - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction; building, ttc
brief: The 504 King streetcar, which carries more than 100,000 people a day, is crawling at as little as 3.7 kilometres per hour on its construction detour, and this motion looks for ways to speed it up. Council would direct Transportation Services to work with the TTC to identify and implement transit priority measures — such as traffic agents, signal timing changes and parking changes — around the King and Church construction zone, in consultation with the local councillor and stakeholders. The King and Church closure is for combined TTC and watermain work. Downtown transit riders are the main beneficiaries if travel times improve.

title: Purchase Order Amendment on Contract with Midome Construction Services Limited for the New Streetcar Tracks on Adelaide Street - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: construction, streetcars; building, street-cars
brief: The contract for new streetcar tracks on Adelaide Street between York and Victoria streets would grow by another $200,000.00 so the remaining work can happen overnight, reducing disruption to TTC operations and corridor traffic during the Ontario Line Queen Street closure detour. Council would amend purchase order 6054610 with Midome Construction Services Limited, which started at $40,240,992 net of HST recoverable in 2023, rose by $3,376,905.60 to $43,617,897.60, then by $5,466,401.89 to $49,084,299.49, and would reach $49,284,299.49 with this amendment. The work is funded by Metrolinx and on schedule for June 2025 completion. Riders and drivers on the downtown detour route are the ones affected by the construction timing.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Above 5 Percent Cash-In-Lieu Funds From the Development at 8 and 30 Widmer Street for Ryerson Community School Playground Improvements - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: playgrounds, school boards, schools; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Ryerson Community School's playground would get a $135,793 upgrade — new play equipment, repaving, seating, plantings, hockey court work, trails, fencing and storage — paid for with developer funds. Council would add $135,793 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Parks and Recreation capital budget, fully funded by Section 42 above-5-percent cash-in-lieu from the development at 8 and 30 Widmer Street, and forward the one-time capital funding to the Toronto District School Board. The Board must sign a Community Access Agreement keeping the improved facilities open to the community. Students and neighbours using the schoolyard would see the full scope delivered on the Board's contractor schedule.

title: 521 Davisville Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: A proposed new home and laneway suite at 521 Davisville Avenue would face the City's opposition at the Toronto Local Appeal Body. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to attend the TLAB to oppose the applicant's appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's February 20, 2025 refusal, which covered variances for setbacks, building depth, wall height and a laneway suite ancillary building. Planning and urban forestry staff had given the Committee reports recommending conditions if the application were approved, along with applicant-agreed modifications; the Committee refused it. The motion also lets the Solicitor hire outside consultants and negotiate a settlement.

title: Authorization to Amend Section 37 Agreement on Parkland Timing of Obligations in Response to Committee of Adjustment Application for 545-601 Sherbourne Street and 3-7 Howard Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: The developer of 545-601 Sherbourne Street and 3-7 Howard Street would have to sign an amended Section 37 agreement on the timing of its parkland obligations if the Committee of Adjustment approves its variance requests. The 51-storey, 532-rental-unit project owes a 607.64-square-metre parkland conveyance — 536.64 square metres of required dedication plus 80.9 square metres over-dedicated as a community benefit — tied to the first above-grade building permit, alongside the redesign of St. James Town Park West. Council's decision would update the timing terms rather than the amount of parkland. The change matters for residents waiting on the park improvements connected to the redevelopment.

title: Friends of Allan Gardens Management Agreement for Allan Gardens - Enhancing Community Engagement through Recurring Activations in the Palm House - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: gardens;
brief: The Friends of Allan Gardens could start hosting regularly scheduled community events — such as recurring Saturday and holiday activations — inside the Palm House of the Allan Gardens Conservatory. Council would authorize the General Manager of Parks and Recreation to amend the group's management agreement, which was first signed in 2022, to cover the expanded programming. All events would still have to follow City policies and coordinate scheduling with staff. The change would affect visitors to the Palm House and community groups using the space.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.GG18.23 for Correction to Supplier Name in Contract - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: contracts, suppliers;
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to fix an administrative error in its December 2024 decision on Toronto Water contracts, changing the supplier name from Automated Logic Ltd. to its correct legal name, Automated Logic - Canada Ltd. The correction is needed so Toronto Water can proceed with maintenance of building automation systems at the Ashbridges Bay Treatment Plant without disrupting water services. No policy or spending change is involved.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Community Matters Toronto for Mural Art on Bell Utility Boxes in Davenport - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification
brief: Eight Bell Canada utility boxes in Davenport would be painted with murals under a $18,080 grant to Box Murals Inc. Council would add $18,080 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Non-Program operating budget, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from developments at 1800-1818 St. Clair Avenue West and 383, 423 and 425 Old Weston Road, and forward the money on signing of a funding agreement. The boxes are at 85, 109 and 129 Rowntree Avenue, 129 Prescott Avenue, 177 Caledonia Road (three boxes), 289 Harvie Avenue and 1282 St. Clair Avenue West. Local residents requested the public art, and the Box Murals Project has painted over 600 boxes across the region since 2009.

title: Assessing Sunshine List Reporting Requirements and Incentive Programs of City Agencies and Corporations - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: [political and administrative areas], legislation, report requests; acts
brief: Residents would see public salary reporting for City agencies and corporations that fall outside Ontario's Sunshine List. Council would direct the City Manager to publish, every year, the equivalent of provincial Public Sector Salary Disclosure information for agencies and corporations not on the provincial list — including those claiming exemption — and to follow up on their compliance with the Act. The motion's rationale says the City currently submits some agency disclosures and exemption attestations to the province through payroll services, and flags a possible gap in due diligence. The change would affect transparency around pay at City-linked agencies.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC23.8 - 2079-2111 Yonge Street, 9-11, 21, 31, 35 and part of 37 Hillsdale Avenue East, and 12-18 and part of 20 Manor Road East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos-Lin
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a procedural item: reopening its earlier decision on the proposed development at 2079-2111 Yonge Street (plus Hillsdale Avenue East and Manor Road East addresses) to give the City Solicitor new directions for the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing goes to Council for approval. The 29-storey, 98-metre mixed-use proposal includes 486 residential units with 31 replacement rental units and partially retains a heritage building at 2111 Yonge Street; Council's earlier position sought a minimum of six retail units along the Yonge frontage to preserve Davisville Village's fine-grained retail, and the motion asks for directions including a minimum of four retail units. The applicant appealed Council's refusal to the Tribunal in April 2024. The outcome will shape the retail character of the block and the number of homes built.

title: Administrative Penalty Administration During Possible Postal Strike - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
topics: customer service, legislation; acts
brief: People disputing red-light camera or automated speed enforcement tickets would get twice as long to respond if a postal strike disrupts mail delivery. Council would amend the administrative penalties by-law to extend response timelines from 30 to 60 calendar days for violations under Municipal Code Chapter 610, which took effect in January 2025. The change is precautionary: tickets are currently delivered by mail, and a strike could prevent drivers from receiving or responding to them in time. It would affect every driver issued a camera-based ticket during a disruption.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 300 Valermo Drive for St. Ambrose Catholic School's School Yard Revitalization Project - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: community development, schools; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development, community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: St. Ambrose Catholic School's schoolyard would be transformed into an inclusive outdoor learning space with $125,000 of developer funds. Council would add $125,000 gross ($0 net, budgeted as $125,000.00) to the 2025 Non-Program operating budget, fully funded by Section 37 benefits from the development at 300 Valermo Drive, and forward the one-time capital funding to the Toronto Catholic District School Board. The Board must sign a Community Access Agreement so the upgraded playscape stays open to the community. The project turns a Section 37 obligation into a schoolyard used by students and neighbours.

title: Tamil Genocide Monument in Scarborough - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: community & life (sc), community associations;
brief: A Tamil Genocide Monument could be placed in a Scarborough park after consultation with the National Council of Canadian Tamils. Council would ask the City Manager, working with Parks and Recreation, to identify a potential site and report to Scarborough Community Council in the fourth quarter of 2025. The motion notes Ontario's Tamil Genocide Education Week, the federal May 18 Tamil Genocide Remembrance Day, and a monument recently unveiled in Brampton's downtown park. Toronto's Tamil community, concentrated in Scarborough, would gain a permanent site of remembrance.

title: Piloting a Red Tape Hotline for Businesses - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Toronto businesses would get a dedicated Red Tape Hotline to report burdensome city rules, permit delays and duplicative or outdated by-laws under a nine-month pilot run by Economic Development and Culture. (The motion text describes a nine-month pilot; the earlier brief summary said four months.) Council would set up the hotline, have staff analyze the reports, and consider interim relief for businesses where feasible, with an evaluation report to the Economic and Community Development Committee in the first quarter of 2026. The initiative follows the 2024 Action Plan for Toronto's Economy, which flagged regulatory modernization as a priority. Local business owners would be the direct users of the line.

title: Establishing an Annual Mayor’s Savings Challenge - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, Seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: City staff with the best money-saving or efficiency ideas would get yearly public recognition under a new Mayor's Savings Challenge. Council would create the annual challenge, with the Mayor celebrating the winning ideas and non-monetary awards for the staff behind the most impactful, implementable proposals — preferably in time for the 2026 budget. The motion frames frontline staff as an untapped source of practical cost-saving ideas, from simpler processes to smarter service delivery. It would affect how the City solicits and rewards employee innovation.

title: 53 Snowdon Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: committees of adjustment, construction; building, committee of adjustment
brief: The fate of a proposed three-storey detached home at 53 Snowdon Avenue would go to the Toronto Local Appeal Body with the City's lawyer arguing against it. Council would authorize the City Solicitor to oppose the applicant's appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's April 17, 2025 refusal of variances for front wall height, floor space index and the west side yard setback. City planning staff had recommended refusal, saying the design did not fit the neighbourhood's physical character and was not minor. The motion also lets the Solicitor settle the matter on the City's behalf.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2024 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Cabbagetown South and Garden District - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, service districts; administrative districts, financing
brief: Allan Gardens' off-leash dog area would get $350,000 in upgrades under this release of resident-voted Section 37 funds for Cabbagetown South and the Garden District. Council would add $350,000 gross ($0 net) to the 2025 Parks and Recreation capital budget, funded by developer benefits from 75, 77 and 83 Mutual Street; the six projects sit within the $750,000 participatory budget envelope and also include $2,530.00 to the Friends of Allan Gardens for commemorative trees with plaques at the Teaching Garden, and $150,000.00 to Central Neighbourhood House for front landscaping at 349 Ontario Street, including tree planting and a stroller storage area. Local residents chose these projects in 2024 voting, so the motion converts their choices into funded work.

title: Renaming Sumach-Shuter Parkette to Louis March Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Sumach-Shuter Parkette would be renamed Louis March Park to honour the founder of the Zero Gun Violence Movement, who died on July 20, 2024. City Council would approve the new name and install new signage at the park near Regent Park, one of the neighbourhoods where March did much of his work. The motion credits March with decades of advocacy on gun violence, youth empowerment, education, mental health, employment and restorative justice. Renaming a park after a community figure would give the neighbourhood a permanent marker of his legacy.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 42 Funds for Improvements to the Jose Rizal Memorial in Earl Bales Park - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: memorials, reserve funds; monuments; permanent memorials, reserves and reserve funds
brief: The Jose Rizal Memorial in Earl Bales Park, a bronze bust gifted by the Philippine government in 1998 for the centennial of Filipino independence, would get landscaping and accessibility upgrades. Council would create a $60,000 capital project — the item's figures list $15,000.00 in the budget detail — funded by Section 37 and Section 42 developer funds; the bust and plaques would be rotated 180 degrees to open up gathering space to the east. The memorial honours Dr. Jose Rizal, the Philippines' national hero, and is a focal point for Toronto's Filipino Canadian community during cultural celebrations.

title: Securing a Dedicated School Location to Support Toronto’s Film Industry - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: film and television industry, schools; cinema industry; film and television cluster; film production; movie industry; television industry, community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums
brief: Toronto's film industry, which the motion says saw a record $2.6 billion spent in the city in 2022 and employs more than 30,000 people, could get a dedicated production home in a closed school building. City Council would direct Economic Development and Culture, with Corporate Real Estate Management, to work with the Toronto Lands Corporation on securing an unused school as a predictable film and television location, building on the existing xoTO Schools program. Staff would report back in mid-2025. The idea targets a bottleneck — school sites are in high demand as sets but hard to permit — and keeping productions in Toronto affects local jobs.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Colborne Street Area Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: road maintenance; roads maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalks maintenance; summer maintenance; winter maintenance
brief: Colborne Street, Leader Lane and Colborne Lane in the Old Town area would get wider sidewalks, a narrower roadway, a pedestrian-only stretch of Leader Lane and room for restaurant patios under this $1,250,000 streetscape plan. Council would release the Section 37 developer funds, sending $850,000 to Transportation Services and $400,000 to the Old Town Toronto Business Improvement Area to deliver the work, with budget lines showing $719,420.43 and $130,579.57. The segments cover Colborne Street between Church Street and Leader Lane, Leader Lane between Wellington Street East and King Street, and Colborne Lane between Colborne Street and Leader Lane, and the changes would affect pedestrians, cyclists and local businesses in the St. Lawrence Market neighbourhood.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Ward 13 2024 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Cabbagetown, Winchester Park, and St. James Town - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: funding, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, financing
brief: Residents of Cabbagetown, Winchester Park and St. James Town voted on how to spend $750,000 of developer-paid community funds, and Council is now asked to release the money for the six winning projects. The motion would amend the Parks and Recreation capital budget to fund sixteen seat benches and four 3x3 ft mosaics at Winchester Park, a 12x12 ft mosaic in St. James Town Open Space, a Cabbagetown Gateway Sculpture, and interactive art sculptures at the Amelia Street/Parliament Street and Spruce Street/Parliament Street parkettes. Budgeted costs for the projects are listed as $80,000, $75,000, $160,000, $100,000.00, $200,000.00 and $300,000.00 within the $750,000 envelope; the $200,000.00, funded by Section 37 benefits at 500 Sherbourne Street, is for Cabbagetown Gateway Features — sculptures at Carlton Street and Sherbourne Street, Wellesley Street East and Parliament Street, and Gerrard Street East and Sherbourne Street. The projects were chosen through 2024 participatory budgeting, so the vote turns resident choices into funded park improvements.

title: Changes to the Marlee-Glencairn Study - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: The Growing Glencairn Study would get a new name — the Growing Marlee-Glencairn Study — reflecting residents' wish to honour the historic Marlee Ville neighbourhood identity. City Council would direct the Chief Planner and Executive Director of Development Review to make the change, and to fold growth data from nearby areas, such as Major Transit Station Areas along Eglinton Avenue West, into the study's analysis of water, sewer, hydro and road capacity. The study shapes how the area around Glencairn grows, so the renaming and broader data would affect how residents see their neighbourhood represented in planning.

title: Ensuring Transparency and Accountability in the Mayor’s Office - by Councillor Brad Bradford, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: accountability, mayor; office of the mayor
brief: Toronto residents would again be able to watch the Mayor's press conferences live online, including the full question-and-answer session with media, if this motion passes. City Council is being asked to request that the Mayor resume livestreaming these availabilities — a practice the motion says was standard for nearly a decade — and to give all councillors and their staff access to attend them. The change would affect how the public and elected officials see and hear the Mayor's announcements. The decision rests with Council making the request to the Mayor's office.

title: Accepting a Donation from Spin Master for Sumach-Shuter Parkette Playground Enhancements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: donation, parks, playgrounds; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, bequest; toy drive, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: A $50,000 cash donation from Spin Master would pay for upgraded play equipment at Sumach-Shuter Parkette, a park at 485 Shuter Street in a dense, high-need neighbourhood next to the Regent Park Athletic Grounds. City Council decides whether to accept the gift, which would be budgeted at $50,000.00 and fund a modernized, inclusive playground as part of a wider park plan that also adds an off-leash dog area, picnic areas and seating. The parkette is heavily used by families living in the surrounding towers, so the upgrade would mainly benefit local children.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.IE14.4 - Cycling Network Plan - 2024 Cycling Infrastructure and Missing Sidewalk Installation - Third Quarter Update - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: cycling, sidewalks; bicycling
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2024.IE14.4 and remove two planned bike lane segments — on Elm Ridge Drive and on Marlee Avenue between Castlefield Avenue and Eglinton Avenue West — and to pause the Beltline Gap Connection project while the Growing Marlee-Glencairn study completes a broader transportation and mobility plan for the corridor.

title: Support for the Canadian Tire Jumpstart Multi-Year Sport Court Refurbishment Initiative - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: basketball, recreational facilities, sports; recreation facilities; recreational amenities
brief: This motion from the Mayor asks City Council to accept a cash donation of up to $3.5 million over five years (2025–2030) from Canadian Tire Jumpstart Charities to refurbish outdoor basketball and multi-sport courts across Toronto, prioritizing high-equity-need areas. The partnership aligns with the City's Parks and Recreation Facilities Plan and state-of-good-repair priorities.

title: Save Toronto’s School Pools - Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: funding, schools; community use of schools; educational institutions; school cafeterias; school classrooms; school gymnasiums, financing
brief: This member motion asks City Council to request that the Ontario government fund the continued operation of school pools in Toronto District School Board facilities for student swim classes and community use. The motion notes that provincial funding provided in 2009 is no longer available, and the school board's rigid funding formula provides no money for aquatic facilities.

title: Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan - Multi-Use Trail Study Delivery Agreement - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: trail systems; footpaths; multi-pupose trails; multi-purpose paths; multi-use pathways; multi-use trails; pedestrian trails; recreational trails; trail networks; trails; walking paths; waterfront trail
brief: This member motion asks City Council to authorize an agreement with the Bentway Conservancy, up to $201,000, to fund a gap analysis and conceptual design for a proposed 7-kilometre multi-use trail under the Gardiner Expressway from Dufferin Street to the Don Valley Parkway.
