The study is an implementation priority of the Under Gardiner Public Realm Plan endorsed by Council in April 2024.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Support Non-Profit Affordable Rental Housing Property Acquisition - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: rental housing, reserve funds; rental properties; rental units, reserves and reserve funds
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $1,200,000.00 to the Housing Secretariat capital budget, funded by developer community benefits, to help the Kensington Market Community Land Trust buy a 26-unit affordable rental building (with 10 commercial units) in Ward 11. The Trust has raised substantial funds, including $1,600,000 in previously approved City funding for eight units; the new funds would fill the remaining gap so the purchase can close next month.

title: Remediating Flooding and Minimizing Flood Vulnerable Areas Associated with Taylor-Massey Creek near Eglinton Avenue East between Birchmount Road and Kennedy Road
topics: culverts, flooding, remediation; brownfields remediation; rehabilitation (property); site remediation; soil remediation, floods
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Manager work with the TTC, the Toronto Region Conservation Authority, and developers on a strategy to fix flooding from Taylor-Massey Creek near Eglinton Avenue East between Birchmount Road and Kennedy Road. An undersized culvert under the CN rail line causes the floodplain to spill in major flood events; provincial, City, and conservation policies block new development in floodplains, limiting redevelopment until the flood hazard is remediated.

title: Unwin Avenue Bailey Bridge Replacement Study
topics: bridge rehabilitation, capital budgets, transportation; bridge reconstruction; bridge repair, transportation services
brief: Up for endorsement at City Council: replacing the temporary single-lane Bailey bridge on Unwin Avenue in the Port Lands with a new two-lane bridge design, so detailed design and construction can move forward. The 17-year-old bridge, built in 2008, came under pressure in 2024 when the Ship Channel bridge closed for emergency repairs. The replacement is a near-term improvement ahead of a future realignment of Unwin Avenue.

title: Authorization to Amend and Extend the License Agreement with High Park Initiatives
topics: agreements, licences, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, licenses; licensing, tenancy agreements
brief: City Council faces a decision on extending the licence agreement with High Park Initiatives — the charity that runs the High Park Nature Centre — for 10 years from August 1, 2025 to July 31, 2035, with a further option to extend. The amendment would formalize the charity's use of a new outdoor nature education space and the building at 440 Parkside Drive during the Forest School renovation, and adjust the annual licence fee.

title: Support for Grants and Incentives Program - Expanding the Urban Forest on Private Lands
topics: environmental incentive programs, subsidies and grants, tree canopy; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs, green rebate program; toilet replacement programs; washer rebate programs; water rebate program; watersaver programs, tree canopy cover; tree cover
brief: Whether to renew authority for the Urban Forestry Grants and Incentives Program, which funds tree planting and stewardship on private land through partnerships with residents, landowners, and organizations is before City Council. The program supports Council's target of 40 per cent tree canopy cover by 2050; 55 per cent of the city's land is privately owned. Staff would be able to collect resident information to run the program and would apply for federal funding.

title: Transitioning Towards Zero-Emission Outdoor Power Equipment
topics: air pollution, by-laws, greenhouse effect; bylaws, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: Choosing an approach for moving gas-powered outdoor equipment — such as two-stroke leaf blowers and hedge trimmers — toward zero-emission options goes to City Council for approval. In July 2023, staff found the individual impacts of two-stroke equipment did not justify a ban; Council instead supported exploring a ban as a precaution against cumulative health and climate impacts from noise and air pollution. This report sets out an implementation approach and next steps if the City proceeds, based on stakeholder consultation, a jurisdictional scan, and equipment and market analysis. The report prices the two paths: without a ban, about $200,000 over 2026 to 2030 for City equipment transition and education campaigns (with about $25,000 a year after that, to be reviewed in 2030); with a ban, about $2,880,000 in start-up and program costs over 2026 to 2030, then about $675,000 a year from 2031.

title: Proposed Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 669, Climate Change Goals and Governance
topics: climate change, greenhouse effect, municipal codes; climate protection, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: City Council faces a decision on amending the Climate Change Goals and Governance by-law to extend the deadline for the next short-term net-zero action plan to the end of 2025, giving staff more time to complete the 2026–2030 plan. The extension is linked to the Building Emissions Performance Standards report expected in the third quarter of 2025; Toronto's target is net zero community-wide emissions by 2040.

title: Recommended Strategies to Address Prematurely Failing Water Meter Transmission Units
topics: strategic plans, water, water meters; remote water meters, strategic planning; strategy
brief: Whether to adopt a strategy for replacing the City's rapidly failing water meter transmission units — devices from sole supplier Aclara that send water meter readings — and to keep the detailed strategy confidential during negotiations is before City Council. Aclara units are manufactured in Mexico and shipped to Canada. Confidential instructions to staff would be made public at the City Solicitor's discretion.

title: Watermain Replacement and Sidewalk Construction on York Downs Drive from Bathurst Street to Sandringham Drive - Amendment to the Plans for Construction Project 25ECS-LU-02SU
topics: sidewalk repairs, sidewalks, watermains; mains; water mains, roadside repair; sidewalk brick installation; sidewalk brick maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalk ramping; sidewalk replacement; sidewalks maintenance; walkway maintenance; walkway repair
brief: Removing the proposed new sidewalk construction on York Downs Drive (Bathurst Street to Sandringham Drive) from the 2025 construction contract, after a survey found 19 of 20 affected residents opposed the sidewalks goes to City Council for approval. Watermain replacement on the street would proceed.

title: Air Conditioner Pilot Program for Low-Income Seniors
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, low income groups, seniors; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems, elderly; geriatric; older adults; senior citizens, in need; low income; low income families; low income households; low income individuals; low income residents
brief: Whether to approve a summer 2025 pilot providing up to 500 portable air conditioners to low-income seniors in multi-unit buildings whose medical needs are worsened by extreme heat is before City Council. Units would be allocated through a randomized draw with a one-window intake system and outreach from community partners; the program is a mayoral priority funded in Budget 2025.

title: Delegation of Development Review Related Authorities for Consolidated Linear Infrastructure Environmental Compliance Approvals
topics: construction, stormwater management, wastewater; building, sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water, storm water management; swm; wet weather flow management
brief: This is a procedural item: letting the Executive Director of Development Review designate staff to sign environmental compliance forms on the City's behalf under the province's new consolidated approval process for wastewater and stormwater systems goes to City Council for approval. The City's development review staff were consolidated under the new Development Review division in September 2024. No policy change is proposed.

title: Requesting a Fair Consultation Process Regarding the North York Centre Secondary Plan
topics: Secondary Plans, meetings, public consultation; community consultation; consultation; public hearing
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Lily Cheng (Ward 18, Willowdale) is asking for a fair consultation process on the review of the North York Centre Secondary Plan now underway. The inquiry follows resident concerns that the engagement survey was overly long and technical, outreach was limited, and responses did not reflect broader community priorities.

title: The Development of the Proposed Demonstrations By-law
topics: by-laws, protests; bylaws, demonstrations; protest marches
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Alejandra Bravo (Ward 9, Davenport) is asking City staff for basic facts about the development of the proposed demonstrations by-law to protect vulnerable institutions — including potential cost, legal risk, and overlap with existing laws — ahead of Council discussion.

title: Service Agreements Awarded and Executed by the Medical Officer of Health for 2025
topics: contracts, health, services; health coverage
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is receiving, for information, the list of 2025 service contracts the Medical Officer of Health awarded to community agencies — covering Healthy Babies Healthy Children, food security, sexual health, dental care for street-involved youth and low-income adults, and the Ontario Seniors Dental Care program. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2025 Student Nutrition Program Service Subsidies
topics: [activities in health], nutrition, students; diet; dieting; healthy eating
brief: City Council is being asked to authorize the 2025 Student Nutrition Program subsidy allocations, totalling $31,020,579, so municipal funds can flow to school food programs across Toronto. The money goes to two administering organizations — $5,508,378 to the Angel Foundation for Learning and $25,512,201 to the Toronto Foundation for Student Success — with $1,448,575 held in reserve for fall applications and appeals, including equipment and start-up supplies for new programs. The item is before the Board of Health on its way to Council. City Council decides.

title: Award of Doc4755698985 to Carla Construction and Maintenance Ltd., for Operation and Maintenance of a Passenger Transportation Shuttle Service for High Park and other Potential Parks
topics: parks, purchasing, transportation; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, transportation services
brief: City Council is being asked to authorize a licence agreement with Carla Construction and Maintenance Ltd., chosen through a 2024 request for proposals, to operate and maintain a passenger shuttle service in High Park, with room for similar agreements at other parks later. Under the licence, the company would pay the city 15 per cent of gross revenue (before HST) and operate the service at no cost to the city. The initial term is five years starting with April 2026 operation, with two optional five-year extensions, supporting the High Park Movement Strategy with an environmentally friendly, accessible service to key destinations in the park. City Council decides.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Purchase Order 6052384 with OnX Enterprise Solutions Ltd for Wiring, Cabling and Hardware for the Provision of Wireless Internet Services at Various Shelter Locations
topics: emergency housing, purchasing, wireless internet; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), wi fi; wifi; wireless hotspot
brief: Adding $1,250,000 ($1,272,000 net of HST recoveries) to the non-competitive OnX Enterprise Solutions purchase order for wiring, cabling and hardware bringing wireless internet to shelter locations, raising it from $248,400 ($252,772 net of HST recoveries) to $1,498,400 ($1,524,772 net of HST recoveries) and extending delivery from April 2026 to April 2028, past the normal five-year term goes to City Council for approval. The service must stay with OnX and cannot be sourced competitively, according to the report. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Contract 47023030 with A Supreme Nursing and Home Care Services Inc., for Nursing Services at Various Shelter Locations
topics: emergency housing, long term care homes, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), homes for the aged; long term care centers; long term care centres; long term care facilities; nursing facilities; nursing homes
brief: Up for approval at City Council: adding $100,000 ($101,760 net of HST recoveries) to the non-competitive nursing services contract with A Supreme Nursing and Home Care Services for city shelters, raising it from $800,000 ($814,080 net of HST recoveries) to $900,000 ($915,840 net of HST recoveries) and extending it to April 30, 2026, past the normal five-year term. The extension keeps nursing services running in directly operated shelters while a new competitive procurement finishes. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Nominal Sublicense Agreement with Malvern Family Resource Centre for Use of a Portion of the Finch Hydro Corridor as a Community Garden
topics: community centres, community gardens, leasing, utility corridors; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes, hydro corridors; hydro rights of way; rail corridors; rail rights of way, leases
brief: On the agenda at City Council: approving a nominal five-year sublicense, with an option for five more years, letting the Malvern Family Resource Centre keep running its community garden on about 2. 6 acres of the Finch Hydro Corridor near Morningside Avenue and McNicoll Avenue. The centre has operated the garden there since 2021 under the city's community gardens pilot program, serving the Malvern neighbourhood. City Council decides.

title: Toronto Zoo Community Conservation Centre - Lease With University of Toronto Scarborough
topics: conservation, environmental programs, facilities, zoos; environmental conservation; environmental improvements; environmental management; environmental protection; environmental stewardship; greening, environmental initiatives; green living
brief: The Toronto Zoo's board is recommending that City Council authorize negotiating a lease letting University of Toronto Scarborough use dedicated and shared lab and classroom space at the Toronto Zoo Community Conservation Centre for post-secondary programs. The deal is subject to finishing a land transfer between the City and the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority. City Council decides.

title: Overview of Security Practices for Employee Access Card Photos
topics: access requests, city-owned properties, security; city owned properties; city properties, foi requests; freedom of information requests
brief: This is a follow-up report on city employee security card photo practices, responding to the committee's earlier request: it summarizes current procedures for issuing and replacing access cards and the steps taken to protect the photo process, with security-sensitive details kept in a confidential attachment. City Council is asked to direct that the confidential information stay confidential. City Council decides.

title: Payments Modernization Framework
topics: city initiatives, finance (sc), payment; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, paying; payment information; payment methods; payment options; pre-authorized payment plans; pre-authorized plans; preauthorized payments
brief: City Council is being asked to adopt the City's Payments Modernization Framework: policy objectives to guide how the city designs payment options for a diverse, multi-generational population, based on research into how Torontonians pay the city — from digital methods to cash, cheques and banks. City Council decides.

title: Application for Approval to Expropriate Temporary Easements for the Mid-Town Toronto Storm Sewer Relief Project - Stage 1
topics: easements, expropriations, storm sewers; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, stormwater sewers
brief: Starting the first stage of expropriating temporary easements at 239 and 243 Hillhurst Boulevard and 595 St. Clements Avenue for the Mid-Town storm sewer relief project goes to City Council for approval. If adopted, owners get 30 days to request a hearing on whether the taking is fair, sound and reasonably necessary, and staff would return with a stage-two report on property values and costs. City Council decides.

title: Expropriation of Property Interests at 320-326 Bloor Street West for the Spadina Station Streetcar Platform Extension - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, land acquisition, properties (real estate), streetcars, transportation; compulsory purchase; eminent domain, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions, property; real estate, street-cars, transportation services, ttc
brief: Up for approval at City Council: the second stage of expropriating permanent and temporary easements at 320-326 Bloor Street West to extend the Spadina Station streetcar platform for two low-floor light rail vehicles, part of the TTC's Line 2 capacity program. City Council decides.

title: Expropriation of Portions of Properties at the Rear of Jolly Way and the Rear East Side of Jenkinson Way for the Scarborough Rapid Transit Bus Replacement - Stage 2
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, buses, construction, expropriations, land acquisition, real estate transactions; building, city buses; coaches (buses), compulsory purchase; eminent domain, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions, ttc
brief: Whether to approve the second stage of expropriating temporary easements at the rear of Jolly Way and the rear east side of Jenkinson Way for a dedicated bus roadway, part of the TTC's Scarborough Rapid Transit bus replacement and busway program is before City Council. No one requested an inquiry into the taking during the first stage. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Acklands-Grainger Inc., for Supply and Delivery of Various Industrial Supplies, Equipment and Services for Various City of Toronto Divisions
topics: contracts, materials, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, commodities; goods
brief: Approval of a non-competitive one-year bridge contract with Acklands-Grainger Inc is before City Council. for industrial supplies, equipment and services used by divisions including Toronto Water, Solid Waste, Parks and Forestry, Paramedic Services, Fire Services and Fleet, valued at $3,053,675 ($3,107,420 net of HST recoveries) from May 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026. The bridge keeps existing terms in place while longer-term arrangements are sorted out. The source documents also list $12,248,846 and $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with G.C. Duke Equipment Limited for the Provision of Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Service for Parks and Recreation
topics: maintenance, purchasing, transportation equipment; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: City Council faces a decision on approving a non-competitive one-year contract with G.C. Duke Equipment, the only authorized Ontario dealer for proprietary Ransomes Jacobsen and Cushman mower parts and service, at $854,771 ($869,815 net of HST recoveries) from August 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026, with four optional one-year extensions. Parks and Recreation must use original manufacturer parts to keep warranties valid on its mowers. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Circular Materials Ontario for Authority to Pay Producer Obligation Fees the 2024 Reporting Year
topics: blue bin materials, fees, services; administrative fees; admission fees; admission prices; rates; service charges; user charges; user fees, single stream recyclable materials
brief: On the agenda at City Council: approving a non-competitive contract with Circular Materials Ontario, a producer responsibility organization, to manage the city's producer obligations and 2025 Blue Box fee payments under provincial regulation, for one year with an optional one-year renewal. The non-competitive route reflects the province's transition to extended producer responsibility and the need to stay compliant on fee payments. The source documents list $500,000 and $1,000,000. City Council decides.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Zamboni Company Limited for Proprietary Original Equipment Manufacturer Parts and Services for Parks and Recreation
topics: arenas, facilities, ice rinks, maintenance, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, airs (rinks); civic centre ice rinks; hockey rinks; ice pads; ice surfaces; natural ice rinks; nirs; rinks; skating rinks, indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: Up for approval at City Council: a non-competitive five-year contract with Zamboni Company Limited, the only authorized dealer for proprietary Zamboni ice resurfacer parts and service, at $1,423,534 ($1,448,588 net of HST recoveries) from November 1, 2025 to October 31, 2030. Parks and Recreation must use original manufacturer parts to keep mower and resurfacer warranties valid. The source documents also list $500,000. City Council decides.

title: Award of Doc4769714345 to Royal Bank of Canada for Banking Services for the City of Toronto
topics: agreements, finance (sc), proposals; bids; request for proposal; rfp, tenancy agreements
brief: Whether to award the city's banking services contract to the Royal Bank of Canada, the highest-scoring supplier, for an initial five-year term from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2030, valued at $10,882,907.87 ($11,074,447.04 net of HST recoveries). If the city exercises two optional five-year extensions, the total potential value is $32,648,723.60 ($33,223,341.14 net of HST recoveries) The committee decides on the award.

title: 1736 and 1746 Weston Road - Non-Residential Demolition Application
topics: commercial properties, demolitions; office real estate; retail space
brief: Two commercial buildings could be torn down. Council is asked to approve demolishing the existing commercial buildings at 1736 and 1746 Weston Road, where no replacement building permit has been issued, on condition the owner beautifies the site with clean fill, landscaping, and a construction fence, under the former City of York demolition control by-law.

title: 1798, 1800, 1802, 1804, 1806, 1808, and 1812 Weston Road - Rental Housing Demolition Application- Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: Six rental units could be demolished for a 40-storey tower. Council is asked to approve demolishing six rental units at 1806 and 1812 Weston Road to make way for a new 40-storey development, on condition that six replacement rental units are provided on the site for at least 20 years. The report cites a $20,000.00 figure.

title: 720 Humberwood Boulevard - Reallocation of Section 37 Benefit Contribution
topics: by-laws, development; bylaws, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: A $53,250 developer contribution is being redirected. Council is asked to redirect the $53,250 Section 37 contribution at 720 Humberwood Boulevard from building a parking lot at Indian Line Park, which was never built and is no longer needed, toward playground equipment and related work in the park. The contribution was secured under By-law 477-2010 for a 9-single and 62-semi-detached home development.

title: 1798-1812 Weston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 40-storey tower is proposed for Weston Road. Council is asked to approve a zoning change for 1798-1812 Weston Road to allow a 40-storey mixed-use building with 490 homes and ground-floor shops, with a building hold until servicing and sewer-clearance requirements are met, and six rental units replaced. The proposal includes about 327 square metres of non-residential space.

title: St. Clair Avenue West - Pay-and-Display Parking
topics: [activities in transportation], parking machines; pay and display machines; pay-and-display machines
brief: Paid parking is coming to a St. Clair layby. Council is asked to approve new paid on-street parking in an existing layby on St. Clair Avenue West in Ward 5, replacing current no-parking restrictions, to encourage parking turnover and support nearby businesses and the community. The Toronto Parking Authority and Transportation Services identified the spot together. TTC transit service requires council approval.

title: Dundas Street West at Dundas Street West - Traffic Regulation Amendments
topics: change, traffic regulations; amendments; conversion; modification
brief: Turn rules are being updated at a Dundas Street West intersection. Council is asked to update lane markings and turn rules at the Dundas Street West intersection, including removing the no-right-turn-on-red rule for northbound traffic and designating the easterly northbound lane as right-turn-only, to match conditions on the ground. TTC transit service on the street requires council approval.

title: 2595 St. Clair Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: More homes are proposed on St. Clair Avenue West. Council is asked to approve planning changes for 2595 St. Clair Avenue West to allow an 11-storey mixed-use building plus a 20-storey tower with 505 homes, ground-floor commercial space, and a public plaza, with the site classed as a noise area under provincial guidelines. The proposal includes 2,453 square metres of commercial space and a 355-square metre privately-owned publicly accessible space.

title: Thistle Down Boulevard - Parking Amendments
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations; no parking, parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: The Thistle Down Boulevard parking changes return. Council is asked to prohibit parking at all times on the inner loop of Thistle Down Boulevard and update parking rules on the outer circle, so parked cars do not block buses using the new speed cushions. TTC transit service on the street requires council approval.

title: Permanent Closure of a Portion of Montesson Street
topics: road closures, transportation (sc); street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Part of Montesson Street could become park space. Council is asked to permanently close part of Montesson Street, an untravelled section of road, so the land can be transferred to Parks and Recreation for building new park space. Permanent closure of public highway requires council approval.

title: Assumption of Services Fernbrook Homes (Lawrence) Limited, 66M-2569, 14 110017 WET 12 SB, Wild Rose Gardens, Creekbank Road
topics: assumption of services, municipal services; city services
brief: The city is taking over roads in a Fernbrook subdivision. Council is asked to formally take over the roads and municipal services in the Fernbrook Homes subdivision at Wild Rose Gardens and Creekbank Road (Plan 66M-2569, dated August 2019), release the developer's performance guarantee, and pass an assumption by-law.

title: 21-25 Windsor Street, 18 Buckingham Street, 60 Newcastle Street and 95 Portland Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, emergency housing, official plan amendments, rezoning; emergency shelters; homeless shelters; hostels (homeless), re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Three development blocks near Mimico are being planned. Council is asked to approve planning changes for three blocks near Windsor, Buckingham, Newcastle, and Portland Streets: a 36- and 42-storey mixed-use building with 933 homes, retail, office space, and a private childcare centre; a 14-storey building with 184 affordable co-op homes; and a third block detailed in the report. The proposal includes over 1,117 new homes.

title: Adjustments to Capital Budget, Carry Forward Funding and Future Year Commitments
topics: capital budgets, funding; financing
brief: Unspent 2024 capital money is being rolled forward. City Council is asked to approve an additional $250.3 million in carry-forward funding from unspent 2024 capital projects into the 2025-2034 capital budget and plan, bringing the total carry-forward to $1.689 billion, plus in-year budget adjustments. With the previously approved $1.438 billion in carry-forward, the total adjusted 2025 Tax and Rate Supported Capital Budget would be $6.098 billion.

title: Leaside Memorial Community Gardens: City Loan Agreement; 2020, 2021 and 2022 Settlement
topics: arenas, loans; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: A community arena's loan deal is being tidied up. City Council is asked to approve a combined settlement of Leaside Memorial Community Gardens' 2020 to 2022 operating results and to amend the city loan agreement for the second ice pad, supported by a tri-partite agreement with Infrastructure Ontario, so that loan prepayments from excess revenues do not create an operating deficit. The report cites a $7.3 million figure in connection with the loan arrangement.

title: City of Toronto’s 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan
topics: assets, management (sc);
brief: The city's infrastructure report card is up for approval. City Council is asked to adopt the city's 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan, covering 11 classes of municipal infrastructure assets, and to approve submitting it to the province by the July 1, 2025 regulatory deadline under Ontario Regulation 588/17. The report cites infrastructure asset values of $215 billion, figures of $26 billion and $18 billion, and gap figures of $26.0, $17.9 and $8.1. The plan guides how the city manages the infrastructure residents rely on.

title: 2025 Update on SafeTO Implementation
topics: funding, programs; financing
brief: The city's ten-year safety plan gets a check-in. City Council is asked to request that staff continue advancing SafeTO, Toronto's 10-year community safety and well-being plan, and to report back with a progress report in 2027, with the update also forwarded to the Toronto Police Service Board. The update covers Phase 1 outcomes from 2022-2024 and Phase 2 priorities for 2025-2027, responding to disparities in violence, crime, and well-being across neighbourhoods. The financial impact section cites $60.6 million for the plan's Phase 1 (2022–2024) implementation.

title: Management Update: Auditor General Recommendations on 9-1-1 Operations and Responses to Calls for Service by the Toronto Police Service
topics: emergency services, police services, safety; 9-1-1; 911; 911 calls; emergency assistance; emergency response, police; policing, public safety
brief: This is a procedural item: staff report an update on the Auditor General's recommendations to improve 9-1-1 operations and Toronto Police Service responses to calls for service, stemming from 51 recommendations across two 2022 reports. Council is asked to forward the update to the Toronto Police Service Board.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Lower Don Bridge and Minton Place Portal - Temporary Lane Closures on the Don Valley Parkway and F.G. Gardiner Expressway and Temporary Delegation of Authority
topics: construction, expressways; building, municipal highways
brief: Overnight highway lane closures are needed for Ontario Line construction. City Council is asked to amend the temporary highway closing bylaw to delegate authority to the General Manager, Transportation Services, to temporarily close lanes of the Don Valley Parkway and Gardiner Expressway overnight for Ontario Line bridge and slope stabilization work in 2025 to 2027, including the Lower Don Bridge and the Minton Place Portal.

title: Ontario-Toronto New Deal - Advancing the Delivery of Transit Oriented Communities along the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension
topics: public transit, transit routes; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, surface routes
brief: City land along the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension could go to the province. City Council is asked to approve transferring city-owned lands to Metrolinx or another provincial body to support transit-oriented communities along the extension, in line with Ontario-Toronto New Deal commitments. The New Deal, reached in November 2023, included over $4 billion in financial supports to the city. The city-owned lands are estimated to be worth between $137 million and $160 million.

title: Legal Services Resourcing to Expedite Priority Affordable Housing Projects
topics: affordable housing, legal matters; affordable homes; housing projects, legal issues
brief: More city lawyers could speed up affordable housing deals. City Council is asked to request that the City Solicitor assign more legal resources to speed up agreements for priority affordable housing projects, set target timelines for legal work on housing files, and report on resourcing needs through the 2026 budget process. Legal Services is a key partner in delivering the dozens of priority affordable housing projects on city land.

title: Status update of funding from the Federal and Provincial Governments for FIFA World Cup 2026
topics: financial reports, sports, sports tournaments; annual financial reports; financial statements, tournaments
brief: Who pays for the World Cup is still an open question. The Executive Committee is asked to request that the World Cup hosting executive director report directly to the May 21 to 23, 2025 council meeting on the status of federal and provincial funding for hosting the FIFA World Cup 2026. Council has restricted tournament expenses to $340 million until savings or federal and provincial funding cover the full $380 million budget without affecting the property tax base. The item cites figures of $380 million, $2 billion, $1.3 billion, $700 million, $460 million and $100 million in connection with tournament costs and funding.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
topics: sports, sports tournaments; tournaments
brief: The World Cup buying plan is being updated. City Council is asked to direct staff to proceed with the updated procurement plan for goods and services needed to deliver the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Toronto, and to authorize negotiating and entering contracts with vendors listed in the confidential attachment. The plan covers capital and operational services previously approved in November 2024.

title: Federation of Municipalities (FCM) March 2025 report to Council
topics: elections, meetings; polls (elections); voting
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Ainslie introduces the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board report from March 2025, covering advocacy ahead of the 2025 federal election, including FCM's push for a National Prosperity Partnership across priority areas. Council is asked to receive it for information.

title: Amendment to Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 219, Records, Corporate (Local Boards) Respecting  Swansea Town Hall Community Centre
topics: community centres, municipal codes; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes

title: Approval of Recommended Retention Schedule for Accountability Records for the Auditor General's Office
topics: accountability, municipal codes, records;
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to amend the Accountability Officers bylaw to establish a records retention schedule for the Auditor General's Office, since city records cannot be destroyed without an approved retention schedule under the City of Toronto Act.

title: Toronto Water 2024 Year End Capital Budget and 2025-2034 Capital Plan Adjustments
topics: capital budgets, costs;
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to authorize reallocating $32.378 million and $6.871 million in cashflows within Toronto Water's 2024 capital budget and 2025-2034 capital plan, to match project delivery schedules, with zero impact on the overall budget.

title: Improved Active Transportation and Water Access to Toronto Island Park
topics: tourism, transportation; transportation services
brief: Getting to Toronto Island Park could get easier. City Council is asked to convene a Toronto Island Access and Inner Harbour Transportation Task Force to coordinate short- and medium-term improvements to reaching the island, and to advance due diligence on long-term options including a fixed link across the Eastern Gap. The island draws over 1.5 million ferry riders and about 485,000 water taxi trips a year, so access changes affect residents and tourists alike.

title: Changes to the Rogers Road Business Improvement Area Board of Management
topics: business improvement areas, public appointments; bia; business improvement associations
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to appoint Sonia Martinho to the Rogers Road Business Improvement Area Board of Management, in accordance with the city's public appointments policy. The BIA spans two wards.

title: Economic Development and Culture Grants - 2024 Funding Allocation and Creative Industries Grants
topics: arts and culture, funding, subsidies and grants; financial assistance; financial incentives; financial subsidy; grant and subsidy programs; grant programs; grants; grants programs; incentives; subsidies; subsidy and grant programs, financing
brief: A new grants program for the creative industries is before council. Council is asked to establish a Creative Industries Grants Program with two funding streams, for skills development and sector development, and to authorize staff to allocate and disburse one-time grants to eligible individuals and non-profit organizations. The program aligns with the city's cultural and economic priorities.

title: Access to Outdoor Ovens in Toronto Parks
topics: [activities in public safety and protection], [objects in property], parks, public health; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Community groups could soon use park ovens for free. Council is asked to remove the booking fee for community use of outdoor ovens in city parks, making the fee zero, and to approve a revised Outdoor Ovens in City Parks Policy to reduce barriers to their use. The review follows council direction to reduce administrative and financial barriers while ensuring public health and safety.

title: Scarborough Bluffs West Project: Environmental Assessment Agreement - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: The Scarborough Bluffs West project needs a formal environmental assessment agreement. The member motion asks council to authorize the City Manager to sign an agreement with the Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks, as a co-proponent with the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, to apply the Environmental Assessment Act to the project. Council allocated $2.912 million from the Toronto Water Capital Reserve to the project in December 2021, and the study will explore enhancing and protecting sensitive shoreline and natural areas.

The legal strategy is kept private.

The City Solicitor recommends council receive it for information.

Confidential details are kept private.

title: Proposed By-law Amendment to Provide Access to Social Infrastructure
topics: by-laws, change, protests; amendments; conversion; modification, bylaws, demonstrations; protest marches
brief: Changing the streets and sidewalks bylaw to address harassment near vulnerable institutions goes to Council for approval. The proposed amendment to Chapter 743 would support the city's commitment to keeping people safe from harassment near places of worship, faith-based schools and cultural institutions, and would take effect July 2, 2025. It follows a December 2024 council direction for a report informed by public consultation and a constitutional legal opinion. Staff anticipate up to $200,000 for public education, communication and outreach about the change, managed within the City Manager's Office 2025 operating budget.

title: Status Update on City Activities Related to the Therme Spa Project
topics: projects, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail

The report advises that the City Manager will submit a report to the May 21-23, 2025 council meeting on all city activities related to the Therme spa project at Ontario Place, in response to a member motion asking staff to report back on the project and the city's public waterfront.

The investigation began after Municipal Licensing and Standards' response to an urgent service request was questioned.

brief: Ward 25 Scarborough-Rouge Park is losing its councillor and council must decide how to fill the seat. title: Cancellation, Reduction or Refund of Property of Taxes or Payment in Lieu of Taxes - May 12th, 2025
topics: hearings, property taxes, ratepayers; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, taxpayers
brief: This is a procedural tax item: the General Government Committee is asked to decide on property tax appeal applications for cancellation, reduction or refund of taxes or payments in lieu of taxes, covering the May 12, 2025 batch. The law allows relief when a property is destroyed or demolished, becomes tax-exempt, changes use, or was overcharged through an assessment error, and the committee must hold a public meeting before deciding. The General Government Committee decides.

title: Apportionment of Property Taxes - May 12, 2025 Hearing
topics: hearings, property taxes, ratepayers; municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts, taxpayers
brief: This is a procedural tax item: the General Government Committee will hold its May 12, 2025 hearing on three property tax apportionment applications, which divide unpaid taxes from severed land onto the newly created parcels. The law requires the committee to hold a public meeting where affected owners can appear before deciding. The committee has delegated authority to make the final decisions.

title: Status update of funding from the Federal and Provincial Governments for FIFA World Cup 2026
topics: funding, sports, sports tournaments; financing, tournaments
brief: Councillor Mike Colle recommends the FIFA World Cup 2026 Subcommittee ask the Executive Director, FIFA World Cup 2026, Toronto Secretariat, to report to the Executive Committee on May 13 on the status of federal and provincial funding for the tournament. A Deloitte Canada study estimates hosting the FIFA World Cup 2026 could generate up to $3.8 billion in economic output for Canada between June 2023 and August 2026, including $2 billion in GDP, $1.3 billion in labour income and $700 million in government revenue, plus 24,100 jobs created or preserved. The source documents also list $460 million and $100 million in funding figures.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: Procurement Plan Update
topics: sports, sports tournaments; tournaments
brief: City Council is being asked to direct the Executive Director, FIFA World Cup 2026, Toronto Secretariat, and the Chief Procurement Officer to proceed under the updated procurement plan for planning and running the tournament: contracts awarded so far, plus requests to negotiate and award items listed in a confidential attachment. The recommendations cover capital and operational services previously approved by Council, and awarded procurements will be made public as soon as doing so does not hurt competitiveness. The item is before the FIFA World Cup 2026 Subcommittee on its way to Council.

The item asks the Accessibility Advisory Committee to recommend that transportation staff attend its June 23, 2025 meeting to explain what they plan to do about snow removal and its impact on people with disabilities. The motion states that the slow clearing left streets and sidewalks impassable and disproportionately affected people with disabilities.

The committee's accessibility feedback will feed into the final policy.

title: Growing Space for Trees: Protecting and Enhancing the Tree Canopy While Supporting Infill Housing and Addressing Concerns with Iceberg Homes - Proposals Report
topics: infill development, tree canopy; infill housing; infilling; residential infill, tree canopy cover; tree cover
brief: Protecting the tree canopy while allowing infill housing is the goal of this proposals report. The report proposes Official Plan changes to give trees growing space as new housing is built, which would shape what homeowners and builders can do with lots across the city.

Public consultation would lead to final recommendations in early 2026.

title: Automated Vehicle Pilot Deployment in Toronto Under the Highway Traffic Act
topics: motor vehicle safety regulations, motor vehicles, pilot projects; vehicles
brief: Having staff report back by late 2026 on findings from Magna's provincially approved pilot testing driverless last-mile delivery vehicles on Toronto streets, and on what the City can learn about automated vehicles goes to City Council for direction. The City has no regulatory authority over the pilot but submitted comments on safety.

The Toronto and East York Community Council makes the final decision.
