brief: This is a procedural item: Metrolinx presents an update on the Ontario Line subway project, including early works at the Exhibition Place site. The line will add 15.6 kilometres of new subway service from Exhibition Place in the west to the future Eglinton Crosstown LRT at Don Mills Road and Eglinton Avenue East. The board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: License Agreement West Annex Team Space
topics: Exhibition Place, leasing, licences; leases, licenses; licensing
brief: Team space in the West Annex is also being renewed. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve a new ten-year-and-eleven-month licence agreement with Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment for team space in the West Annex of the Enercare Centre, running August 2024 to June 2035, subject to city approval. The licence runs alongside the existing sublease arrangements for the space.

title: Lease of West Annex Office Space
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, leasing; leases
brief: A long-term office tenant is staying put. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve a new ten-year-and-eleven-month lease with Maple Leaf Sports and Entertainment for office space on the second floor of the West Annex of the Enercare Centre, running August 2024 to June 2035, subject to city approval. The current lease, dating to 2013, is in overhold.

title: HVAC Upgrades at the General Services Building
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems
brief: Heating and cooling at the General Services Building needs replacing. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve a $669,868.00 contract to Bird Infrastructure Ltd. for HVAC upgrades, since the existing unit is past its useful life, awarded to the lowest compliant bidder among five submissions. The project is time-sensitive because HVAC equipment has a long delivery time. The report also cites a $20,000.00 figure.

title: Horse Palace Riding Ring Upgrade
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, horseback riding, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, riding rings; riding stables; riding trails; stables
brief: The horse-riding ring at the Horse Palace Building is getting an upgrade. The Exhibition Place board is asked to approve a $463,443.76 contract to Greenspace Construction Inc. for the Horse Palace Riding Ring Upgrade, awarded as the only compliant bid. The project is time-sensitive because the ring is heavily used year-round. The report also cites a $15,000.00 figure.

title: 2024 Capital Works Program - Year End Report
topics: Exhibition Place, budgets, capital budgets, property maintenance; budgets and accounts, grounds maintenance; groundskeeping
brief: This is a procedural item: staff report the final progress of the 2024 Capital Works Program, with a total budget of $49,268,618 covering state-of-good-repair projects and BMO Field improvements for the FIFA World Cup. The budget breaks down into $20,080,000 in Exhibition Place-managed state-of-good-repair projects, a $3,791,143 cash-flow carry-forward from 2023, and $25,397,475 in non-Exhibition Place-managed service improvements for BMO Field in support of Toronto hosting the FIFA World Cup 2026. The board is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Strategic Plan - 2024 Key Results and Initiatives
topics: Exhibition Place, strategic plans, work plans; strategic planning; strategy
brief: This is a procedural item: staff report highlights of Exhibition Place's 2024 achievements, the third year of its 2022-2026 strategic plan, including 2,029 events and over 5.5 million attendees. The board is asked to receive the report for information; no decision is attached.

title: Proposed Collective Agreement with The United Association of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe Fitting Industry of the United States and Canada, Local Union 46
topics: Exhibition Place, labour relations, plumbing, unions; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, labour unions; trade unions, master shut-off valve; water pipes
brief: Another labour deal is before the Exhibition Place board. The board is asked to approve the terms of a new three-year collective agreement (2025-2027) with the United Association of Journeymen and Apprentices of the Plumbing and Pipe Fitting Industry, Local Union 46, based on the memorandum of settlement the union ratified on March 24, 2025. The previous agreement expired December 31, 2024.

title: Emergency Generator Replacement at the General Services Building
topics: Exhibition Place, contracts, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems
brief: A new backup generator is needed at Exhibition Place's General Services Building. The board is asked to concur with the earlier approval of a $694,786.00 contract to Superior Boiler Works and Welding Limited to replace the emergency generator, awarded to the lowest compliant bidder through the tender process. The project is time-sensitive because generator delivery takes a long time and the current unit is critical to operations. The report also cites a $100,000.00 figure.

title: Summary of Legal Disputes - 2025 First Quarter Update
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: A request to direct that its first-quarter legal disputes update stay fully confidential, since it contains litigation advice covered by solicitor-client privilege goes to the Toronto Parking Authority board. The disputes relate to supplier issues, personal injuries, commercial tenancies and trademark protection across the authority's operations.

title: Delegation of Authority Update
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to receive for information the update on decisions the President made under delegated authority. The President can make commitments up to $500,000 (raised from $250,000 in 2021) and award non-competitive contracts up to $250,000. No policy change is proposed.

title: Proposed Amendments - Toronto Parking Authority Policy Resolutions 2-1: Parking Rates - Off-Street Facilities and 2-3: Monthly Parking Permits
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: Its off-street parking rate policy so the President can adjust rates by up to 25 percent as needed, instead of only through annual reviews, would be amended, if the Toronto Parking Authority board agrees. Management says yearly rate changes put the authority at a competitive disadvantage against private operators who can change prices day-to-day. The policy guides pricing for North America's largest municipally owned commercial parking operator.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2025 March 31 Year-to-Date Financial Performance (First Quarter Results)
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: financial reports, parking, revenue generation; annual financial reports; financial statements, revenue tools
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to receive for information its first-quarter 2025 financial results. Net income was $8.4 million (+$1.2 million versus plan); revenue was $37.8 million (-$1.3 million versus plan), with transactions at 80.6 percent of pre-pandemic levels and February's snowstorm hitting 47 percent of on-street inventory; operating costs were $26.5 million ($2.0 million below plan); finance income was $0.9 million; amortization was $0.6 million below plan. Capital spending was $2.1 million, on track for a $55.6 million annual plan supported by $25.8 million in city funding for Bike Share and EVs. No policy change is proposed.

title: 2024 Capital Review and 2025 Plan
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to receive for information the review of 2024 capital spending and the 2025 capital plan. Total 2024 capital spending was $57.1 million (80.1 percent of budget); authority-led spending was $36.2 million, beating the $35.6 million target by $0.6 million; 91 percent of projects finished on time or early and 93 percent on or under budget, for a favourable cost variance of $2.37 million. The report also references $55.6 million. No policy change is proposed.

title: Toronto Parking Authority - 2024 Audited Financial Statements
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: Its 2024 audited financial statements — which received a clean audit opinion from KPMG — go to the Toronto Parking Authority board for approval, with a recommendation that city council approve them as well. The statements cover North America's largest municipal parking operator, with over 25 million transactions in 2024, plus Bike Share Toronto (6.9 million rides) and an EV charging network of over 450 chargers that generated over $1.1 million in revenue.

title: Toronto Parking Authority 2025 Board Audit and Risk Management Committee Terms of Reference and 2025 Work Plan
body: Toronto Parking Authority - Audit and Risk Management Committee
topics: parking;
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto Parking Authority board is asked to receive for information the 2025 work plan and terms of reference for its Audit and Risk Management Committee. No policy change is proposed.

title: 111 Peter Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rental housing, zoning bylaws; rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 52-storey mixed-use tower with 852 homes is proposed at 111 Peter Street, keeping the existing building, with 3,888 square metres of non-residential space. The owner would provide 24 affordable rental homes as part of the development. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East Phase 1 - Official Plan and  Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Three already-approved towers at 215 Lake Shore Boulevard East would grow by five storeys each — from 49, 39 and 14 storeys to 54, 44 and 15 — adding 114 homes. About 16 additional affordable rental homes would be delivered in Phase 2. Approval would amend the Official Plan and zoning. The item lists $85,000 in secured benefits. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 315-325 Front Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: housing, zoning bylaws; homes; residences, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Zoning changes would allow a four-building mixed-use development at 315-325 Front Street West with 1,793 homes and a large office building, built in three phases: two residential buildings of 50 storeys, one residential building of 71 storeys, and a 60-storey office building. The site was previously approved in 2022 for a different mix with 832 homes and more office space. The item lists secured community benefit amounts of $150,000.00, $1,250,000, $250,000 and $1,000,000.00. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 707 Dundas Street West and 327 Bathurst Street - City-initiated Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A city-initiated plan change would redesignate the Scadding Court Community Centre and Sanderson Library lands — at 707 Dundas Street West and 327 Bathurst Street — from Parks to Mixed Use Areas. The change would enable redevelopment of the city facilities with additional non-residential and residential uses, including affordable housing, without reducing parkland in Alexandra Park. Approval would amend the Official Plan. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Dovercourt Road - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws
brief: Parking rules on Dovercourt Road would be adjusted, including no-stopping zones near Hallam Street and Geary Avenue and changes to permit parking, after residents reported vehicles blocking access to their cars. Residents say parked vehicles have trapped them for hours waiting for drivers to move or for enforcement. Full council approval is requested.

title: Design Revision to the Woodbine Cycle Track
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, public transit, transportation; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, transportation services, ttc
brief: Staff would be directed to remove the concrete curbs along the east side of the Woodbine Avenue cycle track between Danforth Avenue and Strathmore Boulevard, so TTC shuttle buses can serve Woodbine station more easily during subway outages. The TTC has had operational trouble running shuttle buses at Woodbine station during recent planned and unplanned subway outages. Full council approval is requested.

title: Amending existing Zoning By-law Section 37 Schedules to Facilitate Purchase of Community Space in the Church-Wellesley Village
topics: zoning;
brief: Staff would be directed to prepare by-law changes so developer-paid Section 37 funds in Ward 13 can be used to buy and improve community space for non-profits in the Church-Wellesley Village, mainly serving the 2SLGBTQ+ community. The goal is a long-term home for organizations worried about staying in the neighbourhood, and a chance to buy a building has come up. Staff are evaluating the property's value. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 152-164 Bathurst Street and 623-627 Richmond Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rentals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 29-storey mixed-use building with 362 homes, including nine affordable rentals, is proposed at 152-164 Bathurst Street and 623-627 Richmond Street West. The site was previously approved in 2023 for an 18-storey building with 216 homes and no affordable units; the new plan adds homes near transit. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 158 Sterling Road (Blocks 5B, 5C and 5D) and 190 Sterling Road (Block 3B) - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning; bylaws, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Two mixed-use towers of 28 and 31 storeys, with 349 and 396 homes respectively, are proposed at 158 and 190 Sterling Road, plus a small non-residential building. The 28-storey building would include a 62-space childcare centre, about 928 square metres, conveyed to the City as a community benefit. Approval would amend the Official Plan and zoning. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Accessible Parking Space - April 2025 (Non-Delegated)
topics: accessible permit parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled)
brief: The April 2025 list of on-street accessible parking spaces to be added or removed for people with disabilities needs full council approval because the TTC runs transit on the streets involved. No wider policy change is proposed.

title: Corridor Safety Review Update - Mortimer Avenue, between Pape Avenue and Broadview Avenue
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, public transit; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, ttc
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to receive an update on the safety review for Mortimer Avenue between Pape and Broadview avenues, covering the directives council gave in October 2024. Because the TTC runs transit on Mortimer Avenue, full council approval is required. No policy change is proposed.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2530, 11 286680 STE 17 SB, Somerset Wallace Developments Ltd., Sousa Mendes Street, Macaulay Avenue Extension, Wallace Avenue Subdivision
topics: agreements, assumption of services, subdivision (land); subdivision of land, tenancy agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to formally take over the municipal services in the Wallace Avenue subdivision, including Sousa Mendes Street and the Macaulay Avenue extension, built by Somerset Wallace Developments under its subdivision agreement. The City would assume the roads and services and release the developer's performance guarantee. No policy change is proposed.

title: 78 and 80 Nassau Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The 1885-era houses at 78 and 80 Nassau Street are up for the City's Heritage Register. The semi-detached pair in Kensington-Chinatown was identified as contributing properties in the Kensington Market Heritage Conservation District plan, adopted in February 2025, and reflect the area's immigrant history. Listing recognizes their heritage value but does not ban future changes. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 120 Peter Street, 122-124 Peter Street, 126-128 Peter Street and 357-359 Richmond Street West - Alterations to, Demolition and Construction of, Buildings under Sections 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: buildings, construction, demolitions, heritage properties; building, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Changes to heritage properties at 120, 122-124 and 126-128 Peter Street and 357-359 Richmond Street West, part of a new 40-storey mixed-use building in the King-Spadina Heritage Conservation District, go to Council for approval. The work would alter the Victorian row house at 120 Peter Street (the John Holdford House), demolish other buildings, and update the heritage easement agreement. The Margaret Grimmon Houses at 357-359 Richmond Street West are contributing heritage properties in the district.

title: 847-855 Kingston Road - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of a proposed 11-storey mixed-use building with 99 homes and retail at 847-855 Kingston Road appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed its decision deadline. The proposal replaced an earlier 7-storey plan after the developer bought the neighbouring property. Council is asked to send city lawyers to oppose the current proposal while talks continue.

title: 50-64 Merton Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of an approved 45-storey mixed-use building at 50-64 Merton Street — with 603 homes and partial retention of the heritage Girl Guides of Canada building — appealed the implementing by-laws to the Ontario Land Tribunal. The by-laws were held back while the developer met servicing and heritage requirements. Council is asked to send city lawyers to oppose the appeal while talks toward a resolution continue.

title: 309-311 and 349 George Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: A heritage conservation plan for the City-owned properties at 309-311 and 349 George Street -- the Robert Armstrong Houses and the Allan School -- in the Garden District Heritage Conservation District goes to Council for approval. The plan supports the proposed 10-storey institutional building at 309-349 George Street. Heritage rules require council's permission to alter or demolish buildings in the district.

title: 309-349 George Street - City-Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The City itself proposes a 10-storey institutional building at 309-349 George Street with 180 municipal shelter beds, 124 long-term care beds, 70 affordable rental homes with supports, and a 2,269-square-metre community hub. The project is a core part of the Downtown East Action Plan and replaces a 2017-approved plan for a larger site. Approval would amend the Official Plan and zoning. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 1212-1220 Yonge Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 126.85-metre, 35-storey mixed-use building with 273 homes and 320 square metres of shops is proposed at 1212-1220 Yonge Street. The tower would total 20,873 square metres of space. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 54-70 Brownlow Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rentals, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 59-storey residential building is proposed at 54-70 Brownlow Avenue, with a publicly accessible landscaped walkway forming part of a future mid-block connection through to Redpath Avenue. Nine existing homes would be demolished, two of them rentals; the rental demolition is handled separately by the Chief Planner. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 43, 44 and 45 Price Street - Demolition of Buildings Within the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and Approval of Replacement Buildings
topics: buildings, demolitions, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Three 'Unrated' buildings at 43, 44 and 45 Price Street, within the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District, would be demolished to make way for the Toronto Lawn Tennis Club expansion. Heritage rules require council's permission; the district plan allows demolition of 'Unrated' buildings when the replacement designs follow its guidelines. The replacement would be a new 3-storey clubhouse and a small single-storey building.

title: 30, 40, 43, 44 and 45 Price Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The Toronto Lawn and Tennis Club at 30-45 Price Street would be reconfigured and expanded with a new 3-storey addition. The east end of the existing building and the two houses at 43 and 45 Price Street would be demolished; the 'pavilion' on the west side and the outdoor courts would stay. Approval would amend the zoning by-law. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 522 University Avenue - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes at a Designated Property under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Alterations and partial demolition of the heritage National Life Building at 522 University Avenue are proposed as part of a 64-storey development. The 1971-1974 building, designed by John C. Parkin, is an example of Monumental Modernist architecture. The redevelopment would integrate it as a podium, keeping key heritage parts under a heritage easement agreement. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 522 University Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: heritage properties, zoning bylaws; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Approval of a 64-storey mixed-use building with 579 homes and 21,413 square metres of shops and offices at 522 University Avenue is on the agenda, keeping part of the existing heritage building. The zoning change would allow the taller tower. Before the by-law can pass, the owner must submit revised engineering and servicing reports. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Ensuring Safety for the Ontario Line Construction -  Ward 14
topics: construction, safety; building, public safety
brief: A request for a City Manager report on safety around Ontario Line construction in Ward 14 goes to the Toronto and East York Community Council. The request follows a February incident in which a contractor's truck, off its approved haul route, struck a resident at Mortimer and Pape, causing life-altering injuries, raising community concerns about the years-long project.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Streetcar Service Diversions during King Street East and Church Street Intersection Closures
topics: parking regulations, public transit, streetcars, traffic regulations; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, parking by-laws; parking bylaws, street-cars
brief: Temporary transit-priority measures, including a reserved streetcar lane on Queen Street East, are proposed while the King Street East and Church Street intersection closes for watermain and streetcar-track maintenance from May to August 2025. The 503 Kingston Road, 504 King and 508 Lakeshore routes would be diverted, with streetcars on Queen Street east of Spadina rising from seven to 25 in peak hour. The measures are meant to limit the impact on about 102,900 daily customers. The measures are expected to cost about $60,000 to put in place, funded through the TTC's 2023-2032 capital budget. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Council Member Appointment to Fill a Vacancy on the Association of Municipalities of Ontario Board of Directors
topics: appointments, boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to recommend a council member to fill a vacant seat on the Association of Municipalities of Ontario board, after a councillor resigned. The appointment would run until November 2026. Council makes the final appointment.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities Board of Directors
topics: appointments, boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to recommend two council members for the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board of directors, for a term running from the June 2025 annual meeting to the 2026 meeting. Council makes the final appointments.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Canadian National Exhibition Association, Municipal Section and Board of Directors
topics: appointments, boards of management; boards of directors; boards of governors
brief: This is a procedural item: the Striking Committee is asked to recommend five council members for the Canadian National Exhibition Association's municipal section and board, for a one-year term starting spring 2025. Council makes the final appointments.

title: 5933 and 5951 Steeles Avenue East - Alterations to Heritage Properties and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: heritage designation, heritage designation;
brief: Alterations to two designated heritage houses at 5933 Steeles Avenue East (Underwood House) and 5951 Steeles Avenue East (William Stonehouse House) go to City Council for approval, along with a Heritage Easement Agreement protecting them. The changes relate to a larger approved development on the 7.3-hectare site at 5883-5951 Steeles Avenue East for industrial and limited commercial uses. Heritage Planning staff say the alterations conserve the heritage buildings.

title: 1 Fallingbrook Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Approval of alterations to the designated heritage property at 1 Fallingbrook Road, a Queen Anne Revival house protected under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act is before City Council. The proposal adds a contemporary addition at the north and east elevations. Heritage Planning staff say the changes conserve the property and council permission is required under Section 33 of the Act.

title: 1925 Victoria Park Avenue - Public Art Plan
topics: art programs, public art; art classes; art workshops; arts programs, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: Approval of the public art plan for the development at 1925 Victoria Park Avenue is before City Council. The plan outlines how the owner will commission public art integrated into the north-facing building facade, and it meets the City's Percent for Public Art Guidelines with support from the Toronto Public Art Commission. Approval is a condition of the development.

title: 2221 and 2223 Kennedy Road and 3, 5 and 7 Collingwood Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City staff recommend approving Official Plan and zoning changes to allow three four-storey townhouse buildings with 68 homes at 2221-2223 Kennedy Road and 3-7 Collingwood Street. The buildings would total about 7,700 square metres with one level of underground parking. Council would amend the planning rules to permit the project.

title: 2655 Lawrence Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City staff recommend approving zoning changes to allow two residential towers of 18 and 28 storeys plus eight townhouses at 2655 Lawrence Avenue East, for a total of 412 homes with 1,609 square metres of ground-floor commercial space. Council approved the same permissions in 2018 but the by-law was never enacted, and the old Section 37 community-benefits regime has since been replaced by the Community Benefit Charge framework. Council would amend the zoning by-law to permit the project.

title: Winter Maintenance on Heathfield Drive Path
topics: maintenance, winter;
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks City Council to direct staff to provide regular winter maintenance on the Heathfield Drive Path, between Hill Crescent and Sylvan Drive. The path is a high-volume walking route connecting residents to transit and the Waterfront Trail. Transportation Services has reviewed and supports the request.

title: East Avenue - Road Safety Review
topics: road safety, safety; public safety
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to receive for information a road safety review of East Avenue near William G. Davis Junior Public School. Staff completed the review after community council requested it. No policy change is proposed.

title: Manse Road - U-Turn Prohibition
topics: traffic calming, turn prohibitions (traffic);
brief: Transportation staff recommend banning U-turns in both directions on Manse Road between Hainford Street and Deanscroft Square, to make the street safer near Joseph Brant Public School. Because the TTC runs buses on Manse Road, city council approval is required. Council is asked to approve the ban.

title: Finch Avenue East and Baylawn Drive - Temporary Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic regulations, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: Approval of temporary traffic signals at Finch Avenue East and Baylawn Drive, from May 1, 2025 to December 31, 2031 is before council. The signals are needed during Metrolinx's construction of a rail-over-road grade separation at the Stouffville Rail Corridor. Because the TTC runs buses on Finch Avenue East, city council approval is required.

title: Scarborough Busway - On-Street Measures to Support Busway Operations
topics: bus routes;
brief: Approval of road changes to support the Scarborough Busway, the dedicated bus route converting the former SRT right-of-way between Kennedy Station and Ellesmere Station is before council. The changes include a new traffic signal at Eglinton Avenue East and the future Busway, priority bus lanes near Kennedy Station, and extended Ellesmere Road bus lanes. The busway is projected to open in 2027.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the order paper, the list of items to be considered at the meeting. No decision is being asked for.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements are made during the meeting. No decisions are being asked for.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council may file petitions during the meeting, to be received for the record. No decision is being asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is being asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: committee chairs and the mayor introduce committee reports and new business from the mayor and city officials — including reports from the Executive, Civic Appointments, Economic and Community Development, General Government, Infrastructure and Environment, Planning and Housing and Striking committees and the four community councils. No decision is being asked for.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from its regular meeting held on March 26 and 27, 2025, as an accurate record.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the council meeting begins with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is being asked for.

title: Swansea Mews Initial Development Proposal
topics: development, proposals; bids; request for proposal; rfp, developing land; development (land); land development
brief: Swansea Mews, the 154-unit Toronto Community Housing property at the Queensway and Windermere Avenue, is moving toward redevelopment after a structural failure emptied the site. Council is being asked to approve the initial redevelopment proposal, which would demolish the uninhabitable stacked townhomes across the 5.3-acre property and revitalize the site. Residents were relocated offsite under an Emergency Order in June 2022, so the decision starts the path to new homes on the land.

title: Toronto's Academic Housing Strategy - Improving Housing Outcomes for Post-Secondary Students
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: Student housing in Toronto would get a coordinated plan under the Academic Housing Strategy. Council is being asked to adopt the strategy, developed with post-secondary institutions after a December 2022 council direction, with a five-year implementation plan and annual updates. It sets a framework for the City, other governments and schools to act on student housing needs, which affects students competing for rentals across the city.

title: Authority to Enter into Municipal Housing Project Facility Agreements with Community Housing Providers
topics: agreements, housing; homes; residences, tenancy agreements
brief: Council votes on adding a new chapter to the city's rulebook for housing programs and entering into municipal housing project facility agreements with community housing providers, supporting the upkeep and operation of existing community housing. This builds on the Community Housing Sector Modernization and Growth Strategy adopted in June 2024 and its focus on partnerships with providers facing expiring mortgages.

title: 1 Dundas Street East: Amendments to the Sign By-law
topics: change, signs; amendments; conversion; modification, signage
brief: Council amends the Sign By-law to replace the old Yonge-Dundas Square name in the regulations and simplify the sign permit process. The 2017 rules for the square cover five electronic ground signs and two electronic roof signs mixing advertising, event and art displays, so this affects how the square's high-profile signage is managed.

title: 750, 752, and 756-758 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Four adjacent properties at 750, 752, 756 and 758 Yonge Street are proposed for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate all four under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. If no objections come in, formal designation by-laws can follow.

title: Implementation Guidelines for Rental Replacement
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: The rules for what happens to tenants when rental buildings are demolished are getting a rewrite. Council is being asked to adopt the Rental Replacement Handbook as the new implementation guidelines for calculating rent gap assistance and applying tenant protections under Chapter 667 for rental housing demolitions that require replacement. This is the handbook staff would use for every rental replacement application, so it shapes outcomes for displaced renters.

title: 7-9 Wardlaw Crescent - City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: apartments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A four-storey building with 51 affordable rental homes and on-site support services could rise in Rexdale. Council is being asked to approve a city-initiated zoning change for 7-9 Wardlaw Crescent to allow the 15-metre apartment building with wrap-around supports. The project is part of the city's delivery of affordable housing under the Official Plan, and would bring new supportive homes to the Rexdale neighbourhood.

title: 2 Tippett Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: official plan amendments, residential tenants, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City staff would fight a 33-storey tower proposal at 2 Tippett Road at the Ontario Land Tribunal. The applicant submitted Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment applications in August 2024 for a 103.15-metre residential building with 417 homes, plus a trail setback from W.R. Allen Road and a mid-block pathway, then appealed to the Tribunal on December 30, 2024 after Council did not decide in time; a case management conference is set for March 26, 2025. Staff recommend Council instruct the City Solicitor and staff to attend the hearing in opposition to the proposal in its current form while continuing to discuss resolving the issues. The outcome affects what gets built on the site.

title: 3377 Bayview Avenue, Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, driveways, subdivision (land); application process, subdivision of land
brief: City Council is being asked to approve a draft plan of subdivision at 3377 Bayview Avenue that would create 10 blocks: six residential development blocks, two park blocks, one green space natural heritage block of 13.764 hectares, and one block retained by Tyndale University, which would continue operating as a university. The proposal includes a new 18.5-metre public road looping through the site from Bayview Avenue, entering at the existing northern driveway and reconnecting at Benham Crescent. Staff say the development is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and conforms to the Official Plan and Zoning By-law (to be issued by the Ontario Land Tribunal). Future residents and Tyndale University would be affected.

title: 150 The Donway West and 4 Overland Drive - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, housing, rentals; homes; residences
brief: Ten two-bedroom rental homes at 150 The Donway West and 4 Overland Drive would be converted to one-bedroom units to connect the existing and proposed buildings. North York Community Council is asked to approve the Rental Housing Demolition application — the units would be replaced in the proposed 15-storey building, with a Tenant Assistance Plan securing existing tenants' right to move to a replacement unit of the same type at a similar size and rent — and the item's figures list $20,000.00. The approval would let the related 230-home infill development proceed.

title: Naming Recommendation for a Parcel of Land within Lawrence Park Ravine to "Jaye Robinson Park"
topics: facility naming, naming, parkettes, parks, public realm; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, park naming, public spaces
brief: A parcel of land in Lawrence Park Ravine would be named Jaye Robinson Park to commemorate the late Councillor Jaye Robinson's public service, activism and impact. The naming follows City Council's June 2024 request through item MM19.6 to find a park, street, trail or landmark to honour her; parks staff worked with the local councillor to pick the ravine parcel. North York Community Council is asked to receive the report for information. Park users would see the new name.

title: Duncan Mill Road - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, pedestrian infrastructure, road safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo, pedestrian network
brief: A pedestrian crossover on Duncan Mill Road, about 200 metres east of Lesmill Road, would not be installed. Transportation Services found the warrant criteria were not met, so City Council is asked not to authorize the crossing; if Council approves it anyway, three City-owned trees in the boulevard in front of and opposite 99 Duncan Mill Road would be removed. Pedestrians crossing Duncan Mill Road would be affected.

title: 230 and 240 The Donway West - Exclusion of the Development from the Permit Parking Program
topics: development, parking, permits; developing land; development (land); land development, permit renewal
brief: The development at 230 and 240 The Donway West would be excluded from the on-street overnight permit parking program if permit parking is ever introduced on the street or in the area. City Council is asked to amend Municipal Code Chapter 925 so Transportation Services will not accept applications from residents, visitors or tradespersons at that address, after staff found the exclusion feasible and had no objections. Residents of the development would be affected.

title: 150 The Donway West and 4 Overland Drive - Zoning Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: mid rise buildings, rezoning, zoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Two new rental apartment buildings with 230 homes would be approved at 150 The Donway West and 4 Overland Drive. City Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for a 15-storey (50.8-metre) Building A and a nine-storey (39.1-metre) Building B, with about 17,500 square metres of new residential gross floor area (28,108 square metres total, floor space index 2.99), 199 vehicle parking spaces — 177 residential, 19 visitor and 3 pick-up and drop-off — in a three-level underground garage, and 385 bicycle parking spaces. Future renters of the 230 homes would be affected.

title: 18A Downsview Park Boulevard - Introduction of Overnight On-Street Permit Parking - Permit Area
topics: parking, permit parking, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads), on-street permit parking; parking permits
brief: Overnight on-street permit parking would be introduced on Downsview Park Boulevard between George Butchart Drive and Stanley Greene Boulevard, from 12:01 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., within Permit Area 18A. City Council is asked to move the existing and proposed permit parking to the north side to accommodate road operations, after residents requested the parking to meet long-term needs. Drivers on Downsview Park Boulevard would be affected.

title: 1 Broadlands Boulevard - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Decision Report - Approval
topics: construction, parking, rezoning; building, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A three-storey apartment building with 21 homes would be approved at 1 Broadlands Boulevard in North York. City Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the 10.30-metre building, with 1,183.4 square metres of gross floor area, a density of 0.98 times the site area, 603.28 square metres of landscape area, 10 vehicle parking spaces (including 3 visitor) and 22 bicycle parking spaces, with access from Broadlands Boulevard. Staff say the gentle intensification is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and conforms to the Official Plan. Future residents of the 21 homes would be affected.

title: Working With MLSE Foundation to Explore Feasibility of Reimagining Weston Lions Arena - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: arenas; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff work with the MLSE Foundation and local residents to explore reimagining the 75-year-old Weston Lions Arena as a potential MLSE LaunchPad site offering free youth recreation programming. The downtown LaunchPad at 259 Jarvis Street has delivered free sport, life-skills, and academic programming since 2017.

title: Time for Outdated Park Rules to Touch Grass - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff review the parks by-law and report in late 2025 with recommendations to remove outdated or unnecessary rules, and with options to expand food and beverage offerings in parks. The motion cites examples such as rules against ball playing, kite flying, and cursing, and suggests kiosks and small cafés tailored to park size and use.

title: Committee of Adjustment and Tenancy Information - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have future Committee of Adjustment applications disclose whether residential tenants are expected to be displaced if the application is approved, so the information is publicly posted. The motion also seeks standard tenant notification of applications — currently only owners are notified by mail — and would build on a similar question added to the building permit process.

title: Seasonal Prohibition on Lithium-Ion Battery Powered E-Bikes and E-Scooters on the TTC and the Feasibility of Providing More Secure E-Bike and E-Scooter Storage and Battery Charging and Exchange Facilities near Transit Stations - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: bicycles, electric scooters; bikes, go peds; go-peds; motorized scooters; scooters
brief: This member motion asks City Council to study secure e-bike storage and battery charging and exchange facilities near TTC stations, and to develop an e-bike policy for enclosed TTC spaces. The TTC Board banned lithium-ion battery devices, including e-bikes and e-scooters, until April 15, 2025, after a December 2024 battery explosion and fire on a subway train; the motion notes the ban disproportionately affects food delivery workers.

title: Enhance Oversight of Special Occasion Permits for Non-Profit Organizations - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: This member motion asks City Council to request that the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario add a municipal approval step to its Special Occasion Permit process for non-profit organizations, following complaints about large-scale events — described as rave parties — run by some non-profits. The motion seeks a municipal complaint process and local oversight in event planning to address public safety, overcrowding, and noise concerns.

title: Spirit of York Distillery Co. By-the-Glass Permit Application to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: This member motion asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that it supports Spirit of York Distillery Co.'s application for a by-the-glass sales licence at 12 Trinity Street.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Public Realm and Laneway Improvements to Lane S Eglinton W Glen Cedar in the Humewood-Cedarvale Neighbourhood - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: funding, lanes, neighbourhoods (planning); financing, traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: This member motion asks City Council to release Section 37 funds totalling $210,000 to Transportation Services for laneway construction on Lane S Eglinton W Glen Cedar in Humewood-Cedarvale — funded by $116,826.37 from the 1996–2000 Bathurst Street development and $93,173.63 from the second development listed in the motion — to transform the laneway into a public space with a new retaining wall, decorative fencing, planting, and permeable surfaces.

title: Preservation of Architectural Character in Cliffcrest Community - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: environment (sc);
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff review development guidelines in the Cliffcrest community and create design guidelines reflecting the area's architectural character, in response to concerns about rapid development removing trees and changing drainage. The motion covers the Cliffcrest community from Scarborough Village to Markham Road.

title: Dog Off-Leash Area at Glendora Park - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have Parks and Recreation consult the community on options for a dog off-leash area at Glendora Park in Willowdale, including a seasonal off-leash area on the toboggan hill from spring to fall. Willowdale has only one off-leash area, at Bayview Arena Park; the city has 81 off-leash areas with 13 more in development.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2024.MM24.13 - Preservation of Architectural Character in Guildwood Community - to Extend the Scope of the Architectural Character Study - by Councillor Parthi Kandavel, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2024.MM24.13 and extend the architectural character study for the Guildwood community to also cover Cliffcrest and Scarborough Village, to address concerns about development removing trees, covering permeable land, and changing drainage in an area with a high water table. The study would guide City Planning, Engineering, and the Scarborough Committee of Adjustment on growth parameters.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2024.CC18.10 295 Jarvis Street - Zoning By-law Amendment and Official Plan Amendment Applications - Request for Direction Report - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2024.CC18.10 and give the Chief Building Official authority to enter a limiting distance agreement with the owners of 311 and 319 Jarvis Street, to keep adequate tower separation near the approved 295 Jarvis Street development. Staff lacked authority for some agreements contemplated in the 2024 settlement; the motion is needed to issue the final order.

title: Supporting the Construction of the Armenian Youth Centre - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: This member motion asks City Council to enter a municipal capital facility agreement with the Armenian Community Centre of Toronto to support construction of its Armenian Youth Centre at 50 Hallcrown Place. Outstanding development charges, education levies, and cash-in-lieu of parkland total $626,507.00; the agreement would grant relief so the long-planned expansion can proceed this summer.

title: Requiring Vehicle-For-Hire Companies to Provide Emergency Driver Contact Information to Customers and Toronto Police Services - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff consult the vehicle-for-hire industry and recommend by-law changes so that ride-hailing companies must help customers and police reach drivers quickly in emergency situations. The motion cites a March 2025 incident in which a driver left with a five-year-old child still in the car, and the company refused to give the driver's contact information to the mother or police.

title: Charting a Path to a Healing Memorial for the Yonge Street Tragedy - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: memorials; monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff bring forward a plan for a permanent memorial to the 2018 Yonge Street attack in Olive Square Park — which took the lives of 11 people and injured 15 others — including consultation with victims' families and the memorial steering committee, with a report back to the July 9, 2025 Economic and Community Development Committee meeting.

title: Authority to Align and Extend the Existing Ground Leases at Yonge Street and Eglinton Avenue on the Toronto Transit Commission Lands - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: This member motion asks City Council to authorize the TTC, as landlord, to amend the ground leases for the Canada Square site at Yonge and Eglinton so the tenants — Oxford Properties Group and CP REIT — can secure investment to retrofit and modernize the existing buildings at 2180 and 2200 Yonge Street. In 2018, Council authorized a consolidated 99-year ground lease for a phased redevelopment, with the TTC contributing $25 million toward a new bus terminal.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Public Realm and Streetscape Improvements Within the Highland Creek Community Area - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
topics: community improvement plans, reserve funds; reserves and reserve funds
brief: This member motion asks City Council to release Section 37 funds totalling $29,000.00 to Transportation Services for decorative paving and community signage improvements in the Highland Creek neighbourhood — including $24,000 for decorative boulevard paving and banners along the historic Wesleyan Cemetery, with $5,000 also listed in the motion — in partnership with the Highland Creek Community Association.

title: Building Quality Public Parks and Public Spaces in Scarborough North - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-allocate unspent developer community benefits in Scarborough North toward other ward capital projects, and to allow funds to be redirected to another purpose if unused within three years. The motion, drafted and approved by staff, concerns building quality parks and public spaces in Scarborough North.

title: Scarborough Bluffs West Project: Environmental Assessment Agreement - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This member motion asks City Council to authorize an agreement with the Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks to apply the Environmental Assessment Act to the Scarborough Bluffs West shoreline protection project, jointly with the conservation authority. Council allocated $2.912 million from the Toronto Water Capital Reserve to the project in December 2021; the project explores shoreline protection and waterfront access between the Eastern Beaches (Silver Birch Avenue) and Bluffer's Park.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.DM28.1 - 40-60 St. Lawrence Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2025.DM28.1 and remove an inadvertently added condition about an easement from its earlier directions to the City Solicitor on the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing for 40-60 St. Lawrence Avenue. The condition — satisfactory arrangements to release the easement over the western portion of the site — related to possible community space negotiations that never produced a settlement offer.

title: Freezing Development Charges - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: development charges;
brief: This motion from the Mayor asks City Council to reaffirm its request that Ontario let the City freeze annual indexing of development charges, and to authorize a workaround using Section 27 agreements if the province does not agree. Development charges are set to rise 4 per cent on May 1; Toronto's $59 billion 10-year capital plan includes $6.5 billion from development charges, including $1.2 billion for water and sewer infrastructure, about $950 million for roads, $1 billion for parks and community centres, and $950 million for transit.

title: Improving Public Consultation Meetings for Communities - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: public meetings;
brief: This motion from the Mayor asks City Council to direct that any public consultation planned as online-only be held in person when the local councillor or the Mayor requests it in writing. Councillors could direct consultations on matters relating to their ward; the Mayor could direct consultations relating to multiple wards or all wards.

title: 200 Queens Quay West - Encumbrance and Limiting Distance Agreements - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: development, zoning; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: This member motion asks City Council to allow the parkland dedication at 200 Queens Quay West to be encumbered by up to seven below-grade concrete caissons, subject to Parks and Recreation approval and compensation paid to the City. The caissons, 0.7 to 1.4 metres in diameter, supported a former parking structure and lie within the southern half of the future parkland, which must be at least 488 square metres.

title: Authorizing the Wastewater Energy Project at Exhibition Place - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: This member motion asks City Council to authorize Exhibition Place to sign a wastewater energy project agreement with Noventa Energy Partners for thermal energy services at Exhibition Place, replacing aging equipment and supporting the net-zero-by-2040 target. Under the City's procurement rules, Council approval is required for agreements over $500,000 or with terms exceeding five years; the Exhibition Place Board authorized negotiations in April 2024. The agreement is a 30-year, $82 million contract.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.NY17.6 - 589-599 Lawrence Avenue West - Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: zoning;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2024.NY17.6 and update its earlier zoning approval for 589-599 Lawrence Avenue West with a revised bill, so the applicant can complete its funding application to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation. City staff requested the supplementary report to implement the application.

title: Taking a Stand to Protect Ontario Place and Our City’s Public Waterfront - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Manager report on all City activities related to the provincial Therme spa project at Ontario Place, including the status of City-owned land and options for its return to the City. The motion's supporting text says the province exempted the site from an Environmental Assessment, removed the City's planning review authority through a Ministerial Zoning Order, and expropriated City-owned land within the site. The supporting text cites reporting that Therme would need $2.5 billion to build four planned sites (Manchester, Dubai, Washington and Dallas), while the company was found to hold only $1.1 million US in equity and to be losing money — raising doubt it could deliver the spa.

title: 164 Homewood Avenue - Request for the City Solicitor to Appeal the Committee of Adjustment Decision and Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: appeals, buildings;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of variances for a three-storey fourplex at 164 Homewood Avenue and to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose them. The variances would allow 34.8 per cent lot coverage (30 per cent permitted) and 10.65m height (10m permitted); the City Solicitor already appealed on April 17, 2025.

title: Authority to Enter into a Licence Amending Agreement with Toronto Island Bicycle Rental Ltd. - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: agreements, bicycle rentals; bike rentals; quadracycle rentals; tandem rentals, tenancy agreements
brief: This member motion asks City Council to amend the licence with Toronto Island Bicycle Rental Ltd. to remove its exclusive bike rental rights on Toronto Island, so a Bike Share Toronto pilot can launch, and to extend the agreement to 2031. The pilot would bring 200 Bike Share Toronto bicycles to Ward's Island and Hanlan's Ferry Landings; the current licence expires September 30, 2026, and the licensee supports the change. The licensee currently pays $83,000 a year plus two per cent of gross revenue under the licence being amended.

title: Toronto's Dog Off-Leash Strategy: A Citywide Approach to Dogs Off-Leash Areas
topics: city initiatives, dog off-leash areas, public safety & protection (sc); city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, dog parks; dogs off leash parks; dogs off-leash parks; leash free areas; leash free dog walking areas; leash free parks; leash free zones; leash-free areas; leash-free dog walking areas; leash-free zones; off leash areas; off leash parks
brief: Approval of a new citywide Dog Off-Leash Strategy to guide the planning, design, and upkeep of off-leash areas, plus guidance for commercial dog walkers, replacing the 2010 policy is before City Council. Toronto has 81 off-leash areas across 21 wards, with 13 more in development for a total of 94 in 23 wards by 2027; the city may be home to 600,000 or more dogs.

title: Safety Barriers Along the Leaside Bridge - Feasibility Study Update
topics: bridges, research, safety barriers; studies; surveys (research), suicide barriers
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving a feasibility study for information on installing permanent safety barriers on the Leaside Bridge (Millwood Overpass), identified as a high-risk location for suicide. The study evaluates options balancing safety, aesthetics, functionality, constructability, and cost, with next steps to move toward a permanent solution. No policy change is proposed. The preliminary design work, including public consultation, is estimated to cost about $500,000, with funding to be requested through the Transportation Services 2026-2035 capital budget.

title: Basement Flooding Protection Program Status Update
topics: basement flooding, funding, programs; basement flood cleanup; basement flooding response, financing
brief: Speeding up the Basement Flooding Protection Program — and having staff report back through the 2026 budget process on the resources needed for faster delivery — goes to City Council for approval. The program's studies have identified nearly 1,200 projects valued at about $18 billion to reduce urban flooding; at the current pace, eligible projects would take about 50 years to complete. To date, 167 projects have been built, reducing flood risk for an estimated 31,000 properties. Preliminary estimates suggest spending $50 million more a year on construction could speed up delivery by 50 per cent, protecting about 1,000 more properties a year.

title: Dufferin Organics Processing Facility Update and Contingency Processing Capacity
topics: landfills, organics processing facilities, purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders, dumps; garbage dumps; landfill areas; landfill facilities; landfill sites
brief: Whether to let staff secure additional outside organics processing and haulage capacity on a contingency basis, with authority to spend up to $12,500,000, after the Dufferin Organics Processing Facility faced challenges last year is before City Council. The City collects about 168,500 tonnes of organics a year, above the 130,000-tonne combined capacity of its Disco Road and Dufferin facilities. Spending with any single vendor would be capped at $2,500,000 within the $12,500,000 total.

title: Transition of the Blue Box Program to Extended Producer Responsibility: Post-Transition Update
topics: blue bins, service delivery, solid waste management; blue boxes; recycling boxes, solid waste management planning; swm; waste management
brief: Letting staff negotiate long-term contracts for garbage management at City transfer stations — including premium drop-and-load services with haulage to third-party landfills — for up to ten years, ending December 31, 2035 goes to City Council for approval. The report also updates Council on the Blue Box program's shift to producer responsibility from 2026 onward and on the plan to tell residents about service changes.

title: Request for Temporary Delegation to the General Manager, Transportation Services, to Approve Temporary Road Closures Up To and Including 365 Consecutive Days for Toronto Transit Commission Traction Power Upgrade Projects
topics: approval, public transit, road closures; local transit; mass transit; public transport; public transportation; surface transit; transit; transit services; urban transportation, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: City Council faces a decision on letting the General Manager of Transportation Services approve temporary road closures of up to 365 days — for both vehicle and pedestrian traffic — for two sets of construction projects: Easier Access projects through the end of 2026, and Toronto Transit Commission traction power upgrade projects through the end of 2032. Under both delegations, the General Manager would be exempt from the usual requirement to notify the local ward councillor of a pending closure and to report on it if the councillor asks; Community Council's existing authority over temporary closures would be adjusted so it does not cover closures delegated to the General Manager.

title: Congestion Management Plan - 2025 Update
topics: city initiatives, congestion, traffic management; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives, gridlock, traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: Having staff report back on how well traffic measures for Gardiner and King/Church construction are working — and letting the Green Market Acceleration Program broaden its definition of local green technology companies — goes to City Council for direction. The report notes Toronto's population grew by 125,756 in one year, vehicle registrations are up 26 per cent since 2014, and the 5,600-kilometre road network has not expanded in decades. The item also asks Council to approve a one-year, $400,000 contract ($407,040 net of HST recoveries) with pointA to deliver Smart Commute Program services in Transportation Management Associations from May 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.

title: Annual Strategic Capital Coordination Report
topics: capital budgets, traffic management, transportation infrastructure; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: This is a procedural item: the committee is receiving the first annual report for information from the Strategic Capital Coordination Office, created in April 2024 to coordinate infrastructure construction across City divisions, utilities, and partners. No policy change is proposed.

title: Changing the Night of Garbage Collection for the West-End (Ossington/Queen West/College Promenade Areas)
topics: garbage, garbage collection, waste, waste collection; collection (activity); collection routes, collection (activity); curbside garbage collection; garbage pickup, food containers (waste); household garbage; plastic bags (waste); polystyrene (waste); residual solid waste; residual waste; styrofoam (waste); trash
brief: City Council faces a decision on having the General Manager, Solid Waste Management Services consider moving garbage collection in the Ossington, Queen West, and College Promenade areas from Thursday nights to an off-peak evening such as Monday or Tuesday. Residents and businesses say Thursday pickup hurts the patio-season dining experience and the night economy.

title: Enhancing Capital Construction Delivery
topics: capital budgets, construction, infrastructure; building
brief: On the agenda at City Council: directing staff to improve how major construction projects are delivered, through a new project management framework with faster on-site decisions, better community communication, and coordinated procurement. The City's Infrastructure Services area is projected to invest more than $2 billion in capital in 2025 — the largest municipal capital program in Canada — and Engineering and Construction Services now delivers over $1 billion a year, nearly triple the rate of ten years ago. The plan would cost $1.314 million for seven temporary full-time positions to implement and deliver it.

title: Requesting a Transparent, Clear and Fair Consultation Process Regarding the “Proposed Demonstrations By-law to Protect Vulnerable Institutions”
topics: by-laws, legislation, protests; acts, bylaws, demonstrations; protest marches
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Gord Perks (Ward 4, Parkdale–High Park) is asking for a clear and fair consultation process on the proposed demonstrations by-law to protect vulnerable institutions. brief: City purchasing staff will present how they are co-developing a procurement policy to direct more city contracts to First Nations, Inuit and Métis businesses, and will ask the committee for feedback to shape it. This is a consultation item; no decision is requested.

topics: demolitions, heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties

The Preservation Board is being asked to adopt confidential legal directions from the City Solicitor on the property; the details are not public because they concern a legal matter.

title: 43, 44 and 45 Price Street - Demolition of Buildings Within the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and Approval of Replacement Buildings
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board votes on recommending that City Council approve demolishing three Unrated buildings in the South Rosedale Heritage Conservation District and approve replacement designs at 43, 44 and 45 Price Street, related to modernizing the Toronto Lawn Tennis Club at the district's western edge.

brief: The Preservation Board decides whether to recommend that City Council approve alterations, demolition and new construction at 120, 122-124, 126-128 Peter Street and 357-359 Richmond Street West, in a Part V heritage district, for a new 40-storey mixed-use building integrated with new and heritage base buildings, and amend the heritage easement agreement.
address: 120 122-124 126-128 Peter Toronto Ontario; 357-359 Richmond Toronto Ontario
