brief: The question before the Preservation Board: whether to recommend that City Council approve alterations to the designated heritage properties at 5933 Steeles Avenue East (Underwood House) and 5951 Steeles Avenue East (William Stonehouse House), in connection with developing the 5883-5951 Steeles Avenue East site, and authorize a heritage easement agreement.

title: 1 Fallingbrook Road - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 33 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The owner of 1 Fallingbrook Road (known as Edgemon, the Winstanley House), a designated heritage property, wants to alter the building with a contemporary addition at the north and east elevations. The Preservation Board is being asked to recommend that City Council approve the alterations under the Ontario Heritage Act.

title: 309-311 and 349 George Street - Alterations to Designated Heritage Properties under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The question before the Preservation Board: whether to recommend that City Council approve the conservation strategy for 309-311 George Street (a pair of three-storey semi-detached houses known as the Robert Armstrong houses) and 349 George Street, in the Garden District Heritage Conservation District, in connection with proposed Official Plan and zoning changes for the site.

title: 78 and 80 Nassau Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board recommends adding 78 and 80 Nassau Street, a semi-detached pair of house-form buildings on the north side of Nassau Street between Augusta Avenue and Bellevue Avenue in Kensington-Chinatown, to the Heritage Register. Listing flags the properties as historically significant and requires notice before demolition.

title: 450 Rustic Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The Preservation Board votes on recommending that City Council state its intention to designate 450 Rustic Road, on the north side of Rustic Road south of Highway 401 and west of Keele Street, under Part IV of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. Starting the designation process would limit future demolition and alterations to the property.

title: Update from the Medical Officer of Health Hiring Panel
topics: boards of health, health, hiring process, public health; health coverage, hiring; job recall; recruitment; selection
brief: This is a procedural item: the Board of Health is getting an update on the search for Toronto's next Medical Officer of Health. After a search through the end of 2024, the hiring panel — chaired by Councillor Chris Moise and including Mayor Olivia Chow, Councillor Alejandra Bravo, and directors Abinaya Chandrabalan and Stephanie Zhou — is restarting the process with a Ministry-approved enhanced compensation package, aiming for an appointment at the Board of Health on June 3 and City Council approval on June 25. No policy change is proposed.

title: Update on the City of Toronto’s Downtown Homelessness and Addiction Recovery Treatment (HART) Hub
topics: health (sc), health issues, homelessness, public health, substance abuse; alcohol abuse; drug abuse; drug addiction
brief: This is a procedural item: the Board of Health is receiving an update on the City's downtown Homelessness and Addiction Recovery Treatment (HART) Hub. The update follows Ontario's Community Care and Recovery Act, which required five supervised consumption sites in Toronto to close by March 31, 2025; the province also announced $378 million for HART Hubs across Ontario, and the Ministry of Health approved Toronto's downtown hub application in principle on January 2, 2025.

title: Toronto Public Health Capital Budget for the Year Ending on December 31, 2024
topics: budgets, capital budgets, health, public health; budgets and accounts, health coverage
brief: This is a procedural item: the Board of Health is being given Toronto Public Health's 2024 capital budget update for information, covering the year ending December 31, 2024. No policy change is proposed.

title: Toronto Public Health Operating Budget for the Year Ending on December 31, 2024
topics: budgets, health, operating budgets, public health; budgets and accounts, health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is getting an update on Toronto Public Health's operating budget for the year ending December 31, 2024. The acting Medical Officer of Health asks the board to receive the report for information. The Board of Health decides.

title: City Approved Toronto Public Health 2025 Capital Budget and 2026-2034 Capital Plan
topics: budgets, capital budgets, health, public health; budgets and accounts, health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is getting the City-approved Toronto Public Health 2025 capital budget: $4,130 thousand for four projects with $10,023 thousand in future-year commitments, totalling $14,153 thousand, plus a 2026-2034 capital plan of $7,999 thousand for two projects. Key changes from the board's recommendation include adding a Homelessness and Addiction Recovery Treatment Hubs project, postponing the Digital Strategy project and carrying over 2024 cash flow. The acting Medical Officer of Health asks the board to receive the report for information.

title: City Approved Toronto Public Health 2025 Operating Budget
topics: budgets, health, operating budgets, public health; budgets and accounts, health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is getting the City-approved Toronto Public Health 2025 operating budget: $288,575.6 thousand gross and $85,705.5 thousand net, with 1,884 full-time equivalent positions. That is $2,677.5 thousand gross and $2,836.8 thousand net above what the board recommended, cutting 24 positions, and represents a $3,145.4 thousand gross (1.1 percent) and $6,000.0 thousand net (7.5 percent) increase over the 2024 approved budget. The acting Medical Officer of Health asks the board to receive the report for information.

title: Noise Action Plan Update
topics: [attributes in environment], health, noise, noise complaints, noise control, public health; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, health coverage, noise barriers; sound barriers
brief: Toronto Public Health is updating the Board of Health on noise and health, as requested by Council through its Noise By-law review: latest research continues to show excessive noise affects cardiovascular, cognitive, sleep and mental health, though these impacts are smaller than those of other environmental and social health factors. The update notes progress on the 2019 Noise Action Plan after pandemic pauses, including Municipal Licensing and Standards' 2024 by-law review. The Board of Health receives it for information. The Board of Health decides.

title: Environmental and Occupational-Related Cancer Prevention in Toronto: Public Health Actions
topics: [activities in health], cancer, health; health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is being asked to direct the Medical Officer of Health to continue collaborating with city divisions, public health agencies, academic institutions, and community researchers on environmental and occupational cancer prevention. The report covers carcinogens in the environment like traffic and industrial pollution, radon and solar radiation, and workplace exposures under provincial laws, and highlights prevention work including public awareness, complaint response, research participation, law enforcement and advocacy. The Board of Health decides.

title: Update on the Legal Challenge of the Community Care and Recovery Act
topics: health; health coverage
brief: The item asks the Board of Health to receive an update from Toronto Public Health staff on recent developments in the legal challenge of the Community Care and Recovery Act, the provincial law that will close supervised consumption sites in Toronto. The Board of Health decides.

title: Indigenous Wellness Committee: Update
topics: First Nations, health, public health; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, health coverage
brief: The Board of Health is getting an update on the Indigenous Wellness Committee, which Toronto Public Health co-leads with Indigenous organizations after 2023 roundtables with the Toronto Aboriginal Social Supports Council called for it. The acting Medical Officer of Health asks the board to request another progress report by the first quarter of 2026 and to share this report with the city's Indigenous Affairs Office and Social Development division. The Board of Health decides.

title: 250 Dundas Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A tower at 250 Dundas Street West would grow from 49 to 57 storeys, with changes to the building's shape, less office space, and a new 740-square-metre open space including parkland. The plan amendment would secure 962 square metres of affordable housing in place of some of the required office space. Approval would amend the Official Plan and zoning. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Proposed naming of the Public Lane North of Gerrard Street East and East of Greenwood Avenue
topics: laneways; back alleys; mews
brief: A laneway north of Gerrard Street East, east of Greenwood Avenue, would be named 'Luella Price Lane', honouring the founder of the 1910 Eureka Club — a group of Black women that became Ontario's oldest Black women's organization. Local historical societies and the neighbourhood have backed the name since 2017. Council is also asked to waive the usual signature requirement for the naming.

title: 70-86 Lynn Williams Street - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 44-storey mixed-use building with 520 rental homes, including 13 affordable rentals, is proposed at 70-86 Lynn Williams Street, with a public daycare and a public park. The proposal matches a settlement council endorsed in September 2024, and approval would amend the zoning to allow it.

title: East Bayfront Community Recreation Centre Naming
topics: facility naming, recreation centres; park naming, rec centers; rec centres; recreation centers
brief: Staff would work with Treaty partners and Indigenous communities on a formal name for the new East Bayfront Community Recreation Centre, a 25,000-square-foot facility opening in spring 2025. Council is asked to direct the work. A placeholder name is in use until the naming process finishes. Staff would report back in 2026.

title: Improving Bike Lane Inspections in Toronto and East York Community Council district
topics: bike lanes, inspection; bicycle lanes; on street bike lanes, site inspection; viewing
brief: This is a procedural item: the Toronto and East York Community Council is asked to receive a report on how the City inspects and sweeps bike lanes in the district, including improvements to routine and complaint-based inspections, plus enforcement near private construction sites. A city-wide street-sweeping review with bikeway standards would follow in the second quarter of 2025. No policy change is proposed.

title: Permanent Closure of the Public Laneway between 10A Eastern Avenue and 16 Eastern Avenue
topics: laneways, transportation; back alleys; mews, transportation services
brief: A public laneway between 10A and 16 Eastern Avenue would be permanently closed and sold to a neighbouring property owner to improve access and allow future redevelopment. As this is a permanent closure of a public laneway, full council approval is required.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations - Yonge Street and Delisle Avenue/Private Driveway
topics: driveways, traffic signals; fixed time signals; highway traffic signals; pretimed signals; semi-actuated signals; traffic actuated signals; traffic control signals; traffic lights; traffic signal operations
brief: New traffic lights are proposed at Yonge Street and Delisle Avenue, required as a condition of a nearby development at 1-15 Delisle Avenue and 1496-1510 Yonge Street, and staff say the technical case for the signals is met. The work would also remove a westbound left-turn ban at the intersection. Because the TTC runs transit on Yonge Street, full council approval is required.

title: Various Developments to be Excluded from Permit Parking in the Toronto and East York Community Council Area - Non-Delegated
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, enforcement, permit parking; on-street permit parking; parking permits, ttc
brief: Listed new developments would be excluded from the on-street overnight permit parking program, meaning residents, visitors and tradespeople at those addresses could no longer buy overnight parking permits. Because the TTC runs transit on the streets involved, full council approval is required.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - February 2025 (Non-Delegated)

brief: The February 2025 list of on-street accessible parking spaces to be added or removed for people with disabilities needs full council approval because the TTC runs transit on the streets involved. No wider policy change is proposed.

title: Ontario Honda Dealers Indy Toronto Race 2025 - Temporary Street Closures
topics: races, road closures; marathons; runs; walkathons, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Temporary street closures on Lake Shore Boulevard West, between Strachan Avenue and Ontario Drive, and on Strachan Avenue, between Fleet Street and Lake Shore Boulevard West, are proposed for the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy Toronto car race — expected from July 16 to 21, 2025, with July 21 as the rain date. Because the closures involve a motor vehicle race on a major arterial road, full council approval is required.

title: Road Alteration - King Street East at George Street
topics: pavement markings, road closures, signs; arrows (markings); centre lines (pavement markings); edge lines; lane lines; road markings, signage, street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: One eastbound lane on King Street East at George Street would be permanently closed so the space becomes a wider sidewalk with a streetcar stop, serving the development at 175-185 King Street East. The wider boulevard would extend the existing eastbound lane closure to the west at Jarvis Street, and make room for a parking or loading space. Because the TTC runs transit on King Street East, full council approval is required.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - May 1 - September 30, 2025
topics: [events in culture], culture (sc), festivals and special events; community events; community festivals; cultural events; events; festivals
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to grant exemptions from the public-squares rules so listed festivals, cultural celebrations and community events can be held at Nathan Phillips Square from May 1 to September 30, 2025. The list includes organizers such as Pride Toronto, the Toronto Outdoor Art Exhibition and the Philippines Independence Day Council. No policy change is proposed.

title: 55 Eastern Avenue - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, sidewalks, traffic regulations; building
brief: A 13-storey long-term care home is being built at 55 Eastern Avenue, and the developer wants sidewalks, a traffic lane and a bike lane on Cherry Street and Front Street East closed for 26 months, from April 1, 2025 to May 31, 2027, as a construction staging area. Pedestrians would be redirected, including to a covered walkway on Front Street East. Because the TTC runs transit on Cherry Street, full council approval is required. The item lists a $4.25 fee.

title: 65 Heward Avenue and 135R Berkeley Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Two properties are proposed for the City's Heritage Register: 65 Heward Avenue, with two brick factory/warehouse buildings built in 1914 in South Riverdale, and 135R Berkeley Street, a rare early example of a 1-storey workers' cottage in Moss Park. Staff evaluated both under provincial heritage criteria and found cultural heritage value. Listing recognizes their history but does not ban future changes. City Council makes the final decision.

title: 481 and 483 Church Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage preservation, heritage properties, urban planning; city planning; community planning; regional planning, designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties, historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Two 1870s-era house-form buildings at 481 and 483 Church Street are up for the City's Heritage Register. The Church-Wellesley properties — a 3-storey building and a two-and-a-half-storey building, both built around 1870 — were evaluated by staff under provincial heritage criteria. Listing recognizes their history but does not ban future changes. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Amendment to Item 2024.TE13.5 - 639-653 Yonge Street  - Official Plan and  Zoning By-law Amendment Application
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: One condition from Council's 2024 approval of a 76-storey building at Yonge Street and Isabella Street would be dropped. The condition required a legal deal with the owner of 663 Yonge Street to limit building heights and address tower separation -- but staff say no such deal is feasible, since a limiting agreement is already registered on part of that property. Deleting the condition lets the approved project proceed.

title: 1245 Dupont Street - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Approval
topics: part lot control;
brief: This is a procedural item: council is asked to extend for three more years the exemption from Part Lot Control for part of 1245 Dupont Street. The current exemption expires February 26, 2025; extending it would allow land to be split into lots so a community centre can be finished and a park transferred to the City.

title: 110-112 Adelaide Street East and 85 Lombard Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, rezoning, zoning bylaws; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of a proposed 65-storey mixed-use building at 110-112 Adelaide Street East and 85 Lombard Street — with 600 homes, offices and shops — appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed its decision deadline. Council is asked to send city lawyers to oppose the current proposal at the tribunal while talks with the developer continue.

title: 46 and 58 Spadina Avenue and 378 Wellington Street West - Alterations to and Demolition of Buildings at Heritage Properties Designated Under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: demolitions, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Changes to the protected heritage properties at 46 and 58 Spadina Avenue and 378 Wellington Street West, connected to a new development on the site, go to Council for approval. The work would alter the 1907 "Systems Building" -- a contributing industrial/commercial building in the King-Spadina Heritage Conservation District -- and demolish the non-contributing buildings. The site is also the subject of an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal after council missed its decision deadline on a proposed 28-storey mixed-use building.

title: 40-62 Spadina Avenue and 378 Wellington Street West -  Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The developer of a proposed 30-storey mixed-use building at 40-62 Spadina Avenue appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed its decision deadline. Council is asked to send city lawyers to oppose the current proposal at the tribunal, while talks with the developer continue. The proposal includes retail at grade and 550 homes.

title: 1400, 1408 and 1410 Victoria Park Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: rental housing, zoning bylaws; rental properties; rental units, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Four residential towers of 13 to 26 storeys, with 951 homes including 10 affordable rentals, are proposed at 1400, 1408 and 1410 Victoria Park Avenue, along with shops fronting Victoria Park Avenue and a new 1,225-square-metre public park. The towers would be connected by 8-storey podiums on two blocks. Approval would amend the zoning. City Council makes the final decision.

title: Huntingwood Drive at Ridgecrest Drive - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrian crossovers, road safety; cross walks; cross-walks; crosswalks; pedestrian crosswalks; pxo
brief: Transportation staff studied whether a marked pedestrian crossover is needed on Huntingwood Drive at Ridgecrest Drive and recommend installing one, to improve safety for people crossing to the park, church and nearby elementary schools. Because the TTC runs buses on Huntingwood Drive, city council approval is required. Council is asked to approve.

title: Permanent Closure of portions of Railway Street and Centre Street
topics: road closures; street closures; temporary highway closings
brief: Transportation staff recommend permanently closing small unused sections of Railway Street and Centre Street so the land can be transferred to Parks and Recreation for new park space for Grant Faulkner Park. Because these are public road allowances, council approval is required. City Council is asked to authorize the closures.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plans 66M-2540, 67 Kirkdene Drive
topics: assumption of services;
brief: The city would take over responsibility for the roads and municipal services built for the subdivision at 67 Kirkdene Drive, including Bluebird Place (Registered Plan 66M-2540, Your Home Developments (Kirkdene) Inc.), now that the developer's work is complete, if approved. The performance guarantee held by the city would be released. City Council is asked to approve.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2556, Actonbridge Holding Corp., 8833 Sheppard Avenue East Subdivision, Scarborough
topics: assumption of services, road networks; road infrastructure; street network
brief: The city would take over responsibility for the roads and municipal services built for the subdivision at 8833 Sheppard Avenue East, including Kingbird Grove (Registered Plan 66M-2556, Actonbridge Holding Corp.), now that the developer's work is complete, if approved. The performance guarantee held by the city would be released. City Council is asked to approve.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2555, Goldman Ellesmere 2 Developments Inc., Application No. 13 268033 ESC 37 SB, 1001 Ellesmere Rd Subdivision, Scarborough
topics: assumption of services, subdivision (land); subdivision of land
brief: The city would take over responsibility for the roads and municipal services built for the subdivision at 1001 Ellesmere Road (Registered Plan 66M-2555, Goldman Ellesmere 2 Developments Inc.), now that the developer's work is complete, if approved. The performance guarantee held by the city would be released. City Council is asked to approve.

title: Re-allocating Unused Section 37 Funds Secured in By-law 1022-2014 in Ward 22
topics: capital budgets, funding; financing
brief: Councillor Nick Mantas proposes reallocating $250,000 in unspent Section 37 funds secured from the 1251 Bridletowne Crescent development toward other community facilities in Ward 22, Scarborough-Agincourt. The original purpose, a 1.5-metre pedestrian walkway from Timberbank Boulevard to the bridge over Highland Creek, was abandoned by the city and the money was never used. City Council is asked to direct staff to bring forward the zoning change to reallocate the dormant funds.

title: 253 Markham Road, 12, 20 and 30 Dunelm Street- City-Initiated Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: affordable housing, rezoning; affordable homes; housing projects, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: City staff recommend a city-initiated zoning change for 253 Markham Road and 12, 20 and 30 Dunelm Street, revising rules tied to an earlier 2022 approval for a 783-unit residential development. The amendments would not add development rights but would help deliver Building A, which provides 245 affordable rental and rent-controlled units with federal and city support. Council is asked to approve the amendment.

title: 2759 and 2761 to 2763 Kingston Road and 52 St Quentin Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: City staff recommend approving Official Plan and zoning changes to allow a 10-storey mixed-use building with 95 homes and ground-floor retail at 2759-2763 Kingston Road and 52 St Quentin Avenue. The building would be 36.83 metres tall with two levels of underground parking. Council would amend the planning rules to permit the project.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council reviews the order paper, the list of items to be considered at the meeting. No decision is being asked for.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: This is a procedural item: various presentations, introductions and announcements are made during the meeting. No decisions are being asked for.

title: Petitions
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council may file petitions during the meeting, to be received for the record. No decision is being asked for.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: This is a procedural item: members of council declare any interests under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act. No decision is being asked for.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: This is a procedural item: the mayor and committee chairs introduce committee reports and new business from the mayor and city officials — including reports from the Executive, Audit, Civic Appointments, Economic and Community Development, General Government, Infrastructure and Environment, and Planning and Housing committees and the four community councils. No decision is being asked for.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council will confirm the minutes from its regular meeting on December 17 and 18, 2024, and its special meetings on December 20, 2024, February 5 and February 11, 2025, as an accurate record.

title: Call to Order
brief: This is a procedural item: the City Council meeting opens with the call to order, O Canada and a moment of silence. No decision is being asked for.

title: 2930 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The former New Toronto Post Office at 2930 Lake Shore Boulevard West is proposed for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate the property, at the northeast corner of Lake Shore Boulevard West, under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 1660 Kingston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage designation;
brief: The property at 1660 Kingston Road in Birch Cliff, Scarborough, on the north side of Kingston Road between Birchcliff Avenue and Birchmount Road, is proposed for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate it under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: 877 and 885 Lawrence Avenue East - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: Two former bank branches at 877 and 885 Lawrence Avenue East, built to serve the post-war Don Mills community on the south side of Lawrence Avenue East, are proposed for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate both properties under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act. If no objections come in, formal designation by-laws can follow.

title: 667 King Street West - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: The property at 667 King Street West, at the southwest corner of King and Bathurst with an entrance at 92 Bathurst Street, is in line for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate it under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. If no objections come in, the formal designation by-law can follow.

title: Replacement Units for Demovicted Dwelling Room Tenants
topics: dwellings, tenants; renters; tenancy agreements
brief: Council decides whether to direct staff to report back on whether developers who demolish six or more dwelling rooms should have to provide a replacement unit for every displaced tenant, closing gaps left by the 2019 Official Plan policies that first addressed the loss of dwelling rooms. Dwelling room tenants are among the city's most vulnerable renters, so the stakes are who gets rehoused when their buildings are redeveloped.

title: 1171 - 1173 Avenue Road, 1177 - 1179 Avenue Road, and 372 Briar Hill Avenue - Extension of Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, part lot control, roads; application process, circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads)
brief: The Part Lot Control exemption for a townhouse development at 1171 to 1179 Avenue Road and 372 Briar Hill Avenue would be extended for two more years. City Council enacted By-law 702-2023 in July 2023 to create seven parcels of tied land for three-storey townhouses; only two of the seven have been conveyed to new owners, so City Council is asked to extend the exemption for the remaining five parcels. Buyers of the five remaining townhouses would be affected.

title: 2810 - 2816 Bayview Avenue - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: buildings, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 42-storey residential building with 540 homes would be approved at 2810 to 2816 Bayview Avenue. City Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the 133.23-metre tower (plus mechanical penthouse), which staff say is consistent with the Provincial Planning Statement and conforms to the Official Plan including the Renew Sheppard East Secondary Plan. Future residents of the 540 units would be affected.

title: 104 - 114 Finch Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment, Zoning By-law Amendment, Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: applications, official plan amendments, rezoning; application process, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: An 11-storey mixed-use building with 201 residential units would be approved at 104 to 114 Finch Avenue East. City Council is asked to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law — with a Holding provision — for the 36-metre building (excluding a 5.0-metre mechanical penthouse), with 12,751 square metres of gross floor area including 438 square metres of retail, a density of 5.72 times the lot area, 138 vehicle and 158 bicycle parking spaces, and vehicle access from Willowdale Avenue. Staff say the proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement and conforms to the Official Plan once the Holding conditions are addressed. Future residents and shoppers on Finch Avenue East would be affected.

title: 799 Sheppard Avenue West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, multi-unit dwellings, transportation; building, multi residential apartment buildings; multi residential buildings; multi unit buildings; multi unit dwellings; multi-residential apartment buildings; multi-residential buildings; multi-unit buildings; multi-unit residential buildings; residential multi unit dwellings; residential multi-unit dwellings, transportation services
brief: GCL BUILDS would get a 12-month construction staging area for its nine-storey residential building at 799 Sheppard Avenue West, at the southwest corner of Sheppard Avenue West and Gorman Park Road. City Council is asked to prohibit stopping at all times on the south side of Sheppard Avenue West and the west side of Gorman Park Road from March 31, 2025 to March 31, 2026, with a covered and protected walkway keeping pedestrians safe. Drivers and pedestrians near the site would be affected.

title: 93 Mildenhall Road, 286 and 288 Lawrence Avenue East - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Three single-detached dwellings at 93 Mildenhall Road, 286 and 288 Lawrence Avenue East would get zoning approval for Toronto French School administrative office use. City Council is asked to amend Zoning By-law 569-2013 for the three properties — owned and operated by the abutting Toronto French School at 318 Lawrence Avenue East — with no exterior change and no new gross floor area. The change would let the school run offices in the existing houses.

title: Improving Earl Bales Ski and Snowboard Centre Season and Experience by Investing in Modern Snowmaking Capabilities - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
topics: recreation & tourism (sc), ski centres, skiing, snowboarding; cross-country skiing; downhill skiing, ski centers; ski facilities; ski hills; ski trails; skiing centres; snow centres
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff study options to improve snowmaking technology at the Earl Bales Ski and Snowboard Centre to extend its ski season, and to explore funding from other governments and City sources. The centre needs four straight days below -5 degrees Celsius to start snow production; the report back is due to the July 10, 2025 Infrastructure and Environment Committee meeting.

title: Amending Item 2022.MM45.51 to Support Non-Profit Affordable Rental Housing - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: rental housing; rental properties; rental units
brief: This member motion asks City Council to adjust funding for the Kensington Market Community Land Trust's affordable rental housing project: allocating $50,000 from the Capital Revolving Reserve Fund for Affordable Housing for renovation and operation of an affordable rental property in Ward 11, with $400,000 of the previously allocated $450,000 supporting acquisition of a two-apartment property under the Multi-Unit Residential Acquisition Program, which provides a maximum of $200,000 per home.

title: Authority to Accept a Donation and Enter an Agreement with Toronto and Region Conservation Authority for an Indigenous Outdoor Gathering Space at Morningside Park - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: First Nations, donation, parks; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, bequest; toy drive, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This member motion asks City Council to accept a donation of up to $500,000 from the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority to build an Indigenous outdoor gathering space at Morningside Park, co-developed with Williams Treaty First Nations. Known as Station 1 of the Morningside Legacy Project, the space would sit west of Morningside Avenue and south of Ellesmere Road around a feature granite boulder highlighting treaty history; the City and the TRCA would share maintenance over a five-year warranty period.

title: Better Management of Derelict Buildings - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: buildings, taxes; levies
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff report back in late 2025 on existing and potential tools to deal with vacant and derelict buildings, including better information sharing between City divisions about known vacant properties. Under current by-laws owners must keep derelict buildings boarded and fenced, but the City has no other recourse no matter how long they sit vacant; the motion cites Ward 11 examples including 106 Huron Street and 268 Augusta Avenue.

title: North Spirit Distillery By-The-Glass Permit Application to the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: applications, liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits, application process
brief: This member motion asks City Council to advise the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario that it supports North Spirit Distillery's application for a by-the-glass sales licence at its Finch Avenue West location in Emery Village. The distillery, operating for nearly five years, wants to open for educational tours and tastings; the AGCO requires a municipal council resolution in support, and the business wants the endorsement processed with its May manufacturer licence renewal ahead of a May 2, 2025 grand opening.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 5840, 5868, and 5870 Yonge Street to Toronto Community Housing Corporation for 175 Cummer Avenue - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: housing; homes; residences
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $140,000 to the operating budget, funded by developer community benefits, for an exterior fence with security gates at Willowdale Manor, the supportive seniors' housing community at 175 Cummer Avenue. The manor houses more than 600 seniors aged 59 and older; the fence would protect a garden on the greenspace the residents established.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.PH18.3 - Recommended Parking Requirements for New Development - Accessible, Bicycle, Visitor - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: accessible permit parking, bicycle parking, parking; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), bike parking
brief: This member motion asks City Council to make a technical correction to its earlier parking requirements decision (PH18.3), replacing an outdated zoning by-law clause reference with Clause 230.5.10.20(1) of Zoning By-law 569-2013 for agreements on payments in lieu of bicycle parking. The payment basis is $538 per 'short-term' bicycle parking space reduced, adjusted for inflation; the correction is needed before the bill enacting the program passes.

title: 137 Teddington Park Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment; committee of adjustment
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose an appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of part of a variance application at 137 Teddington Park Avenue. The refused variances would legalize rear-yard soft landscaping of 30 per cent (minimum 50 per cent) and front-yard landscaping of 35 per cent (minimum 60 per cent); the applicant appealed the refusal.

title: 55 Lonborough Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: committees of adjustment, municipal officials; city officials, committee of adjustment
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose an appeal of the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of variances for a fourplex and garden suite at 55 Lonborough Avenue. The applicant appealed the refusal; the motion also authorizes the City Solicitor to hire outside consultants and to settle the matter after consulting the ward councillor and City Planning staff.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds Obtained in the Development at 2, 4 and 6 Teagarden Court for Playscape Improvements at Hollywood Public School in Ward 18 - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
topics: playground equipment, playgrounds; adventure playgrounds; indoor playgrounds; playground structures, park equipment; play apparatus; play equipment; play structures
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $50,000 to the operating budget, funded by developer community benefits, for schoolyard improvements at Hollywood Public School, subject to the school board agreeing to community access terms. The school, serving about 375 students, gave up its previous play yard for an expansion; the upgrades would serve neighbourhood children within a 2-kilometre radius.

title: Temporary Parking Amendments on Dufferin Street, between Queen Street West and Springhurst Avenue - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: parking, traffic management; traffic control; traffic monitoring; traffic operations
brief: This member motion asks City Council to temporarily prohibit stopping on both sides of Dufferin Street between Queen Street West and Springhurst Avenue, from March 31 to December 31, 2025, to ease traffic during planned construction and major events. Dufferin is a key north-south diversion route for Liberty Village; the change also relates to the RapidTO Dufferin surface transit priority project, whose final configuration is expected by late 2025 or early 2026. The motion also lists $4.25.

title: Advancing Justice Centres in Toronto - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: community centres, courts, youth justice; board-run community centres; clubhouses; community centers; community complexes
brief: This member motion asks City Council to extend agreements with Ontario's Ministry of the Attorney General to receive $434,850 supporting the continued operation of community-based Justice Centres in Toronto. The two pilot Justice Centres — Toronto North West and Toronto Downtown East — co-locate justice, health, and social services to provide wraparound supports for vulnerable accused persons. The motion breaks the amount down as $106,000, $116,000, $100,000, $85,000, $6,150, and $21,700.

title: 23 Beechwood Avenue - Appeal of Committee of Adjustment Decision - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: appeals, planning;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of variances for 23 Beechwood Avenue and to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose them, with authority to negotiate a settlement. The variances would increase permitted building length, depth, and height; City Planning staff recommended refusal, saying the proposed massing — nearly double the permitted length and depth — does not fit the neighbourhood.

title: Increasing Toronto Community Housing Corporation Board Remuneration - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: corporations;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to set annual pay for public members of the Toronto Community Housing Corporation board at $50,000 plus per-meeting fees for the Chair, and $10,000 plus per-meeting fees for other members, effective March 2025. Toronto Community Housing is the largest social housing provider in Canada, housing almost 94,000 tenants in 41,000 households and managing over 1,300 buildings worth over $13.8 billion. The per-meeting fee would be $500, with total annual pay capped at $70,000 for the Chair and $20,000 for other members.

title: Co-operative Housing Approval to Lease and Operate Thirty-Two New Affordable Rental Homes - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: approval, housing; homes; residences
brief: This member motion asks City Council to approve agreements with the Naismith Non-Profit Housing Co-operative for the operation of 32 new affordable rental homes at the Don Summerville revitalization site at 1555–1575 Queen Street East. Council approved $6 million in 2021 to support the City's acquisition of the 32 units, which the City will own under a long-term lease, with the co-operative operating the housing focused on eligible members of Toronto's arts and culture industries. The motion also makes up to $150,000 available to the Co-operative Housing Federation of Toronto for legal, administrative and other costs of finalizing the deal.

title: Sign the Deal: Extending the Canada-Ontario Early Learning and Child Care Agreement to 2031 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: child care; childcare
brief: This member motion asks City Council to urge Ontario's education minister and the federal minister to finalize the extension of the Canada-Ontario Early Learning and Child Care Agreement to 2031. An agreement in principle covers $16.77 billion for 2026–2027 to 2030–2031, but a final deal has not been signed; the motion says that without an extension, child care fees would rise and new-space creation would slow.

title: Feasibility of Establishing an Intercultural Hub or Association of Community Centres at 45-47 Sheppard Avenue East - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: cultural facilities; art centres; arts centres; cultural attractions; cultural centres
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff study the feasibility of creating an intercultural hub or association of community centres at 45-47 Sheppard Avenue East in Willowdale, including identifying funding opportunities. The motion describes Willowdale's growing diversity — 80 per cent racialized residents, 76 per cent newcomers — and a development application in process for the site, which includes four towers and a large park.

title: 877 Yonge Street - Saint Clare's Multifaith Housing Society Community Space Tenancy Lease and Lease Amending Agreement - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: affordable housing; affordable homes; housing projects
brief: This member motion asks City Council to amend the ground lease with St. Clare's Multifaith Housing Society at 877 Yonge Street and to negotiate a new below-market lease for ground-floor commercial space to be used for housing-related services. The property was acquired with federal Rapid Housing Initiative funds and converted into 252 affordable rental homes with wraparound supports for people experiencing homelessness, women, Indigenous and racialized people, and seniors; the subbasement now houses the Nancy and Ed Jackman Performance Centre.

title: Request to Accept an In-Kind Donation for the Playground Enhancement and Park Improvements at Pricefield Road Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: donation, park maintenance; bequest; toy drive, parks maintenance
brief: This member motion asks City Council to accept an in-kind donation valued at up to $620,000 from Scrivener Square Nominee Inc. — design and construction administration services by Claude Cormier and Associates — for playground enhancement and park improvements at Pricefield Road Park (50 Pricefield Road). Council approval is required for donations of $50,000 or more; the design phase is scheduled to start in spring 2025, with construction in 2026.

title: 2451 St. Clair Avenue West - by Councillor Frances Nunziata, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: committees of adjustment, noise; amplified music; construction noise; loud music; noise pollution; traffic noise, committee of adjustment
brief: This member motion asks City Council to classify 2451 St. Clair Avenue West as a Class 4 noise area under the provincial noise guideline. The Committee of Adjustment approved a six-storey mixed-use building with ten residential units and ground-floor retail on the site in January 2025, subject to a rail noise and vibration study because of its proximity to rail yards and facilities; the study recommended the Class 4 designation, which allows higher noise levels than normally permitted for residential uses.

title: 135 Glen Road, Removal of Encroachments - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: encroachments;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have Transportation Services require the owners of 135 Glen Road to remove a large wall and other items built on City property without the required heritage permits. The motion says the encroachments were built contrary to the Ontario Heritage Act, are inconsistent with the Rosedale Heritage Conservation Area, and reduce visibility at the corner of Glen Road and Whitney Avenue.

title: Addressing the Financial Industry’s Carbon Footprint  - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
topics: climate change; climate protection
brief: This member motion asks City Council to convene experts to discuss developing a Sustainable Finance Hub in Toronto and to commission a study on how peer cities address the climate impact of the financial industry's lending. The motion's supporting text cites a University of Toronto study finding Bay Street among the world's largest sources of financed fossil-fuel emissions, and notes five major Canadian banks left the Net-Zero Banking Alliance this year.

title: Addressing Vacant Storefronts - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: real estate vacancies, stores; office vacancies; vacancies (real estate); vacancy levels; vacancy rates; vacant buildings; vacant space; vacant units, retail stores; shops
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have staff report by late 2025 on policy options to compel landlords to lease out vacant storefronts, and on existing property standards that apply to vacant properties. The motion cites concerns that long-vacant storefronts hurt streetscape vibrancy, public safety, and economic activity.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to The 519 for Capital Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: community improvement plans, improvement; enhancement; rehabilitation (property)
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $133,564.14 to The 519 Community Centre's operating budget, funded by developer community benefits (Section 45) from the development at 600 Jarvis Street, for capital improvements at 519 Church Street. The projects include security system upgrades, a building resiliency audit, and a lobby redesign for community accessibility and safety.

title: Reimbursement for Environmental Work at 640 Lansdowne Avenue to Magellan Community Charities - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: This member motion asks City Council to reimburse Magellan Community Charities up to $1,500,000 for environmental cleanup costs at 640 Lansdowne Avenue, the City-owned site where it is building 256 long-term care beds and 57 affordable rental homes. The work — including well decommissioning, dewatering, and liner barriers — was needed under the property's Certificate of Property Use; funding is allocated in the 2025–2034 Capital Budget.

title: Aligning Cultural Use Tenancy Agreement - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
topics: community & life (sc), culture (sc);
brief: This member motion asks City Council to let the City sign nominal five-year leases with the Artists' Network for continued programming at the Leslie Grove Fieldhouse, and with East End Arts for programming at the St. Matthew's Lawn Bowling Clubhouse. The City has a history of providing community space to not-for-profit cultural organizations at below-market rent.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Casey House for Accessibility Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: accessibility; barrier-free design; universal design; wheelchair accessible
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $50,993.81 to the Non-Program operating budget — fully funded by developer community benefits (Section 37) from the development at 159 Wellesley Street East — to forward to Casey House for entranceway accessibility renovations at 119 Isabella Street. The project's total cost is approximately $300,000; the upgrades include wheelchair-height reception counters, security access, washroom safety improvements, and refinished floors.

title: Authority to Release Section 37 Funds for Cultural Recognition Street Naming for Little Iran - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
topics: culture (sc), street name signs; street signs
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $5000.00 to the Transportation Services capital budget, funded by developer community benefits, to install Little Iran street signage on Yonge Street from Cummer Avenue to Moore Park Avenue. Council supported exploring a Cultural District for the area's Iranian community in March 2023, but no budget was allocated; the corridor is home to Toronto's oldest Iranian settlement.

title: Protecting Paul Martel Indigenous Botanical Garden - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
topics: First Nations, botanical gardens, native plants; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, botanical plant collection; botanical resources; formal gardens
brief: This member motion asks City Council to allow the Indigenous People Garden Incorporated to lock the gate of the Indigenous Botanical Garden at Paul Martel Park between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. The garden was created by Indigenous volunteers on native and medicinal plantings after Paul Martel's death in 2020, with support from the Annex Residents Association.

title: Authority to Enter into a Nominal Agreement with the Indigenous People Garden Incorporated at Paul Martel Park - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: First Nations, parks; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples, conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This member motion asks City Council to let Parks and Recreation sign a nominal-fee licence agreement with the Indigenous People Garden Incorporated for Indigenous-led training and gardening at Paul Martel Park, for one year renewable up to three years in total. The motion supports Indigenous place-keeping and cultural programming at the park.

title: Authorization to Reallocate Section 37 Funds to STEPS for a Mural at Wellesley Station - Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: public art, urban beautification; 20-minute makeover; beautification projects; clean & beautiful city; clean and beautiful city; clean city beautiful city; community clean-up days; facade improvement; mural program; neighbourhood beautification, outdoor art; outdoor sculptures; outdoor statues
brief: This member motion asks City Council to reallocate developer community benefits funding for a planned Wellesley Station mural from the Church-Wellesley Village Business Improvement Area to the non-profit STEPS Public Art and the TTC. The mural was the second most popular choice in 2023 participatory budgeting for the Bay Cloverhill, Church-Wellesley, and Upper Jarvis neighbourhoods, with 40 per cent of votes. The amount is $80,000.00 in Section 37 community benefits from the development at 55-61 Charles Street East.

title: Requiring Metrolinx to Develop a Heavy Truck Safety Plan - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: community safety, heavy trucks, safety; public safety
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Manager request that Metrolinx develop and publish a comprehensive heavy truck safety plan for Ontario Line construction — including enforcement measures, monitoring protocols, and a way for residents to report concerns — and share it with local councillors and community members. The motion follows two February 2025 incidents in which trucks operated by Metrolinx sub-contractors made right turns from Pape Avenue onto Mortimer Avenue that were not on approved haul routes.

title: Support of Better Hearing for Torontonians - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: hearing care; audiologists; hearing
brief: This member motion asks City Council to request that Ontario's health minister consider allowing earbuds to be used as hearing assistive devices and increasing the availability of over-the-counter hearing aids. Statistics Canada reports 38 per cent of adults aged 20–79 have some hearing loss; the motion notes that hearing-aid features in earbuds are not available in Canada due to regulatory restrictions.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2025.TE19.2 - 450 Dufferin Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2025.TE19.2 and amend its earlier approval for the 450 Dufferin Street development to reflect revised plans that fully enclose the rear loading area — to further mitigate neighbourhood concerns — and allow cooling towers to extend beyond the maximum permitted building height.

title: Under Gardiner Public Realm Lighting Project Delivery Agreement with The Bentway Conservancy - Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: infrastructure, street lighting;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have The Bentway Conservancy lead the design and construction of a pedestrian lighting pilot project under the Gardiner Expressway at Dan Leckie Way, funded through the City's Business Improvement Area capital cost-share streetscape program. The project aims to improve the experience of crossing through the underpass.

title: Authority to Enter into a Licence Agreement with Canada Ireland Foundation for Ireland Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: memorials, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, monuments; permanent memorials
brief: This member motion asks City Council to enter a nominal 20-year licence agreement with the Canada Ireland Foundation for the continued maintenance of Ireland Park, the memorial park commemorating the approximately 39,000 Irish Famine migrants who arrived in Toronto in 1847. The 2004 licence agreement expired July 1, 2024.

title: Authority to Donate Surplus Vehicles to Kyiv - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: donation, motor vehicles; bequest; toy drive, vehicles
brief: This motion from the Mayor asks City Council to donate up to five surplus City vehicles — three from Fleet Services and two from Paramedic Services — to Kyiv for humanitarian purposes in 2025, continuing donations the City made to Ukraine in 2022, 2023, and 2024.

title: Improving Toronto’s Public Washrooms - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: washrooms; bathrooms
brief: This motion from the Mayor asks City Council to have the City Manager study where new public washrooms are most needed, install temporary washrooms starting in spring 2025, develop a long-term plan for more washrooms, and repair the worst existing ones. The study would involve City Planning, Parks and Recreation, Transportation Services, the Chief Technology Officer, and the TTC.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 and Section 45 Funds for Heritage Lighting at the Young People’s Theatre - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: street lighting, theatres (facilities); auditorium; performance spaces; performing arts centres; performing arts facilities
brief: This member motion asks City Council to release Section 37 and Section 45 funds totalling $1,133,859.76 to Economic Development and Culture for heritage lighting at the City-owned Young People's Theatre at 165–169 Front Street East, designated under the Ontario Heritage Act. The building was identified in the 2011 Heritage Lighting Master Plan for Old Town Toronto as an opportunity to use night-time lighting to highlight its architecture. The motion breaks the funding down as $500,000, $633,859.76, $224,704.20, $107,741.73, $32,617.65, $33,651.59, $7,696.72, $94,672.34, $1,782.27, and $496,808.48.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Sam Ching Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, plaques; financing, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $10,000 to the Heritage Toronto operating budget, funded by developer community benefits, for a heritage plaque honouring Sam Ching, one of the first Chinese residents on record in Toronto — owner of a laundry at 9 Adelaide Street East in 1878 — at 9 Adelaide Street East.

title: 114 and 114R Baldwin Street and 75 Cecil Street - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: appeals, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor seek party status at the Toronto Local Appeal Body to support the Committee of Adjustment's refusal of variances for a four-storey, 10-unit townhouse complex at 114 and 114R Baldwin Street and 75 Cecil Street. City Planning staff recommended refusal over concerns about massing, infrastructure servicing, garbage pick-up, pedestrian safety, and emergency access.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Henry “Box” Brown Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $10,000 to the Heritage Toronto operating budget, funded by developer community benefits, for a heritage plaque honouring Henry 'Box' Brown — who escaped slavery by hiding in a wooden shipping crate and later moved to Toronto in 1886 — at Henry 'Box' Brown Lane in Corktown.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Cy McLean Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: plaques; heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $10,000 to the Heritage Toronto operating budget, funded by developer community benefits, for a heritage plaque honouring Cy McLean — one of Toronto's first Black bandleaders, who led Canada's only full-scale Black orchestra in the 1940s — at 201 Yonge Street, the former site of the Colonial Tavern.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for North Star Way Lane Heritage Plaque - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, plaques; financing, heritage plaques; heritage toronto plaques; historic markers; historic plaques; historical markers; local markers; provincial plaques
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $10,000 to the Heritage Toronto operating budget, funded by developer community benefits, for a heritage plaque honouring the North Star's significance to the Underground Railroad at North Star Lane in Corktown.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 1841 Shoreline Interpretation - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
topics: funding, shorelines; financing, lakeshore
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $113,419.07 to the Heritage Toronto operating budget, fully funded by developer community benefits (Section 45) from the development at 311 Adelaide Street, to install two plaques and 10 markers along the historic 1841 Lake Ontario shoreline in the St. Lawrence neighbourhood. The markers would pair with a public launch event in summer 2025, a Heritage Toronto walking tour, and a digital experience.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Laneway Project for Verner Lane and Drovers Lane - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: laneways, redevelopment; back alleys; mews, rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: This member motion asks City Council to forward $330,000.00 in developer community benefits (Section 37) to the Laneway Project to revitalize Verner Lane and Drovers Lane in Cabbagetown South, near the Parliament Street library branch and Lord Dufferin school. The funds were secured from the development at 219 and 231 Dundas Street East.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Clocktower Trail Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: road maintenance; roads maintenance; sidewalk maintenance; sidewalks maintenance; summer maintenance; winter maintenance
brief: This member motion asks City Council to add $200,000.00 to the Transportation Services capital budget, funded by developer community benefits (Section 37), for streetscape and pedestrian safety improvements supporting the Clocktower Trail park network near Yonge Street. Staff identified improvements on Alexander Street, Grosvenor Street, and Maitland Street, including new tree pits, plantings, and pedestrian safety upgrades.

title: 3042 Dundas Street West - Liquor Licence Application 2963606 - Gigli Café Junction - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: This member motion asks City Council to tell the provincial liquor licence registrar that a licence for Gigli Café Junction at 3042 Dundas Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns about noise, litter, and safety are attached. The deadline for objections was February 1, 2025.

title: 1522 Queen Street West - Liquor Licence Application 2972534 - Thamel Toronto - by Councillor Gord Perks, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
topics: liquor sales licences; alcohol permits; liquor licences; liquor permits
brief: This member motion asks City Council to tell the provincial liquor licence registrar that a licence for Thamel Toronto at 1522 Queen Street West is not in the public interest unless conditions addressing community concerns about noise, litter, and safety are attached. The deadline for objections was February 7, 2025.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Pleasantview Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Clydesdale Park and Henry Farm Tennis Club to Retrofit the Outdoor Court Lighting at Havenbrook Park - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
topics: donation, sports clubs, tennis; badminton clubs; baseball associations; baseball leagues; bowling clubs; cross-country ski clubs; curling clubs; gymnastic clubs; hockey associations; hockey leagues; karate clubs; lacrosse clubs; lawn bowling clubs; ride clubs; rifle clubs; slo-pitch leagues; soccer clubs; soccer leagues; softball associations; softball leagues; swim clubs; tennis clubs; volleyball clubs, bequest; toy drive
brief: This member motion asks City Council to accept in-kind donations from two community tennis clubs — Pleasantview Tennis Club, to refurbish four tennis courts at Clydesdale Park (up to $150,000), and Henry Farm Tennis Club, to retrofit outdoor court lighting with LED fixtures at Havenbrook Park (up to $75,000) — each delivered through a construction and donation agreement with Parks and Recreation. Both clubs would use their capital reserve funds to cover the costs.

title: 621-623 The Queensway - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: appeals, committees of adjustment, dwellings; committee of adjustment
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of parking variances for additional dwelling units at 621-623 The Queensway, and to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose them. The applications do not conform to Official Plan policy on tenant assistance; the City Solicitor already appealed the decisions on February 4, 2025 to preserve the City's right of appeal.

title: Amending Item 2021.TE26.4 - 33-49 Avenue Road and 136-148 Yorkville Avenue and Creation of New Park at 819 Yonge Street - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: parkland dedication, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: This member motion asks City Council to approve a development charge credit to the owner of 148 Yorkville Avenue (Greybrook) for building park improvements at 819 Yonge Street, enabling the acquisition and development of that site as a new park. Greybrook has a conditional agreement to buy 819 Yonge Street as an off-site parkland dedication worth more than the required dedication for 148 Yorkville Avenue; staff propose directing Section 42 cash-in-lieu funds from a nearby development at 717 Church Street to cover part of the difference.

title: Proposed Amendments to Municipal Code Chapter 367, Building Emissions Performance
topics: greenhouse effect, municipal codes, property owners; building owners; land owners; property ownership, greenhouse gas emissions
brief: Up for approval at City Council: amending the Building Emissions Performance by-law to postpone the first reporting year for mid-size buildings (929 to 4,645 square metres) from 2025 to 2026, and to set July 2, 2025 as the 2025 extension and exemption deadline. The by-law, adopted in December 2023, requires large building owners to report energy and water use annually; over 3,400 reports were submitted for 2024, with more than 64 per cent compliance.

title: Wastewater Energy Program Implementation
topics: agreements, energy, wastewater; energy resources; energy use, sanitary sewage; sewage; waste water, tenancy agreements
brief: Up for approval at City Council: letting City officials negotiate and sign wastewater energy transfer agreements — for projects that capture heat from sewers as renewable energy — with Toronto Water able to reject unsuitable projects. The program supports TransformTO's goal of sourcing 50 per cent of community-wide energy from renewables by 2030; a pilot project is under construction at Toronto Western Hospital.

title: William R. Allen Road (Wilson Station Bus Underpass and Mezzanine Bridge Rehabilitation) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, transportation infrastructure, underpasses; building, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: On the agenda at City Council: letting the General Manager of Transportation Services temporarily close lanes on William R. Allen Road near Wilson Station, so the TTC can rehabilitate the station's bus underpass and Mezzanine Bridge. The work runs in four stages from April 1 to December 31, 2025, with at least two traffic lanes kept open each direction; access to the Highway 401 westbound on-ramp from southbound Allen Road is restricted from April 1 to June 30, 2025.

title: Street 'A' Environmental Assessment Study (Park Lawn Lake Shore Transportation Master Plan)
topics: Master Plans, environmental assessments, transportation infrastructure; ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: On the agenda at City Council: approving the preferred design for a new Street A in the Park Lawn and Lake Shore area and to advance its environmental assessment. The new public street and rail underpass between Park Lawn Road and Lake Shore Boulevard West supports the former Christie's cookie factory site redevelopment, a future Park Lawn GO station, and a new TTC streetcar loop. The Transportation Master Plan completed in 2023 identified Street A as a Schedule C project needing a full environmental assessment.

title: Anti-idling By-law
topics: by-laws, city vehicles, unnecessary idling; bylaws, city owned vehicles; city-owned vehicles; corporate fleet
brief: City Council is receiving a report responding to its direction to review enforcement, public education, and fleet actions under the Idling Control By-law, which limits idling to one minute per hour to cut emissions and improve air quality. Enforcement is complaint-based, with over 2,120 anti-idling signs installed across the city. No by-law change is proposed in this item.

title: Options to Fund and Expand the HTO To Go Water Trailer Program
topics: parks, programs, water; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland
brief: Formally folding the HTO To Go water trailer program into the City's heat relief response, expanding it so trailers are spread more evenly across the city, and hiring a contractor to supply trailer services at City sites goes to City Council for approval. Toronto Water would also work with Shelter and Support Services to improve drinking water access for vulnerable people during heat warnings, while Parks and Recreation upgrades old fountains with bottle-filling features. Council would also approve up to $220,000, including taxes and contingencies, to buy two 10-tap stainless steel water trailers, amending Toronto Water's 2025 capital budget and 2026-2033 capital plan; the money would come from unspent 2025 capital funds identified in a future variance report.

title: Cycling Network Plan - 2025 Cycling Infrastructure Installation - First Quarter Update
topics: bikeway networks, cycling maps, transportation planning; bicycle facilities; bicycle routes; bike routes; bikeway routes; bikeways; cycling routes; shared roadways; signed routes, transportation operations
brief: Whether to approve installing 12 is before City Council. 5 kilometres of new bikeways across six projects under the Cycling Network Plan — including Bathurst Street (Steeles Avenue West to Bainbridge Avenue and Raoul Wallenberg Road), Bedford Road, Ellesmere Road (Orton Park Road to Kingston Road), Ontario Street, and Wallace Avenue. No motor vehicle travel lanes would be removed. The projects are part of the 2025–2027 near-term implementation of the Cycling Network Plan. The item also adds a temporary position of up to two years to Transportation Services' 2025 operating budget at $98,000 gross and $0 net, funded from the Transportation Services capital budget.

title: Sankofa Square Signage
topics: attractions, signs; cultural attractions; places of interest; tourist attractions; tourist sites, signage
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Stephen Holyday (Ward 2, Etobicoke Centre) is asking City staff about the status of the Sankofa Square signage — production costs, installation costs, expected installation date, and what happened to the original Yonge-Dundas Square signs.

title: February 2025 Snow Events
topics: non emergency municipal services, sidewalk snow ploughs, snow removal; 3-1-1; 311; 311 calls; non-emergency city services, ploughs; sidewalk plows; sidewalk snow plows, snow melting; windrow clearing (snow)
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Jennifer McKelvie (Ward 25, Scarborough–Rouge Park) is asking City staff for information about the City's response to the February 2025 snow events, Toronto's largest snow accumulation since January 2022. The inquiry asks detailed questions about downtown sidewalk plowing, 311 snow-related service requests, response times, and equipment readiness.

title: Micro-Shelters
topics: homelessness, social housing; community housing; housing allowance; housing projects; low income housing; non profit housing; non-profit housing; public housing; rent geared to income assistance; rent geared to income housing; rent subsidies; rent supplement; subsidized housing; subsidized rent; subsidized units
brief: This is an administrative inquiry: Councillor Chris Moise (Ward 13, Toronto Centre) is asking City staff for an update on the City's encampment approach and strategy, including micro-shelters and temporary modular shelter options. In June 2024, Council directed staff to report back on costs to fully accommodate everyone living in encampments and to prioritize rapid shelter models for people in encampments. Homelessness was declared an emergency in Toronto in May 2023. The item also lists figures of $20 million and $5.5 million.

title: The Growing Crisis of Public Safety in the City of Toronto and the Urgent Need to Seek Clarity on the Date City Staff will Present Long Overdue “Bubble Zone” By-laws to Toronto City Council and Protect the Charter Rights of Those Trying to Access Faith-Based and Other Vulnerable Institutions
topics: by-laws, culture (sc), safety; bylaws, public safety
