The item's source material also references $963 million, $4 billion, $610.8 million, $10,562,651, $10,748,554, $51,857,637, $52,770,331, $62,420,288, $63,518,885, $500,000, $1.5 billion and $60 million.

title: Housing Action Plan: Avenues Policy Review - Decision Report
brief: Toronto's Avenues, the main streets designated for growth, would get a new vision and new policies to host more housing alongside shops and services. Council is being asked to approve the Avenues Policy Review under the Housing Action Plan 2022-2026, the latest step in a two-decade strategy of focusing growth on major corridors. It matters to residents and businesses along those main streets, where the rules for adding homes are set to change.

title: Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods - Ward 23 Multiplex Study - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Homeowners in Ward 23, Scarborough North, could soon build multiplexes with up to six homes on their properties: Council is being asked to approve the study's Official Plan and zoning amendments for the area, which would also raise the maximum building depth to 19 metres. The change builds on the city-wide multiplex study under Expanding Housing Options in Neighbourhoods. For Scarborough North residents, this is about whether gentle density becomes legal on their streets.

title: Recommended Parking Requirements for New Development - Accessible, Bicycle, Visitor
topics: accessible permit parking, bicycle parking, standards; accessible parking permits; accessible parking spaces; designated disabled parking spaces; disabled parking permits; disabled parking spaces; disabled parking spots; disabled permit parking; disabled person parking permits; handicapped parking; permit parking (disabled), bike parking
brief: Zoning rules for accessible, visitor and bicycle parking at new developments are due for an update. Council is being asked to adopt new standards for these parking types, completing a review of the city-wide parking rules that began in 2021 and last changed in 2022 for car and bike parking. The item's source material also references $538 and $1076.

title: City-Initiated Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendments to Support the ReNew Golden Mile Municipal Class Environmental Assessment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: environmental assessments, official plan amendments, zoning bylaws; ea; ecological assessment; environmental assessment; environmental evaluation, zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: The street network for the ReNew Golden Mile is moving to approval: Council adopts city-initiated Official Plan and zoning changes that allow the new and reconfigured major streets along O'Connor Drive, Victoria Park Avenue and Eglinton Square. The amendments carry out the street designs chosen in the Golden Mile Municipal Class Environmental Assessment. Residents and businesses along this corridor would see the planned street layout locked in.

title: 29, 31, and 33 Sussex Avenue - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation; historic preservation; historical preservation
brief: Three houses at 29, 31 and 33 Sussex Avenue, between Huron Street and Spadina Avenue in the Huron-Sussex neighbourhood, are headed for heritage protection. Council is being asked to state its intention to designate the three properties under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for their cultural heritage value. If no objections come in, formal by-laws can follow.

title: 3100 Weston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
topics: heritage designation, heritage properties; designated heritage properties; heritage buildings; heritage sites; listed heritage properties
brief: The property at 3100 Weston Road, on the west side of Weston Road at Sheppard Avenue West, is one step closer to heritage protection: Council is being asked to state its intention to designate it under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act for its cultural heritage value. If no one objects, the formal designation by-law can follow. Council is the decision-maker.

title: Thermal Comfort Guidelines: For Large Area Studies, Public Realm Capital Projects, and Large Site Developments - Final Report
topics: heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems; air conditioning; air conditioning systems; boilers; climate control systems; cooling systems; furnaces; heat; heating systems; hvac; ventilation; ventilation systems
brief: Large developments, major public-space projects and big neighbourhood studies would be judged on heat and wind comfort under new Thermal Comfort Guidelines before Council. Council is being asked to adopt the guidelines and have staff apply them to city-initiated large area studies, outdoor public realm capital projects, and large sites over 5 hectares with buildings over 6 storeys. As the climate warms, this is about designing shade and wind protection into the places people live and gather.

title: Community Benefits Charge: In-Kind Guidelines
topics: community benefits;
brief: Developers in Toronto may soon get clearer rules for giving community benefits as real projects, like parks or child care spaces, instead of paying the Community Benefits Charge in cash. Council is being asked to adopt in-kind guidelines for the charge, which funds parks, libraries, child care, cultural spaces and affordable housing tied to growth. The guidelines affect what neighbourhoods get out of new development.

title: Transit-Oriented Communities Update on Downtown Proposals and Affordable Housing
topics: affordable housing, community & life (sc), urban transit systems; affordable homes; housing projects, local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies
brief: The Province's Ontario Line South transit-oriented community proposals at Exhibition, Corktown, King-Bathurst and Queen-Spadina are back before Council, which is being asked to authorize the City Manager to finalize a site-specific memorandum of understanding for the Queen-Spadina site. Council is also being asked to direct the City Manager to seek a firm commitment from the Province that the Additional Community Benefit will equal 8 percent of each project's value, rather than 'up to 8 percent,' and to direct staff to work with the Province to maximize the affordable housing the provincial value can support. The Queen-Spadina MOU terms are the concrete decision in front of Council.

title: Woodbine Transit Oriented Community Secondary Plan - Authorization to Enter into Agreements for Resourcing
topics: [activities in transportation], agreements, urban transit systems; local transit authorities; municipal transit authorities; public transit authorities; public transportation organizations; transit agencies; transit operating agencies, tenancy agreements
brief: Council would authorize city staff to negotiate a Resourcing Agreement with the Woodbine Entertainment Group so the company covers the cost of city staff time needed to finish planning a mixed-use transit-oriented community around the future Woodbine GO station. The agreement comes out of the Toronto-Ontario New Deal's push to speed up transit-oriented communities. Council is the decision-maker.

title: 267-275 Merton Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: Staff recommend approving a zoning change for 267-275 Merton Street to allow a 128-metre, 40-storey mixed-use purpose-built rental building with 494 homes, 148 of them (30 percent) affordable rental, and 32,000 square metres of floor area including 100 to 300 square metres of ground-floor commercial space. City Council is being asked to approve the zoning amendment.

title: Green Gates Court (9 Fairmeadow Avenue) Subdivision, North York - Assumption of Services, Registered Plans 66M-2531
topics: assumption of services, development, subdivision (land); developing land; development (land); land development, subdivision of land
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council would formally assume the municipal services and roads installed in the Green Gates Court subdivision (Registered Plan 66M-2531, subdivision agreement dated June 30, 2015, between Orchard Ridge (Fairmeadow) G.P. Inc. and the City) by passing an assumption by-law. The acting director would release the performance guarantee held under the subdivision agreement and the City Solicitor would register the by-law. Residents of the subdivision would see the City take over the roads and services.

title: 94 Cortleigh Boulevard - Alterations to and Demolition of Heritage Attributes of a Designated Heritage Property Under Sections 33 and 34 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Alterations and partial demolition of heritage attributes at the William Weeks House at 94 Cortleigh Boulevard would be approved. City Council is asked to permit the work — the designated Part IV heritage property, a 1914 Arts and Crafts house in the Lytton Park neighbourhood finished in rustic red brick with stone detailing and half-timbered gables — in connection with a new one-storey addition at the rear. The property backs onto the Lytton Sunken Gardens Park. The changes would reshape the heritage house while keeping its protected character.

title: Recipient of the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award
topics: awards, community development; community building; community capacity building; community engagement; social development
brief: Jason Ash would be approved as the 2025 Agnes Macphail Award recipient. The award, established by the Borough of East York, annually recognizes an outstanding volunteer who upholds the values and causes of Agnes Macphail and lives within the former borough's boundaries; the Recognition Committee selected Ash at its January 6, 2025 meeting. City Council is asked to confirm the choice.

title: 2 Tecumseth Street - Appeal of Committee of Adjustment Decision  -  Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
topics: committees of adjustment, hearings; committee of adjustment
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Solicitor appeal the Committee of Adjustment's approval of variances for the 2 Tecumseth Street development and to attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body to oppose them, with authority to negotiate a settlement. The variances would allow the 33-storey and 26-storey mixed-use buildings to increase height and floor area and proceed without minimum parking requirements.

title: Approval of Property Tax Exemptions for new Affordable Rental Homes at 253 Markham Road - Building A - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
topics: affordable housing, property taxes; affordable homes; housing projects, municipal taxes; property tax accounts; property tax bills; tax accounts
brief: This member motion asks City Council to approve property tax exemptions for the affordable rental and rent-controlled homes at 253 Markham Road, Building A, developed by the Cedars Non-Profit Housing Co-operative under the Rental Housing Supply Program. The project would create 49 affordable rental homes and 196 rent-controlled homes; the exemptions are needed to satisfy Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation conditions for federal funding and financing by February 20, 2025. The exemption is valued at about $10.25 million in today's dollars over the 50-year affordability period: $7,946,724 in City taxes, $2,192,354 in education taxes, and $110,337 in the City building levy.

title: Creation of a City of Toronto "Buy Local, Buy Canadian" Campaign - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: city initiatives; city council priorities; corporate campaigns; council priorities; municipal initiatives
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Manager develop a comprehensive 'Buy Local, Buy Canadian' campaign encouraging residents and businesses to purchase Canadian-made goods and services, in response to threatened US tariffs. The motion cites a potential 25 per cent tariff announced by the Trump Administration and warns of hundreds of thousands of job losses if imposed.

title: Parkland obligations at 25 Fisherville Road - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
topics: land acquisition, parkland dedication, parks; conservation areas; greenbelts; parkland, land acquisitions; park acquisition; parkland acquisition; parks acquisitions; property acquisition; property acquisitions
brief: This member motion asks City Council to allow the parkland dedication for the 25 Fisherville Road redevelopment to be transferred to the City within 36 months of the first above-grade building permit, rather than at the usual earlier timing. The delay is meant to let a new public road and signalized intersection at Bathurst Street be built first and to expedite new rental housing on the site.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.CC24.10 - 2350-2352 Yonge Street - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2024.CC24.10 and amend its earlier decision on the 2350-2352 Yonge Street zoning appeal, so the City Solicitor's confidential instructions on the Ontario Land Tribunal matter remain confidential at the City Solicitor's discretion, as they contain material subject to settlement privilege.

title: Toronto Public Library Transfer to City of Toronto of 0.40 Metre Widening - 575 Van Horne Avenue (Pleasant View Branch) - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
topics: land, transfers; property
brief: This member motion asks City Council to approve transferring a small 0.40-metre-wide strip of land (about 32.6 square metres) at the Toronto Public Library's Pleasant View branch, 575 Van Horne Avenue, from the Library Board to the City to satisfy site plan conditions for exterior alterations. The Library Board approved the transfer on January 27, 2025.

title: Accepting a Donation from Public Services and Procurement Canada to the City of Toronto - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
topics: purchasing; acquisition; buying; procurement; sourcing; tenders
brief: This member motion asks City Council to accept a donation from Public Services and Procurement Canada of Mobile Hospital Units valued at $6,101,373, to support Toronto Fire Services' emergency response and the Heavy Urban Search and Rescue team (Canada Task Force 3) lifecycle needs. The donation exceeds the $50,000 threshold in the City's donations policy, so Council approval is required; the donor set a March 31, 2025 deadline for the agreement and transfer of the goods.

title: Changes to On-Street Paid Parking Hours of Operation on Avenue Road - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: This member motion asks City Council to approve amendments to the parking meter by-law reflecting changes to paid parking hours on a four-block stretch of Avenue Road, reverting extended weekday hours from a 12 midnight end time back to 9:00 p.m., and to authorize the City Solicitor to introduce the necessary bills. The motion cites concerns about operational feasibility, enforcement, and Green P mobile app usage after 9:00 p.m.

title: Affirming Our Canadian Independence - by Councillor Stephen Holyday, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
topics: constituencies, population; electoral districts; ridings
brief: This member motion asks City Council to affirm that Toronto, as Canada's largest city, opposes any proposal for Canada to join the United States, and to forward the item to all Toronto Members of Parliament. The motion's supporting text cites statements from the US President questioning Canada's independence.

title: Study of Redesign Options to Address the High Level of Congestion and Neighbourhood Traffic at the Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Expressway - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
topics: congestion, traffic; gridlock, motor vehicle traffic; motorized traffic; traffic conditions; traffic flow; trip info; tripinfo
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have Transportation Services study redesign options to ease congestion at the intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Expressway, and to report back in early 2026 with a progress update and workplan. The motion describes long-running congestion and traffic infiltration on local residential streets during the Eglinton Crosstown construction.

title: Let's Amplify the Need for a New Fiscal Framework - New Deal for Cities - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
topics: finance (sc), municipalities; boroughs; cities; counties; regional municipalities; towns
brief: This member motion asks City Council to have the City Manager work with the Federation of Canadian Municipalities and the Association of Municipalities of Ontario to push for sustainable funding frameworks for cities, so municipal revenues keep up with population and economic growth. The motion cites Toronto's structural deficit, state-of-good-repair backlog, and the burden of responsibilities downloaded from higher orders of government.

title: Public Appointments to the Moss Park Arena Board - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jennifer McKelvie
topics: arenas, public appointments; indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: This member motion asks City Council to rescind the current appointments to the Moss Park Arena Board and appoint six new members — including Ines Garcia, a long-standing Moss Park and Regent Park community advocate, and Chris Matthews — to serve until November 2026.

title: Re-Opening and Amending Item 2024.EX15.3 - Advancing the Homelessness Services Capital Infrastructure Strategy (HSCIS) and the 2025 Shelter Infrastructure Plan - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
topics: homelessness, housing services;
brief: This member motion asks City Council to re-open Item 2024.EX15.3 and exclude the Toronto Parking Authority site at 1220 Wilson Avenue from development as a shelter — instead exploring a supportive housing partnership with Humber River Hospital, which sits across the street — and to have staff study creating a park on the site. The motion's supporting text says discussions about a shelter on the site have been superseded by the opportunity to partner with the hospital on an integrated services model.

title: Ormont Drive - Parking Amendments
topics: change, driveways, parking prohibitions; amendments; conversion; modification, no parking
brief: A no-parking zone is being extended on Ormont Drive. Council is asked to extend the no-parking zone on the south side of Ormont Drive 30 metres further east, to keep the area clear and improve heavy-truck access to the driveway at 1290 Ormont Drive. TTC transit service on the street requires council approval.

title: 99 Birmingham Street and 210 Islington Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: planning, zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: A 26-storey tower is also headed to the Tribunal. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose a 26-storey tower with 352 homes at 99 Birmingham Street and 210 Islington Avenue at the Ontario Land Tribunal, appealed after council missed its decision deadline, while talks continue. A Case Management Conference is scheduled for January 28, 2025.

title: 2485 Eglinton Avenue West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: [buildings by height], mixed use areas, official plan amendments, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: A 45-storey tower is headed to the Ontario Land Tribunal. Council is asked to direct the City Solicitor and staff to oppose, in its current form, a 45-storey mixed-use building with 500 homes at 2485 Eglinton Avenue West at the Ontario Land Tribunal, appealed after council missed its decision deadline, while talks continue. A Case Management Conference has yet to be scheduled.

title: 87 Ethel Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, mixed use areas, rezoning; developing land; development (land); land development, re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments
brief: Four towers could rise at 87 Ethel Avenue. Council is asked to approve a zoning change, with a Holding Provision, to allow two mixed-use buildings with four towers of 31 to 34 storeys, with 1,409 rental homes, 141 of them affordable, plus retail space and a legal agreement securing the affordable units. The proposal includes 7,243 square metres of non-residential space, 947 vehicle parking spaces, and 1,580 bicycle parking spaces.

title: The East Mall at West Deane Park Drive - Lane Designation
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, lanes; traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes, ttc
brief: A lane is being marked right-turn-only on The East Mall. Council is asked to approve marking the easterly northbound lane on The East Mall at West Deane Park Drive, from West Deane Park Drive to 30.5 metres south, as right-turn-only except buses, to clarify lane use and reduce conflicts between vehicles. TTC transit service on the street requires council approval.

title: Thirtieth Street at Elder Avenue - Lane Designation
topics: lanes, transit routes; surface routes, traffic lanes; turn lanes; turning lanes
brief: A lane is being marked left-turn-only on Thirtieth Street. Council is asked to approve marking the easterly southbound lane on Thirtieth Street at Elder Avenue, from Elder Avenue to 30.5 metres north, as left-turn-only, to clarify lane use and reduce conflicts between vehicles. TTC transit service on the street requires council approval.

title: 210 Markland Drive - Zoning Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: [buildings by height], residential properties, rezoning; re-zoning; zoning by-law amendment applications; zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: More homes are proposed at 210 Markland Drive. Council is asked to approve a zoning change to allow three new residential buildings of 9, 10, and 12 storeys with 484 homes, while keeping the existing 13-storey rental building with 152 units, plus on-site parkland. The proposal includes 438 vehicle parking spaces and 328 square metres of non-residential space.

title: Advancing Eglinton East Light Rail Transit
topics: rail transportation, transportation infrastructure; railway transport; railway transportation, transportation network; transportation networks
brief: The Eglinton East LRT in Scarborough is moving through design. City Council is asked to approve the 10 percent functional design for the 18.6-kilometre, 27-stop Eglinton East Light Rail Transit from Kennedy Station to Sheppard-McCowan Station and Malvern Town Centre, approve the Kennedy Station alternative design, and direct staff to keep exploring three alternative maintenance and storage facility sites and report back in early 2026. The line would bring higher-order transit to Scarborough.

title: Renewing the City's Partnership with Toronto Global
topics: attractions, investment; cultural attractions; places of interest; tourist attractions; tourist sites
brief: Toronto is renewing its bet on the region's investment attraction agency. City Council is asked to approve the city's continued participation in Toronto Global, the regional investment attraction organization, with $7.2 million in funding over three years from April 2025 to March 2028, and at least three city representatives on its board. The report notes Toronto Global has helped attract about 280 investment initiatives to the GTA, generating roughly 33,000 jobs and approximately $3.8 billion in capital investment, with 74 percent landing in Toronto, and cites annual figures of $2.3 million, $2.4 million and $2.5 million.

title: Moss Park Arena - Governance and Operational Transition Plan
topics: arenas, labour relations; collective bargaining; employee relations; labor relations; union-management relations, indoor hockey rinks; rinks
brief: Moss Park Arena's management is changing hands. This item concerns the plan to change the arena's governance from a Board of Management to a city-operated arena by the end of 2025, with options to improve equitable community access to its programs. Council is asked to keep the confidential attachment confidential. The financial impact section estimates operating costs at $1.0 million a year gross ($0.30 million net), with $0.70 million a year in revenue from ice rentals and program fees, if the arena moves to city operation.

title: Transmittal of a Report from the Board of Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation: Request regarding the composition of the Board
topics: board members, seniors housing;
brief: A board seat change at the seniors housing corporation is before council. City Council, as shareholder of Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation, is asked to approve adding the City Manager, or a city employee designate, to the board in an ex-officio non-voting capacity until December 31, 2026.

title: Old City Hall - Future Uses Analysis
topics: courts, redevelopment, restoration; rehabilitation (property), rehabilitation (property); renewal; revitalization
brief: The future of Old City Hall is being re-examined. City Council is asked to direct staff and CreateTO to re-examine potential future uses for Old City Hall, the historic 1889-1899 landmark at Bay and Queen Streets and a National Historic Site, in line with revitalization and management principles, and to report back by the second quarter of 2026. The report cites a $225 million figure. The landmark's primary tenant, Infrastructure Ontario, leased the space for the provincial courts since 1972.

title: 705 Progress Avenue - City-initiated Development Master Plan and Planning Approval Process
topics: board members, development; developing land; development (land); land development
brief: A 10.9-acre city-and-school-board site is headed for redevelopment. City Council is asked to approve advancing a City-initiated Development Master Plan and planning approval process for 705 Progress Avenue, jointly owned by the city and the school board, with CreateTO and the Toronto Lands Corporation (acting for the Toronto District School Board) on delivery.

title: Authorization to Enter into Agreements to Deliver a Successful FIFA World Cup 2026
topics: agreements, budgets, soccer; budgets and accounts, tenancy agreements
brief: Deals with FIFA's official vendors need quick sign-off. City Council is asked to authorize the City Manager and the World Cup hosting executive director to negotiate and sign agreements with FIFA's exclusive vendors for the 2026 World Cup, provided they meet host city requirements and stay within the approved procurement plan. With the tournament approaching, the motion aims to let staff act quickly while reporting back on community workforce opportunities, transparency, and accountability.

title: Good Roads November Advocacy and Board Meeting
topics: board members, bridges, roads; circles (roads); circuits (roads); courts (roads); crescents (roads); drives (roads); gardens (roads); gates (roads); groves (roads); heights (roads); roadways; squares (roads); streets; terraces (roads); trails (roads)
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Ainslie reports on representing Toronto at Good Roads' Queens Park Advocacy Days and board meetings in November 2024, advocating on municipal liability under the OHSA, reversing the downloading of road and bridge infrastructure to municipalities, and supporting rural roads, including a proposed five-year, $168 million program for rural road funding. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Federation of Canadian Municipalities Report to Council
topics: board members, meetings;
brief: This is a procedural item: Councillor Ainslie reports on the Federation of Canadian Municipalities board meeting held December 3 to 5, 2024 in Ottawa, covering advocacy ahead of the federal election, including over 100 meetings with MPs and Senators. Council is asked to receive the report for information.

title: Toward Municipal Autonomy and Effective Local Governance
topics: advisory committees, local governments; ad hoc committees; advisory groups; council reference groups; liaison committees; panels; political reference groups; public advisory committees; reference groups; round tables; roundtables; special committees; steering committees; sub-committees; subcommittees; task forces; working groups, city governments; municipal governments; regional governments
brief: How Toronto relates to the province is the subject of this motion. City Council is asked to direct the City Manager to establish a Program Advisory Body on Municipal Autonomy and Effective Local Governance, in response to provincial involvement in municipal decisions. The motion's supporters frame it as a response to the province overturning city decisions, while the province has presented its actions as within its constitutional role; the advisory body would examine that relationship. It matters to how local decisions on transit, roads, housing, and recreation are made and who can override them.

title: Reducing Stormwater Runoff and Mitigating Basement Flooding
topics: flooding, stormwater management; floods, storm water management; swm; wet weather flow management
brief: Bigger subsidies for flood-proofing homes are being explored. City Council is asked to direct staff to report back by the third quarter of 2025 on a plan for new and expanded subsidies under the Basement Flooding Protection Subsidy Program, including a home stormwater assessment subsidy and higher subsidies for backwater valves and sump pumps. The item follows the July and August 2024 storms that caused basement and surface flooding affecting over a thousand properties.

title: ReNew Golden Mile Environmental Assessment:   Final Report
topics: assessment, construction; building
brief: New streets in the Golden Mile area are up for endorsement. City Council is asked to endorse the preferred alignments and designs for five new and reconfigured streets under the ReNew Golden Mile Environmental Assessment, and to authorize staff to prepare the Environmental Study Report and issue the notice of completion. The study covers lands along Eglinton Avenue East and Craigton Drive, between Victoria Park Avenue and Birchmount Road.

title: Advancing the Waterfront East Light Rail Transit
topics: light rail transit, waterfronts; lakefronts; waterfront trail, lrt
brief: The Waterfront East streetcar line is moving forward in stages. City Council is asked to authorize staff to develop a phasing and delivery plan with updated costs for the Waterfront East Light Rail Transit, and to approve advancing design of the Queens Quay East extension between Parliament and Cherry Streets. When fully built, the 3.8-kilometre line is projected to provide over 50,000 daily trips, serving an estimated 100,000 residents and 50,000 jobs along its alignment, including the Central Waterfront, East Bayfront, and the Port Lands.

title: Advancing Truth, Reconciliation and Justice: Supporting 2-Spirited People of the 1st Nations' Development of a 2SLGBTQIA+ Indigenous Emergency Shelter at 996 Woodbine Avenue
topics: First Nations, aboriginal services; aboriginal community; aboriginal peoples; aboriginals; indians (native); indigenous peoples; inuit; metis; métis; native peoples
brief: Whether to sell city land for $2 for an Indigenous 2SLGBTQIA+ emergency shelter goes to council. City Council is asked to accept an offer from 2-Spirited People of the 1st Nations to buy part of the city-owned property at 996 Woodbine Avenue for a nominal $2.00, so the organization can construct and operate an 11-bed emergency shelter meeting the unique needs of 2SLGBTQIA+ Indigenous individuals seeking shelter or fleeing violence. The site has been identified as the preferred location after work with the organization since July 2023, and the shelter would be Toronto's first purpose-built emergency shelter for 2SLGBTQIA+ Indigenous people.

title: 261-285 Queen Street East and 410 Richmond Street East - Development Charges Complaint - Request for Directions
brief: This is a legal directions item: council will give the City Solicitor confidential directions. The city received a complaint from Queen Ontario GP Inc. under section 20 of the Development Charges Act, 1997 about development charges paid for 261-285 Queen Street East and 410 Richmond Street East, and the solicitor needs instructions on the response. Details are protected by legal privilege.

title: 19 Belfield Road - Toronto Local Appeal Body Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: This is a legal directions item: the City Solicitor gets private instructions. The Toronto Local Appeal Body case concerns 19 Belfield Road, where the applicant sought a minor variance for a vehicle dealership and the city appealed the Committee of Adjustment's approval in November. The decision determines whether the dealership use is allowed.

title: 1437-1455 Queen Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: planning & development (sc), planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a legal directions item: council's directions are confidential. The Ontario Land Tribunal case concerns 1437-1455 Queen Street West, where the applicant proposed a 12-storey mixed-use building with one level of underground parking, ground-floor retail and 249 homes, then appealed after council did not decide. The result shapes development on Queen West.

title: 1040 Martin Grove Road, Units 8 and 9 - Toronto Local Appeal Body Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: This is a legal directions item: council will instruct the City Solicitor privately. The case is a Toronto Local Appeal Body hearing over 1040 Martin Grove Road, Units 8 and 9, where the applicant sought a minor variance to open a vehicle dealership and the city appealed the Committee of Adjustment's approval. The ruling affects whether the dealership can operate there.

title: 1930-1938 Bloor Street West and 3, 5 and 21 Quebec Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: hearings, planning tribunals; omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a legal directions item: the strategy stays behind closed doors. It concerns an Ontario Land Tribunal case over 1930-1938 Bloor Street West and 3, 5 and 21 Quebec Avenue, where the applicant proposed a 17-storey mixed-use building with ground-floor retail and 144 homes above, then appealed in March 2024 after council did not decide. The outcome decides what gets built at Bloor and Quebec.

title: Ookwemin Minising - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: by-laws, hearings, official plan amendments, planning tribunals; bylaws, omb; ontario municipal board
brief: This is a legal directions item about the Port Lands revitalization. The City Solicitor is seeking confidential directions on Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings tied to Ookwemin Minising (formerly Villiers Island), where council adopted Official Plan Amendment 409 and zoning changes in June 2024 as part of the Waterfront Toronto and CreateTO revitalization. The directions set the city's legal position on the island's future.

title: 86, 100 - 108 Lombard Street, 103 Richmond Street East - Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
topics: zoning bylaws; zoning by-laws; zoning bylaw project; zoning project
brief: This is a legal directions item: the City Solicitor needs confidential instructions. It covers the Ontario Land Tribunal proceedings on the zoning by-law amendment applications for 86, 100-108 Lombard Street and 103 Richmond Street East, which the applicant appealed after council failed to decide within the legislated timeline. topics: parking regulations, traffic regulations; parking by-laws; parking bylaws

The Mobile Only Zone on the north side of Berryman, between Hazelton Avenue and Davenport Road, would run 11:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. Monday to Saturday and 1:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Sunday, with a one-hour maximum. North York Community Council is asked to amend the existing 10-minute parking rule — in effect 8:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, on the west side between Franklin Avenue and Stuart Avenue — so it applies between Franklin Avenue and a point 65 metres south, and to prohibit parking at all times from Stuart Avenue to a point 32 metres north. The change would keep a clear passage for vehicles around the intersection geometry. Drivers who park on Botham Road would be affected.

title: 425 Manor Road East - Application to Remove a Private Tree
topics: privately-owned trees, removal, trees; ash trees, private owned trees; private trees; privately owned trees; trees on private property
brief: A permit to remove a privately owned red oak tree at 425 Manor Road East would be denied. North York Community Council is asked to refuse the application — the applicant cited concerns about falling acorns or dead branches and personal safety — because the three-stemmed tree (30, 48 and 52 centimetres in diameter) is healthy and maintainable under the City's tree by-laws. Community Council has final say on appeals of denied tree permits. The tree would stay.
